He repeated the drills until the movements became smoother. During the team scrimmage, he managed to hold his ground against the second-string offense. He reviewed the playbook that evening and highlighted the calls for his new position. He planned to ask the coach about a few alignments.
text_zh: 在春季训练期间，卡洛斯被要求从进攻线改打防守线。他花了一上午学习新的姿势和间隙职责。防守教练向他展示了如何阅读进攻方的第一步。当他尝试用新技术摆脱阻挡时，他感到笨拙。他反复练习，直到动作变得更加流畅。在球队分队比赛中，他成功抵挡住了二队进攻。当晚他复习了战术手册，并标出了新位置的关键战术。他计划向教练请教一些站位问题。

topic: An athlete is asked to switch positions
text_en: When the volleyball coach asked Dana to switch from outside hitter to setter, she agreed to try it during the next tournament. In practice, she worked on her footwork and hand placement for sets. The ball often spun off her fingers when she tried to set from the back row. She practiced with a teammate who gave her tips on wrist action. During a scrimmage, she managed a few clean sets to the outside. She still felt more natural hitting, but she began to appreciate the rhythm of setting. She decided to keep working on it.
text_zh: 当排球教练要求达娜从主攻改打二传时，她同意在接下来的锦标赛中尝试。训练中，她练习了传球时的步法和手型。当她尝试从后排传球时，球经常从她的手指上旋转出去。她与一位队友一起练习，队友给了她一些关于手腕动作的建议。在一次分队比赛中，她成功传出了几次干净的球到四号位。她仍然觉得扣球更自然，但她开始欣赏二传的节奏。她决定继续努力练习。

topic: An athlete is asked to switch positions
text_en: Marcus had always been a defender, so the coach's request to play as a holding midfielder took some getting used to. In the first training match, he found himself dropping back too deep and leaving space in the middle. The coach shouted instructions to push up. Marcus adjusted his positioning and started to intercept passes. He linked up with the forwards a few times and created a chance. After the match, he spoke with the coach about his responsibilities during transitions. He felt he had a clearer idea of what was expected. He planned to study some match footage.
text_zh: 马库斯一直踢后卫，所以教练要求他踢防守型中场需要一些时间来适应。在第一场训练赛中，他发现自己回撤太深，在中场留下了空间。教练大声喊叫让他压上。马库斯调整了站位，开始拦截传球。他与前锋进行了几次配合，并创造了一次机会。赛后，他与教练讨论了在攻防转换中的职责。他觉得自己对教练的期望有了更清晰的认识。他计划研究一些比赛录像。

topic: An athlete is asked to switch positions
text_en: Jonah had played shortstop his whole career, but the manager wanted him at first base. He borrowed a first baseman's mitt and spent extra time taking throws from the infielders. The stretch felt unfamiliar, and he fumbled a couple of low tosses. He worked on footwork around the bag, learning to keep his heel on the base. During the intrasquad game, he handled a few routine grounders without issue. The manager mentioned he'd get more reps there tomorrow. Jonah hung up his glove and headed to the showers, thinking about the positioning he'd need to practice.
text_zh: 乔纳整个职业生涯都打游击手，但教练希望他打一垒。他借了一个一垒手手套，花了额外的时间接内场手的传球。伸展动作感觉很陌生，他几次接低传球时失误。他练习了垒包周围的步法，学会了保持脚跟踩在垒包上。在队内比赛中，他处理了几个常规地滚球，没有出现问题。教练提到明天会让他在这里获得更多训练机会。乔纳挂好手套，走向淋浴间，思考着需要练习的站位。

topic: An athlete is asked to switch positions
text_en: When the basketball coach asked Sam to play point guard instead of shooting guard, Sam spent extra time after practice on ball-handling drills. He practiced the pick-and-roll reads with the big men. In the scrimmage, he tried to distribute the ball early and get everyone involved. He made a few turnovers when he forced passes into traffic. The coach reminded him to be patient and use the screen. Sam started to find his teammates in better spots. He noted the plays that worked and the ones that didn't. He stayed late to practice the entry passes.
text_zh: 当篮球教练要求萨姆改打控球后卫而不是得分后卫时，萨姆在训练后花了额外的时间进行控球训练。他与内线球员练习了挡拆配合的阅读。在分队比赛中，他试图尽早分配球，让每个人都参与进来。当他强行传球到人堆里时，他出现了几次失误。教练提醒他要耐心，利用掩护。萨姆开始找到更好的位置传球给队友。他记下了哪些战术有效，哪些无效。他留下来加练了传球。

topic: An athlete is asked to switch positions
text_en: The swim coach asked Tom to switch from freestyle sprints to the individual medley for the upcoming meet. Tom had not swum butterfly competitively in years. He started each practice with drill work on the fly and backstroke turns. His times were slower than his usual freestyle splits, but he focused on technique. He asked the coach to film his strokes so he could compare them with the model. After reviewing the footage, he worked on his underwater pull. He felt he was making gradual progress in the new events.
text_zh: 游泳教练要求汤姆在即将到来的比赛中从自由泳短距离改游个人混合泳。汤姆已经多年没有参加过蝶泳比赛了。他每次训练都从蝶泳和仰泳转身的技术练习开始。他的成绩比他通常的自由泳分段成绩慢，但他专注于技术。他请教练拍摄他的划水动作，以便与标准动作进行比较。回顾录像后，他练习了水下划水。他觉得自己在新项目中取得了逐步的进步。

topic: An athlete is asked to switch positions
text_en: The tennis coach wanted Nadia to move from singles to doubles for the team match. Nadia had always preferred the singles court and its straightforward rhythm. In her first doubles practice, she struggled with the net play and the communication with her partner. They kept calling for the same balls. They tried a few different formations and settled on a one-up, one-back strategy. Nadia worked on her volleys and reflex shots. By the end of the session, they had won a couple of practice games. She agreed to try the new role in the upcoming match.
text_zh: 网球教练希望纳迪亚在团体赛中从单打改打双打。纳迪亚一直更喜欢单打场地及其简单的节奏。在第一次双打训练中，她在网前技术和与搭档的沟通上遇到了困难。他们总是争抢同一个球。他们尝试了几种不同的站位，最终确定了一前一后的策略。纳迪亚练习了截击和反应球。到训练结束时，他们赢了几场练习赛。她同意在即将到来的比赛中尝试新的角色。

topic: An athlete is asked to switch positions
text_en: When the lacrosse coach asked Ben to move from attack to midfield, Ben spent the practice working on his transition running and ground-ball picks. He was used to staying near the goal and taking shots. Now he had to track back on defense and then sprint forward on the break. He missed a few checks and got beaten on the wing once. He asked a teammate for tips on footwork in the defensive end. By the end of practice, he had made a few good clears. He still felt more comfortable on offense but saw the value in the new role.
text_zh: 当曲棍球教练要求本从攻击位转到中场时，本在训练中专注于他的转换跑动和地面球捡拾。他习惯于待在球门附近并射门。现在他必须回防，然后在快攻时冲刺向前。他漏掉了几次拦截，还有一次在边路被突破。他向队友请教防守端的步法技巧。训练结束时，他成功完成了几次漂亮的解围。他仍然觉得在进攻端更自在，但也看到了新角色的价值。

topic: An athlete is asked to switch positions
text_en: Jonas had been a goalkeeper for years, but the team needed him on the field. At training, he joined the outfield drills, passing and moving without the ball. His footwork was slower than the others, and he gave away possession a few times. The coach called out instructions, and Jonas adjusted his runs. During a small-sided game, he managed a decent cross that led to a chance. Afterward, he helped pack up the cones and nets. On the drive home, he thought about the new role and what he would need to improve.
text_zh: 乔纳斯多年来一直担任守门员，但球队需要他上场。训练中，他加入了外场球员的练习，进行传球和无球跑动。他的步法比别人慢，几次丢球。教练大声喊出指示，乔纳斯调整了他的跑动。在小场比赛期间，他传出了一记不错的传中，创造了一次机会。之后，他帮忙收拾锥桶和球网。开车回家的路上，他思考着新角色以及自己需要改进的地方。

topic: An athlete is asked to switch positions
text_en: The track coach asked Leo to move from the sprints to the long jump for the upcoming meet. Leo had not jumped since middle school. He practiced his approach run and measured his steps repeatedly. His first few jumps were flat and he landed awkwardly. He watched a teammate demonstrate the hitch-kick technique. Leo tried to emulate the motion and focused on his takeoff angle. By the end of practice, he had improved his distance slightly. He knew he needed more work on his landing. He planned to come early the next day to measure his steps again.
text_zh: 田径教练要求利奥在即将到来的比赛中从短跑转为跳远。利奥自初中以来就没有跳过。他练习助跑，并反复测量步点。他的前几次跳跃很平，落地姿势也别扭。他观看队友演示挺身式跳远技术。利奥试图模仿这个动作，并专注于起跳角度。训练结束时，他的成绩略有提高。他知道自己还需要在落地方面下功夫。他计划第二天早点来重新测量步点。

topic: An athlete is asked to switch positions
text_en: The softball coach asked Nina to move from catcher to third base for the tournament. Nina had caught for years and knew the hitters well from behind the plate. At third, she had to react to bunts and line drives. In the first practice, she missed a hard grounder that skipped past her. She worked on her footwork and glove positioning with the infield coach. She practiced charging slow rollers and making the throw to first. By the end of the session, she had fielded a few cleanly. She still felt less experienced but was getting the hang of it.
text_zh: 垒球教练要求妮娜在锦标赛中从捕手转到三垒。妮娜多年来一直担任捕手，在本垒板后对击球手很了解。在三垒，她必须对短打和直线球做出反应。在第一次训练中，她漏掉了一个从她身边弹过的硬地滚球。她与内场教练一起练习步法和手套位置。她练习了冲向慢速滚球并传向一垒。训练结束时，她干净利落地接住了几个球。她仍然觉得自己经验不足，但正在逐渐掌握要领。

topic: An athlete is asked to switch positions
text_en: The rugby coach asked Jack to move from flanker to inside center for the upcoming match. Jack had always played in the forwards, so the backline was unfamiliar. He worked on his passing and running angles in the backs' drills. He struggled with the timing of the crash ball and often arrived too early. The fly-half gave him some advice on straightening the line. During the scrimmage, he made a line break and offloaded to the winger. He felt he was adapting to the new position, though the defensive reads were still tricky.
text_zh: 橄榄球教练要求杰克在即将到来的比赛中从侧翼前锋转到内中锋。杰克一直打前锋，所以后卫线对他来说很陌生。他在后卫训练中练习传球和跑动角度。他在冲击球的时机上遇到困难，经常到得太早。飞卫给了他一些关于拉直进攻线的建议。在对抗训练中，他完成了一次突破，并将球传给了边锋。他觉得自己正在适应新位置，尽管防守阅读仍然棘手。

topic: An athlete is asked to switch positions
text_en: The soccer coach asked Hannah to move from goalkeeper to defender for the next match. Hannah had played outfield in youth soccer, but she had been a keeper for years. In practice, she had to adjust to heading the ball and tackling. She was tentative in her first challenge and let the striker get past her. The coach encouraged her to trust her positioning. She worked on her distribution and timing of tackles. By the end of the session, she had made a few clearances and even started an attack. She felt more comfortable with each drill.
text_zh: 足球教练要求汉娜在下一场比赛中从守门员转为后卫。汉娜在青少年足球时期踢过外场，但她多年来一直担任守门员。在训练中，她必须适应头球和铲球。她在第一次对抗中犹豫不决，让前锋突破了她。教练鼓励她相信自己的站位。她练习了传球和铲球时机。训练结束时，她完成了几次解围，甚至发起了一次进攻。随着每次训练，她感觉越来越自在。

topic: An athlete is asked to switch positions
text_en: The baseball coach asked Chris to switch from shortstop to second base for the doubleheader. Chris had played shortstop his whole life and was used to the throws from the hole. At second, he had to cover first on bunt plays and turn double plays differently. He practiced the pivot footwork with the first baseman. He missed a couple of throws but gradually found the rhythm. He asked the coach about the cutoff positioning for the new spot. By the end of practice, he was turning double plays more smoothly. He felt ready for the games.
text_zh: 棒球教练要求克里斯在双赛中从游击手转到二垒。克里斯一生都在打游击手，习惯了从游击区深位的传球。在二垒，他必须在短打战术中补一垒，并以不同的方式完成双杀。他和一垒手练习了轴心脚步法。他漏掉了几个传球，但逐渐找到了节奏。他向教练询问了新位置的截球站位。训练结束时，他完成双杀更加流畅。他觉得自己已经为比赛做好了准备。

topic: An athlete is asked to switch positions
text_en: Tomas had always played midfield, but the coach wanted him to drop back to sweeper. He took the new position during the scrimmage, staying behind the defensive line and reading the opposing attack. He made a few clearances and directed the fullbacks into position. His first long pass went out of bounds, but his next one found the winger in stride. The coach called out a correction about his starting angle, and Tomas adjusted his stance. After the session, he spoke with the goalkeeper about communication on set pieces. He gathered the balls and carried them to the equipment shed.
text_zh: 托马斯一直踢中场，但教练希望他回撤到清道夫位置。他在对抗赛中担任新位置，站在防线后面，阅读对手的进攻。他完成了几次解围，并指挥边后卫站位。他的第一脚长传出了界，但第二脚找到了跑动中的边锋。教练指出了他起始角度的错误，托马斯调整了站位。训练结束后，他和守门员讨论了定位球时的沟通。他收集了球，把它们搬到了器材棚。

topic: An athlete is asked to switch positions
text_en: The volleyball coach asked Rachel to switch from middle blocker to opposite hitter. Rachel had played middle for years and was used to quick attacks and blocking at the net. At opposite, she had to hit from the right side and play the back row more often. She practiced her approach from the right side and worked on her back-row attacks. She struggled with the timing of the setter's dump plays. She talked with the setter about the signals. By the end of practice, she had landed a few kills and was getting the hang of the new rotation.
text_zh: 排球教练要求瑞秋从副攻手转到接应二传。瑞秋多年来一直打副攻，习惯了快攻和网前拦网。在接应位置，她必须从右侧进攻，并且更多地在后排参与防守。她练习了从右侧的助跑，并练习了后排进攻。她在二传手的二次球时机上遇到困难。她和二传手讨论了信号。训练结束时，她扣中了几次，逐渐掌握了新的轮转。

topic: An athlete is asked to switch positions
text_en: The football coach asked Derek to move from tight end to fullback for the upcoming game. Derek had been a receiver-oriented tight end, so blocking was not his strongest skill. In practice, he worked on his lead blocks and pass protection. He missed a few assignments and got pushed back by the linebacker. The running back gave him tips on staying low and driving his feet. During the scrimmage, he opened a hole for a touchdown. He still preferred catching passes, but he understood the team's need. He planned to review the playbook that night.
text_zh: 橄榄球教练要求德里克在即将到来的比赛中从近端锋转到全卫。德里克一直是偏接球型的近端锋，所以阻挡不是他的强项。在训练中，他练习了领路阻挡和传球保护。他漏掉了几次任务，并被线卫推了回去。跑卫给了他一些建议，让他保持低重心并持续蹬地。在对抗赛中，他为达阵打开了一个缺口。他仍然更喜欢接球，但他理解球队的需要。他计划当晚复习战术手册。

topic: A student is accused of plagiarism
text_en: Elena checked the email from her professor again. The subject line read "Plagiarism Concern" and the body mentioned her recent essay on Victorian poetry. She had cited her sources, she was sure of it. She opened the document on her laptop and scrolled through the paragraphs. The flagged sentence was a quote from a critical essay she remembered finding in the library database. She had put quotation marks around it and included the author's name. But the professor had noted that the citation format was incorrect. Elena closed the laptop and picked up her phone to text her classmate about the assignment guidelines.
text_zh: 埃琳娜再次查看了教授发来的电子邮件。主题行写着“抄袭疑虑”，正文提到了她最近关于维多利亚时代诗歌的论文。她确信自己引用了来源。她打开笔记本电脑上的文档，滚动浏览各个段落。被标记的句子是她记得在图书馆数据库中找到的一篇评论文章的引文。她给它加上了引号，并包含了作者的名字。但教授指出引文格式不正确。埃琳娜合上笔记本电脑，拿起手机给同学发短信询问作业指南。

topic: A student is accused of plagiarism
text_en: Marcus sat in the front row of the lecture hall while the teaching assistant handed back the term papers. When his copy was placed face down on the desk, he flipped it over to see a red note at the top: "See me after class." He waited until the other students had filed out. The TA pointed to a paragraph in the middle of the paper. "This section matches a source almost word for word," she said. Marcus explained that he had used the source's ideas but thought he had paraphrased it. He asked if he could revise and resubmit the section.
text_zh: 马库斯坐在演讲厅的前排，助教正在发还学期论文。当他的那份被面朝下放在桌上时，他翻过来看到顶部有一条红色批注：“课后见我。”他一直等到其他学生都离开了。助教指着论文中间的一段说：“这部分几乎逐字逐句地匹配了一个来源。”马库斯解释说，他使用了来源的想法，但以为自己已经改写了。他问是否可以修改并重新提交这一部分。

topic: A student is accused of plagiarism
text_en: Priya was in the library when her phone buzzed with an email from the academic integrity office. The message stated that her lab report had been flagged for potential plagiarism because it contained passages identical to a previous semester's submission. She remembered writing the report with her lab partner, and they had shared notes. She looked over her report on the screen. Some of the phrasing did look familiar. She wondered if her partner had copied from an old file. She decided to contact the office to ask for more details about the specific passages.
text_zh: 普里亚在图书馆时，手机收到学术诚信办公室发来的电子邮件。邮件称她的实验报告因包含与上学期提交的内容相同的段落而被标记为可能存在抄袭。她记得是和实验伙伴一起写的报告，他们共享了笔记。她在屏幕上查看自己的报告。有些措辞确实看起来很眼熟。她想知道她的伙伴是否从旧文件中复制了内容。她决定联系办公室，询问有关具体段落的更多细节。

topic: A student is accused of plagiarism
text_en: Jonah was helping his younger sister with her homework when his advisor called. The advisor said a professor had reported that Jonah's history paper contained unattributed quotes. Jonah put down the pencil and listened. He recalled using a book from the library and taking extensive notes. He had intended to go back and add citations but had run out of time. He told the advisor he could provide his research notes and drafts. After the call, he went to his desk and started looking for the folder with his handwritten notes.
text_zh: 乔纳正在帮妹妹做作业时，他的导师打来电话。导师说一位教授报告乔纳的历史论文中有未注明出处的引文。乔纳放下铅笔，听着。他记得用过图书馆的一本书，并做了大量笔记。他本打算回去补充引文，但时间不够了。他告诉导师他可以提供他的研究笔记和草稿。挂断电话后，他走到书桌前，开始寻找他手写笔记的文件夹。

topic: A student is accused of plagiarism
text_en: Aisha sat in the departmental office, waiting to speak with her professor about the grade on her sociology paper. The professor entered and sat down, explaining that a section of her paper was nearly identical to an article published in a journal. Aisha thought about the article. She had read it and summarized it in her own words, or so she believed. The professor opened the paper and pointed to a paragraph. Aisha read it silently. The wording was close to the article, closer than she remembered. She told the professor she would like to see the article to compare.
text_zh: 艾莎坐在系办公室里，等着和教授谈论她社会学论文的成绩。教授走进来坐下，解释说她的论文有一部分与期刊上发表的一篇文章几乎完全相同。艾莎想到了那篇文章。她读过它，并用自己的话进行了总结，至少她是这么认为的。教授打开论文，指着一段落。艾莎默默地读了一遍。措辞与文章很接近，比她记忆中的还要接近。她告诉教授她想看看那篇文章以便比较。

topic: A student is accused of plagiarism
text_en: Daniel received a notification from the online submission system that his essay had been flagged by the plagiarism checker. He clicked the link and saw the similarity report. Several sentences were highlighted, matching a website he had used for background information. He had cited the website in his bibliography but had not used quotation marks in the text. He sat back in his chair and looked at the report. He decided to email his instructor to explain that the flagged text was a direct quote that he had failed to format correctly.
text_zh: 丹尼尔收到在线提交系统的通知，说他的论文被抄袭检查器标记了。他点击链接，看到了相似度报告。有几个句子被高亮显示，与一个他用来获取背景信息的网站匹配。他在参考书目中引用了该网站，但在正文中没有使用引号。他靠在椅背上，看着报告。他决定给导师发邮件，解释被标记的文本是直接引文，但他没有正确格式化。

topic: A student is accused of plagiarism
text_en: Leah was at her part-time job when she got a message from her chemistry professor asking her to come to office hours. The next day, she stopped by. The professor explained that her lab report had been flagged because it was similar to a report from a previous year. Leah remembered working alone on the report. She had used the lab manual and her own data. She asked if she could see the other report. The professor said she would send it by email. Leah thanked her and left the office, thinking about her notes.
text_zh: 利亚在做兼职时收到化学教授的消息，让她去办公室答疑时间。第二天，她去了。教授解释说，她的实验报告被标记，因为它与上一年的报告相似。利亚记得她是独自完成报告的。她使用了实验手册和自己的数据。她问是否可以看看另一份报告。教授说她会通过电子邮件发送。利亚谢过她，离开了办公室，心里想着自己的笔记。

topic: A student is accused of plagiarism
text_en: Omar was reviewing his class notes when his roommate mentioned that a notice had been posted on the course page about a plagiarism case. Omar opened the course website and saw that his name was not listed, but he had heard that the instructor had sent individual emails. He checked his inbox. There was a message from the instructor with the subject "Academic Integrity." The email said that his final paper contained a paragraph that matched a source without proper citation. Omar read the paragraph in question. He had copied the text from a textbook but thought he had changed enough words. He wrote a reply to the instructor.
text_zh: 奥马尔正在复习课堂笔记时，室友提到课程页面上发布了一则关于抄袭案件的通知。奥马尔打开课程网站，看到自己的名字没有被列出，但他听说讲师已经发送了个人电子邮件。他检查了收件箱。有一封来自讲师的邮件，主题是“学术诚信”。邮件说他的期末论文中有一段与来源匹配，但没有正确引用。奥马尔读了相关段落。他从教科书中复制了文本，但以为已经改了足够多的词。他给讲师写了回复。

topic: A student is accused of plagiarism
text_en: Tara was in the student lounge when her friend came over with a concerned look. "Did you get the email about the group project?" the friend asked. Tara opened her phone and saw an email from the professor stating that parts of their group presentation had been copied from an online source. Tara remembered that they had divided the sections and she had written the introduction. She thought she had paraphrased the source. She looked at her friend and asked if she had written the section in question. The friend said she had used a few phrases directly. Tara suggested they meet with the professor together.
text_zh: 塔拉在学生休息室时，她的朋友带着担忧的表情走过来。“你收到关于小组项目的邮件了吗？”朋友问道。塔拉打开手机，看到教授发来的一封邮件，说他们小组演示的部分内容是从在线来源复制的。塔拉记得他们分了部分，她写了引言。她以为自己改写了来源。她看着朋友，问她是否写了有问题的部分。朋友说她直接用了几个短语。塔拉建议他们一起见教授。

topic: A student is accused of plagiarism
text_en: Ethan was walking across campus when he saw his professor outside the library. The professor waved him over and said, "I need to talk to you about your essay." They stepped aside. The professor explained that a paragraph in Ethan's essay was nearly identical to an essay submitted in another section. Ethan felt his face get warm. He remembered writing that paragraph late at night. He had used an online summary and thought he had rewritten it. He told the professor he could show his notes and the original source. The professor said they could discuss it during office hours.
text_zh: 伊桑正穿过校园时，看到教授在图书馆外面。教授挥手让他过来，说：“我需要和你谈谈你的论文。”他们走到一边。教授解释说，伊桑论文中的一段与另一部分提交的论文几乎完全相同。伊桑感到脸热。他记得那段是深夜写的。他使用了一个在线摘要，并以为已经重写了。他告诉教授他可以展示他的笔记和原始来源。教授说他们可以在办公时间讨论。

topic: A student is accused of plagiarism
text_en: Nadia was in the middle of making dinner when her phone buzzed with an email from the university's academic conduct committee. The email said that her short story for the creative writing class had been flagged because it contained a passage similar to a published work. Nadia put down the spoon and read the email again. She had written the story based on her own experiences, but she had read a similar story in a magazine last year. She wondered if she had subconsciously borrowed a phrase. She set her phone aside and finished preparing the meal, then went to her computer to check her original draft.
text_zh: 娜迪亚正在做晚饭时，手机收到了一封来自大学学术行为委员会的电子邮件。邮件说她的创意写作课短篇小说因包含与已发表作品相似的段落而被标记。娜迪亚放下勺子，又读了一遍邮件。她是根据自己的经历写的故事，但去年她在一本杂志上读过类似的故事。她想知道自己是否下意识地借用了一个短语。她把手机放在一边，做完饭，然后去电脑前查看她的原始草稿。

topic: A student is accused of plagiarism
text_en: Gabriel sat in the back of the classroom as the instructor handed back the research papers. When he received his, he noticed a sticky note on the first page: "Please see me." After class, he approached the desk. The instructor showed him a highlighted sentence in the conclusion. "This appears in a paper I read last year," the instructor said. Gabriel looked at the sentence. He had written it himself, but it was a common phrase. He told the instructor that he had not seen the other paper. The instructor said they would look into it further. Gabriel nodded and left the classroom.
text_zh: 加布里埃尔坐在教室后面，老师正在发回研究论文。当他收到自己的论文时，他注意到第一页上有一张便利贴：“请来见我。”下课后，他走到讲台前。老师给他看了结论中一个高亮显示的句子。“这句话出现在我去年读过的一篇论文中，”老师说。加布里埃尔看了看那个句子。那是他自己写的，但这是一个常见的短语。他告诉老师他没有看过那篇论文。老师说他们会进一步调查。加布里埃尔点点头，离开了教室。

topic: A student is accused of plagiarism
text_en: Maya was in the library printing her final paper when she noticed an email from her professor. She opened it and read that her paper had been flagged for potential plagiarism because of the reference list. The email said some of the cited sources were not mentioned in the text. Maya had included several sources she had read for background but had not directly referenced. She thought that was acceptable. She walked to the circulation desk and asked the librarian for help with the citation style. The librarian showed her the guidelines for in-text citations.
text_zh: 玛雅正在图书馆打印她的期末论文时，注意到教授发来的一封电子邮件。她打开邮件，读到她的论文因参考文献列表而被标记为可能存在抄袭。邮件说有些引用的来源在正文中没有被提及。玛雅收录了几篇她为背景阅读但未直接引用的来源。她认为这是可以接受的。她走到借阅台，向图书管理员寻求引用格式方面的帮助。图书管理员向她展示了文中引用的指南。

topic: A student is accused of plagiarism
text_en: Carlos was at the gym when his phone rang. It was his academic advisor. The advisor said that one of his professors had submitted a report about his midterm essay. The essay contained a section that was copied from a classmate's essay from the previous semester. Carlos remembered sharing notes with an older student who had taken the same course. He had used some of the notes in his essay. He told the advisor he had not meant to copy. The advisor said they would need to discuss it with the professor. Carlos left the gym and walked to the student center to find the advisor's office.
text_zh: 卡洛斯正在健身房时，电话响了。是他的学术顾问。顾问说，他的一位教授提交了一份关于他期中论文的报告。论文中包含一部分是从上学期一位同学的论文中复制的。卡洛斯记得他曾与一位修过同一门课的高年级学生分享过笔记。他在论文中使用了一些笔记。他告诉顾问他不是故意抄袭的。顾问说他们需要与教授讨论这件事。卡洛斯离开健身房，走到学生中心去找顾问的办公室。

topic: A student is accused of plagiarism
text_en: Hannah was in her dorm room when her roommate returned with a stack of mail. There was an official envelope from the university. Hannah opened it and found a letter stating that her anthropology paper had been flagged because it contained uncredited paraphrasing from a book. Hannah recalled using the book for her research and taking notes. She thought she had paraphrased the ideas correctly. She put the letter on her desk and looked at the book on her shelf. She opened it to the chapter she had used and began comparing the text with her paper.
text_zh: 汉娜在宿舍时，室友拿着一叠邮件回来了。其中有一个来自大学的官方信封。汉娜打开信封，发现一封信，信中说她的人类学论文因包含未注明出处的一本书的转述而被标记。汉娜记得她曾用那本书做研究并做了笔记。她以为自己正确地转述了这些观点。她把信放在桌上，看着书架上的那本书。她打开她用过的那一章，开始将文本与她的论文进行比较。

topic: A student is accused of plagiarism
text_en: Liam was working on a group assignment when his group chat lit up with a message from one of the members. "Did you guys see the email?" The email was from the professor, saying that the group's final report had been flagged for plagiarism. Liam had written the methods section. He had used the lab manual's wording, thinking it was standard. He replied to the chat asking who had written the other sections. One member said they had copied a paragraph from a website. Liam suggested they all review the report and prepare an explanation for the professor.
text_zh: 利亚姆正在做小组作业时，小组聊天群里一位成员发来消息：“你们看到邮件了吗？”邮件来自教授，说小组的最终报告被标记为抄袭。利亚姆写了方法部分。他使用了实验室手册的措辞，认为这是标准的。他在聊天中回复，问其他部分是谁写的。一位成员说他们从网站上复制了一段。利亚姆建议他们都审查报告，并为教授准备一份解释。

topic: A student is accused of plagiarism
text_en: Sofia was at her desk in the campus computer lab when the instructor from her English class approached her. "Can you come to my office for a moment?" the instructor asked. Sofia saved her work and followed. In the office, the instructor closed the door and said that Sofia's essay had been flagged because it was very similar to an essay found online. Sofia felt a knot in her stomach. She had written the essay herself, but she had used an online outline as a guide. She told the instructor about the outline. The instructor asked to see the outline. Sofia said she could find it in her browser history.
text_zh: 索菲亚正在校园计算机实验室的桌前，英语课的老师走近她。“你能来我办公室一下吗？”老师问。索菲亚保存了工作，跟着去了。在办公室里，老师关上门，说索菲亚的论文因与网上找到的一篇论文非常相似而被标记。索菲亚感到胃里一阵紧张。她是自己写的论文，但她使用了网上的一个提纲作为指导。她告诉了老师提纲的事。老师要求看提纲。索菲亚说她可以在浏览器历史记录中找到它。

topic: A student is accused of plagiarism
text_en: Andre was in the middle of a shift at the bookstore when he got a text from a classmate: "Check your email." He went to the back room and opened his email. There was a message from the biology professor stating that his lab report had been flagged because it contained a passage identical to a published article. Andre remembered reading the article and using a sentence from it in his introduction. He had not put it in quotation marks. He texted the classmate back, asking if they had the same issue. The classmate said they had not. Andre returned to the front of the store to finish his shift.
text_zh: 安德烈正在书店值班时，收到同学发来的短信：“查看你的电子邮件。”他走到后面的房间，打开邮件。有一封来自生物学教授的消息，说他的实验报告因包含与已发表文章相同的段落而被标记。安德烈记得读过那篇文章，并在引言中使用了一句。他没有加引号。他给同学回短信，问他们是否有同样的问题。同学说他们没有。安德烈回到店前继续值班。

topic: A student is accused of plagiarism
text_en: Julia was in the campus cafe when she ran into her philosophy professor. The professor said, "I was going to email you about your essay." Julia set down her coffee. The professor explained that a passage in her essay was nearly identical to a passage in a book she had consulted. Julia thought back to her research. She had highlighted the passage in the book and then included it in her essay, thinking she had paraphrased it. She asked the professor if she could revise the essay. The professor said they could discuss it during office hours. Julia picked up her coffee and said she would come by.
text_zh: 茱莉亚在校园咖啡馆遇到了她的哲学教授。教授说：“我正打算给你发邮件谈你的论文。”茱莉亚放下咖啡。教授解释说，她论文中的一段与她查阅过的一本书中的一段几乎完全相同。茱莉亚回想她的研究。她曾高亮了书中的那段话，然后把它写进论文，以为她已经转述了。她问教授是否可以修改论文。教授说他们可以在办公时间讨论。茱莉亚拿起咖啡，说她会来。

topic: A student is accused of plagiarism
text_en: Ravi was at home when his mother called to ask about his semester. He told her things were going fine. After the call, he checked his email and saw a message from the university's academic integrity office. The message said that his economics paper had been flagged because it contained a paragraph similar to a paper submitted by another student. Ravi remembered working on the paper alone. He thought about the possibility that he had used a similar source. He opened his paper and read the flagged paragraph. It was about supply and demand, a common topic. He decided to respond to the email to request more information.
text_zh: 拉维在家时，母亲打电话来询问他的学期情况。他告诉她一切顺利。挂断电话后，他查看了电子邮件，看到一封来自大学学术诚信办公室的消息。消息说他的经济学论文因包含与另一名学生提交的论文相似的段落而被标记。拉维记得他是独自完成论文的。他想到可能使用了相似的来源。他打开论文，阅读了被标记的段落。那是关于供需的，一个常见的话题。他决定回复邮件以获取更多信息。

topic: A person discovers their mentor has retired without saying goodbye
text_en: Marta arrived at the pottery studio on Tuesday, expecting to find Elena at the wheel as usual. Instead, the room was quiet, the shelves bare of her mentor's distinctive pieces. A note on the workbench simply said she had moved to the coast. Marta ran her hand over the smooth clay she had prepared, then began wedging it, her motions automatic. She glanced at the empty stool where Elena always sat, then turned back to her own work, shaping a bowl she had been practicing for weeks. The studio felt different, but she continued as the wheel spun.
text_zh: 玛尔塔周二来到陶艺工作室，原以为会像往常一样看到埃琳娜在拉坯机前工作。然而，房间里很安静，架子上她导师的特色作品也不见了。工作台上的一张纸条只说她搬到了海边。玛尔塔用手抚过她准备好的光滑黏土，然后开始揉泥，动作机械。她瞥了一眼埃琳娜常坐的空凳子，然后转回自己的工作，塑形一个她练习了好几周的碗。工作室感觉不一样了，但她继续着，拉坯机旋转着。

topic: A person discovers their mentor has retired without saying goodbye
text_en: James walked into the library's back office, expecting to see Mr. Henderson sorting through the new arrivals. Instead, the desk was cleared, the nameplate gone. A young librarian told him that Henderson had retired and moved to Arizona, leaving no forwarding address. James stood in the doorway, holding a book he had meant to return. He set it on the desk and walked out, then paused by the reading room window. He remembered the way Henderson had taught him to find old newspaper archives. He left the library, the book still in his hand.
text_zh: 詹姆斯走进图书馆的后办公室，原以为会看到亨德森先生整理新到的书籍。然而，桌子被清空了，名牌也不见了。一位年轻图书管理员告诉他，亨德森已经退休，搬到了亚利桑那州，没有留下转寄地址。詹姆斯站在门口，手里拿着一本他本想归还的书。他把书放在桌上，走了出去，然后在阅览室窗边停下。他记得亨德森教他查找旧报纸档案的方法。他离开了图书馆，书还在他手里。

topic: A person discovers their mentor has retired without saying goodbye
text_en: Priya arrived at the community garden to find the plot her mentor, Mr. Alvarez, had tended for years now overgrown with weeds. The garden coordinator said he had retired and moved to live with his daughter, leaving no message. Priya knelt by the tomato plants he had started, their leaves yellowing. She pulled a few weeds, then stopped. She had planned to ask him about soil preparation. She stood, brushed off her hands, and walked to the tool shed to get a watering can, though she wasn't sure what to do with it.
text_zh: 普里亚来到社区花园，发现她的导师阿尔瓦雷斯先生多年来照料的土地现在杂草丛生。花园协调员说他退休了，搬去和女儿住，没有留下任何消息。普里亚跪在他种下的番茄植株旁，叶子已经发黄。她拔了几根杂草，然后停了下来。她本打算问他关于土壤准备的事。她站起来，拍了拍手，走到工具棚拿了一个浇水壶，尽管她不确定该用它做什么。

topic: A person discovers their mentor has retired without saying goodbye
text_en: Maya arrived at the ceramics studio on Tuesday, expecting to find Mr. Alvarez at the wheel, shaping clay as he had for years. Instead, the room was quiet. His tools were gone from the shelf, and the kiln had been cleaned. A note on the board said the studio would be closed for the week. Maya packed her apron and walked to the front desk. The assistant told her Mr. Alvarez had left the previous Friday, without a word. She nodded, picked up a small bowl he had made, and set it back down. Then she gathered her things and headed home, thinking about the glazes he had taught her.
text_zh: 玛雅周二来到陶瓷工作室，原以为会看到阿尔瓦雷斯先生在拉坯机前，像多年一样塑形黏土。然而，房间里很安静。他的工具从架子上消失了，窑也被清理干净了。公告板上的一张纸条说工作室将关闭一周。玛雅收拾好围裙，走到前台。助理告诉她阿尔瓦雷斯先生上周五离开了，没有说一句话。她点点头，拿起他做的一个小碗，又放了回去。然后她收拾好东西回家，想着他教她的釉料。

topic: A person discovers their mentor has retired without saying goodbye
text_en: Tomás went to the auto repair shop where his mentor, Frank, had taught him everything about engines. The shop was closed, the garage door down. A neighbor said Frank had retired and moved to Florida, leaving no note. Tomás stood on the empty lot, kicking a stray bolt. He remembered the day Frank showed him how to rebuild a carburetor. He thought about calling the neighbor for a forwarding address, but instead he walked to his own car and drove home. He didn't know what to do with the tools Frank had given him.
text_zh: 托马斯去了汽车修理店，他的导师弗兰克在那里教会了他关于发动机的一切。店铺关门了，车库门也放下了。一位邻居说弗兰克退休了，搬到了佛罗里达，没有留下任何纸条。托马斯站在空地上，踢着一颗散落的螺栓。他记得弗兰克教他重建化油器的那一天。他想过打电话给邻居要转寄地址，但最终他走向自己的车，开车回家了。他不知道该怎么处理弗兰克给他的工具。

topic: A person discovers their mentor has retired without saying goodbye
text_en: Elena noticed the empty desk in the back office on Monday morning. Dr. Patel's laptop was gone, and the framed photo of the mountains had been taken down. She asked the receptionist, who said the doctor had retired over the weekend. Elena had not received a call or an email about it. She sat down at her own desk and opened the schedule for the week. There were a few patients to reschedule. She made the calls, left messages, and updated the files. At lunch, she ate her sandwich in the break room, then returned to work without mentioning it to anyone.
text_zh: 埃琳娜周一早上注意到后办公室的空桌子。帕特尔博士的笔记本电脑不见了，那幅装裱好的山景照片也被取了下来。她问接待员，接待员说医生周末退休了。埃琳娜没有接到任何电话或邮件。她坐在自己的桌前，打开本周的日程表。有几个病人需要重新安排。她打了电话，留了言，更新了文件。午餐时，她在休息室吃了三明治，然后回去工作，没有向任何人提起这件事。

topic: A person discovers their mentor has retired without saying goodbye
text_en: When Sam walked into the repair shop, the usual smell of oil and solder was faint, and the workbench had been cleared. His mentor, Frank, had always been there by mid-morning, tinkering with a radio or a toaster. The new owner, a younger man, said Frank had sold the place and moved south. Sam stood by the door for a moment, then picked up a broken clock he had brought. The new owner said he could look at it. Sam set it on the bench and described the issue, then left his phone number and walked out into the afternoon sun.
text_zh: 当山姆走进修理店时，通常的油和焊料气味很淡，工作台也被清理干净了。他的导师弗兰克以前总是在上午中段在那里，修理收音机或烤面包机。新老板，一个年轻男子，说弗兰克卖掉了这个地方，搬到了南方。山姆在门口站了一会儿，然后拿起他带来的一个坏钟。新老板说可以看看。山姆把钟放在工作台上，描述了问题，然后留下电话号码，走进午后的阳光中。

topic: A person discovers their mentor has retired without saying goodbye
text_en: Sofia arrived at the dance studio for her private lesson with Madame Elena. The studio was empty, the barre polished, the mirrors reflecting the empty room. The receptionist said Madame Elena had retired and moved to Spain. Sofia stood by the barre, her dance bag still on her shoulder. She had been preparing for an audition. She walked to the corner and did a few pliés, her movements quiet. Then she sat on the floor, her back against the mirror, and looked at the empty space where her mentor usually stood.
text_zh: 索菲亚来到舞蹈工作室，准备上埃琳娜夫人的私人课程。工作室空无一人，把杆擦得锃亮，镜子映照着空荡荡的房间。接待员说埃琳娜夫人退休了，搬到了西班牙。索菲亚站在把杆旁，舞包还挂在肩上。她一直在为一场试镜做准备。她走到角落，做了几个plié，动作很轻。然后她坐在地板上，背靠着镜子，看着她的导师通常站着的空位。

topic: A person discovers their mentor has retired without saying goodbye
text_en: Lena walked into the community garden and saw that the plot near the fence had been dug up and replanted with winter vegetables. The old gardener, Mr. Okafor, had always tended that corner, but he was not there. A woman with a watering can said he had retired and moved to live with his daughter. Lena knelt by the new seedlings and pulled a few weeds. She watered the tomatoes she had planted earlier in the season, then gathered some ripe beans and put them in her bag. She left a note on the shed door, just in case he came back.
text_zh: 莉娜走进社区花园，看到栅栏旁的那块地已被翻过，种上了冬季蔬菜。老园丁奥卡福先生一直照料那个角落，但他不在那里。一个拿着浇水壶的女人说他退休了，搬去和女儿住了。莉娜跪在新苗旁，拔了几根杂草。她给她这个季节早些时候种的番茄浇了水，然后摘了一些成熟的豆子放进包里。她在棚屋门上留了张纸条，以防他回来。

topic: A person discovers their mentor has retired without saying goodbye
text_en: On the first day of the new semester, Daniel looked for Professor Hargrove in the history department office. The door was closed, and the nameplate had been removed. A colleague passing by mentioned that the professor had retired at the end of the previous term, without any farewell gathering. Daniel stood in the hallway for a moment, then went to the library and checked out a book on local railroad history, one of the topics they had discussed. He sat down in his usual corner and began reading, occasionally glancing at the empty office door through the window.
text_zh: 新学期第一天，丹尼尔在历史系办公室找哈格罗夫教授。门关着，名牌也被摘掉了。一位路过的同事提到，教授在上学期末退休了，没有任何告别聚会。丹尼尔在走廊里站了一会儿，然后去了图书馆，借了一本关于当地铁路历史的书，这是他们讨论过的话题之一。他坐在他常坐的角落开始阅读，偶尔透过窗户瞥一眼那扇空荡荡的办公室门。

topic: A person discovers their mentor has retired without saying goodbye
text_en: Daniel went to the repair shop where his mentor, an older watchmaker named Mr. Kowalski, had taught him to fix timepieces. The shop was closed, the blinds drawn. A handwritten note on the door said 'Closed for good.' Daniel cupped his hands against the glass, seeing the workbench with the magnifying lamp. He remembered the day Mr. Kowalski showed him how to oil a balance wheel. He walked to the nearby café, ordered coffee, and sat by the window, looking at the shop's dark front. He didn't know what to do with the tools he had inherited.
text_zh: 丹尼尔去了修理店，他的导师，一位名叫科瓦尔斯基先生的老钟表匠，曾在那里教他修理钟表。店关门了，百叶窗拉了下来。门上有一张手写的纸条，写着“永久停业”。丹尼尔双手拢在玻璃上，看到了带放大灯的工作台。他想起科瓦尔斯基先生教他给摆轮上油的那一天。他走到附近的咖啡馆，点了咖啡，坐在窗边，望着店铺黑暗的门面。他不知道如何处理他继承的那些工具。

topic: A person discovers their mentor has retired without saying goodbye
text_en: Elena arrived at the hospital's volunteer office, where her mentor, a retired nurse named Mrs. Okafor, coordinated the program. The office was occupied by a new coordinator who said Mrs. Okafor had retired and moved to Nigeria. Elena stood in the doorway, holding a stack of patient-visit forms. She had been shadowing Mrs. Okafor for months. She set the forms on the desk, thanked the new coordinator, and walked to the ward. She passed the room where Mrs. Okafor had taught her to take blood pressure, then continued to the waiting area.
text_zh: 埃琳娜来到医院的志愿者办公室，她的导师，一位名叫奥卡福夫人的退休护士，曾在那里协调项目。办公室被一位新协调员占用，他说奥卡福夫人已经退休并搬到了尼日利亚。埃琳娜站在门口，手里拿着一叠患者探访表格。她已经跟随奥卡福夫人几个月了。她把表格放在桌上，感谢了新协调员，然后走向病房。她经过奥卡福夫人教她量血压的房间，然后继续走到等候区。

topic: A person discovers their mentor has retired without saying goodbye
text_en: Priya arrived at the bakery early, expecting to see Mrs. Chen rolling dough at the back counter. Instead, the ovens were cold, and the display case was empty. A sign on the door said the shop was closed until further notice. Priya walked to the nearby café, where she sometimes met Mrs. Chen for coffee. The barista said Mrs. Chen had retired and moved to be near her grandchildren. Priya ordered a plain coffee and sat by the window, watching the street. She finished her drink, then walked home, passing the bakery again and glancing at the dark windows.
text_zh: 普里娅早早来到面包店，期待看到陈太太在后柜台擀面团。然而，烤箱是冷的，展示柜是空的。门上有一个告示，说店铺关闭，直至另行通知。普里娅走到附近的咖啡馆，她有时在那里和陈太太喝咖啡。咖啡师说陈太太已经退休，搬去靠近孙子孙女的地方了。普里娅点了一杯清咖啡，坐在窗边，看着街道。她喝完饮料，然后走回家，再次经过面包店，瞥了一眼黑暗的窗户。

topic: A person discovers their mentor has retired without saying goodbye
text_en: Hannah went to the community theater where her mentor, a director named Margaret, had been rehearsing a play. The stage was empty, the chairs stacked. The stage manager said Margaret had retired and moved to Vermont, leaving no word. Hannah stood in the wings, looking at the empty stage. She had been cast in a lead role. She picked up a script from a chair, flipped through it, then set it down. She walked to the front of the theater and sat in the back row, looking at the empty seats.
text_zh: 汉娜去了社区剧院，她的导师，一位名叫玛格丽特的导演，曾在那里排练一部剧。舞台空着，椅子堆叠起来。舞台经理说玛格丽特已经退休，搬去了佛蒙特州，没有留下任何消息。汉娜站在侧台，看着空荡荡的舞台。她曾被选为主角。她从椅子上捡起一个剧本，翻了翻，然后放下。她走到剧院前面，坐在后排，看着空座位。

topic: A person discovers their mentor has retired without saying goodbye
text_en: Omar went to the university lab where his mentor, a postdoc named Dr. Patel, had been guiding his research. The lab was quiet, the bench cleared. A colleague said Dr. Patel had taken a job in industry and left abruptly. Omar stood by his own bench, holding a notebook with their latest data. He had been planning to ask about a statistical method. He opened the notebook, read a few lines, then closed it. He walked to the window and looked out at the campus, then returned to his computer and stared at the screen.
text_zh: 奥马尔去了大学实验室，他的导师，一位名叫帕特尔博士的博士后，曾在那里指导他的研究。实验室很安静，工作台已经清理干净。一位同事说帕特尔博士已经接受了业界的工作，突然离开了。奥马尔站在自己的工作台旁，手里拿着一个笔记本，里面是他们最新的数据。他一直打算询问一种统计方法。他打开笔记本，读了几行，然后合上。他走到窗边，望着校园，然后回到电脑前，盯着屏幕。

topic: A person discovers their mentor has retired without saying goodbye
text_en: Marcus showed up at the woodworking shop on Saturday morning, expecting to find Joe at the lathe, turning a bowl. The shop was locked, and the lights were off. Marcus peered through the window and saw the shelves empty, the workbench cleared. He called Joe's number, but it went to voicemail. A neighbor walking by said Joe had retired and moved to a smaller place upstate. Marcus stood on the sidewalk, then drove to the hardware store and bought a set of sandpaper. He went home and finished the chair he had been working on, using the techniques Joe had shown him.
text_zh: 马库斯周六早上来到木工店，期望找到乔在车床上转动一个碗。店锁着，灯也关着。马库斯透过窗户往里看，看到货架空了，工作台也清干净了。他拨打乔的电话，但是转到了语音信箱。一位路过的邻居说乔已经退休，搬到了北部一个更小的地方。马库斯站在人行道上，然后开车去五金店买了一组砂纸。他回到家，用乔教他的技术完成了他在做的那把椅子。

topic: A person discovers their mentor has retired without saying goodbye
text_en: Victor went to the metalworking shop where his mentor, a sculptor named Elena, had a forge. The shop was locked, the anvil covered. A neighbor said Elena had retired and moved to a ranch in Montana. Victor stood outside, hearing the faint sound of a hammer from another building. He remembered the day she showed him how to forge a leaf. He left a note under the door with his number, then walked to his car. He sat in the driver's seat, his hands on the wheel, before starting the engine.
text_zh: 维克多去了金属加工店，他的导师，一位名叫埃莱娜的雕塑家，在那里有一间锻炉。店锁着，铁砧被盖着。一位邻居说埃莱娜已经退休，搬到了蒙大拿的一个牧场。维克多站在外面，听到另一栋楼传来锤子的微弱声音。他想起她教他锻造一片叶子的那一天。他在门下留了一张字条，上面写了他的电话号码，然后走向他的车。他坐在驾驶座上，双手放在方向盘上，然后才发动引擎。

topic: A person discovers their mentor has retired without saying goodbye
text_en: Tessa arrived at the language school for her evening class, but the room was dark. She checked the schedule on the door, and her teacher's name had been replaced. The coordinator in the front office explained that Mr. Delgado had retired at the end of the previous week. Tessa had not heard anything about it. She walked to the bus stop, then decided to go home instead. On the way, she stopped at the library and borrowed a Spanish grammar book. That evening, she reviewed the verb conjugations she had learned, writing them out in her notebook.
text_zh: 泰莎来到语言学校上晚上的课，但房间是黑的。她查看了门上的时间表，她老师的名字已经被替换了。前办公室的协调员解释说，德尔加多先生在上个周末退休了。泰莎对此一无所知。她走到公交车站，然后决定回家。在路上，她停在图书馆，借了一本西班牙语语法书。那天晚上，她复习了学过的动词变位，把它们写在了笔记本上。

topic: A person discovers their mentor has retired without saying goodbye
text_en: Jordan went to the auto garage on Wednesday to pick up his car. The mechanic, Ray, had been working on it for a few days. When Jordan arrived, a different mechanic handed him the keys and said the work was done. Jordan asked where Ray was. The mechanic said Ray had retired and moved to the coast. Jordan paid the bill and drove home, noticing the car felt smoother. He parked in the driveway and sat for a moment, then got out and checked the oil level. He thought about the time Ray had shown him how to change a tire.
text_zh: 乔丹周三去汽车修理厂取他的车。技师雷已经修了几天。乔丹到达时，另一位技师递给他钥匙，说工作已经完成。乔丹问雷在哪里。技师说雷已经退休，搬到了海边。乔丹付了账单，开车回家，注意到车子开起来更平稳了。他把车停在车道上，坐了一会儿，然后下车检查了机油量。他想起了雷教他换轮胎的时光。

topic: A person discovers their mentor has retired without saying goodbye
text_en: Nina walked into the small bookshop and saw that the usual stack of poetry volumes near the register was gone. The owner, Mr. Bell, was not at his desk. A young woman at the counter said the shop had been sold, and Mr. Bell had retired to the countryside. Nina browsed the shelves for a while, then picked up a used novel with a cracked spine. She paid and left, walking slowly down the street. She passed the café where Mr. Bell sometimes read in the afternoons, but he was not there. She continued home and set the book on her nightstand.
text_zh: 尼娜走进小书店，看到收银机附近平时堆着的诗集不见了。店主贝尔先生不在他的桌后。柜台的一位年轻女士说书店已经卖了，贝尔先生已经退休去了乡下。尼娜在书架上浏览了一会儿，然后拿起一本书脊裂开的旧小说。她付了钱，离开，沿着街道慢慢走着。她经过贝尔先生有时下午在那里看书的那家咖啡馆，但他不在。她继续回家，把书放在床头柜上。

topic: A person runs into their ex at a mutual friend's wedding
text_en: At the reception, Maya spotted him across the room, holding a glass near the bar. She hadn't seen him since the breakup, and now here he was at their friend's wedding. He looked the same, maybe a bit older. She turned to talk to her cousin, but he approached and said hello. They exchanged small talk about the ceremony and the food. Then he excused himself to join his friends. Maya watched him walk away, then went to find her seat. The band started playing, and she focused on the music and the people around her.
text_zh: 在招待会上，玛雅在房间对面发现了他，他正拿着酒杯站在吧台附近。自从分手后她就没见过他，现在他却出现在他们朋友的婚礼上。他看起来和以前一样，也许老了一点。她转身去和表妹说话，但他走过来打了招呼。他们聊了聊仪式和食物。然后他借口离开去加入他的朋友。玛雅看着他走开，然后去找自己的座位。乐队开始演奏，她专注于音乐和周围的人。

topic: A person runs into their ex at a mutual friend's wedding
text_en: During the cocktail hour, Julia found herself at the same table as her ex, Daniel. He was talking with another guest about the couple's honeymoon plans. Julia reached for a glass of water, and their eyes met briefly. He nodded, and she nodded back. She turned to compliment the bride's mother on her dress. Later, when the toasts began, Julia listened, occasionally glancing around the room. She didn't seek Daniel out, but she didn't avoid him either. When dinner was served, she was seated with old friends, and the evening continued without much thought to the encounter.
text_zh: 在鸡尾酒会期间，朱莉娅发现自己和前男友丹尼尔坐在同一张桌子旁。他正在和另一位客人谈论这对夫妇的蜜月计划。朱莉娅伸手去拿一杯水，他们的目光短暂相遇。他点了点头，她也点了点头。她转身去称赞新娘母亲的裙子。后来，当祝酒开始时，朱莉娅听着，偶尔环顾房间。她没有去找丹尼尔，但也没有刻意避开他。晚餐上桌时，她和老朋友坐在一起，晚上继续着，没有多想这次相遇。

topic: A person runs into their ex at a mutual friend's wedding
text_en: The reception hall was crowded, and Ethan almost walked past her. His ex, Rachel, was standing with a group of their mutual college friends. She laughed at something someone said, and he recognized the sound. He paused, then continued to his table. During the buffet line, they ended up beside each other. "Hi, Ethan," she said. "Hi," he replied, and they both reached for the same serving spoon. She let him take it first. They talked about the weather and how nice the venue was. Then they went their separate ways to eat.
text_zh: 招待会大厅里挤满了人，伊桑差点走过她身边。他的前女友瑞秋正和他们大学共同的朋友们站在一起。她听到有人说了什么而大笑，他认出了那个声音。他停顿了一下，然后继续走向自己的桌子。在自助餐队伍中，他们最终并排站在一起。“嗨，伊桑，”她说。“嗨，”他回答，然后他们同时伸手去拿同一个勺子。她让他先拿。他们聊了聊天气和场地有多好。然后他们各自去吃饭了。

topic: A person runs into their ex at a mutual friend's wedding
text_en: As the bride and groom had their first dance, Nina spotted her ex, Tom, standing near the dance floor. He was with a woman Nina didn't know. Nina looked away and took a sip of her champagne. Later, when the music slowed, Tom came over and asked how she was. She said she was fine, and they talked about their jobs for a few minutes. Then he mentioned he had to get back to his date. Nina said it was nice to see him. She went to find the restroom, and when she came back, she joined a conversation about the wedding cake.
text_zh: 当新娘和新郎跳第一支舞时，尼娜发现她的前男友汤姆站在舞池附近。他身边有一个尼娜不认识的女人。尼娜移开视线，啜了一口香槟。后来，当音乐变慢时，汤姆走过来问她过得怎么样。她说她很好，然后他们聊了几分钟工作。然后他提到他必须回到他的约会对象身边。尼娜说很高兴见到他。她去找洗手间，回来时，她加入了关于婚礼蛋糕的谈话。

topic: A person runs into their ex at a mutual friend's wedding
text_en: At the outdoor ceremony, Liam saw his ex, Sarah, seated a few rows ahead. She was wearing a blue dress he hadn't seen before. He kept his eyes on the couple as they exchanged vows. During the reception, he got a drink and stood with some old colleagues. Sarah passed by with a plate of appetizers and said, "Nice ceremony." He agreed. They talked about the bride's family and the weather. Then she said she needed to find her friends. Liam watched her go, then turned to listen to the best man's speech.
text_zh: 在户外仪式上，利亚姆看到他的前女友莎拉坐在前面几排。她穿着一件他以前没见过的蓝色连衣裙。他目光一直注视着这对夫妇交换誓言。在招待会上，他拿了一杯饮料，和一些老同事站在一起。莎拉端着一盘开胃菜走过来说：“仪式不错。”他同意。他们聊了聊新娘的家人和天气。然后她说她需要去找她的朋友。利亚姆看着她离开，然后转身去听伴郎的演讲。

topic: A person runs into their ex at a mutual friend's wedding
text_en: The wedding was at a vineyard, and Ava arrived early to help set up the place cards. She saw her ex, Chris, helping arrange chairs. They hadn't spoken in months. They exchanged a brief "hello" and continued working. When the guests arrived, Ava was busy directing people to their seats. Chris was on the other side of the lawn. During dinner, she sat with the bride's cousins and didn't look for him. After the cake, she danced with a few people. Chris was dancing with someone else, and they passed each other on the floor without a word.
text_zh: 婚礼在一个葡萄园举行，艾娃提前到达帮忙摆放座位卡。她看到她的前男友克里斯在帮忙摆放椅子。他们已经好几个月没说话了。他们简短地打了个招呼，然后继续工作。客人到达时，艾娃忙着引导人们入座。克里斯在草坪的另一边。晚餐时，她和新娘的表姐妹们坐在一起，没有找他。蛋糕之后，她和几个人跳了舞。克里斯在和别人跳舞，他们在舞池上擦肩而过，没有说话。

topic: A person runs into their ex at a mutual friend's wedding
text_en: In the reception hall, Grace noticed her ex, Mark, standing by the photo booth. He was with his brother, laughing at something. Grace felt her stomach tighten a little, but she walked to the bar to order a drink. The bartender handed her a glass of wine. She saw Mark look over and raise his hand in a small wave. She raised her glass in return. Later, they were both in line for the restroom, and he said, "The place looks nice." She agreed. They talked about the bride's work. Then the line moved, and they went inside.
text_zh: 在招待会大厅里，格蕾丝注意到她的前男友马克站在照相亭旁。他和他的兄弟在一起，正笑着什么。格蕾丝感到胃有点收紧，但她走到吧台点了一杯饮料。酒保递给她一杯葡萄酒。她看到马克看过来，举起手微微挥了挥。她也举起酒杯回应。后来，他们都在排队上洗手间，他说：“这个地方看起来不错。”她同意。他们聊了聊新娘的工作。然后队伍移动了，他们走了进去。

topic: A person runs into their ex at a mutual friend's wedding
text_en: At the reception, Owen saw his ex, Lauren, near the dessert table. She was with a friend, pointing at the cupcakes. He remembered she always liked the vanilla ones. He walked to the other side of the room to talk to the groom's brother. When he came back, Lauren was gone. He got a piece of cake and found a seat. Later, he saw her dancing with a group of people. He watched for a moment, then finished his cake. When the night ended, he said goodbye to the couple and headed home, thinking about the drive.
text_zh: 在招待会上，欧文看到他的前女友劳伦在甜点桌附近。她和朋友在一起，指着纸杯蛋糕。他记得她总是喜欢香草味的。他走到房间另一边去和新郎的兄弟说话。当他回来时，劳伦已经走了。他拿了一块蛋糕，找了个座位。后来，他看到她在一群人中跳舞。他看了一会儿，然后吃完了蛋糕。夜晚结束时，他向这对夫妇道别，然后开车回家，想着路上的行程。

topic: A person runs into their ex at a mutual friend's wedding
text_en: The wedding was in a garden, and Emma arrived just as the ceremony was starting. She saw her ex, Jake, seated near the front. She found a seat in the back. During the vows, she listened to the couple's promises. At the reception, she was at a table with old friends. Jake came over to say hello, and they talked about the bride's new job. He said he was glad she came. She said she was too. They didn't talk again until the send-off, when they both grabbed handfuls of rose petals and threw them at the newlyweds.
text_zh: 婚礼在一个花园里举行，艾玛到达时仪式刚刚开始。她看到她的前男友杰克坐在靠近前排的位置。她在后面找了个座位。在誓言环节，她听着这对夫妇的承诺。在招待会上，她和老朋友坐在一张桌子旁。杰克过来打招呼，他们聊了聊新娘的新工作。他说他很高兴她来了。她说她也是。直到送别时，他们才再次交谈，当时他们都抓了一把玫瑰花瓣扔向新婚夫妇。

topic: A person runs into their ex at a mutual friend's wedding
text_en: Inside the barn, Leo spotted his ex, Hannah, by the string lights. She was talking to the groom's sister. He went to get a drink from the cooler. When he turned, she was right there, reaching for a soda. They both laughed. "Small world," she said. He agreed. They talked about the drive there and the traffic. Then she said she saw a friend she needed to catch up with. Leo said goodbye and went to find his friends. They played a game of cornhole, and he didn't think about her again until later.
text_zh: 在谷仓里，利奥发现他的前女友汉娜在彩灯旁。她正在和新娘的妹妹说话。他去冷却器那里拿饮料。当他转身时，她就在那里，伸手去拿汽水。他们都笑了。“世界真小，”她说。他同意。他们聊了聊开车去那里的路和交通。然后她说她看到一个朋友需要去打个招呼。利奥说了再见，然后去找他的朋友们。他们玩了一场沙包游戏，直到后来他才又想起她。

topic: A person runs into their ex at a mutual friend's wedding
text_en: At the hotel ballroom, Nora saw her ex, Ben, at the coat check. He was handing in his jacket. She waited until he left, then checked hers. During the cocktail hour, she stayed near the appetizer table. Ben came by to grab a spring roll, and they said hello. They talked about the bride's dress. Then he mentioned he was here with a group from work. Nora said she was with the bride's family. They both went to find their seats. At the end of the night, she saw him waiting for the elevator, and they rode up together in silence.
text_zh: 在酒店宴会厅，诺拉在衣帽间看到了她的前男友本。他正在寄存夹克。她等他离开后才寄存了自己的。在鸡尾酒时间，她待在开胃菜桌附近。本过来拿了一个春卷，他们打了招呼。他们聊了新娘的裙子。然后他提到他是和一群同事一起来的。诺拉说她和新娘的家人在一起。他们各自去找座位。晚上结束时，她看到他在等电梯，他们一起乘电梯上去，一路无言。

topic: A person runs into their ex at a mutual friend's wedding
text_en: The reception was at a rooftop bar, and Adam saw his ex, Chloe, standing at the railing. She was looking at the city lights. He walked over and stood a few feet away. "Nice view," he said. She turned and smiled. "Yeah, it is." They talked about the wedding and how they knew the couple. Then she mentioned she had to get back to her table. He said he'd see her around. He went to the bar and ordered a drink. When he looked back, she was talking to someone else, and he turned to join his friends.
text_zh: 招待会在一个屋顶酒吧举行，亚当看到他的前女友克洛伊站在栏杆旁。她正看着城市的灯光。他走过去，站在几英尺远的地方。“风景不错，”他说。她转过身来，微笑着说：“是啊，确实不错。”他们聊了婚礼以及他们如何认识这对新人。然后她提到她得回她的桌子了。他说回头见。他走到酒吧点了一杯饮料。当他回头看时，她正在和别人说话，他转身加入了他的朋友们。

topic: A person runs into their ex at a mutual friend's wedding
text_en: At the wedding, Megan saw her ex, Ryan, across the dance floor. He was dancing with his niece, spinning her around. Megan smiled and looked away. She went to the table to refill her glass. Later, Ryan came over and said, "You look nice." She thanked him. They talked about the band and how they had been to a concert together once. He said that was a long time ago. She agreed. Then the song ended, and he went back to his family. Megan stayed with her friends and watched the bride and groom cut the cake.
text_zh: 在婚礼上，梅根在舞池对面看到了她的前男友瑞安。他正和他的侄女跳舞，转着她转圈。梅根笑了笑，移开了视线。她走到桌边去续杯。后来，瑞安走过来说：“你看起来不错。”她道了谢。他们聊了乐队，以及他们曾经一起去看过一场音乐会。他说那是很久以前的事了。她表示同意。然后歌曲结束了，他回到了他的家人身边。梅根和她的朋友们待在一起，看着新娘和新郎切蛋糕。

topic: A person runs into their ex at a mutual friend's wedding
text_en: In the courtyard, Jordan saw his ex, Alex, talking to the groom. He waited until they were done, then went to congratulate the groom himself. Alex nodded at him as he passed. Later, they were both at the bar, and Alex said, "Great wedding." Jordan agreed. They talked about the couple's honeymoon plans. Then Alex's phone buzzed, and he said he had to take a call. Jordan watched him walk toward the garden. He ordered another drink and joined a conversation about the best man's toast. The night went on, and they didn't speak again.
text_zh: 在庭院里，乔丹看到他的前男友亚历克斯在和新郎说话。他等他们说完，然后自己去祝贺新郎。亚历克斯经过时向他点了点头。后来，他们都在酒吧，亚历克斯说：“婚礼很棒。”乔丹表示同意。他们聊了这对新人的蜜月计划。然后亚历克斯的手机响了，他说他得接个电话。乔丹看着他走向花园。他又点了一杯饮料，加入了关于伴郎祝酒词的谈话。夜晚继续，他们再也没有说话。

topic: A person runs into their ex at a mutual friend's wedding
text_en: At the reception, Sophie saw her ex, David, standing near the gift table. He was holding a card. She looked away and went to find her seat. During dinner, she was at a table with the bride's cousins. David was at the next table, and they occasionally glanced at each other. After the meal, there was a photo booth, and Sophie went with her friends. She saw David go in with his friends. They came out laughing, and she saw him look at her. She turned to her friends and said something about the props. They both went back to their groups.
text_zh: 在招待会上，苏菲看到她的前男友大卫站在礼品桌附近。他手里拿着一张卡片。她移开视线，去找自己的座位。晚餐时，她和新娘的表姐妹们坐在一起。大卫坐在隔壁桌，他们偶尔会瞥对方一眼。饭后有一个拍照亭，苏菲和她的朋友们去了。她看到大卫和他的朋友们也进去了。他们笑着出来，她看到他看向她。她转向她的朋友们，说了些关于道具的话。他们都回到了各自的群体中。

topic: A person runs into their ex at a mutual friend's wedding
text_en: At the reception, Maya spotted him near the dessert table, holding a plate of cake. They exchanged a brief nod before she turned back to her conversation with an old college friend. Later, during the toast, she noticed he had moved to the other side of the room. When the dancing started, they ended up near each other during a group dance, and he smiled politely. She smiled back, then found her way to the bar for a glass of water. The evening continued with laughter and music, and she enjoyed catching up with people she hadn't seen in years.
text_zh: 在招待会上，玛雅在甜点桌旁发现了他，他端着一盘蛋糕。他们简短地点了点头，然后她转回去和一位大学老友继续交谈。后来，在祝酒时，她注意到他已经移到了房间的另一边。当舞会开始时，他们在一次集体舞中靠近了彼此，他礼貌地笑了笑。她也回以微笑，然后找到去酒吧的路，要了一杯水。夜晚在笑声和音乐中继续，她享受着和多年未见的人叙旧。

topic: A person runs into their ex at a mutual friend's wedding
text_en: At the wedding, Olivia saw her ex, Marcus, at the buffet. He was piling food onto his plate. She waited until he moved on, then got her own. During the meal, she sat with the groom's aunts. Marcus was across the room. After the cake, there was a toast, and Olivia raised her glass. She saw Marcus do the same. They caught each other's eyes for a second. Then the music started, and people got up to dance. Olivia danced with her uncle. Marcus danced with someone. They didn't talk again, and Olivia left early because she had work the next day.
text_zh: 在婚礼上，奥利维亚在自助餐台看到了她的前男友马库斯。他正在往盘子里堆食物。她等他走开后才去拿自己的。用餐时，她和新郎的姑姑们坐在一起。马库斯在房间的另一边。蛋糕之后是祝酒，奥利维亚举起了杯子。她看到马库斯也举起了杯子。他们对视了一秒钟。然后音乐响起，人们站起来跳舞。奥利维亚和她的叔叔跳舞。马库斯和别人跳舞。他们再也没有说话，奥利维亚因为第二天要上班而提前离开了。

topic: A person runs into their ex at a mutual friend's wedding
text_en: The reception was in a tent, and Ethan saw his ex, Rachel, by the entrance. She was talking to the bride. He waited outside until they were done, then went in. Later, they were both at the dessert table, and Rachel said, "These are good." He agreed. They talked about the wedding cake flavor. Then she said she needed to find her seat. He did too. They walked back to their tables. During the dancing, they were on opposite sides of the floor. At the end, Ethan went to the restroom, and when he came back, Rachel was gone.
text_zh: 招待会在一个帐篷里举行，伊桑在入口处看到了他的前女友瑞秋。她正在和新娘说话。他在外面等到她们说完，然后走了进去。后来，他们都在甜点桌旁，瑞秋说：“这些很好吃。”他表示同意。他们聊了婚礼蛋糕的味道。然后她说她需要找到她的座位。他也需要。他们走回各自的桌子。跳舞时，他们在舞池的两端。最后，伊桑去了洗手间，当他回来时，瑞秋已经走了。

topic: A person runs into their ex at a mutual friend's wedding
text_en: At the wedding, Hannah saw her ex, Leo, at the bar. She ordered a water, and he ordered a beer. They stood next to each other. "How have you been?" he asked. She said she was fine, and asked him the same. They talked about their jobs and the weather. Then the bartender gave them their drinks, and they went back to their tables. Later, they were both in the photo booth line. They took pictures separately. When the night ended, they were in the parking lot at the same time. They said goodnight and got into their cars.
text_zh: 在婚礼上，汉娜在酒吧看到了她的前男友利奥。她点了一杯水，他点了一杯啤酒。他们并排站着。“你最近怎么样？”他问。她说她很好，也问了他同样的问题。他们聊了各自的工作和天气。然后酒保给了他们饮料，他们回到了各自的桌子。后来，他们都在拍照亭排队。他们分别拍了照片。夜晚结束时，他们同时出现在停车场。他们互道晚安，然后上了各自的车。

topic: A person runs into their ex at a mutual friend's wedding
text_en: At the reception, Jack saw his ex, Emma, by the dance floor. She was with a group of friends, laughing. He watched for a moment, then went to talk to the groom. Later, Emma came over and said, "You came alone?" He said he did. She said she came with a friend. They talked about the couple's honeymoon. Then the music got louder, and they had to raise their voices. Emma said she was going to dance. Jack said he'd catch up with her later. He stayed with the groom's friends. At the end, he saw her leaving, and he waved from across the room.
text_zh: 在招待会上，杰克在舞池边看到了他的前女友艾玛。她和一群朋友在一起，笑着。他看了一会儿，然后去和新郎说话。后来，艾玛走过来说：“你一个人来的？”他说是的。她说她和一个朋友一起来的。他们聊了这对新人的蜜月。然后音乐声变大，他们不得不提高声音。艾玛说她要去跳舞。杰克说稍后找她。他和新郎的朋友们待在一起。最后，他看到她离开，他从房间对面挥了挥手。

topic: Someone discovers their friend has been lying about their job
text_en: Maya had always known her friend Lena worked in marketing, but when she stopped by the office building Lena claimed to work in, the receptionist said no one by that name was employed there. Maya called Lena later, mentioning she'd visited. Lena laughed it off, saying she'd moved to a different floor. Maya didn't press further. The next week, at a coffee shop, she spotted Lena in a uniform behind the counter. Lena waved, looking a bit sheepish. Maya ordered her usual latte, and they chatted about the weather. Neither mentioned the office building again.
text_zh: 玛雅一直知道她的朋友莉娜在市场部工作，但当她顺路去莉娜声称工作的办公楼时，前台说那里没有叫这个名字的员工。玛雅后来给莉娜打电话，提到自己去过。莉娜一笑置之，说她搬到了另一层楼。玛雅没有追问。第二周，在一家咖啡店，她看到莉娜穿着制服站在柜台后面。莉娜向她挥手，看起来有点不好意思。玛雅点了她常喝的拿铁，她们聊了聊天气。两人都没有再提起那栋办公楼。

topic: Someone discovers their friend has been lying about their job
text_en: Maya had always thought her friend worked at the art museum, giving tours and handling the archives. When she stopped by for lunch, the security guard at the desk said no one by that name worked there. Maya waited outside, watching the entrance. Her friend arrived an hour later, carrying a coffee and a gym bag, and waved casually. Maya mentioned the museum mix-up, and her friend laughed, saying she must have confused the days. Maya nodded and walked back to her car, noticing her friend’s name tag from a nearby retail store peeking out of her jacket pocket.
text_zh: 玛雅一直以为她的朋友在美术馆工作，负责导览和档案管理。当她顺路去吃午饭时，门口的保安说没有叫那个名字的人在那里工作。玛雅在外面等着，看着入口。她的朋友一小时后到了，拿着咖啡和健身包，随意地挥了挥手。玛雅提到美术馆的误会，她的朋友笑了，说她一定是搞错了日子。玛雅点点头，走回她的车，注意到她朋友夹克口袋里露出的附近一家零售店的姓名牌。

topic: Someone discovers their friend has been lying about their job
text_en: For months, Jordan had heard his friend Alex talk about being a chef at a downtown bistro. Alex described specials and kitchen politics. When Jordan finally booked a table there, he asked for Alex. The hostess said no one by that name worked there. Jordan called Alex later, saying he’d tried the place. There was a pause. “I got let go last week,” Alex said. “I’m helping at my uncle’s food truck now.” Jordan remembered Alex had mentioned an uncle who ran a truck. He said he’d stop by sometime. Alex said sure. They talked about the menu for a few minutes, then Jordan said he had to run.
text_zh: 几个月来，乔丹一直听他的朋友亚历克斯说他在市中心一家小酒馆当厨师。亚历克斯描述过特色菜和厨房里的勾心斗角。当乔丹终于在那里订了位子，他问起亚历克斯。女招待说没有叫那个名字的人在那里工作。乔丹后来给亚历克斯打电话，说自己去过那家店。电话那头停顿了一下。“我上周被解雇了，”亚历克斯说。“我现在在我叔叔的餐车帮忙。”乔丹想起亚历克斯提过他叔叔经营一辆餐车。他说他改天会去看看。亚历克斯说好。他们聊了几分钟菜单，然后乔丹说他得走了。

topic: Someone discovers their friend has been lying about their job
text_en: Nina’s friend Tom always said he was an accountant for a logistics company. He’d complain about quarterly reports and tax season. One Saturday, Nina saw him at a flea market, selling handmade wooden bowls. She walked over, and he gave a small wave. “This is my side thing,” he said, gesturing at the bowls. “I do the accounting during the week.” Nina picked up a bowl, turned it over, and set it down. She asked how the market was going. He said it was steady. She bought a small bowl and said she liked the grain. He thanked her, and she headed to the next stall.
text_zh: 尼娜的朋友汤姆总是说他在一家物流公司当会计。他会抱怨季度报告和报税季。一个周六，尼娜在跳蚤市场看到他，在卖手工木碗。她走过去，他微微挥了挥手。“这是我的副业，”他指着那些碗说。“我平时做会计。”尼娜拿起一个碗，翻过来看了看，又放下。她问市场怎么样。他说生意稳定。她买了一个小碗，说她喜欢木纹。他谢了她，她走向下一个摊位。

topic: Someone discovers their friend has been lying about their job
text_en: Leo had known his friend Maya for years, and she’d always said she was a research assistant at a university lab. She’d mention experiments and data entry. When Leo needed to drop off a book for her, he went to the address she’d given. It was a small bookstore, not a lab. Maya was at the counter, scanning a novel. She saw him and blinked. “I work here part-time,” she said. “The lab job ended.” Leo set the book on the counter. He asked if she liked the work. She said it was quiet. He said he’d been meaning to pick up a book anyway. He browsed for a few minutes, then paid and left.
text_zh: 利奥认识他的朋友玛雅多年，她总是说她是大学实验室的研究助理。她会提到实验和数据录入。当利奥需要给她送一本书时，他去了她给的地址。那是一家小书店，不是实验室。玛雅在柜台后面，正在扫描一本小说。她看到他，眨了眨眼。“我在这里兼职，”她说。“实验室的工作结束了。”利奥把书放在柜台上。他问她喜不喜欢这份工作。她说很安静。他说他反正也一直想买本书。他浏览了几分钟，然后付了钱离开了。

topic: Someone discovers their friend has been lying about their job
text_en: Chloe’s friend Ben always said he was a web developer for a startup. He’d talk about coding sprints and product launches. One evening, Chloe’s laptop broke, and Ben offered to fix it. He came over with a toolbox, not a laptop. He opened the back panel and fiddled with the fan. “I do this on the side,” he said, blowing dust off the motherboard. “The startup folded last month.” Chloe watched him reseat the RAM. She asked if he was looking for something new. He said he was taking it easy. The laptop booted up. He charged her half of what a shop would, and she paid him.
text_zh: 克洛伊的朋友本总是说他在一家初创公司做网页开发。他会谈论编码冲刺和产品发布。一天晚上，克洛伊的笔记本电脑坏了，本主动提出帮她修。他带着工具箱来了，而不是笔记本电脑。他打开后盖，摆弄风扇。“我这是兼职，”他说着，吹掉主板上的灰尘。“那家初创公司上个月倒闭了。”克洛伊看着他重新插好内存条。她问他是不是在找新工作。他说他在放松。笔记本电脑启动了。他收了她维修店一半的费用，她付了钱。

topic: Someone discovers their friend has been lying about their job
text_en: Priya had always believed her friend Anika was a graphic designer. They'd met in an art class, and Anika often shared sketches. One evening, Priya attended a community meeting and saw Anika there, wearing a badge that said 'City Clerk'. Priya approached her, and Anika looked flustered. She explained that she'd taken the clerk job temporarily while her design work was slow. Priya nodded, not entirely convinced. A few weeks later, Priya needed a permit and went to the city office. Anika was at the counter, processing forms. She handled Priya's application efficiently. They exchanged polite smiles, and Priya left without mentioning the discrepancy.
text_zh: 普里亚一直相信她的朋友阿尼卡是平面设计师。她们在艺术课上认识，阿尼卡经常分享素描。一天晚上，普里亚参加一个社区会议，看到阿尼卡也在那里，戴着写着“市政文员”的徽章。普里亚走近她，阿尼卡看起来很慌张。她解释说，她暂时做文员的工作，因为她的设计工作进展缓慢。普里亚点点头，但并没有完全相信。几周后，普里亚需要办许可证，去了市政办公室。阿尼卡在柜台后面，正在处理表格。她高效地处理了普里亚的申请。她们交换了礼貌的微笑，普里亚没有提那件事就离开了。

topic: Someone discovers their friend has been lying about their job
text_en: Mia’s friend David always said he was a high school science teacher. He’d talk about lesson plans and lab safety. One Saturday, Mia saw him at the community center, teaching a pottery class. He had clay on his hands and was showing a kid how to center a wheel. Mia watched from the doorway. David noticed her and nodded. After the class, he came over. “I’m doing this on weekends,” he said. “The teaching job didn’t work out.” Mia said the class looked fun. He said it was. She said she’d been thinking about trying pottery. He gave her the schedule.
text_zh: 米娅的朋友大卫总是说他是高中科学老师。他会谈论教案和实验室安全。一个周六，米娅在社区中心看到他，在教陶艺课。他手上沾着黏土，正在教一个孩子怎么让轮子居中。米娅在门口看着。大卫注意到她，点了点头。下课后，他走过来。“我周末做这个，”他说。“教书的工作没成。”米娅说这课看起来很有趣。他说是的。她说她一直在考虑试试陶艺。他把时间表给了她。

topic: Someone discovers their friend has been lying about their job
text_en: Noah’s friend Emma always said she was a travel blogger. She’d post photos of airports and hotel rooms. When Noah ran into her at the grocery store, she was wearing a store uniform and scanning items at the self-checkout. She saw him and stopped. “I’m just helping out here,” she said. “The blog doesn’t pay much.” Noah looked at the conveyor belt. He asked if she was still writing. She said she was, but it was slow. He said he’d read her last post. She smiled, said thanks, and scanned his milk. He paid and left.
text_zh: 诺亚的朋友艾玛总是说她是个旅行博主。她会发机场和酒店房间的照片。当诺亚在杂货店碰到她时，她穿着店里的制服，在自助结账机前扫描商品。她看到他，停了下来。“我只是在这里帮忙，”她说。“博客赚不了多少钱。”诺亚看着传送带。他问她还在写吗。她说在写，但很慢。他说他读过她最近的一篇文章。她笑了，说了声谢谢，然后扫描了他的牛奶。他付了钱离开了。

topic: Someone discovers their friend has been lying about their job
text_en: Lucas’s friend Sarah always said she was a nurse at a clinic. She’d talk about shifts and patient intake. One afternoon, Lucas sprained his ankle and went to the clinic. Sarah wasn’t there. The nurse on duty said she didn’t know anyone by that name. Lucas called Sarah later. “I work at the animal shelter now,” she said. “I had to leave the clinic.” Lucas said he’d hurt his ankle. She asked if it was swollen. He said a little. She told him to ice it and keep it elevated. He said he would, and they hung up.
text_zh: 卢卡斯的朋友莎拉总是说她在诊所当护士。她会谈论轮班和病人接收。一天下午，卢卡斯扭伤了脚踝，去了诊所。莎拉不在那里。当班的护士说她不认识叫那个名字的人。卢卡斯后来给莎拉打电话。“我现在在动物收容所工作，”她说。“我不得不离开诊所。”卢卡斯说他伤了脚踝。她问是不是肿了。他说有点。她让他冰敷并抬高。他说他会照做，然后他们挂了电话。

topic: Someone discovers their friend has been lying about their job
text_en: Ava’s friend Ryan always said he was an architect. He’d show her sketches of buildings and talk about client meetings. One day, Ava saw him at a construction site, wearing a hard hat and holding a blueprint. She walked over. He looked up. “I’m the site supervisor,” he said. “The architecture firm let me go.” Ava looked at the blueprint, then at the half-built frame. She asked if he liked the work. He said it was hands-on. She said it seemed like it. He offered to show her around, but she said she had to get back to the office.
text_zh: 艾娃的朋友瑞安总是说自己是建筑师。他会给她看建筑的草图，谈论客户会议。有一天，艾娃在一个建筑工地看到他，戴着安全帽，拿着蓝图。她走过去。他抬起头。“我是现场主管，”他说。“建筑事务所把我解雇了。”艾娃看了看蓝图，又看了看半建成的框架。她问他是否喜欢这份工作。他说这是动手实践的工作。她说看起来确实如此。他提出带她四处看看，但她说她得回办公室了。

topic: Someone discovers their friend has been lying about their job
text_en: Mason’s friend Olivia always said she was a museum curator. She’d talk about exhibits and artifact loans. When Mason visited the museum, he didn’t see her. He asked at the front desk. The attendant said Olivia worked in the gift shop. Mason found her there, restocking postcards. She saw him and paused. “I’m doing this while I look for something else,” she said. Mason picked up a postcard of a painting they’d once discussed. He asked if she missed the exhibits. She said she still got to see them on breaks. He bought the postcard and left.
text_zh: 梅森的朋友奥利维亚总是说自己是博物馆馆长。她会谈论展品和文物借展。当梅森参观博物馆时，他没有看到她。他在前台询问。工作人员说奥利维亚在礼品店工作。梅森在那里找到了她，她正在补货明信片。她看到他，停了下来。“我在做这个，同时找别的工作，”她说。梅森拿起一张他们曾经讨论过的一幅画的明信片。他问她是否想念那些展品。她说她休息时仍然能看到它们。他买了明信片，然后离开了。

topic: Someone discovers their friend has been lying about their job
text_en: Isabella’s friend Ethan always said he was a journalist for a local paper. He’d talk about deadlines and sources. One evening, Isabella saw him at a restaurant, waiting tables. He came over with a notepad, then recognized her. “I’m picking up shifts,” he said. “The paper cut my hours.” Isabella ordered a salad. She asked if he was still writing. He said he was, but it was mostly freelance. She asked about a story he’d mentioned. He said it had fallen through. He took her order, and later brought her a free dessert. She left a good tip.
text_zh: 伊莎贝拉的朋友伊桑总是说自己是当地报纸的记者。他会谈论截稿日期和消息来源。一天晚上，伊莎贝拉在一家餐厅看到他，正在当服务员。他拿着记事本走过来，然后认出了她。“我在加班，”他说。“报纸削减了我的工时。”伊莎贝拉点了一份沙拉。她问他是否还在写作。他说是的，但主要是自由撰稿。她问起他提到过的一篇报道。他说那篇报道泡汤了。他记下她的订单，后来给她送来一份免费甜点。她留下了一笔可观的小费。

topic: Someone discovers their friend has been lying about their job
text_en: Jordan had known Sam for years, and Sam often talked about his job as a financial analyst. One day, Jordan's car broke down, and Sam offered to give him a lift to work. Sam drove to a warehouse on the outskirts of town and parked. Jordan asked what they were doing there. Sam said he had to pick up some supplies for a client. They went inside, and a man in overalls greeted Sam as 'the new inventory guy'. Sam laughed and said it was a side gig. Jordan didn't respond. He just watched as Sam helped unload boxes, then they drove back in silence.
text_zh: 乔丹认识萨姆多年，萨姆经常谈论他作为金融分析师的工作。有一天，乔丹的车抛锚了，萨姆提出载他去上班。萨姆开车到镇郊的一个仓库，停了下来。乔丹问他们在这里做什么。萨姆说他必须为一位客户取一些补给品。他们走进去，一个穿工装裤的男人称呼萨姆为“新来的库存员”。萨姆笑了笑，说这是副业。乔丹没有回应。他只是看着萨姆帮忙卸箱子，然后他们沉默地开车回去。

topic: Someone discovers their friend has been lying about their job
text_en: Jack’s friend Lily always said she was a wedding photographer. She’d show him albums and talk about bookings. One Saturday, Jack saw her at a park, taking photos of a family. He waited until she finished. Lily lowered the camera. “I’m doing this on the side,” she said. “The wedding season is slow.” Jack looked at the family posing. He asked if she liked it. She said it was different. He said the photos would be nice. She said she hoped so. They chatted for a minute, then she had to take another shot.
text_zh: 杰克的朋友莉莉总是说自己是婚礼摄影师。她会给他看相册，谈论预订。一个星期六，杰克在公园看到她，正在给一个家庭拍照。他等到她拍完。莉莉放下相机。“我在做这个作为副业，”她说。“婚礼季很淡。”杰克看着摆姿势的家庭。他问她是否喜欢这份工作。她说这不一样。他说照片会很好看的。她说希望如此。他们聊了一分钟，然后她不得不去拍下一张照片。

topic: Someone discovers their friend has been lying about their job
text_en: Nina and her friend Carlos had been close since college. Carlos always described his job as a project manager for a tech startup. One weekend, Nina went to a farmers market and saw Carlos at a stall selling handmade candles. She walked over, and Carlos seemed startled. He said he was helping a friend with the stall. Nina bought a candle and left. A month later, she saw him again, this time with a sign that said 'Carlos's Candles'. She approached, and Carlos admitted the startup had folded and he'd started the candle business. Nina nodded, said the candle was nice, and walked on.
text_zh: 妮娜和她的朋友卡洛斯从大学起就很亲密。卡洛斯总是把自己的工作描述为一家科技初创公司的项目经理。一个周末，妮娜去农贸市场，看到卡洛斯在一个卖手工蜡烛的摊位上。她走过去，卡洛斯似乎吃了一惊。他说他在帮朋友看摊子。妮娜买了一支蜡烛，然后离开了。一个月后，她又看到他，这次带着一个写着“卡洛斯的蜡烛”的牌子。她走上前，卡洛斯承认初创公司倒闭了，他开始了蜡烛生意。妮娜点点头，说蜡烛不错，然后继续往前走。

topic: Someone discovers their friend has been lying about their job
text_en: Tara had always known her friend Ben was a teacher at a local high school. He often complained about grading papers and faculty meetings. One evening, Tara needed to drop off a book at Ben's apartment. The door was opened by a woman who said Ben was at his shift at the hospital. Tara was confused, but the woman explained Ben worked as a nurse. When Tara saw Ben later, she mentioned the visit. Ben looked away and said he'd taken a part-time nursing job for extra income. Tara didn't ask more. She just handed him the book and said she hoped his shifts weren't too long.
text_zh: 塔拉一直知道她的朋友本是当地一所高中的老师。他经常抱怨批改试卷和教职工会议。一天晚上，塔拉需要把一本书送到本的公寓。开门的是一个女人，她说本在医院上夜班。塔拉很困惑，但那个女人解释说本是一名护士。当塔拉后来见到本时，她提到了那次拜访。本把目光移开，说他做了一份兼职护理工作来增加收入。塔拉没有多问。她只是把书递给他，说希望他的班次不要太长。

topic: Someone discovers their friend has been lying about their job
text_en: Lily’s friend James always said he was a lawyer. He’d talk about briefs and court appearances. One afternoon, Lily needed a notary and went to a shipping store. James was behind the counter, stamping documents. He saw her and stopped. “I’m doing this while I study for the bar,” he said. “I haven’t passed yet.” Lily handed him her document. He notarized it and handed it back. She asked how the studying was going. He said it was a lot of material. She said she hoped it went well. He said thanks.
text_zh: 莉莉的朋友詹姆斯总是说自己是律师。他会谈论案情摘要和出庭。一天下午，莉莉需要公证，去了一家快递店。詹姆斯在柜台后面，正在给文件盖章。他看到她，停了下来。“我在做这个，同时准备律师资格考试，”他说。“我还没通过。”莉莉把她的文件递给他。他做了公证，然后递了回去。她问他学习进展如何。他说材料很多。她说希望一切顺利。他说谢谢。

topic: Someone discovers their friend has been lying about their job
text_en: Alex and his friend Jamie had been roommates for a year. Jamie claimed to work as a software developer at a big company. One day, Alex's laptop broke, and Jamie offered to fix it. Jamie spent hours tinkering, but eventually said he couldn't figure it out. Alex took it to a repair shop, and the technician mentioned the software was a common type used by data entry clerks. Alex thought about Jamie's job. That evening, he asked Jamie about his work. Jamie shrugged and said he did some data entry on the side. Alex didn't push. He just nodded and went back to reading, the broken laptop still on his desk.
text_zh: 亚历克斯和他的朋友杰米做了一年室友。杰米声称在一家大公司做软件开发人员。有一天，亚历克斯的笔记本电脑坏了，杰米主动提出修理。杰米花了几个小时摆弄，但最终说修不好。亚历克斯把它拿到修理店，技术人员提到这个软件是数据录入员常用的类型。亚历克斯想到了杰米的工作。那天晚上，他问杰米他的工作。杰米耸耸肩，说他做了一些数据录入的兼职。亚历克斯没有追问。他只是点点头，继续看书，坏掉的笔记本电脑还在他的桌子上。

topic: Someone discovers their friend has been lying about their job
text_en: Avery’s friend Noah always said he was a data analyst for a bank. He’d talk about spreadsheets and quarterly reports. One weekend, Avery saw Noah at a coffee shop, but he was behind the counter, making drinks. He saw her and waved. Avery ordered a latte. Noah steamed the milk. “I’m doing this on weekends,” he said. “The bank job is remote now.” Avery took the latte. She asked if he missed the office. He said he didn’t. She said the coffee was good. He said it was a new blend.
text_zh: 艾弗里的朋友诺亚总是说自己是银行的数据分析师。他会谈论电子表格和季度报告。一个周末，艾弗里在一家咖啡店看到诺亚，但他在柜台后面做饮料。他看到她，挥了挥手。艾弗里点了一杯拿铁。诺亚蒸了牛奶。“我周末做这个，”他说。“银行的工作现在是远程的。”艾弗里接过拿铁。她问他是否想念办公室。他说不想。她说咖啡很好喝。他说这是一种新拼配。

topic: A person discovers their partner has been taking secret phone calls
text_en: Maya was folding laundry in the living room when Leo's phone buzzed on the coffee table. He was in the shower, so she glanced at it—just a number, no name. She didn't think much of it until she heard him pick up in the hallway, his voice low. He said, "I'll call you back," and then walked into the bedroom, closing the door. Maya continued folding, but her hands slowed. Later, when he came out, she asked if everything was okay. He said it was work, just a quick thing. She nodded and went back to the laundry, the question resting in her mind.
text_zh: 玛雅正在客厅叠衣服，这时利奥的手机在咖啡桌上嗡嗡作响。他正在洗澡，所以她瞥了一眼——只是一个号码，没有名字。她没太在意，直到她听到他在走廊里接起电话，声音低沉。他说：“我稍后给你回电话。”然后走进卧室，关上了门。玛雅继续叠衣服，但她的手慢了下来。后来，当他出来时，她问是否一切都好。他说是工作上的事，只是件小事。她点了点头，又回去叠衣服，那个问题在她心中萦绕。

topic: A person discovers their partner has been taking secret phone calls
text_en: Maya noticed that every evening around the same time, her partner, Leo, would step out onto the balcony with his phone, speaking in a low murmur. She continued washing the dishes, catching only the occasional word through the window. When he came back inside, he smiled and asked about her day, but she couldn't shake the image of his turned back and cupped hand. The next evening, she lingered in the living room, straightening a stack of magazines, listening to the muffled conversation. She didn't confront him, just noted the pattern and wondered what he might be discussing with such care.
text_zh: 玛雅注意到，每天傍晚大约同一时间，她的伴侣利奥会拿着手机走到阳台上，低声细语。她继续洗碗，透过窗户只能偶尔听到只言片语。当他回到屋里时，他微笑着问起她的一天，但她无法摆脱他背对着她、手捂着手机的画面。第二天傍晚，她在客厅里逗留，整理着一摞杂志，听着那模糊的谈话声。她没有质问他，只是注意到了这个模式，并好奇他可能在如此谨慎地谈论什么。

topic: A person discovers their partner has been taking secret phone calls
text_en: Priya and her husband were watching a movie when his phone rang. He muted it, looked at the screen, and said he'd take it in the study. The movie played on, but Priya found herself watching the study door. When he returned, he said it was his sister, and she was having a rough time. Priya asked if everything was okay, and he said yes, just needed to talk. He sat back down, and they finished the movie. Priya didn't bring it up again, but she noticed he kept his phone face-down on the armrest for the rest of the evening.
text_zh: 普里亚和丈夫正在看电影，这时他的手机响了。他调成静音，看了看屏幕，说要去书房接。电影继续播放，但普里亚发现自己一直在看书房的门。当他回来时，他说是他妹妹，她最近不太好。普里亚问是否一切都好，他说是的，只是需要聊聊。他坐回沙发上，他们看完了电影。普里亚没有再提起这件事，但她注意到，那天晚上剩下的时间里，他一直把手机屏幕朝下放在扶手上。

topic: A person discovers their partner has been taking secret phone calls
text_en: Jake was in the kitchen when he heard his girlfriend's phone ring in the bedroom. She was in the bathroom, and she called out, "Can you get that?" He picked it up, but the caller had already hung up. When she came out, he told her someone had called. She looked at the phone, then said it was probably a telemarketer. But later that night, she took her phone into the hallway and spoke in a hushed tone. Jake went back to washing dishes, the water running, and he didn't ask who it was.
text_zh: 杰克在厨房里，这时他听到女朋友的手机在卧室里响了。她在浴室里，喊道：“你能接一下吗？”他接起电话，但对方已经挂断了。当她出来时，他告诉她有人打过电话。她看了看手机，然后说可能是推销电话。但那天晚上晚些时候，她拿着手机走到走廊里，低声说着什么。杰克回去洗碗，水哗哗地流着，他没有问是谁。

topic: A person discovers their partner has been taking secret phone calls
text_en: Elena was cleaning the bathroom when she heard her partner's phone vibrate on the nightstand.
