He was in the living room, and she saw him glance at it, then pick it up and walk to the balcony. She finished wiping the sink, then went to the kitchen to start dinner. When he came back, he said it was his mom, and she was having trouble with her internet. Elena nodded and asked if she needed help. He said no, it was sorted. They sat down to eat, and Elena didn't mention the call again.
text_zh: 埃琳娜正在打扫浴室，这时她听到伴侣的手机在床头柜上震动。他在客厅里，她看到他瞥了一眼手机，然后拿起它走到阳台上。她擦完水槽，然后去厨房开始做晚饭。当他回来时，他说是他妈妈，她的网络出了问题。埃琳娜点了点头，问她是否需要帮助。他说不用，已经解决了。他们坐下来吃饭，埃琳娜没有再提起那个电话。

topic: A person discovers their partner has been taking secret phone calls
text_en: For a few weeks, Marcus had been stepping out of the restaurant to take calls. His partner, Dana, would watch him through the window, his hand over the speaker. When he came back, he'd say it was his brother or a wrong number. Dana didn't ask, but she noticed he'd stopped leaving his phone on the table. One evening, after dinner, she saw him in the parking lot, talking, his back to her. She waited in the car, and when he got in, he said, "Sorry, just some stuff to handle." She said, "Okay," and started the engine.
text_zh: 几个星期以来，马库斯一直走出餐厅去接电话。他的伴侣达娜会透过窗户看着他，他的手捂着听筒。当他回来时，他会说是他哥哥或者打错了。达娜没有问，但她注意到他不再把手机放在桌上了。一天晚上，晚饭后，她看到他在停车场打电话，背对着她。她在车里等着，当他上车时，他说：“抱歉，只是有些事要处理。”她说：“好的。”然后发动了引擎。

topic: A person discovers their partner has been taking secret phone calls
text_en: Lena and her girlfriend were cleaning up after a party. Lena was putting away glasses when she saw her girlfriend's phone light up on the counter. Her girlfriend picked it up, looked at it, and said she'd be right back. She went into the bedroom and shut the door. Lena finished wiping the counter, then checked on the leftovers. When her girlfriend came out, she said it was her cousin, and she'd been having a bad night. Lena said, "I hope she's okay." Her girlfriend said, "She will be," and they went back to cleaning.
text_zh: 莉娜和她的女朋友正在打扫派对后的现场。莉娜正在收拾杯子，这时她看到女朋友的手机在柜台上亮了起来。她的女朋友拿起手机，看了看，说她马上回来。她走进卧室，关上了门。莉娜擦完柜台，然后检查了一下剩菜。当她的女朋友出来时，她说她表妹打来的，她今晚心情不好。莉娜说：“我希望她没事。”她的女朋友说：“她会没事的。”然后他们继续打扫。

topic: A person discovers their partner has been taking secret phone calls
text_en: Jordan had been with Alex for years, and they usually shared everything, so the quiet calls were noticeable. Alex would take the phone into the bedroom and close the door, or walk to the far end of the yard. Jordan tried to keep busy, sorting laundry or checking the mail, but the habit repeated. One afternoon, Jordan stood in the hallway, hearing Alex's voice but not the words. After the call, Alex emerged and asked if Jordan wanted to order takeout. Jordan said yes, and they ate together, the unanswered questions sitting quietly between them.
text_zh: 乔丹和亚历克斯在一起多年，他们通常无话不谈，所以那些安静的电话显得格外显眼。亚历克斯会拿着电话走进卧室关上门，或者走到院子尽头。乔丹试图让自己忙起来，整理衣物或查看邮件，但这个习惯反复出现。一天下午，乔丹站在走廊里，听到亚历克斯的声音，却听不清话语。电话结束后，亚历克斯出来问乔丹想不想点外卖。乔丹说好，他们一起吃了饭，那些未解的问题静静地横亘在他们之间。

topic: A person discovers their partner has been taking secret phone calls
text_en: Aisha was sorting mail at the kitchen table when her husband's phone rang. He was in the garage, and she heard him answer, his voice muffled. She went back to sorting, but she noticed he stayed in the garage for a long while. When he came in, he said it was his old colleague, and they'd lost touch. Aisha asked if they were doing well. He said yes, just catching up. She put the mail in a pile and went to check the laundry. She didn't mention the call again, but she remembered the long silence in the garage.
text_zh: 艾莎正在厨房桌子旁整理邮件，这时她丈夫的手机响了。他在车库里，她听到他接起电话，声音模糊。她继续整理，但她注意到他在车库里待了很长时间。当他进来时，他说是他以前的老同事，他们失去了联系。艾莎问他们过得好吗。他说是的，只是叙叙旧。她把邮件堆成一摞，然后去查看洗衣情况。她没有再提起那个电话，但她记得车库里那段漫长的沉默。

topic: A person discovers their partner has been taking secret phone calls
text_en: Sam had never seen Chris take calls so privately. They'd always been open about their phones, but now Chris would slip into the bathroom or step outside, speaking softly. Sam noticed the pattern over several days, and each time, it felt like a small shift in their usual rhythm. One evening, Chris came back from a call and mentioned a work project, but the timing didn't quite match. Sam nodded, not pressing further, and continued setting the table. The calls continued, and Sam went about the evenings, aware of the closed doors and lowered voices, but not knowing what they meant.
text_zh: 山姆从未见过克里斯如此私密地接电话。他们一直对手机很坦诚，但现在克里斯会溜进浴室或走到外面，轻声说话。山姆在几天内注意到了这个模式，每一次，都感觉像是他们平常节奏中的一个小变化。一天晚上，克里斯接完电话回来，提到了一个工作项目，但时间不太对得上。山姆点了点头，没有追问，继续摆桌子。电话还在继续，山姆度过了一个个夜晚，意识到那些紧闭的门和压低的声音，但不知道它们意味着什么。

topic: A person discovers their partner has been taking secret phone calls
text_en: Rebecca was in the bedroom when she heard her partner's phone buzz in the living room. He was on the couch, and she heard him say, "Hey, can I call you back?" Then he got up and went to the bathroom. When he came back, he said it was his friend from college. Rebecca asked if they were planning a reunion. He said maybe, and they'd talk later. She went back to reading her book, and he turned on the TV. Neither of them said much for the rest of the evening, but the phone stayed on the table.
text_zh: 丽贝卡在卧室里，听到客厅里伴侣的手机嗡嗡作响。他在沙发上，她听到他说：“嘿，我能稍后给你回电话吗？”然后他起身去了洗手间。他回来后，说是他大学的朋友。丽贝卡问他们是否在计划同学聚会。他说也许吧，晚点再谈。她继续看书，他打开了电视。那天晚上剩下的时间里，他们俩都没怎么说话，但手机一直放在桌子上。

topic: A person discovers their partner has been taking secret phone calls
text_en: Jasmine was baking bread when her boyfriend came into the kitchen, phone in hand, and said he'd be right back. He stepped into the backyard, and she saw him through the window, talking and pacing. She kneaded the dough, then shaped it into a loaf. When he came back, he said it was his aunt, and she needed help with a legal document. Jasmine asked if he was going to help her. He said yes, probably. She put the bread in the oven and wiped her hands. He sat at the table, and she joined him, waiting for the bread to bake.
text_zh: 茉莉正在烤面包，这时她的男朋友手里拿着手机走进厨房，说马上就回来。他走到后院，她透过窗户看到他一边说话一边踱步。她揉着面团，然后把它塑成一条面包。他回来后，说是他的姑妈，她需要帮忙处理一份法律文件。茉莉问他是否打算帮她。他说是的，可能会。她把面包放进烤箱，擦了擦手。他坐在桌旁，她也坐了过去，等着面包烤好。

topic: A person discovers their partner has been taking secret phone calls
text_en: Alex was fixing a loose shelf in the hallway when his partner's phone rang in the bedroom. She was in the bathroom, and she called out, "Can you see who it is?" He looked at the screen—it was a number he didn't recognize. He told her, and she said, "Probably spam." But later, she went into the bedroom and closed the door, and he heard her talking. When she came out, she said it was her doctor's office. Alex said, "Everything okay?" She said yes, just a follow-up. He went back to the shelf, tightening the screws.
text_zh: 亚历克斯正在走廊里修理一个松动的架子，这时他伴侣的手机在卧室里响了。她在洗手间里，喊道：“你能看看是谁吗？”他看了看屏幕——是一个他不认识的号码。他告诉了她，她说：“可能是骚扰电话。”但后来，她走进卧室，关上了门，他听到她在说话。她出来后，说是她的医生办公室打来的。亚历克斯说：“一切都好吗？”她说是的，只是复查。他回到架子旁，拧紧螺丝。

topic: A person discovers their partner has been taking secret phone calls
text_en: Nina and her partner were walking the dog when his phone rang. He stopped, pulled it out, and said, "I need to take this." He stepped a few feet away, and she stood with the dog, watching him talk. The dog tugged at the leash, and she patted its head. When he came back, he said it was his boss, and there was an issue at work. Nina asked if they needed to go home. He said no, it was handled. They continued walking, but he kept his phone in his hand for the rest of the walk.
text_zh: 尼娜和她的伴侣正在遛狗，这时他的手机响了。他停下来，掏出手机，说：“我得接一下。”他走开几步，她牵着狗站在那里，看着他说话。狗拽着牵引绳，她拍了拍它的头。他回来后，说是他的老板，工作上出了点问题。尼娜问他们是否需要回家。他说不用，已经处理好了。他们继续走着，但他在剩下的散步时间里一直把手机拿在手里。

topic: A person discovers their partner has been taking secret phone calls
text_en: Omar was in the living room when his wife took a call in the bedroom, closing the door behind her. He could hear her voice, but not the words. When she came out, she said it was her friend from work, and they were discussing a project. Omar asked if it was going well. She said yes, just some details to sort out. He went back to reading, and she sat on the couch with her laptop. Later, when her phone buzzed again, she looked at it and put it on silent. Omar watched, then turned a page.
text_zh: 奥马尔在客厅里，他的妻子在卧室里接了个电话，随手关上了门。他能听到她的声音，但听不清内容。她出来后，说是她工作上的朋友，他们在讨论一个项目。奥马尔问是否进展顺利。她说是的，只是有些细节需要整理。他继续看书，她拿着笔记本电脑坐在沙发上。后来，她的手机又嗡嗡作响，她看了一眼，然后调成了静音。奥马尔看着，然后翻了一页。

topic: A person discovers their partner has been taking secret phone calls
text_en: Hannah was in the kitchen when she saw her partner's phone on the counter, vibrating. He was in the shower, so she let it ring. When he came out, she told him he'd missed a call. He picked up the phone, looked at it, and said, "I'll call them back." He went into the bedroom, and she heard him talking. When he came out, he said it was his mechanic, and the car was ready. Hannah said, "Great." He said he'd pick it up tomorrow. She went back to stirring the soup, and he sat down at the table.
text_zh: 汉娜在厨房里，看到伴侣的手机在柜台上震动。他正在洗澡，所以她让它响着。他出来后，她告诉他他错过了一个电话。他拿起手机，看了看，说：“我会给他们回电话。”他走进卧室，她听到他在说话。他出来后，说是他的修理工，车已经修好了。汉娜说：“太好了。”他说他明天去取车。她继续搅拌汤，他在桌旁坐下。

topic: A person discovers their partner has been taking secret phone calls
text_en: Every few days, Pat's partner, Morgan, would take a call in the back bedroom, shutting the door behind them. Pat noticed because they usually shared everything, but this seemed different. Pat would hear Morgan's voice rise and fall, but the words stayed muffled. One Saturday, Pat was in the kitchen making coffee when Morgan stepped out, phone still in hand. Morgan said it was an old friend and then changed the subject to the weather. Pat poured the coffee, handed Morgan a mug, and they sat together, the unanswered questions lingering in the quiet between them.
text_zh: 每隔几天，帕特的伴侣摩根就会在后卧室接一个电话，然后关上门。帕特注意到了，因为他们通常什么都分享，但这次似乎不同。帕特会听到摩根的声音起伏，但话语始终模糊不清。一个星期六，帕特在厨房煮咖啡，摩根走出来，手里还拿着手机。摩根说是一个老朋友，然后把话题转到了天气上。帕特倒了咖啡，递给摩根一个杯子，他们坐在一起，未解的问题在两人之间的寂静中萦绕。

topic: A person discovers their partner has been taking secret phone calls
text_en: Grace and her husband were in the car, driving to the grocery store, when his phone rang. He glanced at it, then said, "It's work." He didn't answer, but he turned down the music. Grace watched the road, and after a few rings, it stopped. He said, "They'll leave a message." She asked if he needed to call back. He said no, it could wait. They drove in silence for a bit, then he turned the music back up. When they got to the store, he left his phone in the car.
text_zh: 格蕾丝和她的丈夫在车里，正开车去杂货店，这时他的手机响了。他看了一眼，然后说：“是工作上的事。”他没有接，但调低了音乐音量。格蕾丝看着路，响了几声后，电话停了。他说：“他们会留言的。”她问他是否需要回电话。他说不用，可以等。他们沉默地开了一会儿车，然后他把音乐调高了。到了商店，他把手机留在了车里。

topic: A person discovers their partner has been taking secret phone calls
text_en: Lucy was in the study, paying bills, when her partner came in, phone in hand, and said, "I'll be in the backyard." She heard the screen door close. She finished writing a check, then looked out the window. He was standing by the fence, talking. When he came back, he said it was his sister, and she was having a rough time with her kids. Lucy asked if he wanted to talk about it. He said no, it was private. She nodded and went back to the bills. He sat down with a magazine, but he didn't turn any pages.
text_zh: 露西在书房里付账单，这时她的伴侣手里拿着手机走进来，说：“我去后院。”她听到纱门关上的声音。她写完一张支票，然后看向窗外。他站在篱笆旁，正在说话。他回来后，说是他的妹妹，她和孩子们相处得很艰难。露西问他是否想谈谈这件事。他说不用，这是私事。她点点头，继续处理账单。他拿着一本杂志坐下，但一页也没有翻。

topic: A person discovers their partner has been taking secret phone calls
text_en: Ivan was in the hallway when he saw his partner slip into the bathroom with her phone. The door clicked, and he heard a low murmur. He went to the kitchen and poured a glass of water. When she came out, she said it was her aunt, and she needed advice about a medical procedure. Ivan asked if her aunt was okay. She said she was, just needed to talk. He took a sip of water, and she went to the living room. He stood in the kitchen for a moment, then followed her, sitting on the other end of the couch.
text_zh: 伊万在走廊里，看到他的伴侣拿着手机溜进了洗手间。门咔哒一声关上了，他听到一阵低语。他走进厨房，倒了一杯水。她出来后，说是她的姑妈，她需要关于一个医疗程序的建议。伊万问她姑妈是否还好。她说她还好，只是需要谈谈。他喝了一口水，她去了客厅。他在厨房站了一会儿，然后跟着她，坐在沙发的另一端。

topic: A person's car is towed from their own driveway
text_en: Margie walked outside with her coffee and saw the empty spot where her sedan had been. She stood on the driveway, then walked to the curb and looked both ways. Her neighbor was watering plants. "Did you see anyone take my car?" Margie called. The neighbor shook her head. Margie went back inside, found the towing company's number on her phone, and called. They confirmed they had it. She asked about fees and the lot's location. After hanging up, she grabbed her keys and purse, then headed out to get it back.
text_zh: 玛吉端着咖啡走到外面，看到她的轿车原本停放的位置空空如也。她站在车道上，然后走到路边，向两边张望。她的邻居正在浇花。“你看到有人开走我的车了吗？”玛吉喊道。邻居摇了摇头。玛吉回到屋里，在手机上找到拖车公司的号码，打了过去。他们确认车在他们那里。她询问了费用和停车场的地址。挂断电话后，她拿起钥匙和钱包，然后出门去把车取回来。

topic: A person's car is towed from their own driveway
text_en: Liam had parked in his usual spot behind the house. When he came out with the recycling bin, the Honda was gone. He set the bin down and walked around the yard, checking the side street. A white slip was tucked under the windshield wiper of the neighbor's car—no, it was on his front door. The notice said unauthorized parking. Liam read it twice, then called the number. They explained the tow. He asked if he could pick it up now. They said yes. He grabbed his wallet and jacket and drove with a friend to the lot.
text_zh: 利亚姆把车停在房子后面他常停的位置。当他拿着回收箱出来时，本田车不见了。他放下回收箱，绕着院子走了一圈，查看了旁边的小路。邻居车的雨刷下夹着一张白色纸条——不，是在他的前门上。通知上写着违规停车。利亚姆读了两遍，然后拨打了上面的号码。他们解释了拖车的情况。他问现在能不能去取车。他们说可以。他抓起钱包和夹克，和朋友一起开车去了停车场。

topic: A person's car is towed from their own driveway
text_en: Priya was unloading groceries from the trunk when she noticed the driveway felt more open than usual. She looked up and saw her blue hatchback was not there. She put the grocery bag on the porch and walked to the street. The neighbor's security camera pointed toward her driveway. She knocked on their door. The neighbor checked the footage and saw a tow truck hooking up her car that morning. Priya thanked them and called the towing company listed on the door tag. She arranged to retrieve it later that afternoon.
text_zh: 普里亚正从后备箱卸杂货，忽然觉得车道比平时空旷了些。她抬头一看，发现自己的蓝色两厢车不见了。她把购物袋放在门廊上，走到街上。邻居的安防摄像头正对着她的车道。她敲了敲邻居的门。邻居查看了录像，看到那天早上有一辆拖车把她的车拖走了。普里亚谢过他们，拨打了门牌标签上列出的拖车公司的电话。她安排当天下午去取车。

topic: A person's car is towed from their own driveway
text_en: After work, Tom pulled into his driveway and saw a pile of gravel where his truck should have been. He got out and stood there for a moment. The house key was in his hand. He walked to the front door and found a notice from the city about street sweeping. His truck was parked legally, but the notice said it had been moved. Tom called the number on the notice. They said his truck was at the city lot. He asked about the fee and the hours. Then he went inside to get his wallet.
text_zh: 下班后，汤姆把车开进车道，看到本该停着他的卡车的地方堆着一堆碎石。他下了车，在那里站了一会儿。房门钥匙在他手里。他走到前门，发现了一张市政关于街道清扫的通知。他的卡车是合法停放的，但通知上说车被移走了。汤姆拨打了通知上的号码。他们说他的卡车在市政停车场。他询问了费用和营业时间。然后他进屋去拿钱包。

topic: A person's car is towed from their own driveway
text_en: Aisha had parked her coupe in the driveway the night before. In the morning, she looked out the kitchen window and saw only the oil stain on the concrete. She opened the door and stepped out in her bathrobe. The driveway gate was closed. The car was gone. She went back in and found a slip on the kitchen counter—no, that was a receipt. She checked the front door. There was a notice. She called the number and learned it was a private tow for an unpaid ticket. She asked how to get it back. They gave her the address.
text_zh: 艾莎前一天晚上把她的双门小轿车停在车道上。早上，她从厨房窗户往外看，只看到水泥地上的油渍。她打开门，穿着睡袍走了出去。车道门是关着的。车不见了。她回到屋里，在厨房台面上找到一张纸条——不，那是一张收据。她检查了前门。有一张通知。她拨打了上面的号码，得知是因为一张未付的罚单被私人拖车公司拖走了。她问怎么把车取回来。他们给了她地址。

topic: A person's car is towed from their own driveway
text_en: Carlos was washing dishes when he saw through the window that his SUV was not in the driveway. He dried his hands and went outside. The driveway was empty. He walked to the curb and looked down the street. A leaflet on the windshield of his neighbor's car had a towing company's phone number. Carlos called. They confirmed they had his vehicle. He asked why. They said it was parked in a tow-away zone. He explained it was his driveway. They said the address matched a different street. He noted the lot location and hung up.
text_zh: 卡洛斯正在洗碗，透过窗户看到他的SUV不在车道上。他擦干手，走到外面。车道是空的。他走到路边，顺着街道望去。邻居车挡风玻璃上的一张传单上有拖车公司的电话号码。卡洛斯打了过去。他们确认拖走了他的车。他问为什么。他们说车停在禁止停车区。他解释说那是他自己的车道。他们说那个地址对应的是另一条街。他记下了停车场的位置，然后挂了电话。

topic: A person's car is towed from their own driveway
text_en: Elena returned from a run and saw the space where her sedan had been parked was empty. She slowed to a walk and looked around. The driveway had a chalk mark on the concrete. She went inside and checked her phone. No messages. She called her husband, but he didn't answer. She then found a notice on the side gate. It was from the city. She called the number and learned her car was towed for expired registration. She asked about the process and the fee. She then called a friend for a ride to the lot.
text_zh: 埃琳娜跑步回来，看到她的轿车停放的位置空着。她放慢脚步，环顾四周。车道上有一道粉笔标记。她走进屋里，查看手机。没有消息。她给丈夫打了电话，但没人接。然后她在侧门上发现了一张通知。是市政发的。她拨打了上面的号码，得知她的车因为注册过期被拖走了。她询问了流程和费用。然后她给朋友打电话，请朋友载她去停车场。

topic: A person's car is towed from their own driveway
text_en: Ben was backing out of the driveway when he noticed his own car was not in the spot where he left it. He stopped the car and got out. The driveway was empty. He walked around the house, checking the back alley. Nothing. He went inside and looked at the kitchen table, where he usually put the mail. There was a towing notice. He read it and called the company. They said they had his car. He asked about the fee and the location. Then he went to get his keys and drove to the lot with his wife.
text_zh: 本正把车倒出车道，忽然注意到自己的车不在他停放的位置。他停下车，走了出来。车道是空的。他绕着房子走了一圈，检查了后面的小巷。什么也没有。他走进屋里，看了看厨房桌子——他通常把邮件放在那里。有一张拖车通知。他读了一遍，然后给公司打了电话。他们说有他的车。他询问了费用和地点。然后他去拿钥匙，和妻子一起开车去了停车场。

topic: A person's car is towed from their own driveway
text_en: Hannah came outside with a bag of trash and saw that her compact car was gone. She dropped the bag on the porch and walked to the driveway. The spot was empty except for a few leaves. She looked up and down the street. A neighbor was walking a dog. "Did you see anyone tow a car?" Hannah asked. The neighbor said he saw a truck earlier. Hannah thanked him and went inside to call the number on the door tag. She learned the fee and the lot's address. She then called her brother for a ride.
text_zh: 汉娜提着一袋垃圾出来，发现她的小型车不见了。她把垃圾袋扔在门廊上，走到车道上。那个位置空空的，只有几片落叶。她上下打量着街道。一个邻居正在遛狗。“你看到有人拖车了吗？”汉娜问道。邻居说他之前看到一辆卡车。汉娜谢过他，进屋拨打了门牌标签上的号码。她得知了费用和停车场的地址。然后她给哥哥打电话，请他载她一程。

topic: A person's car is towed from their own driveway
text_en: Omar was about to leave for work and noticed his car was not in the driveway. He stood by the front door with his briefcase, looking at the empty space. He walked to the street and saw a notice on a lamppost. It was from a private towing company. He called the number. They said his car was towed for blocking a driveway. He said it was his own driveway. They said the complaint came from the house next door. He asked about the fee and the lot. He then called his office to say he'd be late.
text_zh: 奥马尔正要出门上班，发现他的车不在车道上。他拎着公文包站在前门，看着空荡荡的位置。他走到街上，看到灯柱上有一张通知。是一家私人拖车公司发的。他拨打了上面的号码。他们说他的车因为堵塞车道被拖走了。他说那是他自己的车道。他们说投诉来自隔壁的房子。他询问了费用和停车场的情况。然后他给办公室打电话说他会迟到。

topic: A person's car is towed from their own driveway
text_en: Julia had parked her station wagon in the driveway after shopping. When she went out to get the mail, the car was gone. She looked at the spot, then at the street. She walked to the neighbor's house and rang the bell. The neighbor said she saw a tow truck but didn't know why. Julia found a notice on her front door. She called the number. They said her car was towed for expired plates. She asked how to get it back. They gave her the address. She went inside, grabbed her purse, and called a cab.
text_zh: 朱莉娅购物后把旅行车停在车道上。当她出去取邮件时，车不见了。她看了看那个位置，又看了看街道。她走到邻居家按了门铃。邻居说她看到了一辆拖车，但不知道为什么。朱莉娅在前门上发现了一张通知。她拨打了上面的号码。他们说她的车因车牌过期被拖走了。她问怎么取回。他们给了她地址。她走进屋里，抓起钱包，叫了一辆出租车。

topic: A person's car is towed from their own driveway
text_en: Marcus was in the backyard when he heard a truck. He looked out and saw a tow truck pulling away with his pickup. He ran to the front, but the truck was already gone. He stood on the driveway, breathing a little hard. He checked the front door for a notice. There was one. He called the company and asked why. They said it was parked in a no-parking zone. He explained it was his driveway. They said the street sign applied. He asked about the fee and the lot. He then called his neighbor to ask for a ride.
text_zh: 马库斯在后院时听到一辆卡车的声音。他向外看去，看到一辆拖车正拖着他的皮卡车离开。他跑到前面，但卡车已经不见了。他站在车道上，呼吸有点急促。他检查了前门是否有通知。有一张。他打电话给拖车公司询问原因。他们说车停在了禁止停车区。他解释说那是他的车道。他们说街道标志适用。他询问了费用和停车场。然后他打电话给邻居请求搭车。

topic: A person's car is towed from their own driveway
text_en: Maya glanced out the kitchen window and saw the empty space where her sedan had been parked. She set down the coffee mug and walked outside, checking the driveway again. A small sticker on the mailbox indicated the towing company's name. She pulled out her phone and dialed the number listed, then waited through the rings. When someone answered, she explained the situation and gave her address. The dispatcher confirmed the vehicle had been removed due to a mistaken tag. Maya jotted down the lot location and pickup fee, then went inside to grab her keys and wallet.
text_zh: 玛雅瞥了一眼厨房窗外，看到她的轿车停放的地方空了。她放下咖啡杯，走到外面，再次检查了车道。邮箱上的一个小贴纸标明了拖车公司的名称。她掏出手机，拨打了上面列出的号码，然后等待铃声响起。有人接听时，她说明了情况并提供了地址。调度员确认车辆因标签错误而被移走。玛雅记下了停车场位置和取车费用，然后进屋去拿钥匙和钱包。

topic: A person's car is towed from their own driveway
text_en: After finishing his breakfast, Daniel walked to the front door to leave for work. His car was not in the driveway. He stood on the porch for a moment, scanning the street, but it was nowhere in sight. He went back inside and checked the garage, though he knew it was empty. On the kitchen counter, he found a notice slipped under the door. It listed a local towing service and a phone number. Daniel called the number and spoke with a woman who confirmed his car had been towed that morning. He asked about the process for retrieving it and wrote down the address.
text_zh: 丹尼尔吃完早餐后，走到前门准备去上班。他的车不在车道上。他在门廊上站了一会儿，扫视街道，但哪里也看不到。他回到屋里，检查了车库，尽管他知道车库是空的。在厨房台面上，他发现了一张从门缝塞进来的通知。上面列出了一家本地拖车服务和电话号码。丹尼尔拨打了号码，与一位女士交谈，她确认他的车那天早上被拖走了。他询问了取车流程，并记下了地址。

topic: A person's car is towed from their own driveway
text_en: Elena returned from her morning jog and noticed her blue hatchback was gone from its usual spot. She slowed to a stop, looking at the oil stain on the concrete where it had been. A white envelope was tucked under the welcome mat. She opened it and read the notice from the city's contracted towing company. She called the number on the paper, and a recorded message gave the impound lot's hours and location. Elena folded the notice and put it in her pocket. She went inside, changed out of her running clothes, and picked up her purse from the hook by the door.
text_zh: 埃琳娜晨跑回来，注意到她的蓝色掀背车不在通常的位置。她放慢脚步停下来，看着混凝土上原本停车位置的油渍。一个白色信封塞在门垫下面。她打开信封，读了来自城市签约拖车公司的通知。她拨打了纸上的号码，一段录音留言提供了扣押场的营业时间和地点。埃琳娜折好通知放进口袋。她走进屋里，换下跑步衣服，从门边的挂钩上拿起钱包。

topic: A person's car is towed from their own driveway
text_en: Maya came home from the grocery store and found the driveway empty. Her sedan was gone, leaving only a faint oil stain on the concrete. She set the bags down on the porch and walked to the street, checking both directions. A neighbor across the road was watering his lawn, and she called out to ask if he had seen anything. He mentioned a tow truck had been there earlier, but he hadn't paid much attention. Maya pulled out her phone and looked up the local towing company's number. She dialed and waited through a few rings before someone answered.
text_zh: 玛雅从杂货店回到家，发现车道空了。她的轿车不见了，只在混凝土上留下淡淡的油渍。她把袋子放在门廊上，走到街上，朝两个方向看了看。街对面的一位邻居正在给草坪浇水，她大声问他是否看到了什么。他提到早些时候有一辆拖车来过，但他没太注意。玛雅掏出手机，查找当地拖车公司的号码。她拨打了电话，等了几声铃响后有人接听。

topic: A person's car is towed from their own driveway
text_en: Priya was packing her lunch in the kitchen when she heard the mail slot click. She went to the hallway and found a small card on the floor. It was from a towing company, stating her vehicle had been relocated. She looked out the front window; the spot where her compact car had been was empty. She picked up the card and read the details twice. The lot was across town. She called the number and reached an automated system that gave the retrieval hours and required documents. Priya put the card on the counter and finished making her sandwich before getting ready to leave.
text_zh: 普里亚正在厨房打包午餐，听到邮箱口咔嗒一声。她走到走廊，发现地板上有一张小卡片。卡片来自一家拖车公司，说明她的车辆已被移走。她看向前窗；她紧凑型轿车原本停放的位置空了。她捡起卡片，把细节读了两遍。停车场在城镇的另一边。她拨打了号码，接通了一个自动系统，提供了取车时间和所需文件。普里亚把卡片放在台面上，继续做完三明治，然后准备离开。

topic: A person's car is towed from their own driveway
text_en: James came out of the house carrying a bag of trash for the bin. He noticed his silver coupe was not in the driveway. He set the bag down and walked around the side of the house, checking the back alley, but it wasn't there. He went back inside and looked through the front window. A small envelope was taped to the door frame. He opened it and found a receipt from a towing service with a phone number. He called the number, and a man confirmed the vehicle had been impounded. James asked about the fee and the lot's closing time, then hung up.
text_zh: 詹姆斯拿着垃圾袋走出房子，准备扔进垃圾桶。他注意到他的银色双门轿车不在车道上。他放下袋子，绕到房子侧面，检查了后巷，但车不在那里。他回到屋里，透过前窗向外看。一个小信封贴在门框上。他打开信封，发现一张拖车服务的收据，上面有电话号码。他拨打了号码，一名男子确认车辆已被扣押。詹姆斯询问了费用和停车场的关闭时间，然后挂断了电话。

topic: A person's car is towed from their own driveway
text_en: Leah had just finished showering when she heard a knock. She wrapped a towel around herself and peered through the peephole. A neighbor was standing there, holding a piece of paper. She opened the door slightly, and he explained that a tow truck had taken her car earlier. He handed her the notice he'd found on the curb. Leah thanked him and closed the door. She read the paper, which listed the towing company's name and phone number. She dressed quickly, then called the number. A woman answered and confirmed the vehicle was at their lot. Leah asked for directions and wrote them on the back of the envelope.
text_zh: 莉亚刚洗完澡，听到敲门声。她用毛巾裹住自己，透过猫眼向外看。一位邻居站在那里，手里拿着一张纸。她稍微打开门，他解释说早些时候一辆拖车拖走了她的车。他把在路边找到的通知递给她。莉亚谢过他，关上了门。她读了那张纸，上面列出了拖车公司的名称和电话号码。她迅速穿好衣服，然后拨打了号码。一位女士接听并确认车辆在他们的停车场。莉亚询问了路线，并把路线写在信封背面。

topic: A person's car is towed from their own driveway
text_en: Owen was sitting at the dining table reading the newspaper when he heard the sound of a truck outside. He looked up and saw a tow truck pulling away from his driveway, his station wagon hooked to the back. He stood and walked to the window, watching the truck turn at the corner and disappear. He found a business card on the front step. He called the number and reached a dispatcher who gave him the impound yard's address. Owen put on his jacket and grabbed his keys from the bowl by the door. He drove to the lot, where a clerk processed the release.
text_zh: 欧文正坐在餐桌旁看报纸，听到外面卡车的声音。他抬头看到一辆拖车正从他的车道上离开，他的旅行车挂在后面。他站起来走到窗前，看着卡车在拐角处转弯消失。他在前台阶上发现了一张名片。他拨打了号码，接通了一位调度员，调度员给了他扣押场的地址。欧文穿上夹克，从门边的碗里抓起钥匙。他开车去了停车场，一名职员处理了放行手续。

topic: A person finds out their article was published under someone else's name
text_en: Maya opened the morning paper and found an article about local community gardens that she had written last month. The byline listed another name, a man she had never met. She read through the piece, recognizing her own sentences and the details she had gathered from interviews. Maya set the paper down and called the editor's office. The receptionist said the editor was in a meeting. Maya left a message asking who had submitted the piece. She then sat at her kitchen table, staring at the article again, and wondered how her work had ended up under someone else's name.
text_zh: 玛雅打开晨报，发现了一篇关于当地社区花园的文章，那是她上个月写的。署名却是另一个名字，一个她从未见过的男人。她通读了全文，认出了自己的句子以及她从采访中收集到的细节。玛雅放下报纸，给编辑办公室打了电话。接待员说编辑正在开会。玛雅留言询问是谁提交了这篇文章。然后她坐在厨房的餐桌旁，再次盯着那篇文章，想知道她的作品怎么会以别人的名字发表。

topic: A person finds out their article was published under someone else's name
text_en: During a slow afternoon at the library, Tom found the latest issue of a local history journal shelved in the reference section. He opened it to his article on the town's old railway station, the one he'd spent weeks researching and writing. The author listed was someone he didn't know. He stared at the page for a moment, then turned to the table of contents to confirm. The title and his own phrasing were unmistakable. He closed the journal and placed it back on the shelf, then returned to his desk to sort a stack of returned books.
text_zh: 在图书馆一个悠闲的下午，汤姆在参考书区发现了最新一期的当地历史杂志。他翻开杂志，看到了自己关于镇上旧火车站的文章，那篇他花了数周研究和撰写的文章。列出的作者是他不认识的人。他盯着页面看了一会儿，然后翻到目录确认。标题和他自己的措辞是清晰可辨的。他合上杂志，放回书架，然后回到自己的办公桌前整理一堆归还的书。

topic: A person finds out their article was published under someone else's name
text_en: After finishing her shift at the library, Dana checked the new issue of a regional history journal. Her essay on old mill towns appeared in the table of contents, but the author was listed as a professor she had never contacted. Dana flipped to the pages and confirmed the text was hers, including the footnotes. She placed the journal in her bag and walked to the circulation desk, where she asked a coworker if they knew the professor. The coworker shrugged. Dana borrowed the journal overnight and planned to write to the editor the next day.
text_zh: 在图书馆完成轮班后，达娜查看了新一期的地区历史杂志。她的关于旧磨坊镇的散文出现在目录中，但作者却是一位她从未联系过的教授。达娜翻到那些页面，确认文本是她的，包括脚注。她把杂志放进包里，走到借阅台，问一位同事是否认识那位教授。同事耸了耸肩。达娜借了那本杂志过夜，并计划第二天给编辑写信。

topic: A person finds out their article was published under someone else's name
text_en: Maya opened the magazine and flipped to the article she had written. Her name wasn't there. Instead, it credited a colleague from another department. She read the opening lines, which were exactly as she had submitted them. She closed the magazine and set it on her desk, then picked up her phone. She considered calling the editor, but the office was quiet and she didn't know what to say. She placed the phone back down and looked at the printed pages again, tracing the byline with her finger. She wondered how this had happened, but she didn't dwell on it for long. Later, she mentioned it to a coworker over lunch.
text_zh: 玛雅打开杂志，翻到她写的那篇文章。她的名字不在那里。相反，署名是另一个部门的同事。她读了开头几行，和她提交的一模一样。她合上杂志，放在桌上，然后拿起手机。她考虑给编辑打电话，但办公室很安静，她不知道该说什么。她把手机放回去，又看了看打印出来的页面，用手指描摹着署名。她想知道这是怎么发生的，但没有多想。后来，她在午餐时向一位同事提起了这件事。

topic: A person finds out their article was published under someone else's name
text_en: Priya was browsing an online news site when she saw a piece about urban beekeeping that she had written for a class assignment. The article had been edited slightly, but the core content was hers. The author profile belonged to a staff writer. Priya took a screenshot and sent it to her instructor, who replied that they would look into it. She then closed the browser and continued with her evening chores. A week later, the instructor confirmed the article had been republished without permission and offered to contact the site.
text_zh: 普里亚在浏览一个在线新闻网站时，看到了一篇关于城市养蜂的文章，那是她为课堂作业写的。文章被稍微编辑过，但核心内容是她写的。作者资料属于一位特约撰稿人。普里亚截了图，发给她的导师，导师回复说他们会调查此事。然后她关闭了浏览器，继续做晚上的家务。一周后，导师确认文章未经许可被重新发表，并提出联系该网站。

topic: A person finds out their article was published under someone else's name
text_en: Ethan attended a small literary reading where the host introduced a story by a local author. As the story was read aloud, Ethan realized it was the same short piece he had submitted to a contest months earlier. The reader used his exact dialogue and scene descriptions. Ethan stayed through the rest of the reading, then approached the host afterward. He explained that the story was his. The host looked confused and gave him the name of the person who had submitted it. Ethan wrote the name on a napkin and left without further discussion.
text_zh: 伊桑参加了一场小型文学朗读会，主持人介绍了一位当地作者的故事。当故事被大声朗读时，伊桑意识到这正是他几个月前提交给比赛的那个短篇。朗读者使用了他原封不动的对话和场景描写。伊桑待到朗读结束，然后走近主持人。他解释说这个故事是他的。主持人看起来很困惑，给了他提交者的名字。伊桑把名字写在餐巾纸上，没有进一步讨论就离开了。

topic: A person finds out their article was published under someone else's name
text_en: Lena found her article in the journal while waiting for her coffee to cool. The byline read Marcus Webb, a colleague who had submitted a similar draft months ago. She turned the pages, scanning the familiar paragraphs and her own phrasing. Her name appeared nowhere except in a citation. She closed the journal and set it aside, then picked it up again to check the acknowledgments. Marcus had thanked her for feedback. She finished her coffee, left the journal on the table, and walked to the bus stop without deciding what to do next.
text_zh: 莉娜在等咖啡冷却时，在杂志上发现了她的文章。署名是马库斯·韦伯，一位几个月前提交过类似草稿的同事。她翻动书页，扫过熟悉的段落和她自己的措辞。她的名字除了引用之外没有出现。她合上杂志，放在一边，然后又拿起来查看致谢部分。马库斯感谢了她的反馈。她喝完咖啡，把杂志留在桌上，走向公交车站，没有决定下一步该做什么。

topic: A person finds out their article was published under someone else's name
text_en: Priya's research article appeared in the journal with a different name as the lead author. She had done the data collection and much of the writing. She read the abstract, noting that the text was unchanged. She closed the PDF and went back to her lab work. At the end of the day, she emailed the journal's office asking for a correction, but she didn't expect an immediate reply. She saved the email in her drafts folder. When a colleague asked about the publication, Priya said it had come out, without specifying the byline. She continued her evening routine as usual.
text_zh: 普里亚的研究文章出现在期刊上，但第一作者是另一个名字。她做了数据收集和大部分写作。她读了摘要，注意到文本没有改变。她关闭了PDF，回到实验室工作。一天结束时，她给期刊办公室发了邮件要求更正，但她不期望立即得到回复。她把邮件保存在草稿文件夹里。当一位同事问起这篇发表的文章时，普里亚说它已经发表了，没有具体说明署名。她像往常一样继续晚上的例行公事。

topic: A person finds out their article was published under someone else's name
text_en: Lena found her blog post republished on a larger website under another person's name. The post included her original photos and wording. She scrolled through the comments, seeing readers praise the author. She didn't comment or contact the site. Instead, she copied the link and saved it in a folder. A week later, she told a friend about it while they were having coffee. Her friend asked if she was going to do something about it. Lena said she wasn't sure. She finished her coffee and went back to work. The post remained online, and she didn't check it again.
text_zh: 莉娜发现她的博客文章被重新发表在一个更大的网站上，署名是另一个人。文章包括她原来的照片和措辞。她滚动浏览评论，看到读者称赞作者。她没有评论或联系该网站。相反，她复制了链接并保存在一个文件夹里。一周后，她和朋友喝咖啡时告诉了她这件事。朋友问她是否打算采取行动。莉娜说她不确定。她喝完咖啡，回去工作。那篇文章仍然在线，她没有再查看。

topic: A person finds out their article was published under someone else's name
text_en: Omar had written a guide for the company's internal wiki. When he opened the page, the revision history showed that a manager had replaced his name with the manager's own. Omar read through the text, which was unchanged. He closed the browser and continued with his tasks. Later, he mentioned it to a teammate, who suggested he report it. Omar said he'd think about it. He didn't report it. The next time he needed to update the guide, he made the edits as usual, without adding his name back. He didn't bring up the byline again.
text_zh: 奥马尔为公司内部维基写了一份指南。当他打开页面时，修订历史显示一位经理用他自己的名字替换了奥马尔的名字。奥马尔通读了文本，没有变化。他关闭了浏览器，继续他的任务。后来，他向一位队友提到了这件事，队友建议他举报。奥马尔说他会考虑。他没有举报。下次他需要更新指南时，他像往常一样进行了编辑，没有加回他的名字。他再也没有提起署名的事。

topic: A person finds out their article was published under someone else's name
text_en: Nina's poem was printed in the literary journal under another contributor's name. She had received the acceptance email with her own name, so she was puzzled when she saw the print edition. She read the poem twice, confirming it was hers. She set the journal on her shelf and went to prepare dinner. Her roommate noticed the journal and asked about the poem. Nina explained that it was hers, but the name was wrong. She said she might email the editor, but she didn't do it that night. The journal stayed on the shelf, and she didn't mention it again.
text_zh: 尼娜的诗发表在文学期刊上，但署名却是另一位投稿者。她收到了录用邮件，上面是自己的名字，所以看到印刷版时她感到困惑。她读了两遍那首诗，确认是自己的。她把期刊放在书架上，然后去做晚饭。她的室友注意到期刊，问起那首诗。尼娜解释说那是她的，但名字弄错了。她说她可能会给编辑发邮件，但那天晚上她没有发。期刊一直放在书架上，她也没有再提起。

topic: A person finds out their article was published under someone else's name
text_en: Maya had submitted her research piece to the regional journal months ago. When the print issue arrived at her office, she flipped through the pages and spotted the article title she recognized. But the byline listed a colleague from another department. She set the journal down and read the opening paragraph, which matched her draft almost exactly. Later, she carried the journal to the break room and left it on the table. She mentioned the mix-up to her supervisor, who said he would look into the submission records. Maya returned to her desk and opened her email to draft a note to the editor.
text_zh: 玛雅几个月前向地区期刊提交了她的研究文章。当印刷版送到她办公室时，她翻阅页面，看到了她认识的文章标题。但署名却是另一个部门的同事。她放下期刊，读了开头一段，几乎和她的草稿一模一样。后来，她把期刊带到休息室，放在桌子上。她向主管提起了这个混淆，主管说他会查看投稿记录。玛雅回到办公桌前，打开电子邮件，起草了一封给编辑的便条。

topic: A person finds out their article was published under someone else's name
text_en: Hannah had contributed a chapter to a collaborative book. When the book arrived, her chapter was credited to the editor instead. She flipped through the pages, finding her own words under the editor's name. She put the book on her bookshelf. That weekend, she mentioned it to her sister, who was visiting. Her sister said she should demand a correction. Hannah said she might. She didn't call or write. The book remained on the shelf, and she occasionally saw it when she looked for something to read, but she never opened it again. She continued with her daily routines.
text_zh: 汉娜为一本合作书籍贡献了一章。书出版后，她的那一章却被署上了编辑的名字。她翻阅页面，发现自己的文字出现在编辑名下。她把书放在书架上。那个周末，她向来访的妹妹提起了这件事。妹妹说她应该要求更正。汉娜说她可能会。她没有打电话也没有写信。书一直放在书架上，她偶尔在找书读时会看到它，但再也没有打开过。她继续着日常的生活。

topic: A person finds out their article was published under someone else's name
text_en: Ethan wrote a review for an online magazine. When the review went live, the author was listed as a staff writer he had never met. He read the review, recognizing his own analysis and phrasing. He closed the tab and went back to his own writing. The next day, he sent a short email to the editor, saying the byline was incorrect. The editor replied that they would look into it. Ethan didn't follow up. The review remained under the wrong name for several months. He occasionally saw it when searching for his work, but he didn't pursue it further.
text_zh: 伊桑为一家在线杂志写了一篇评论。评论上线时，作者却是一位他从未见过的编辑人员。他读了评论，认出了自己的分析和措辞。他关闭了标签页，继续自己的写作。第二天，他给编辑发了一封简短的电子邮件，说署名有误。编辑回复说他们会调查。伊桑没有跟进。评论在错误的名字下保留了几个月。他偶尔在搜索自己的作品时会看到它，但没有进一步追究。

topic: A person finds out their article was published under someone else's name
text_en: Julia's case study was published in a medical newsletter with the lead researcher's name, not hers. She had written the initial draft and collected the patient data. She read the published version, which was nearly identical to her draft. She closed the newsletter and continued her rounds. A colleague asked if she had seen the article. Julia said she had. The colleague asked why her name wasn't on it. Julia said she wasn't sure. She didn't ask the researcher about it. She continued with her patient charts and didn't bring it up again.
text_zh: 朱莉娅的案例研究发表在医学通讯上，署名是首席研究员，而不是她。她写了初稿并收集了患者数据。她读了发表版本，几乎和她的草稿一模一样。她合上通讯，继续查房。一位同事问她是否看到了那篇文章。朱莉娅说看到了。同事问为什么上面没有她的名字。朱莉娅说她不确定。她没有向研究员询问此事。她继续处理她的病历，没有再提起。

topic: A person finds out their article was published under someone else's name
text_en: Ethan had written a long essay about local farming practices for the community newsletter. When the new issue appeared online, he clicked the link his neighbor shared. The essay was there, but the author credit went to the editor's cousin. He scrolled through the text, recognizing his own sentences and the anecdotes from his interviews. He closed the browser and called the editor's office, leaving a voicemail about the mistake. That evening, he read a book instead of checking for a reply. The next morning, he checked his phone once and saw no response, then went to his garden to pull weeds.
text_zh: 伊桑为社区通讯写了一篇关于当地农业实践的长文。新一期在网上发布时，他点击了邻居分享的链接。文章在那里，但作者署名却是编辑的表弟。他滚动文本，认出了自己的句子和采访中的轶事。他关闭浏览器，打电话给编辑办公室，留言说明了这个错误。那天晚上，他读了一本书，没有查看回复。第二天早上，他看了一眼手机，没有看到回复，然后去花园拔草。

topic: A person finds out their article was published under someone else's name
text_en: Mark's opinion piece was published in the newspaper under the name of a political columnist. He had written it as a freelance submission. He read the piece, finding his arguments and examples intact. He set the newspaper aside and went to work. At lunch, a coworker mentioned the column and praised it. Mark said he had written it, but the coworker didn't believe him. Mark didn't insist. He finished his lunch and returned to his desk. He didn't contact the newspaper. The column remained as it was, and he didn't bring it up again.
text_zh: 马克的评论文章发表在报纸上，署名却是一位政治专栏作家。他是作为自由投稿写的。他读了这篇文章，发现自己的论点和例子都完好无损。他把报纸放在一边，去上班了。午餐时，一位同事提到专栏并称赞了它。马克说他写的，但同事不相信。马克没有坚持。他吃完午餐，回到办公桌前。他没有联系报社。专栏保持原样，他也没有再提起。

topic: A person finds out their article was published under someone else's name
text_en: Ava's travel article was printed in a regional magazine under the name of a staff photographer. She had written it after a trip she took on her own. She saw the article in a waiting room and read it, recognizing her descriptions of the places. She left the magazine on the table and went to her appointment. When she came out, she didn't take the magazine. She told her partner about it later that evening. He suggested she write to the magazine. Ava said she might. She didn't. She moved on to other tasks and didn't think about it again.
text_zh: 艾娃的旅行文章发表在地区杂志上，署名却是一位员工摄影师。她是在自己独自旅行后写的。她在候诊室看到了这篇文章，读了起来，认出了她对那些地方的描述。她把杂志留在桌子上，去赴约了。出来时，她没有带走杂志。那天晚上，她告诉了她的伴侣。他建议她写信给杂志。艾娃说她可能会。她没有。她继续做其他事情，没有再想这件事。

topic: A person finds out their article was published under someone else's name
text_en: David's technical guide was posted on the company's public blog with a manager's name attached. He had written it as part of his job. He opened the blog, saw the byline, and read a few paragraphs. The content was his. He closed the browser and continued working on a different project. A colleague asked if he'd seen the post. David said he had. The colleague asked why David's name wasn't on it. David said he didn't know. He didn't ask the manager. He returned to his code and didn't mention it again.
text_zh: 大卫的技术指南发布在公司公共博客上，署名却是一位经理。他是作为工作的一部分写的。他打开博客，看到署名，读了几段。内容是他的。他关闭浏览器，继续做另一个项目。一位同事问他是否看到了那篇帖子。大卫说看到了。同事问为什么上面没有大卫的名字。大卫说他不知道。他没有问经理。他回到代码中，没有再提起。

topic: A person finds out their article was published under someone else's name
text_en: Rachel's short story was accepted by an anthology, but when the book came out, the story was attributed to another writer. She had the acceptance email, so she knew it was hers. She read the story in the book, confirming every sentence. She closed the book and placed it on her nightstand. She didn't contact the publisher. A few days later, a friend who had bought the book asked about it. Rachel explained that the name was wrong. The friend said that was strange. Rachel agreed. She didn't pursue it. The book remained on her nightstand, and she read other books instead.
text_zh: 瑞秋的短篇小说被一本选集收录，但书出版时，故事却被归功于另一位作家。她有录用邮件，所以她知道那是她的。她读了书中的故事，确认了每一句话。她合上书，放在床头柜上。她没有联系出版商。几天后，一位买了书的朋友问起这件事。瑞秋解释说名字弄错了。朋友说那很奇怪。瑞秋同意。她没有追究。书一直放在床头柜上，她改读其他书了。

topic: An employee is transferred to a different department
text_en: When the transfer notice arrived, Maya packed her desk belongings into a small cardboard box. Her new department was on the third floor, a different layout with cubicles instead of the open workspace she had known for years. On her first morning there, she introduced herself to a colleague named Tom, who showed her where the printer and coffee machine were located. She spent most of the day reading through the project files on her computer, taking notes on a pad she kept beside her keyboard. At lunch, she ate at her desk while familiarizing herself with the team's workflow. By late afternoon, she had set up her phone and arranged her pens in the drawer.
text_zh: 当调动通知到达时，玛雅把自己的办公用品收拾进一个小纸箱。她的新部门在三楼，布局不同，是隔间式工位，而不是她多年来熟悉的开放式工作区。第一天早上，她向一位名叫汤姆的同事介绍了自己，汤姆带她看了打印机和咖啡机的位置。她大部分时间都在电脑上阅读项目文件，并在键盘旁边的便签本上做笔记。午餐时，她在办公桌前吃饭，同时熟悉团队的工作流程。到傍晚时分，她已经设置好电话，并把笔整理进抽屉里。

topic: An employee is transferred to a different department
text_en: The transfer notice came through on a Tuesday. Liam had been in the accounting department for several years, and now he was moving to the procurement office. He spent the first day meeting his new coworkers and learning the software they used. The work was different, but the procedures were explained clearly. He took notes during the training sessions and asked questions when something was unclear. By Friday, he had processed a few purchase orders under supervision. He still had much to learn, but he understood the basic workflow. He planned to review the manual over the weekend.
text_zh: 调动通知是在周二收到的。利亚姆在会计部门工作了好几年，现在他要搬到采购办公室。第一天他用来认识新同事并学习他们使用的软件。工作内容不同，但流程解释得很清楚。他在培训期间做笔记，遇到不清楚的地方就提问。到周五，他已经在监督下处理了几份采购订单。他还有很多要学，但他理解了基本的工作流程。他计划在周末复习手册。

topic: An employee is transferred to a different department
text_en: Priya's manager told her she would be joining the human resources team next month. She had been in customer service, so this was a shift. She spent her remaining weeks wrapping up her current projects and handing over files. On her first day in HR, she was given a tour of the office and introduced to the staff. Her new role involved maintaining employee records and assisting with onboarding. She found the tasks straightforward, though the regulations were detailed. She referred to the policy handbook often. Her supervisor checked in periodically to see if she had questions.
text_zh: 普里亚的经理告诉她，下个月她将加入人力资源团队。她之前做客户服务，所以这是一个转变。她利用剩下的几周时间完成当前项目并移交文件。在人力资源部的第一天，她参观了办公室并认识了员工。她的新职责包括维护员工记录和协助入职。她觉得这些任务简单明了，尽管规章制度很详细。她经常查阅政策手册。她的主管定期来查看她是否有问题。

topic: An employee is transferred to a different department
text_en: James was moved from the warehouse to the logistics planning department. His new job involved scheduling deliveries and coordinating with drivers. He had a small desk with a computer and a phone. His trainer, Angela, explained the routing system and showed him how to handle delays. He spent the afternoon shadowing her as she made calls. The pace was steadier than the warehouse, and he had to sit for most of the day. He found it different but manageable. He made a few notes on the procedures to remember for the next day.
text_zh: 詹姆斯从仓库调到了物流规划部门。他的新工作是安排送货时间表并协调司机。他有一张小桌子，上面放着电脑和电话。他的培训师安吉拉解释了路线系统，并教他如何处理延误。下午他跟着她打电话。节奏比仓库稳定，他大部分时间都得坐着。他觉得这不一样，但可以应付。他记了一些流程笔记，以备第二天使用。

topic: An employee is transferred to a different department
text_en: Elena had worked in the marketing department for a year, and now she was being transferred to the research division. She gathered her personal belongings and said goodbye to her teammates. Her new office was on a different floor, and she had to get used to the quieter atmosphere. Her first task was to compile survey data from the previous quarter. She used spreadsheets and created charts. The work was detailed and required concentration. She completed the task by the end of the week and sent it to her supervisor for review. She was still getting familiar with the team's expectations.
text_zh: 埃琳娜在市场营销部门工作了一年，现在她被调到研究部门。她收拾好个人物品，和队友们道别。她的新办公室在另一层楼，她不得不适应更安静的氛围。她的第一个任务是整理上一季度的调查数据。她使用电子表格并创建图表。这项工作很细致，需要集中注意力。她在周末前完成了任务，并发送给主管审阅。她还在逐渐熟悉团队的期望。

topic: An employee is transferred to a different department
text_en: After the company reorganization, Tom found himself in the facilities department instead of the maintenance crew. His new duties included overseeing cleaning schedules and ordering supplies. He had a small office near the loading dock. He met with the facilities manager, who gave him a list of vendors. He spent the day calling suppliers and comparing prices. The work was less physical than his previous role, but it involved more paperwork. He had to keep track of inventory levels. By the end of the week, he had placed a few orders and updated the supply closet.
text_zh: 公司重组后，汤姆发现自己被调到了设施部门，而不是维修队。他的新职责包括监督清洁时间表和订购用品。他在装卸码头附近有一间小办公室。他会见了设施经理，经理给了他一份供应商名单。他花了一天时间给供应商打电话并比较价格。这份工作体力消耗比之前少，但涉及更多文书工作。他必须跟踪库存水平。到周末，他已经下了几份订单并更新了储物间。

topic: An employee is transferred to a different department
text_en: Aisha was reassigned from the sales team to the product development unit. She had been used to client meetings, and now she was working with engineers and designers. Her first week was spent reading through product specifications and attending design reviews. She offered input from a customer perspective, which the team seemed to appreciate. She had to learn the technical jargon and the development timeline. She took notes during the meetings and followed up on action items. The work was collaborative, and she gradually understood her role in the process.
text_zh: 艾莎从销售团队被重新分配到产品开发部门。她习惯了客户会议，现在她和工程师、设计师一起工作。她的第一周用来阅读产品规格和参加设计评审。她从客户角度提出意见，团队似乎很欣赏。她必须学习技术术语和开发时间表。她在会议期间做笔记，并跟进行动项目。工作是协作性的，她逐渐理解了她在流程中的角色。

topic: An employee is transferred to a different department
text_en: Robert's transfer to the quality assurance department came as part of a company-wide shift. He had been in production, so he was familiar with the products but not the testing procedures. His new supervisor assigned him to inspect finished items and document defects. He was trained on the testing equipment and the reporting forms. He found the work repetitive but important. He had to be careful to follow the standards. He made a few mistakes at first, but his supervisor pointed them out and he corrected them. He was getting the hang of it by the end of the second week.
text_zh: 罗伯特调到质量保证部门是公司范围调整的一部分。他之前在生产线，所以熟悉产品但不熟悉测试程序。他的新主管指派他检查成品并记录缺陷。他接受了测试设备和报告表格的培训。他觉得工作重复但很重要。他必须小心遵守标准。起初他犯了一些错误，但主管指出来，他改正了。到第二周结束时，他已经开始上手了。

topic: An employee is transferred to a different department
text_en: Marcus had been in the same department for years, so the transfer felt like starting over. On his first day, he arrived early and found his new cubicle. The walls were bare, and the desk had a faint coffee stain. He unpacked his notebook and a photo of his dog, placing them carefully. A colleague from the next cubicle introduced herself and mentioned the weekly meeting schedule. Marcus listened, then asked about the printer location. After that, he opened his laptop and began reviewing the files in his inbox, adjusting to the new rhythm.
text_zh: 马库斯在同一部门工作多年，所以这次调动感觉像是重新开始。第一天，他早早就到了，找到了自己的新隔间。墙壁光秃秃的，桌子上有一块淡淡的咖啡渍。他拿出笔记本和一张他的狗的照片，小心地放好。隔壁隔间的一位同事介绍了自己，并提到了每周会议的时间表。马库斯听着，然后问了打印机的位置。之后，他打开笔记本电脑，开始查看收件箱里的文件，适应新的节奏。

topic: An employee is transferred to a different department
text_en: Carlos had been a technician in the IT support center, and now he was being transferred to the network security team. He had basic knowledge of security concepts, but the new role required a deeper understanding. He was given a series of training modules to complete online. He also shadowed a senior analyst who monitored alerts and responded to incidents. He had to learn the company's security policies and the tools they used. He spent the week reading documentation and running test scenarios. He still had a lot to learn, but he was starting to see how the team operated.
text_zh: 卡洛斯曾是IT支持中心的技术员，现在他被调到网络安全团队。他有基本的安防概念知识，但新角色需要更深入的理解。他得到了一系列在线培训模块要完成。他还跟随一位高级分析师学习，这位分析师监控警报并响应事件。他必须学习公司的安全策略和他们使用的工具。他花了一周时间阅读文档和运行测试场景。他还有很多要学，但他开始了解团队是如何运作的。

topic: An employee is transferred to a different department
text_en: Sara's transfer to the public relations department was unexpected. She had been working in customer support, so she was used to talking to people, but this was different. Her new role involved writing press releases and managing the company's social media accounts. She had a background in writing, so she picked up the basics quickly. She worked with the PR manager to draft a statement about a new product launch. She had to coordinate with the design team for images. She found the work engaging and the deadlines manageable. She was still learning the company's tone and style.
text_zh: 萨拉被调到公关部门是出乎意料的。她一直在做客户支持工作，所以习惯了与人交谈，但这次不同。她的新角色涉及撰写新闻稿和管理公司的社交媒体账号。她有写作背景，所以很快掌握了基础知识。她与公关经理合作起草了一份关于新产品发布的声明。她必须与设计团队协调图片。她发现这份工作很有吸引力，截止日期也可以管理。她仍在学习公司的语气和风格。

topic: An employee is transferred to a different department
text_en: David was moved from the shipping department to the inventory control team. His new job involved monitoring stock levels and coordinating with purchasing. He had to use a barcode scanner and a computer system to track items. His supervisor explained the reorder points and the process for flagging low stock. He spent the day walking through the warehouse, counting items and updating the system. He found the work physical and technical at the same time. He had to be accurate with the counts. He completed the daily cycle count and reported any discrepancies.
text_zh: 大卫从运输部门调到了库存控制团队。他的新工作是监控库存水平并与采购部门协调。他必须使用条形码扫描仪和计算机系统来跟踪物品。他的主管解释了再订货点和标记低库存的流程。他花了一天时间在仓库里走动，清点物品并更新系统。他发现这份工作既需要体力又需要技术。他必须确保计数准确。他完成了每日周期盘点并报告了任何差异。

topic: An employee is transferred to a different department
text_en: Fatima had been a junior accountant, and now she was being transferred to the internal audit department. She had learned the basics of auditing in school, but she hadn't applied them in practice. Her new team was preparing for an upcoming review of the company's financial statements. She was assigned to help gather documentation and verify transactions. She worked with a senior auditor who showed her how to sample invoices and trace them to the ledger. She found the work detailed and slow-paced. She had to be patient and precise. She was becoming more comfortable with the procedures.
text_zh: 法蒂玛曾是一名初级会计师，现在她被调到内部审计部门。她在学校学过审计的基础知识，但没有在实践中应用过。她的新团队正在准备对公司财务报表进行即将到来的审查。她被指派帮助收集文件和核实交易。她与一位高级审计师合作，后者向她展示了如何抽样发票并追踪到分类账。她发现这份工作细致且节奏缓慢。她必须耐心和精确。她对这些程序越来越熟悉。

topic: An employee is transferred to a different department
text_en: George was transferred from the call center to the training department. He had often helped new hires during their first weeks, so the move made sense. His new role involved developing training materials and conducting orientation sessions. He spent his first week reviewing the existing curriculum and updating outdated sections. He also observed a few training sessions led by his colleague. He had to learn how to use the presentation software and the learning management system. He found the work creative but also structured. He was preparing a session for the next batch of new employees.
text_zh: 乔治从呼叫中心调到了培训部门。他经常在新员工入职的头几周帮助他们，所以这次调动是有道理的。他的新角色涉及开发培训材料和进行入职培训。他第一周花在审查现有课程和更新过时的部分上。他还观察了同事主持的几次培训课程。他必须学习如何使用演示软件和学习管理系统。他发现这份工作既有创造性又有结构性。他正在为下一批新员工准备一次培训。

topic: An employee is transferred to a different department
text_en: Hannah's move to the legal department was a change from her previous role in records management. She had experience with documentation, but she was not familiar with legal terminology. Her new supervisor gave her a stack of contracts to organize and file. She had to review each document for completeness and enter the key dates into the system. She had a checklist to follow. She found the work meticulous and quiet. She had to concentrate to avoid missing details. She asked her supervisor when she encountered unfamiliar clauses. She was learning the basics of contract administration.
text_zh: 汉娜调到法律部门是她之前记录管理角色的一个变化。她有文档处理经验，但不熟悉法律术语。她的新主管给了她一叠合同让她整理和归档。她必须检查每份文件的完整性，并将关键日期输入系统。她有一份检查清单要遵循。她发现这份工作细致且安静。她必须集中注意力以避免遗漏细节。当她遇到不熟悉的条款时，她会询问主管。她正在学习合同管理的基础知识。

topic: An employee is transferred to a different department
text_en: Ivan was shifted from the maintenance team to the building services department. His new duties included managing the janitorial staff and ensuring the building was clean and safe. He had to create schedules and order cleaning supplies. He had never supervised anyone before, so this was new. He met with the team members and listened to their concerns. He adjusted the schedule to cover all areas. He spent the week checking the building and addressing minor issues. He found the role more administrative than he was used to, but it was straightforward. He was getting to know the staff.
text_zh: 伊万从维护团队调到了建筑服务部门。他的新职责包括管理清洁人员，确保建筑干净安全。他必须制定时间表并订购清洁用品。他以前从未监督过任何人，所以这是新的。他会见了团队成员并听取了他们的担忧。他调整了时间表以覆盖所有区域。他花了一周时间检查建筑并处理小问题。他发现这个角色比他习惯的更具行政性，但很简单。他正在逐渐了解员工。

topic: An employee is transferred to a different department
text_en: Julia had been a graphic designer in the creative department, and now she was being transferred to the web development team. Her design skills were still useful, but she had to learn about coding and responsive layouts. She was given access to the company's website and a list of updates to make. She worked with a developer who explained the content management system. She had to test the pages on different devices. She found the work technical and creative at the same time. She made a few edits and previewed them. She was still learning the process, but she had completed her first task.
text_zh: 朱莉娅曾是创意部门的平面设计师，现在她被调到网页开发团队。她的设计技能仍然有用，但她必须学习编码和响应式布局。她被授予公司网站的访问权限和一份要进行的更新列表。她与一位开发人员合作，后者解释了内容管理系统。她必须在不同设备上测试页面。她发现这份工作既需要技术又需要创意。她做了一些编辑并预览了它们。她仍在学习这个过程，但她已经完成了第一个任务。

topic: An employee is transferred to a different department
text_en: When Priya was told she'd be moving to the logistics team, she spent the afternoon clearing her old workspace. She labeled a few folders and transferred her files to a shared drive. The next morning, she reported to the new office, where the layout was open and busy. Her new supervisor handed her a list of current projects and suggested she shadow a colleague for the day. Priya followed along, taking notes on the workflow. At lunch, she ate at her desk, observing the pace of the team. By the end of the day, she had a better sense of the tasks ahead.
text_zh: 当普里亚被告知她将调到物流团队时，她花了一下午清理她原来的工作空间。她给几个文件夹贴了标签，并将文件转移到共享驱动器。第二天早上，她到新办公室报到，那里的布局开放而繁忙。她的新主管递给她一份当前项目列表，并建议她跟随一位同事学习一天。普里亚跟着做，记下工作流程的笔记。午餐时，她在办公桌前吃饭，观察团队的节奏。到一天结束时，她对未来的任务有了更好的了解。

topic: An employee is transferred to a different department
text_en: Lena was moved from the front desk to the events coordination team. She had often helped with office events, so this was a natural progression. Her new role involved planning meetings and conferences. She had to book venues, arrange catering, and send invitations. She worked with her supervisor to organize an upcoming client appreciation dinner. She spent the day calling vendors and comparing menus. She also created a timeline for the event. She found the work varied and busy. She had to keep track of many details. She was looking forward to the event, though she still had to finalize the seating arrangements.

text_zh: 汉娜正坐在厨房餐桌旁，看到一个让她回忆起往事的名字——本——发来的好友请求。初中时，本总是拿她的雀斑开玩笑。她看了看他的个人资料，发现他现在是一名教师，还有他在教室里的照片。她接受了请求，并发了一条消息：“嗨，本，我记得你，我们同校。”他回了一个笑脸，说他在加老友。他们聊了几句关于教学的事。汉娜随后放下手机，拿起一本书。

topic: Someone receives a friend request from a childhood bully
text_en: Isaac was waiting for a train when he saw a friend request from a name that gave him pause—Chris. In middle school, Chris had been the one who always hid his backpack. He looked at the request and then at Chris's profile, which showed him with a motorcycle. Isaac accepted and typed a short message: "Hey Chris, hope you're doing well." Chris replied with a smiley face and said he was just catching up with old classmates. They exchanged a few messages about their hobbies. Isaac then put his phone in his pocket as the train arrived.
text_zh: 艾萨克正在等火车时，看到一个让他停顿的名字——克里斯——发来的好友请求。初中时，克里斯总是藏他的背包。他看了看请求，又看了看克里斯的个人资料，上面有他和一辆摩托车的照片。艾萨克接受了请求，并打了一条简短的消息：“嘿，克里斯，希望你一切都好。”克里斯回了一个笑脸，说他在和老同学叙旧。他们聊了几句各自的爱好。艾萨克随后把手机放进口袋，这时火车到了。

topic: A person finds out their partner has been learning their native language
text_en: Elena was putting away groceries when she noticed a small notebook on the counter. It was her partner's, but the handwriting inside was unfamiliar. She flipped it open and saw lists of words with translations into her native language. There were notes on grammar and little drawings of common objects. Her partner walked in, and she closed the notebook, placing it back where it was. She didn't say anything about it, but later that evening, she heard him practicing a simple phrase under his breath. She recognized the accent, still rough, but it was her language. She continued preparing dinner, thinking about the notebook and the effort it represented.
text_zh: 埃琳娜正在收拾杂货，这时她注意到柜台上有一个小笔记本。那是她伴侣的，但里面的笔迹她不熟悉。她翻开笔记本，看到一列列单词，附有翻译成她母语的释义。还有语法笔记和常见物品的小图画。她的伴侣走进来，她合上笔记本，放回原处。她什么也没说，但那天晚上晚些时候，她听到他低声练习一个简单的短语。她听出了那个口音，仍然很生硬，但那是她的语言。她继续准备晚餐，想着那个笔记本以及它所代表的努力。

topic: A person finds out their partner has been learning their native language
text_en: Marta was cleaning the study when she found a stack of flashcards tucked inside a drawer. They were for her native language, with words like "bread" and "tree" written on them. She picked one up and read the back, where her partner had written the pronunciation. She hadn't known he was learning it. She put the cards back and went to the kitchen, where he was washing dishes. She said nothing, but she watched him for a moment. He turned and smiled at her, and she smiled back. She thought about the flashcards and wondered when he had started them. She decided to ask him about it over dinner.
text_zh: 玛尔塔正在打扫书房，这时她在抽屉里发现了一叠闪卡。这些卡片是用于她的母语的，上面写着“面包”和“树”之类的单词。她拿起一张，翻到背面，看到她的伴侣写了发音。她不知道他一直在学。她把卡片放回去，走到厨房，他正在那里洗碗。她什么也没说，但看了他一会儿。他转过身来对她微笑，她也回以微笑。她想着那些闪卡，想知道他是什么时候开始学的。她决定在晚餐时问问他这件事。

topic: A person finds out their partner has been learning their native language
text_en: Jonas was looking for a book on the shelf when he noticed a small audio player wedged between volumes. He picked it up and pressed play, and a voice spoke in his native language. It was a lesson, with pauses for repetition. He recognized his partner's voice, stumbling over the words. He stopped the player and put it back. Later, he found his partner sitting on the porch, listening to the same lesson through earbuds. Jonas sat down beside him. He didn't say anything, but he noticed his partner's lips moving, forming the words. He felt a quiet sense of something he couldn't name, and he just sat there, listening to the faint sound of the lesson.
text_zh: 乔纳斯正在书架上找一本书，这时他注意到一个小的音频播放器夹在书卷之间。他拿起它，按下播放键，一个声音用他的母语说话。那是一节课，中间有停顿以便跟读。他听出那是他伴侣的声音，磕磕绊绊地念着单词。他停下播放器，把它放了回去。后来，他发现他的伴侣坐在门廊上，戴着耳机听着同一节课。乔纳斯在他旁边坐下。他什么也没说，但他注意到他伴侣的嘴唇在动，在念那些词。他感到一种安静的、说不出的感觉，他就那样坐在那里，听着那微弱的课程声。

topic: A person finds out their partner has been learning their native language
text_en: Priya was sorting through the mail when she found a receipt for an online language course. The course was for her native language. She looked at the date, which was a few weeks ago. She hadn't mentioned it to her partner, but she didn't know he had signed up. She put the receipt on the table and went to the living room, where he was reading. She asked him about it, and he looked up, slightly embarrassed. He said he wanted to understand her better. She nodded and sat down next to him. She didn't know what to say, so she just picked up a book and read, but she was aware of his presence beside her.
text_zh: 普里亚正在整理邮件，这时她发现了一张在线语言课程的收据。那门课程是教她的母语的。她看了看日期，是几周前的。她没有向伴侣提起过这件事，但她不知道他已经报名了。她把收据放在桌上，走到客厅，他正在那里看书。她问了他这件事，他抬起头，略显尴尬。他说他想更好地理解她。她点点头，在他旁边坐下。她不知道该说什么，于是只是拿起一本书读了起来，但她能感觉到他在她身边。

topic: A person finds out their partner has been learning their native language
text_en: Lena was tidying the bedroom when she found a dictionary hidden under the pillow. It was a pocket dictionary for her native language. She opened it and saw that some pages were marked with little sticky notes. She recognized her partner's handwriting on the notes, with words like "home" and "together" underlined. She put the dictionary back and went to find him in the kitchen. He was making coffee, and he seemed to be humming a tune that she recognized from her childhood. She paused in the doorway, listening. He turned and saw her, and he stopped humming. She didn't say anything, but she walked over and took the cup he offered her.
text_zh: 莉娜正在整理卧室，这时她在枕头下发现了一本词典。那是一本她的母语的袖珍词典。她打开它，看到有些页面上贴着小小的便利贴。她认出便利贴上是她伴侣的笔迹，有些词像“家”和“在一起”被划了线。她把词典放回去，去厨房找他。他正在煮咖啡，似乎在哼着一首她童年时听过的曲子。她在门口停住，听着。他转过身，看见了她，便停止了哼唱。她什么也没说，但走过去，接过了他递来的杯子。

topic: A person finds out their partner has been learning their native language
text_en: Omar was unpacking a box of books when he found a notebook filled with practice sentences. They were in his native language, and they were simple, like "My name is..." and "I live in..." The handwriting was his partner's, and there were corrections in red ink. He flipped through the pages, seeing progress from the beginning to the end. He closed the notebook and put it on the shelf. Later, he heard his partner on the phone, speaking haltingly in his language. He listened from the other room, and he felt a strange mix of feelings. He didn't interrupt, but he made a note to mention it later.
text_zh: 奥马尔正在打开一箱书，这时他发现了一个写满练习句子的笔记本。那些句子是用他的母语写的，很简单，比如“我的名字是……”和“我住在……”。笔迹是他伴侣的，上面还有红笔的批改。他翻着书页，看到了从开头到结尾的进步。他合上笔记本，把它放在书架上。后来，他听到他的伴侣在打电话，用他的语言断断续续地说着。他在另一个房间听着，感到一种奇怪而复杂的情绪。他没有打断，但记下了稍后要提这件事。

topic: A person finds out their partner has been learning their native language
text_en: Sofia was looking for a pen in the desk drawer when she found a small notepad with words written in her native language. They were everyday words, like "morning" and "evening" and "thank you." She recognized her partner's careful handwriting. She put the notepad back and went to the living room, where her partner was watching TV. She sat down next to him, and she noticed that he was mouthing something under his breath. She leaned closer, and she heard him say a word in her language. She didn't react, but she felt a warmth in her chest. She turned her attention back to the TV, but she was thinking about the notepad.
text_zh: 索菲亚正在书桌抽屉里找笔，这时她发现了一个小记事本，上面写着她的母语单词。都是些日常用语，比如“早上”、“晚上”和“谢谢”。她认出了她伴侣那工整的笔迹。她把记事本放回去，走到客厅，她的伴侣正在那里看电视。她在他旁边坐下，她注意到他在低声嘟囔着什么。她凑近了些，听到他用她的语言说了一个词。她没有反应，但感到胸口一阵温暖。她把注意力转回电视，但心里想着那个记事本。

topic: A person finds out their partner has been learning their native language
text_en: Elena was folding laundry when she heard a muffled voice from the bedroom. She paused, recognizing the cadence but not the words. Her partner, Marcus, was on the phone, speaking in Portuguese—her language. She had never heard him attempt it before. When he hung up, she asked about it. Marcus shrugged, saying he'd been practicing with an app during his lunch breaks for a few weeks. He stumbled over a phrase, and Elena corrected his pronunciation. He repeated it slowly, then smiled. She handed him a folded towel and returned to the basket, noting the odd mix of familiar sounds in his mouth.
text_zh: 埃琳娜正在叠衣服，这时她听到卧室里传来一个低沉的声音。她停下来，听出了那种节奏，但听不懂词。她的伴侣马库斯正在打电话，说的是葡萄牙语——她的语言。她以前从未听过他尝试说葡萄牙语。他挂断电话后，她问起了这件事。马库斯耸耸肩，说他几周来一直在午休时间用一款应用练习。他结结巴巴地说了一个短语，埃琳娜纠正了他的发音。他慢慢地重复了一遍，然后笑了。她递给他一条叠好的毛巾，然后回到洗衣篮旁，注意到那些熟悉的音调从他嘴里说出来时那种奇特的混合感。

topic: A person finds out their partner has been learning their native language
text_en: Ana was cleaning the living room when she found a piece of paper with a poem written on it. It was in her native language, and it was a simple love poem. She recognized her partner's handwriting, and she saw that he had crossed out some words and written alternatives above them. She folded the paper and put it in her pocket. Later, she found him in the garden, and she showed him the paper. He looked embarrassed, but he said he had been trying to write something for her. She didn't know what to say, so she just nodded and put the paper away.
text_zh: 安娜正在打扫客厅，这时她发现了一张写着诗的纸。那是一首用她的母语写的简单情诗。她认出了她伴侣的笔迹，她看到他划掉了一些词，并在上面写了替代词。她把纸叠好放进口袋。后来，她在花园里找到了他，她把那张纸拿给他看。他看起来很尴尬，但他说他一直在试着为她写点什么。她不知道该说什么，只是点了点头，把纸收了起来。

topic: A person finds out their partner has been learning their native language
text_en: Priya noticed the Korean phrasebook on the nightstand, its spine cracked and pages dog-eared. Her partner, Daniel, had never mentioned learning Korean. She picked it up and flipped through it, finding notes in his handwriting—translations of common greetings and food terms. When he came in from the garden, she held up the book. He explained that he'd started lessons online a couple of months ago, wanting to understand her conversations with her family. He read a line aloud, his accent thick but recognizable. Priya nodded, replaced the book on the stand, and went back to sorting the mail.
text_zh: 普里亚注意到床头柜上的韩语常用语手册，书脊已经裂开，书页也卷了边。她的伴侣丹尼尔从未提过要学韩语。她拿起手册翻了翻，发现里面有他的笔迹——常见问候语和食物词汇的翻译。当他从花园进来时，她举起了那本书。他解释说，他几个月前开始上网课，想听懂她与家人的对话。他大声读了一行，口音很重，但能辨认出来。普里亚点了点头，把书放回床头柜上，然后继续整理邮件。

topic: A person finds out their partner has been learning their native language
text_en: Hannah was in the kitchen when she saw a cookbook propped open on the counter. It was a cookbook from her home country, with recipes she remembered from her childhood. She looked at the page, and she saw that someone had written notes in the margins, in her partner's handwriting, asking questions about ingredients. She closed the book and put it away. Later, she found her partner trying to make one of the recipes, and the kitchen was a mess. She watched from the doorway, and he looked up, embarrassed. She didn't say anything, but she went over and helped him with the dish.
text_zh: 汉娜在厨房里，看到柜台上摊开着一本食谱。那是她家乡的食谱，里面是她童年记忆中的菜谱。她看了看那一页，发现页边空白处有人用她伴侣的笔迹写了笔记，询问食材的问题。她合上书，把它收了起来。后来，她发现伴侣正在尝试做其中一道菜，厨房里一片狼藉。她从门口看着，他抬起头，显得很尴尬。她什么也没说，但走过去帮他一起做那道菜。

topic: A person finds out their partner has been learning their native language
text_en: Tomas was in the bedroom when he found a book on the nightstand. It was a grammar book for his native language. He opened it, and he saw that it was well-worn, with pages marked and notes in the margins. He put it down and went to the living room, where his partner was sitting on the couch. He asked about the book, and his partner said he had been trying to learn the language. Tomas didn't know what to say, so he just sat down next to him. They watched TV in silence, but Tomas was aware of the book in the other room.
text_zh: 托马斯在卧室里，发现床头柜上有一本书。那是他母语的语法书。他打开一看，发现书已经很旧了，书页上有标记，页边还有笔记。他放下书，走到客厅，他的伴侣正坐在沙发上。他问起那本书，伴侣说一直在试着学这门语言。托马斯不知道该说什么，就只是在他旁边坐下。他们沉默地看着电视，但托马斯能感觉到另一间房间里的那本书。

topic: A person finds out their partner has been learning their native language
text_en: Nadia was looking for her phone charger when she found a notebook in the drawer. It was filled with vocabulary lists in her native language. She recognized her partner's handwriting, and she saw that he had written the words in both languages. She put the notebook back and went to find him. He was in the study, and he was listening to an audio lesson. He had earbuds in, so he didn't hear her come in. She stood there for a moment, watching him, and then she left quietly. She didn't mention it, but she thought about it for the rest of the day.
text_zh: 纳迪亚在找手机充电器时，在抽屉里发现了一个笔记本。里面写满了她母语的词汇表。她认出那是伴侣的笔迹，而且他把单词用两种语言都写了出来。她把笔记本放回去，去找他。他在书房里，正在听音频课程。他戴着耳机，所以没听到她进来。她站在那里看了一会儿，然后悄悄离开了。她没有提起这件事，但一整天都在想着它。

topic: A person finds out their partner has been learning their native language
text_en: Maya found Liam’s phone on the kitchen counter, screen lit with a language app. The words on the display were in her native tongue—phrases about groceries, directions, small talk. She picked it up, scrolling through the lesson history. He’d been practicing for weeks, the streak counter showing consistent daily sessions. She set the phone down and walked to the living room, where Liam was reading a book. He glanced up, and she nodded toward the kitchen. “I saw your phone,” she said. He closed the book, waiting. She sat across from him, the evening quiet around them.
text_zh: 玛雅发现利亚姆的手机在厨房柜台上，屏幕亮着，显示着一个语言学习应用。屏幕上的文字是她的母语——关于买菜、问路、闲聊的短语。她拿起手机，翻看了学习记录。他已经练习了好几个星期，连续打卡记录显示他每天都在学习。她放下手机，走到客厅，利亚姆正在那里看书。他抬头看了一眼，她朝厨房点了点头。“我看到你的手机了，”她说。他合上书，等着她开口。她在他对面坐下，夜晚在他们周围安静下来。

topic: A person finds out their partner has been learning their native language
text_en: Paul was in the garage when he found a set of language learning CDs. They were for his native language, and they were still in their shrink wrap. He picked them up and looked at them, and he saw that they had been bought recently. He put them down and went back inside. He found his partner in the kitchen, and he asked about the CDs. His partner said he had been thinking about learning the language. Paul didn't say anything more, but he felt a little odd. He went to the living room and sat down, and he didn't mention it again.
text_zh: 保罗在车库里发现了一套语言学习光盘。那是为他母语准备的，而且还没有拆封。他拿起来看了看，发现是最近才买的。他放下光盘，回到屋里。他在厨房里找到伴侣，问起光盘的事。伴侣说一直在考虑学这门语言。保罗没有再说什么，但感觉有点奇怪。他走到客厅坐下，之后再也没有提起这件事。

topic: A person finds out their partner has been learning their native language
text_en: Mia was in the bedroom when she found a small notebook on the dresser. It was open to a page with a list of phrases in her native language. She read them, and they were phrases like "How are you?" and "I miss you." She closed the notebook and put it back. Later, she was in the kitchen, and her partner came in. He said something in her language, but he said it wrong. She corrected him, and he repeated it. She didn't say anything about the notebook, but she felt a little touched.
text_zh: 米娅在卧室里，发现梳妆台上有一个小笔记本。它翻开的那一页上列着一些她母语的短语。她读了一下，都是些像“你好吗？”和“我想你”这样的短语。她合上笔记本，把它放回原处。后来，她在厨房里，伴侣走了进来。他用她的语言说了些什么，但说错了。她纠正了他，他又重复了一遍。她没有提起笔记本的事，但心里有点感动。

topic: A person finds out their partner has been learning their native language
text_en: Maya had been dating Tom for nearly a year, and she'd always spoken English with him. One evening, while she was on the phone with her mother back in Poland, Tom walked in holding a grocery bag. He set it down and said, in careful Polish, "I bought the things you like for dinner." Maya paused mid-sentence, her mother's voice still chattering in her ear. She blinked at him. He'd never mentioned learning Polish. She finished the call slowly, then asked him how long he'd been practicing. He shrugged, saying he'd been taking lessons for a few months. She nodded, noticing the slightly awkward pronunciation of the word for bread.
text_zh: 玛雅和汤姆交往快一年了，她一直和他说英语。一天晚上，她正在和波兰的母亲通电话，汤姆拎着一个食品杂货袋走了进来。他放下袋子，用小心翼翼的波兰语说：“我买了你喜欢的晚餐吃的东西。”玛雅话说到一半停了下来，母亲的声音还在耳边絮叨。她眨了眨眼看着他。他从来没提过学波兰语。她慢慢说完电话，然后问他练了多久。他耸耸肩，说他已经上了几个月的课。她点点头，注意到他“面包”这个词的发音有点别扭。

topic: A person finds out their partner has been learning their native language
text_en: Nadia found the Korean flashcards in the study drawer while looking for a pen. They were worn, with Hangul characters on one side and English on the other. Her husband, Eric, had been coming home later than usual, but she hadn't thought much of it. She flipped through a few cards—"가족" for family, "음식" for food. She remembered him asking her to teach him a phrase once, years ago, and how she'd laughed it off. Now here he was, studying on his own. She put the cards back carefully. That night, she asked him about it. He admitted he'd been taking lessons for a while. "I just wanted to know more about your world," he said.
text_zh: 纳迪亚在书房抽屉里找笔时，发现了那些韩语单词卡。它们已经很旧了，一面是韩文，另一面是英文。她的丈夫埃里克最近回家比平时晚，但她没怎么在意。她翻了几张卡片——“가족”是家庭，“음식”是食物。她想起多年前他曾让她教他一个短语，她当时一笑置之。现在他却在自学。她小心地把卡片放回去。那天晚上，她问起这件事。他承认他已经上了一段时间的课。“我只是想多了解一点你的世界，”他说。

topic: A person finds out their partner has been learning their native language
text_en: Gabriel was in the study when he found a stack of papers on the desk. They were printouts of language lessons, and they were in his native language. He looked at them, and he saw that his partner had written notes on them. He put them back and went to the living room, where his partner was watching TV. He sat down next to him, and he didn't say anything. But he noticed that his partner was mouthing something, and he realized it was a word in his language. He didn't react, but he felt a little odd.
text_zh: 加布里埃尔在书房里，发现书桌上有一叠纸。那是语言课程的打印件，而且是他母语的。他看了看，发现伴侣在上面写了笔记。他把纸放回去，走到客厅，伴侣正在那里看电视。他在他旁边坐下，什么也没说。但他注意到伴侣在无声地动着嘴唇，他意识到那是一个他语言中的词。他没有反应，但感觉有点奇怪。

topic: A person finds out their partner has been learning their native language
text_en: Isabella was in the kitchen when she found a list of words on the fridge. They were in her native language, and they were written in her partner's handwriting. She read them, and they were words like "apple" and "water" and "house." She left the list on the fridge and went about her day. Later, she heard her partner in the other room, practicing the words out loud. She listened for a moment, and then she went back to what she was doing. She didn't mention it, but she noticed that he was getting better.
text_zh: 伊莎贝拉在厨房里，发现冰箱上贴着一张单词表。那些单词是她的母语，而且是伴侣的笔迹。她读了一下，都是些像“苹果”“水”“房子”这样的词。她把那张表留在冰箱上，继续过自己的日子。后来，她听到伴侣在另一个房间里大声练习这些单词。她听了一会儿，然后又回去做自己的事。她没有提起这件事，但她注意到他进步了。

topic: A chef receives a harsh review from a food critic
text_en: Marco wiped down the stainless steel counter after the lunch rush, the familiar rhythm of the rag moving in circles. The review had been posted that morning, and a few of the waitstaff had already read it aloud in the back. He had skimmed it himself over a quick coffee, noting the critic's complaints about the seasoning in the fish dish and the wait between courses. He finished wiping the counter, then checked the prep list for the evening. He would adjust the salt in the marinade and talk to the front of house about pacing.
text_zh: 午餐高峰过后，马可擦拭着不锈钢台面，抹布画圈的熟悉节奏。评论是那天早上发布的，几个服务员已经在后面大声读过。他自己在快速喝咖啡时略读了一遍，注意到评论家对鱼料理调味和上菜间隔的抱怨。他擦完台面，然后检查了晚上的备料清单。他会调整腌料中的盐分，并与前厅人员讨论上菜节奏。

topic: A chef receives a harsh review from a food critic
text_en: Marco set the newspaper on the kitchen counter, the critic's words about his tasting menu still fresh. He had read it twice, noting the specific dishes mentioned. His hands moved to the pantry, pulling out the ingredients for the evening's service. He adjusted the seasoning on the lamb, a dish the review had called heavy-handed. The line cooks watched him, waiting for a reaction. He simply told them to refocus on the plating. The afternoon rush began, and he moved through the kitchen, tasting sauces and checking temperatures. The review stayed in his mind, but there was work to do.
text_zh: 马可把报纸放在厨房台面上，评论家关于他品尝菜单的评论还历历在目。他读了两遍，记下了提到的具体菜肴。他的手伸向储藏室，拿出晚间服务的食材。他调整了羊肉的调味，这道菜被评论称为调味过重。流水线上的厨师们看着他，等待他的反应。他只是告诉他们重新专注于摆盘。下午的高峰开始了，他在厨房里穿梭，品尝酱汁，检查温度。评论留在他脑海中，但有工作要做。

topic: A chef receives a harsh review from a food critic
text_en: Elena found the review online during her break. The critic had praised the ambiance but found her signature soup bland. She closed the browser and returned to the prep station, where a pile of onions awaited. She began dicing them, the familiar rhythm calming her thoughts. Her sous chef asked about the review, and she mentioned the soup comment. They discussed adjusting the broth's depth. She finished the onions, then moved to the fish station to check the day's delivery. The evening service would proceed as usual, with a few small tweaks to the recipe.
text_zh: 埃琳娜在休息时在网上看到了评论。评论家称赞了氛围，但认为她的招牌汤味道平淡。她关闭浏览器，回到备餐台，那里有一堆洋葱等着她。她开始切洋葱，熟悉的节奏让她的思绪平静下来。她的副厨问起评论的事，她提到了关于汤的评论。他们讨论了调整汤底的深度。她切完洋葱，然后去鱼台检查当天的到货。晚市将照常进行，只是对食谱稍作调整。

topic: A chef receives a harsh review from a food critic
text_en: The printed review sat on the hostess stand when David arrived. He read it while tying his apron. The critic had disliked the dessert, calling it overly sweet. David walked to the pastry station and looked at the chocolate tart. He considered the sugar ratio, then decided to leave it for the night. He had a regular customer who loved it. The prep work for dinner was already laid out. He checked the reservation book and spoke with the waitstaff about the specials.
