The kitchen buzzed with activity, and he fell into the familiar flow of service.
text_zh: 大卫到达时，打印的评论放在领位台。他边系围裙边读。评论家不喜欢甜点，称其过甜。大卫走到甜点台，看着巧克力挞。他考虑了糖的比例，然后决定今晚保持原样。他有一位常客喜欢这道甜点。晚餐的备料已经摆好。他查看了预订簿，并与服务员讨论了特色菜。厨房里一片忙碌，他进入了熟悉的出餐节奏。

topic: A chef receives a harsh review from a food critic
text_en: Priya skimmed the critic's column on her phone between lunch and dinner service. The review mentioned her duck dish was tough. She remembered that table, a busy Saturday night. She pulled the duck from the cooler, examining its quality. She thought about the cooking time, perhaps a few minutes less. She wrote a note to the evening line cook about the adjustment. The rest of the afternoon she spent preparing the garnishes and sauces. When the first orders came in, she focused on the timing of each course, ensuring the duck came out just right.
text_zh: 普里亚在午餐和晚餐服务之间用手机浏览了评论家的专栏。评论提到她的鸭肉菜太硬。她记得那桌客人，那是一个繁忙的周六晚上。她从冷藏库取出鸭肉，检查其质量。她考虑了烹饪时间，也许可以减少几分钟。她给晚上的流水线厨师写了一张关于调整的便条。下午剩下的时间她用来准备配菜和酱汁。当第一批订单进来时，她专注于每道菜的时间，确保鸭肉恰到好处。

topic: A chef receives a harsh review from a food critic
text_en: Liam noticed the review in the morning paper. The critic had found his service slow and the food uninspired. He folded the paper and placed it in the recycling bin. At the restaurant, he checked the schedule and made sure the front-of-house had enough staff. He reviewed the menu with the kitchen team, pointing out a few dishes that could use more seasoning. He didn't mention the review directly, but the changes were subtle. During service, he expedited orders with more attention, calling out times and checking plates before they left the pass.
text_zh: 利亚姆在晨报上注意到了评论。评论家认为他的服务缓慢，食物缺乏创意。他折起报纸，放进回收箱。在餐厅，他检查了排班，确保前厅有足够的人手。他与厨房团队一起审阅了菜单，指出几道菜可以多加调味。他没有直接提及评论，但变化是微妙的。服务期间，他更加专注地催单，报出时间，并在菜品离开出餐口前检查盘子。

topic: A chef receives a harsh review from a food critic
text_en: Sofia read the harsh critique while waiting for the produce delivery. The critic had called her risotto gummy. She put the phone away and helped unload the crates of vegetables. In the kitchen, she started the stock for the evening. She recalled the risotto, thinking about the stirring technique and the broth temperature. She decided to use a different rice for tonight. She prepped the ingredients, then set up her station. The first risotto of the evening she made with extra care, tasting it before serving. The rest of the service followed its usual pace.
text_zh: 索菲亚在等待农产品送货时读了严厉的评论。评论家称她的烩饭太黏糊。她放下手机，帮忙卸下成箱的蔬菜。在厨房里，她开始为晚上熬高汤。她回想起那道烩饭，思考搅拌技巧和汤的温度。她决定今晚换一种米。她准备好食材，然后布置好工作台。晚上的第一份烩饭她格外用心，上菜前先尝了尝。接下来的服务照常进行。

topic: A chef receives a harsh review from a food critic
text_en: Andre saw the review on the restaurant's social media page. The critic had given a negative write-up of his bistro's fixed menu. He turned off his phone and went to the walk-in cooler to check the vegetables. He selected the carrots and leeks for the day's soup. Back at the stove, he started the base, adding a bit more thyme than usual. His staff arrived and he gave them their assignments. The lunch rush was steady. He plated each dish with the same precision, not changing anything major. The review was a topic of brief conversation, but the work continued.
text_zh: 安德烈在餐厅的社交媒体页面上看到了评论。评论家对他的小酒馆固定菜单写了负面评价。他关掉手机，走进冷藏库检查蔬菜。他为当天的汤挑选了胡萝卜和韭葱。回到炉灶前，他开始熬制汤底，比平时多加了一点百里香。他的员工到了，他给他们分配了任务。午餐高峰平稳。他以同样的精准度摆盘每道菜，没有做任何大的改变。评论成为短暂交谈的话题，但工作继续着。

topic: A chef receives a harsh review from a food critic
text_en: Nadia's coworker handed her the printed review during a lull. The critic had dismissed her pork belly as fatty. She read it, then set it aside on the counter. She continued portioning the pork for the evening, trimming it more carefully than usual. She adjusted the braising liquid, adding a touch more apple cider vinegar. Her line cook asked if she was okay, and she said she was fine, just thinking about the recipe. She tasted the sauce and nodded. The orders came in, and she cooked the pork to a crisp finish, hoping to address the comment.
text_zh: 纳迪亚的同事在空闲时递给她打印的评论。评论家认为她的五花肉太肥。她读了，然后把它放在台面上。她继续为晚上分割猪肉，比平时更仔细地修整。她调整了炖煮液，多加了一点苹果醋。她的流水线厨师问她是否还好，她说她没事，只是在想食谱。她尝了酱汁，点了点头。订单来了，她把猪肉煮到酥脆，希望能回应那条评论。

topic: A chef receives a harsh review from a food critic
text_en: Tom was prepping vegetables when the hostess brought in the newspaper. He wiped his hands and read the review. The critic had complained about the noise level and the overcooked pasta. He folded the paper and returned to the carrots. He thought about the pasta station, telling the cook to reduce the boiling time by a minute. He also mentioned to the manager that they might need to adjust the seating arrangement. The rest of his shift he spent moving between stations, checking on dishes and keeping the kitchen running smoothly.
text_zh: 汤姆正在准备蔬菜时，领位员拿来了报纸。他擦干手，读了评论。评论家抱怨噪音水平和意面煮过头。他折起报纸，回到胡萝卜旁。他想着意面台，告诉厨师把煮沸时间减少一分钟。他还向经理提到，他们可能需要调整座位安排。剩下的班次，他在各个工作台之间穿梭，检查菜品，保持厨房顺畅运转。

topic: A chef receives a harsh review from a food critic
text_en: Isabel read the review on her tablet during a quiet moment. The critic had panned her lamb chops, saying they were underseasoned. She closed the tablet and went to the spice rack. She examined her rosemary and garlic, then made a new marinade for the evening's lamb. She rubbed it into the meat, letting it sit. Her sous chef came by and they discussed the critic's palate. They agreed to add a pinch more salt to the rub. She then moved on to the vegetable prep, slicing mushrooms and shallots. The dinner service was busy, and she kept the seasoning consistent.
text_zh: 伊莎贝尔在安静的时刻用平板电脑阅读了评论。评论家批评了她的羊排，说调味不足。她合上平板电脑，走到香料架前。她检查了迷迭香和大蒜，然后为晚餐的羊肉调制了新的腌料。她将腌料揉进肉里，让它静置。她的副厨走过来，他们讨论了评论家的味觉。他们同意在腌料中多加一点盐。然后她继续进行蔬菜准备工作，切蘑菇和青葱。晚餐服务很忙碌，她保持了调味的一致性。

topic: A chef receives a harsh review from a food critic
text_en: George found the review tucked into the reservation book. The critic had written that his soup was too salty and the bread stale. He read it, then placed it in the office drawer. He went to the bakery section and checked the morning's loaves. They were fresh, but he made a note to bake a second batch for the evening. He tasted the soup from the pot, thinking it was fine, but he added a little water to balance it. He then started on the evening's specials, writing them on the board. The kitchen staff arrived, and he gave them the prep list.
text_zh: 乔治在预订簿里发现了那份评论。评论家写道他的汤太咸，面包不新鲜。他读完后，把它放进了办公室的抽屉里。他走到面包区，检查了早晨的面包。面包是新鲜的，但他记下要为晚上再烤一批。他尝了尝锅里的汤，觉得还可以，但他加了一点水来平衡味道。然后他开始准备晚上的特色菜，把它们写在黑板上。厨房工作人员到了，他给了他们备料清单。

topic: A chef receives a harsh review from a food critic
text_en: Owen finished his shift and sat in the back alley, having a smoke. The review had come out that day, and the critic had not held back, calling the restaurant 'a shadow of its former self.' Owen had been working there for a few years and had seen the changes. He stubbed out the cigarette and went back inside. He checked the schedule for the next day and saw he was on the line. He would focus on the basics, making sure the grill was clean and the temperatures were right.
text_zh: 欧文结束了轮班，坐在后巷抽烟。评论那天出来了，评论家毫不留情，称这家餐厅“昔日辉煌的影子”。欧文在那里工作了好几年，目睹了这些变化。他掐灭香烟，走回室内。他查看了第二天的排班表，看到自己负责炒锅。他会专注于基本功，确保烤架干净，温度合适。

topic: A chef receives a harsh review from a food critic
text_en: Hannah saw the review on her phone while sitting in the office. The critic had called her fish dish bland. She put the phone down and walked to the fish station. She examined the cod fillets, then prepared a new herb butter to serve with them. She asked her line cook to taste the butter, and he nodded. She made a note to add a squeeze of lemon at the end. The rest of the afternoon she spent checking the inventory and ordering supplies. When service began, she cooked the fish with more attention to the seasoning, hoping the critic's comment would be addressed.
text_zh: 汉娜坐在办公室里，在手机上看到了评论。评论家称她的鱼菜平淡无味。她放下手机，走到鱼台。她检查了鳕鱼片，然后准备了一种新的香草黄油来搭配。她让她的线厨尝尝黄油，他点了点头。她记下要在最后挤一点柠檬汁。下午剩下的时间她用来检查库存和订购物资。服务开始时，她更加注意调味来烹饪鱼，希望评论家的评论能得到回应。

topic: A chef receives a harsh review from a food critic
text_en: Omar read the critic's review in the local paper. The review was harsh, criticizing his restaurant's signature dish. He folded the paper and placed it under the counter. He went to the stove and tasted the sauce from the day before. He added a bit more pepper. His sous chef asked about the review, and Omar shrugged, saying they'd keep cooking. He then went to the front of the house to check the reservation list. The evening was fully booked. He returned to the kitchen and started the prep for the night, his movements efficient and practiced.
text_zh: 奥马尔在当地报纸上读到了评论家的评论。评论很严厉，批评了他餐厅的招牌菜。他折起报纸，放在柜台下面。他走到炉子前，尝了尝昨天的酱汁。他加了一点胡椒。他的副厨问起评论的事，奥马尔耸耸肩，说他们会继续做菜。然后他走到前厅查看预订名单。晚上已经订满了。他回到厨房开始准备晚上的工作，动作高效而熟练。

topic: A chef receives a harsh review from a food critic
text_en: Rachel's phone buzzed with a notification about the review. She read it, noting the critic's complaints about her dessert. She set the phone aside and went to the pastry station. She pulled out the ingredients for the chocolate mousse, adjusting the recipe slightly, adding less sugar. She whisked the cream and folded it into the chocolate. Her assistant watched, asking if she was changing the menu. Rachel said she was just tweaking it. She filled the ramekins and placed them in the fridge. She then cleaned her station and started on the next task, the day continuing as usual.
text_zh: 瑞秋的手机嗡嗡作响，收到关于评论的通知。她读了评论，注意到评论家对她甜点的抱怨。她把手机放在一边，走到糕点台。她拿出巧克力慕斯的配料，稍微调整了配方，减少了糖的用量。她搅打奶油，然后将其折叠进巧克力中。她的助手看着，问她是否在改变菜单。瑞秋说她只是在调整。她填满小烤盅，放进冰箱。然后她清理了自己的工作台，开始下一项任务，这一天照常继续。

topic: A chef receives a harsh review from a food critic
text_en: Peter came across the review while scrolling through his phone during a break. The critic had lambasted his restaurant's service and food. He put the phone away and returned to the kitchen, where he started chopping onions for the evening's stew. His mind drifted to the review, but he focused on the knife work. He checked the simmering pot, adding a bay leaf. His waitstaff came in for the pre-service meeting, and he went over the specials with them. He didn't bring up the review, but he reminded them to be attentive. The night's service began, and he moved through it with his usual routine.
text_zh: 彼得在休息时刷手机，看到了评论。评论家严厉批评了他餐厅的服务和食物。他收起手机，回到厨房，开始为晚上的炖菜切洋葱。他的思绪飘向评论，但他专注于刀工。他检查了炖锅，加了一片月桂叶。他的服务员进来参加服务前会议，他和他们过了一遍特色菜。他没有提起评论，但提醒他们要细心周到。晚上的服务开始了，他按照惯常的流程进行。

topic: A chef receives a harsh review from a food critic
text_en: Mia found the review on the restaurant's website. The critic had given her bistro a poor write-up, mentioning the tough steak. She closed the laptop and walked to the meat locker. She selected the ribeyes for the evening, looking at the marbling. She decided to tenderize them a bit more and let them come to room temperature before cooking. She seasoned them with salt and pepper. Her grill cook came in, and she told him to cook them a little less. She then started on the side dishes, making a fresh batch of mashed potatoes. The service was steady, and she kept an eye on the grill.
text_zh: 米娅在餐厅网站上看到了评论。评论家对她的餐馆评价很差，提到了牛排太硬。她合上笔记本电脑，走到肉类冷藏室。她为晚上挑选了肋眼牛排，看了看大理石花纹。她决定再嫩化一下，让它们在烹饪前恢复到室温。她用盐和胡椒调味。她的烤台厨师进来，她告诉他烤的时间稍微短一点。然后她开始准备配菜，做了一批新鲜的土豆泥。服务稳定进行，她留意着烤架。

topic: A chef receives a harsh review from a food critic
text_en: Carlos read the review in the morning, the critic's words about his paella being dry. He put the paper aside and went to the market to pick up fresh seafood. Back at the kitchen, he started the sofrito, letting the onions and garlic cook slowly. He added the rice and broth, adjusting the liquid ratio. He tasted it, thinking it needed a bit more stock. His line cook came in, and Carlos had him taste it too. They agreed on the adjustment. The lunch service began, and Carlos made the paella with extra care, checking the rice's texture before serving.
text_zh: 卡洛斯早上读了评论，评论家说他的海鲜饭太干。他把报纸放在一边，去市场采购新鲜海鲜。回到厨房，他开始做炒底料，让洋葱和大蒜慢慢煮。他加入米饭和高汤，调整了液体比例。他尝了尝，觉得需要再加点高汤。他的线厨进来，卡洛斯也让他尝了尝。他们同意调整。午餐服务开始了，卡洛斯格外小心地制作海鲜饭，上菜前检查米饭的口感。

topic: A chef receives a harsh review from a food critic
text_en: Ava saw the review on the counter, left by the owner. The critic had panned her restaurant's tasting menu. She read it, then went to the kitchen to start the day's prep. She checked the produce and began cleaning the greens. Her sous chef asked about the review, and she mentioned the critic's comment about the foam. She considered removing it from one dish. She prepared the stock and began the sauces. The afternoon passed with the usual tasks. As the dinner service started, she plated the dishes, deciding to keep the foam but reduce its amount. The kitchen was busy, and she worked through the orders.
text_zh: 艾娃在柜台上看到了评论，是老板留下的。评论家批评了她餐厅的品尝菜单。她读完后，去厨房开始一天的备料。她检查了农产品，开始清洗绿叶菜。她的副厨问起评论，她提到了评论家关于泡沫的评论。她考虑从一道菜中去除泡沫。她准备了高汤，开始制作酱汁。下午像往常一样过去了。晚餐服务开始时，她摆盘，决定保留泡沫但减少用量。厨房很忙，她处理着订单。

topic: Someone finds their childhood teddy bear at a yard sale
text_en: Maya stopped at a yard sale on her way back from the grocery store. She was browsing through a box of old toys when she spotted a worn brown bear with a missing eye. It looked just like the one she had carried everywhere as a child. She picked it up and turned it over. The stitch on its left paw matched the repair her mother had made. Maya stood there for a moment, holding the bear, then asked the woman at the table how much it cost. She paid and carried it home, setting it on the shelf beside her books.
text_zh: 玛雅从杂货店回来的路上，在一个庭院拍卖会前停了下来。她正在翻看一箱旧玩具时，发现了一只磨损的棕色熊，少了一只眼睛。它看起来就像她小时候随身携带的那只。她捡起来翻过来看。左爪上的缝线与母亲修补的痕迹相符。玛雅站在那里，手里握着熊，过了一会儿，问桌旁的女人多少钱。她付了钱，把它带回家，放在书架旁的书架上。

topic: Someone finds their childhood teddy bear at a yard sale
text_en: Margaret stopped at a yard sale on her way back from the grocery store, scanning the tables of mismatched dishes and old paperbacks. Near the back, propped against a box of vinyl records, sat a small brown bear with a faded red bow. She picked it up, turning it over in her hands. The stitching along its side matched the repair her mother had made years ago. The woman running the sale said it was from an estate a few streets over. Margaret set it back down gently, then paid the asking price and carried it home.
text_zh: 玛格丽特从杂货店回来的路上，在一个庭院拍卖会前停了下来，扫视着摆满不配套的盘子和旧平装书的桌子。在后面，靠着一箱黑胶唱片，坐着一只系着褪色红蝴蝶结的小棕熊。她捡起来，在手里翻来覆去地看。它侧面的缝线与母亲多年前修补的痕迹相符。经营拍卖会的女人说，这只熊来自几条街外的一处房产。玛格丽特轻轻把它放回去，然后按要价付了钱，把它带回了家。

topic: Someone finds their childhood teddy bear at a yard sale
text_en: Elena was helping her neighbor clear out a garage when she saw a box labeled "stuffed animals." Inside, on top, was a brown bear with a red bow that had come loose. She recognized it immediately. It had been hers before she gave it to her younger cousin years ago. The cousin had moved away, and Elena had never thought about the bear again. She lifted it out and brushed off some dust. The fur was softer than she remembered. She placed it back in the box and closed the lid, then helped carry the box to the curb.
text_zh: 埃琳娜正在帮邻居清理车库，这时她看到一个标着“毛绒玩具”的箱子。里面，最上面是一只棕熊，红蝴蝶结松了。她立刻认出了它。这是她的熊，多年前她把它送给了表妹。表妹搬走了，埃琳娜再也没有想过这只熊。她把它拿出来，掸了掸灰尘。皮毛比她记忆中的更柔软。她把它放回箱子里，盖上盖子，然后帮忙把箱子搬到路边。

topic: Someone finds their childhood teddy bear at a yard sale
text_en: While waiting for a friend at a flea market, Tom wandered past a table with old children's items. A small bear sat among the books and toys. It had a patch on its stomach, just like the one his grandmother had sewn on his bear. He picked it up and examined the stitching. The patch was the same fabric, a piece from an old shirt. Tom held it for a moment, then put it down. He walked away, but later came back and asked the seller if the bear had any history. The seller shrugged. Tom bought it anyway.
text_zh: 在跳蚤市场等朋友时，汤姆走过一张摆着旧儿童用品的桌子。一只小熊坐在书和玩具中间。它的肚子上有一块补丁，就像他祖母缝在他的熊上的那块一样。他捡起来检查缝线。补丁是同样的布料，来自一件旧衬衫。汤姆拿了一会儿，然后放下。他走开了，但后来又回来，问卖家这只熊有没有什么来历。卖家耸耸肩。汤姆还是买下了它。

topic: Someone finds their childhood teddy bear at a yard sale
text_en: Priya was at a neighborhood sale when she noticed a teddy bear lying on a blanket with other stuffed animals. The bear had a blue ribbon around its neck, which was unusual because her bear had a red one. But the shape and the way the ears were set were exactly right. She knelt down and touched its paw. There was a small tear near the seam. Priya had a similar tear on her bear from when she had dragged it along the sidewalk. She stood up and walked to the next table, then came back and bought the bear for a small price.
text_zh: 普里亚在一个社区售卖会上，注意到一只泰迪熊躺在毯子上，和其他毛绒玩具在一起。这只熊脖子上系着蓝色丝带，这很不寻常，因为她的熊是红色的。但形状和耳朵的安放方式完全正确。她蹲下来，摸了摸它的爪子。靠近接缝处有一个小裂口。普里亚的熊上也有类似的裂口，那是她拖着它沿人行道走时弄的。她站起来，走到下一张桌子，然后又回来，以低价买下了这只熊。

topic: Someone finds their childhood teddy bear at a yard sale
text_en: At a church bazaar, Rachel found a teddy bear in a bin of donated toys. It was a light brown color, with a stitched smile and button eyes. She picked it up and turned it over. The back had a faint ink mark that looked like a name, but it was too worn to read. Rachel had a bear with a similar mark from when she had written her name on it as a child. She held it for a while, then put it back in the bin. She bought a few other items and left, but she kept thinking about the bear. She returned before the bazaar closed and bought it.
text_zh: 在教堂义卖会上，雷切尔在一箱捐赠的玩具中发现了一只泰迪熊。它是浅棕色的，有缝制的微笑和纽扣眼睛。她捡起来翻过来看。背面有一个模糊的墨迹，看起来像名字，但磨损得无法辨认。雷切尔有一只类似的熊，那是她小时候在上面写名字留下的。她拿了一会儿，然后放回箱子里。她买了其他几样东西就离开了，但她一直在想那只熊。她在义卖会结束前回来，买下了它。

topic: Someone finds their childhood teddy bear at a yard sale
text_en: Mark was helping his aunt sort through items for her yard sale. He carried a box of old toys from the attic and set it on the grass. When he opened it, the first thing he saw was a small bear with a missing arm. It was his bear from childhood, the one he had lost during a camping trip. He had forgotten about it completely. He picked it up and looked at the torn seam where the arm used to be. His aunt came over and asked if he wanted to keep it. He shook his head and placed it back in the box, then helped her arrange the sale.
text_zh: 马克正在帮姨妈整理庭院拍卖的物品。他从阁楼搬了一箱旧玩具，放在草地上。当他打开时，第一眼看到的就是一只少了一只胳膊的小熊。这是他童年的熊，露营时丢失的那只。他完全忘记了它。他捡起来，看着胳膊曾经所在处的撕裂接缝。姨妈走过来，问他想不想留着它。他摇摇头，把它放回箱子里，然后帮她布置售卖。

topic: Someone finds their childhood teddy bear at a yard sale
text_en: During a walk through a residential area, Laura saw a yard sale with a table of old toys. A small brown bear sat at the edge, its fur matted in places. She stopped and picked it up. The bear had a small bell inside that jingled when she shook it. Laura remembered having a bear with a bell when she was very young. She had lost it during a move. She held the bear for a moment, then set it down. She walked a few steps, then came back and asked the owner if she could buy it. The owner said yes, and Laura paid and tucked it into her bag.
text_zh: 在住宅区散步时，劳拉看到了一个庭院拍卖会，桌上摆着旧玩具。一只小棕熊坐在边缘，皮毛有些地方打结了。她停下来，捡起来。熊肚子里有个小铃铛，摇晃时会叮当作响。劳拉记得自己很小的时候也有一只带铃铛的熊。她在搬家时弄丢了。她拿了一会儿，然后放下。她走了几步，又回来问主人能不能买下它。主人说可以，劳拉付了钱，把它塞进包里。

topic: Someone finds their childhood teddy bear at a yard sale
text_en: At a weekend market, Kevin noticed a teddy bear on a shelf among other knickknacks. It was a dark brown bear with a red vest. Kevin had a bear like that as a child, one he had received for his birthday. He picked it up and felt the fabric. It was rougher than his had been. The vest had a small pocket, which his bear also had. He put the bear down and moved on to look at some tools. Later, he came back and bought the bear, thinking it could be a gift for his niece.
text_zh: 在周末市场上，凯文注意到货架上摆着其他小饰品中间的一只泰迪熊。那是一只深棕色的熊，穿着红色背心。凯文小时候有一只那样的熊，是他生日时收到的。他捡起来摸了摸布料。它比他原来的那只粗糙。背心上有个小口袋，他的熊也有。他放下熊，继续去看一些工具。后来，他回来买下了这只熊，想着可以送给侄女当礼物。

topic: Someone finds their childhood teddy bear at a yard sale
text_en: Sandra was at a garage sale with her roommate. She was looking through a box of old clothes when she saw a teddy bear tucked underneath. She pulled it out. It was a small, cream-colored bear with a pink nose. Sandra recognized it as the bear she had taken to kindergarten. She had left it in the classroom one day and never got it back. She held it up to the light. The fur was a little yellowed. She showed it to her roommate, who said it looked old. Sandra put it back in the box and continued looking through the clothes.
text_zh: 桑德拉和室友在一个车库拍卖会上。她正在翻看一箱旧衣服时，看到下面塞着一只泰迪熊。她把它拉出来。那是一只小巧的奶油色熊，粉红色的鼻子。桑德拉认出这是她上幼儿园时带的熊。有一天她把它留在教室里，再也没有拿回来。她把它举到光线下。皮毛有点发黄。她给室友看，室友说它看起来很旧。桑德拉把它放回箱子里，继续翻看衣服。

topic: Someone finds their childhood teddy bear at a yard sale
text_en: At a community swap meet, Alex was browsing through a stall of secondhand goods. He saw a teddy bear sitting on a stack of old magazines. It was a grayish bear with a lopsided head. Alex remembered having a bear that was similarly lopsided, a factory mistake that made it unique. He picked it up and examined it. The stitching on the head was uneven, just like his old bear. He put it down and looked at other items, then returned and bought it for a couple of dollars. He placed it in his backpack and walked on.
text_zh: 在社区旧物交换会上，亚历克斯正在浏览一个二手货摊位。他看到一只泰迪熊坐在一摞旧杂志上。那是一只灰扑扑的熊，头有点歪。亚历克斯记得自己也有一只类似的歪头熊，那是工厂的失误，让它变得独一无二。他拿起它仔细端详。头上的缝线不均匀，就像他那只旧熊一样。他放下它，看了看其他物品，然后又回来，花了几美元把它买了下来。他把它放进背包，继续往前走。

topic: Someone finds their childhood teddy bear at a yard sale
text_en: While driving through a small town, Nina noticed a yard sale sign and pulled over. She walked around the tables and found a teddy bear in a basket of stuffed animals. It was a small brown bear with a worn patch on its ear. Nina had a bear with a similar patch, one she had chewed on as a baby. She picked it up and touched the patch. It felt like the same fabric. She looked at the price tag, which was low. She bought the bear and put it in her car, then continued browsing the sale.
text_zh: 开车穿过一个小镇时，尼娜注意到一个庭院旧货出售的牌子，便把车停到路边。她绕着桌子走了一圈，在一个装满毛绒玩具的篮子里发现了一只泰迪熊。那是一只棕色的小熊，耳朵上有一块磨损的补丁。尼娜有一只类似的补丁熊，那是她小时候咬过的。她拿起它，摸了摸那块补丁。感觉像是同一种布料。她看了看价格标签，价格很低。她买下了这只熊，放进车里，然后继续浏览出售的物品。

topic: Someone finds their childhood teddy bear at a yard sale
text_en: At a charity sale at a community center, Omar found a teddy bear on a table with other donated toys. It was a large bear with a blue bow. Omar had a bear like that when he was young, one that had been given to him by his uncle. He picked it up and hugged it briefly. The bear smelled faintly of dust and old fabric. He set it back down and walked around the room. He came back to the table and asked a volunteer about the bear. The volunteer didn't know anything about it. Omar bought it and carried it out.
text_zh: 在社区中心的一场慈善义卖会上，奥马尔在一张放着其他捐赠玩具的桌子上发现了一只泰迪熊。那是一只戴着蓝色蝴蝶结的大熊。奥马尔小时候也有一只这样的熊，是他叔叔送给他的。他拿起它，短暂地抱了一下。熊身上隐约散发着灰尘和旧布料的气味。他把它放回去，在房间里走了走。他又回到桌边，向一位志愿者询问这只熊的情况。志愿者对它一无所知。奥马尔买下了它，把它带了出去。

topic: Someone finds their childhood teddy bear at a yard sale
text_en: At a neighbor's yard sale, Grace saw a small teddy bear sitting on a chair. It was a white bear with a red scarf. Grace had a white bear with a red scarf as a child. She had taken it to a family reunion and left it behind. She picked it up and looked at the scarf. It was tied in a similar way. She held the bear for a minute, then placed it back on the chair. She bought a few other items from the sale and left. Later, she came back and asked if the bear was still there. It was, and she bought it.
text_zh: 在邻居家的庭院旧货出售会上，格蕾丝看到一只小泰迪熊坐在椅子上。那是一只戴着红围巾的白熊。格蕾丝小时候也有一只戴着红围巾的白熊。她曾把它带到家庭聚会上，却把它落在了那里。她拿起它，看了看围巾。围巾的系法很相似。她抱着熊待了一分钟，然后把它放回椅子上。她从出售会上买了几件其他物品，然后离开了。后来，她又回来问那只熊是否还在。它还在，于是她买下了它。

topic: Someone finds their childhood teddy bear at a yard sale
text_en: At a roadside sale, Peter noticed a teddy bear propped against a crate of old records. It was a brown bear with a green bow tie. Peter had a bear with a green bow tie when he was a child. He had won it at a carnival. He picked it up and examined it. The bow tie was slightly frayed, like his had been. He put it down and looked through the records. After a while, he picked the bear up again and bought it from the seller. He placed it on the passenger seat of his car and drove home.
text_zh: 在路边摊，彼得注意到一只泰迪熊靠在一箱旧唱片上。那是一只系着绿色领结的棕色熊。彼得小时候也有一只系着绿色领结的熊。那是在嘉年华上赢来的。他拿起它仔细端详。领结有点磨损，就像他那只一样。他放下它，翻了翻那些唱片。过了一会儿，他又拿起那只熊，从卖家那里买了下来。他把它放在副驾驶座上，开车回家了。

topic: Someone finds their childhood teddy bear at a yard sale
text_en: At a church rummage sale, Hannah found a teddy bear in a box of used toys. It was a small, tan bear with a stitched mouth. Hannah recognized it as the bear she had carried during a long illness as a child. She had lost it during a hospital stay. She picked it up and felt the familiar shape. The fur was worn smooth in places. She held it for a moment, then placed it back in the box. She browsed the rest of the sale, but she kept returning to the box. Eventually, she bought the bear and took it home.
text_zh: 在教堂的旧物义卖会上，汉娜在一个装满旧玩具的箱子里发现了一只泰迪熊。那是一只浅棕色的、嘴巴缝着线的小熊。汉娜认出这正是她小时候生病时一直抱着的那只熊。她在住院期间把它弄丢了。她拿起它，感受着那熟悉的形状。有些地方的绒毛已经磨得光滑了。她抱了一会儿，然后把它放回箱子里。她浏览了义卖会的其他物品，但总是回到那个箱子旁。最后，她买下了这只熊，把它带回了家。

topic: Someone finds their childhood teddy bear at a yard sale
text_en: At a neighborhood garage sale, Jason was looking at a table of old electronics when he spotted a teddy bear on a shelf behind the seller. It was a dark brown bear with a red bandana. Jason had a bear with a red bandana when he was young. He had taken it to a friend's house and forgotten it there. He asked the seller about the bear. The seller said it was from a box of old toys. Jason picked it up and looked at the bandana. It was tied the same way. He bought the bear and put it in his car.
text_zh: 在社区车库旧货出售会上，杰森正在看一桌旧电子产品，这时他注意到卖家身后架子上有一只泰迪熊。那是一只系着红色印花头巾的深棕色熊。杰森小时候也有一只系着红色印花头巾的熊。他把它带到朋友家，忘在了那里。他向卖家询问这只熊的情况。卖家说它来自一箱旧玩具。杰森拿起它，看了看头巾。系法是一样的。他买下了这只熊，放进车里。

topic: Someone finds their childhood teddy bear at a yard sale
text_en: At a flea market, Emily came across a stall with old children's books and toys. A small teddy bear sat among them, its fur a little matted and one eye slightly loose. Emily had a bear that looked just like that, one she had received for her first Christmas. She picked it up and gently touched the loose eye. It was the same kind of loose. She put it down and looked at the books. Later, she came back and bought the bear. She wrapped it in a paper bag and carried it with her for the rest of the afternoon.
text_zh: 在跳蚤市场，艾米丽来到一个卖旧童书和玩具的摊位。一只小泰迪熊坐在其中，绒毛有点结块，一只眼睛稍微有点松。艾米丽有一只看起来一模一样的熊，那是她收到的第一份圣诞礼物。她拿起它，轻轻碰了碰那只松动的眼睛。松动的程度一模一样。她放下它，看了看那些书。后来，她又回来买下了这只熊。她用纸袋把它包好，下午余下的时间一直带着它。

topic: Someone finds their childhood teddy bear at a yard sale
text_en: At a yard sale down the street, Carlos saw a teddy bear on a blanket with other stuffed animals. It was a medium-sized bear with a blue shirt. Carlos had a bear with a blue shirt when he was a child. He had left it at a hotel during a family trip. He picked it up and looked at the shirt. It had a small tear on the sleeve, just like his had. He put the bear back and talked with the owner about some other items. Before leaving, he bought the bear and tucked it under his arm.
text_zh: 在街那头的庭院旧货出售会上，卡洛斯看到一只泰迪熊和其他毛绒玩具一起放在一条毯子上。那是一只穿着蓝衬衫的中等大小的熊。卡洛斯小时候也有一只穿蓝衬衫的熊。在一次家庭旅行中，他把它落在了酒店里。他拿起它，看了看衬衫。袖子上有一个小裂口，就像他那只一样。他把熊放回去，和摊主聊了聊其他物品。离开前，他买下了这只熊，夹在胳膊下。

topic: Someone finds their childhood teddy bear at a yard sale
text_en: At a community garage sale, Aisha found a teddy bear in a bin of stuffed animals. It was a light brown bear with a yellow ribbon. Aisha had a bear with a yellow ribbon that she had carried when she was young. She had dropped it in a puddle and it had gotten ruined. She picked this one up and examined it. The ribbon was a little faded, but the bear was in good condition. She held it for a moment, then put it back. She walked around the sale and came back to the bin. She bought the bear and took it home.
text_zh: 在社区车库旧货出售会上，艾莎在一个装满毛绒玩具的箱子里发现了一只泰迪熊。那是一只系着黄丝带的浅棕色熊。艾莎小时候也有一只系着黄丝带的熊，她一直带着它。她把它掉进了水坑里，熊被弄坏了。她拿起这只，仔细看了看。丝带有点褪色，但熊的状况很好。她抱了一会儿，然后把它放回去。她在出售会上逛了一圈，又回到箱子旁。她买下了这只熊，带回了家。

topic: A homeowner discovers previous residents left items in the attic
text_en: When Margot and her husband bought the old house, the realtor mentioned the attic was full of odds and ends from the previous owners. On a Saturday morning, Margot climbed the pull-down stairs with a flashlight. She found cardboard boxes labeled "Kitchen" and "Photos," along with a dusty rocking chair and a stack of vinyl records. She opened one box and saw mismatched mugs and a set of chipped plates. She carried the box down to the kitchen, wiped each item clean, and set them on the counter. She decided to sort through the rest later, maybe donate what they didn't need.
text_zh: 当玛戈特和她的丈夫买下那栋老房子时，房地产经纪人提到阁楼里堆满了前房主留下的零碎物品。一个周六的早晨，玛戈特拿着手电筒爬上折叠梯。她发现了标着“厨房”和“照片”的纸板箱，还有一把落满灰尘的摇椅和一叠黑胶唱片。她打开一个箱子，看到了一些不配套的马克杯和一套有缺口的盘子。她把箱子搬下楼到厨房，把每件物品擦干净，放在台面上。她决定稍后再整理其余的，也许把他们不需要的东西捐出去。

topic: A homeowner discovers previous residents left items in the attic
text_en: Evan had lived in the house for almost a year before he bothered to open the attic door. The previous owner had left behind several suitcases and a rolled-up rug. He pulled down the suitcases, unzipped one, and found old clothes and a pair of worn leather boots. The other suitcase held books and a small wooden box with sewing supplies. He carried the clothes to a local charity drop-off and left the books on a shelf in his study. The rug he unrolled in the living room, though it was faded in places.
text_zh: 埃文在这栋房子里住了将近一年，才想起去打开阁楼的门。前房主留下了几个手提箱和一卷地毯。他拉下手提箱，拉开其中一个的拉链，发现里面是旧衣服和一双磨损的皮靴。另一个手提箱里装着书和一个小木盒，里面是缝纫用品。他把衣服送到当地的慈善捐赠点，把书放在书房的书架上。地毯他铺在了客厅里，尽管有些地方已经褪色。

topic: A homeowner discovers previous residents left items in the attic
text_en: Priya's new home had a small attic accessible from the hallway ceiling. She had been meaning to check it for weeks. When she finally opened it, she found a child's bicycle with training wheels, a stack of board games, and a plastic bin full of holiday decorations. She lifted the bike down and set it by the garage door, thinking she might give it to a neighbor with a young child. The board games she brought inside and placed on a shelf. The decorations she left in the attic for now, since the season was still months away.
text_zh: 普里亚的新家有一个小阁楼，可以从走廊天花板进入。她几个星期来一直想去查看。当她终于打开它时，发现了一辆带辅助轮的儿童自行车、一叠棋盘游戏和一个装满节日装饰品的塑料箱。她把自行车搬下来，放在车库门边，想着也许可以送给有小孩的邻居。棋盘游戏她带进屋里，放在架子上。装饰品暂时留在阁楼里，因为离那个季节还有好几个月。

topic: A homeowner discovers previous residents left items in the attic
text_en: Lena climbed the pull-down ladder into the attic, dust motes swirling in the flashlight beam. She had bought the house a month ago and was finally getting around to sorting through what the previous owners left behind. A stack of cardboard boxes sat near the eaves, their tape yellowed and peeling. She opened the first one and found old vinyl records, their sleeves worn at the corners. Another held a collection of glass bottles, some with faded labels. She carried the boxes down to the garage, deciding to donate what she could and toss the rest. The attic felt emptier when she finished, though she hadn't expected to find anything personal.
text_zh: 莉娜爬上折叠梯进入阁楼，手电筒的光束中灰尘微粒旋转飞舞。她一个月前买了这栋房子，现在终于抽出时间来整理前房主留下的东西。靠近屋檐处放着一堆纸板箱，胶带已经发黄翘起。她打开第一个箱子，发现是旧黑胶唱片，封套的边角已经磨损。另一个箱子里装着一批玻璃瓶，有些标签褪色了。她把箱子搬到车库，决定能捐的就捐，其余扔掉。她整理完后，阁楼显得空荡了许多，尽管她并没有期望找到什么私人物品。

topic: A homeowner discovers previous residents left items in the attic
text_en: Marta had lived in the house for years, but she'd never bothered to explore the attic beyond a quick glance. When a loose shingle caused a leak, she finally went up to check the damage. Beneath a tarp, she found a wooden crate filled with children's drawings and school papers. The names on them weren't familiar. She flipped through a few pages, then set them aside. She patched the roof leak with a temporary seal and made a note to call a roofer. The drawings stayed in the crate, which she pushed back against the wall before climbing down.
text_zh: 玛尔塔在这栋房子里住了多年，但除了匆匆一瞥，她从未认真探索过阁楼。当一块松动的木瓦导致漏水时，她终于上去检查损坏情况。在防水布下面，她发现了一个木箱，里面装满了儿童画和学校作业。上面的名字她不熟悉。她翻了几页，然后放在一边。她用临时密封剂修补了屋顶的漏水处，并记下要打电话给屋顶修理工。那些画留在箱子里，她把箱子推回墙边，然后爬了下来。

topic: A homeowner discovers previous residents left items in the attic
text_en: After inheriting the house from an aunt, Owen spent his first weekend clearing out rooms. The attic held a trunk with old clothes and a stack of letters tied with string. He opened one envelope and read a few lines about a family picnic from decades ago. He didn't recognize the names. He set the letters back in the trunk and carried it to the curb for a bulk pickup. The clothes he donated to a local charity shop. By Sunday evening, the attic was bare, and he locked the door behind him.
text_zh: 从姑妈那里继承了房子后，欧文第一个周末就忙着清理房间。阁楼里有一个箱子，里面装着旧衣服和一叠用绳子捆着的信。他打开一个信封，读了几行关于几十年前一次家庭野餐的内容。他不认识那些名字。他把信放回箱子里，把箱子搬到路边等待大件垃圾回收。衣服他捐给了当地的慈善商店。到周日晚上，阁楼已经空了，他锁上了身后的门。

topic: A homeowner discovers previous residents left items in the attic
text_en: Maya climbed the pull-down stairs into the attic, flashlight in hand, to look for holiday decorations. The beam swept over dusty boxes and old furniture. Near the far wall, she noticed a stack of cardboard boxes with faded labels reading "Kitchen" and "Misc." She opened one and found a collection of ceramic mugs, each with a different cartoon animal painted on it. Another box held a set of mismatched silverware and a wooden recipe box full of index cards. Maya lifted out a card and read the handwriting, recipes for casseroles and pies. She set it aside, deciding she would ask the realtor if the previous owners wanted these things back. She closed the box and moved to check the other containers.
text_zh: 玛雅爬上折叠梯进入阁楼，手里拿着手电筒，想找节日装饰品。光束扫过满是灰尘的箱子和旧家具。靠近远处的墙边，她注意到一叠纸板箱，上面褪色的标签写着“厨房”和“杂物”。她打开一个，发现里面是一批陶瓷马克杯，每个杯子上都画着不同的卡通动物。另一个箱子里装着一套不配套的银器和一木盒索引卡片，里面装满了索引卡。玛雅拿起一张卡片，读着上面的笔迹，是砂锅菜和馅饼的食谱。她把它放在一边，决定要问房地产经纪人前房主是否想要回这些东西。她关上箱子，继续检查其他容器。

topic: A homeowner discovers previous residents left items in the attic
text_en: Evan pulled himself into the attic to find his old camping gear. He scanned the dim space, noting the rafters and insulation. In a corner, propped against a beam, stood a rolled-up rug and a canvas bag. He unzipped the bag and found a set of folded tarps and a portable camp stove. Below the bag, a wooden crate held a few paperback novels and a deck of cards with a worn elastic band. Evan flipped through one of the books, a mystery novel with a cracked spine. He placed the deck back in the crate and moved the bag aside to see if his tent was hidden underneath. He made a mental note to call the previous owner about the items.
text_zh: 埃文爬上阁楼去找他的旧露营装备。他扫视了一下昏暗的空间，注意到椽子和隔热层。在一个角落里，靠着一根梁，立着一卷地毯和一个帆布包。他拉开包的拉链，发现里面是几块折叠的防水布和一个便携式露营炉。包下面，一个木箱里装着几本平装小说和一副橡皮筋磨损的纸牌。埃文翻了翻其中一本书，是一本书脊开裂的悬疑小说。他把纸牌放回箱子里，把包移到一边，看看他的帐篷是否藏在下面。他记下要打电话给前房主询问这些物品。

topic: A homeowner discovers previous residents left items in the attic
text_en: Lena had bought the house a few months ago, but she had never fully gone through the attic. One Saturday, with sunlight coming through the small attic window, she decided to sort its contents. On a dusty shelf, she found a shoebox tied with twine. Inside were letters and postcards, addressed to a woman named Ruth, each stamped with dates from many years ago. Lena carefully read one, a short note about a garden and a neighbor's dog. She set the letters aside, wondering if Ruth's family might want them. She kept reading a few more postcards, then placed them back in the box and continued looking through the rest of the attic.
text_zh: 莉娜几个月前买了这栋房子，但她从未彻底翻看过阁楼。一个周六，阳光透过小阁楼窗户照进来，她决定整理里面的东西。在一个布满灰尘的架子上，她发现一个用细绳捆着的鞋盒。里面是信件和明信片，收件人是一位名叫露丝的女性，每张都盖着多年前的邮戳。莉娜仔细读了一封，是一张关于花园和邻居家狗的简短便条。她把信放在一边，想知道露丝的家人是否可能想要这些。她又读了几张明信片，然后把它们放回盒子里，继续查看阁楼的其余部分。

topic: A homeowner discovers previous residents left items in the attic
text_en: Marta climbed the pull-down ladder to the attic to look for a box of winter coats. Dust coated the floorboards, and she spotted a stack of old vinyl records near the chimney. Beside them sat a leather photo album with a faded cover. She opened it and saw pictures of people she did not recognize, likely the family who lived here before. She flipped through several pages, then set the album aside. She found the coats in a trunk by the far wall, pulled out a heavy wool one, and carried it downstairs.
text_zh: 玛尔塔爬上折叠梯到阁楼去找一箱冬季外套。灰尘覆盖着地板，她注意到烟囱附近有一叠旧黑胶唱片。旁边放着一本封面褪色的皮面相册。她打开它，看到一些她不认识的人的照片，很可能是以前住在这里的那家人。她翻了几页，然后把相册放在一边。她在靠墙的箱子里找到了外套，拿出一件厚重的羊毛外套，带下楼去。

topic: A homeowner discovers previous residents left items in the attic
text_en: Tom and his wife had moved into the house weeks ago, but the attic remained full of the prior owner's belongings. Tom finally braved the cramped space, wearing a dust mask. He pulled open a dresser drawer and found neatly folded men's shirts and a pair of suspenders. The next drawer revealed socks and a small box of cufflinks. Tom picked up a cufflink, turned it over, then put it back. He lifted a shirt and saw a faint monogram on the pocket, the initials J.H. Tom folded the shirt and placed it back, thinking he might contact the estate agent to see if relatives wanted the clothing. He continued to rifle through the remaining drawers.
text_zh: 汤姆和妻子几周前搬进了这所房子，但阁楼里仍然堆满了前房主的物品。汤姆终于鼓起勇气，戴着防尘口罩，进入了这个狭窄的空间。他拉开一个梳妆台抽屉，发现里面整齐地叠放着男士衬衫和一副背带。下一个抽屉里放着袜子和一小盒袖扣。汤姆拿起一枚袖扣，翻过来看了看，然后又放了回去。他拿起一件衬衫，看到口袋上有一个模糊的字母组合，首字母是J.H.。汤姆把衬衫叠好放了回去，想着他可能会联系房产中介，看看是否有亲属想要这些衣物。他继续翻找其余的抽屉。

topic: A homeowner discovers previous residents left items in the attic
text_en: When Ben went up to check the insulation, he noticed a cardboard box tucked behind the water heater. Inside were school notebooks, a ceramic mug, and a small wooden box with a latch. He opened the latch and found a stack of letters tied with string. The handwriting was neat, and the envelopes had old postmarks. He read the first few lines of one letter, then put it back. He closed the wooden box and set it on the shelf near the other stored items before heading back down to finish his work.
text_zh: 当本上去检查隔热层时，他注意到热水器后面藏着一个纸板箱。里面装着学校笔记本、一个陶瓷杯子和一个带闩锁的小木盒。他打开闩锁，发现一叠用绳子捆着的信件。字迹工整，信封上有旧邮戳。他读了其中一封信的开头几行，然后把它放了回去。他合上木盒，把它放在架子上的其他储物物品旁边，然后下楼继续干活。

topic: A homeowner discovers previous residents left items in the attic
text_en: Greg entered the attic to locate a box of tax documents he had stored there. He rummaged through labeled plastic bins until he reached one marked "Files." Inside, he found several old ledgers and a stack of bank statements, but they were all from previous owners, not his own records. He looked through the first ledger, seeing columns of numbers and entries about purchases for a household. He realized these might have been left accidentally. He thumbed through a few pages, then closed the ledger and placed it back in the bin. He would set up a box for the previous owners and leave it by the front door for them to collect.
text_zh: 格雷格进入阁楼，想找到他存放在那里的一箱税务文件。他翻遍了贴有标签的塑料箱，直到找到一个标有“文件”的箱子。在里面，他发现了几本旧账本和一叠银行对账单，但这些都是前房主的，不是他自己的记录。他翻看了第一本账本，看到一列列数字和关于家庭采购的记录。他意识到这些可能是被意外留下的。他翻阅了几页，然后合上账本，放回箱子里。他打算为前房主准备一个箱子，放在前门旁边，让他们来取。

topic: A homeowner discovers previous residents left items in the attic
text_en: Jennifer brought a broom and dustpan to the attic, intending to sweep the floor. She noticed a large trunk under a sloped eave. She pulled it out and lifted the latch. Inside, she found a patchwork quilt folded carefully, and beside it a bundle of letters tied with ribbon. She untied the ribbon and read the first letter, which began "Dearest Margaret." The handwriting was careful and formal. Jennifer read a few lines about a train journey and a visit to a cousin. She tucked the letter back in the bundle, retied the ribbon, and left the quilt and letters as she found them. She swept the floor, then closed the trunk.
text_zh: 詹妮弗带着扫帚和簸箕来到阁楼，打算扫地。她注意到倾斜的屋檐下有一个大箱子。她把它拉出来，打开闩锁。里面，她发现一条精心折叠的拼布被子，旁边是一捆用丝带系着的信件。她解开丝带，读了第一封信，信的开头是“亲爱的玛格丽特”。字迹工整而正式。詹妮弗读了几行关于一次火车旅行和拜访表亲的内容。她把信塞回捆里，重新系好丝带，把被子和信件按原样放好。她扫了地，然后合上了箱子。

topic: A homeowner discovers previous residents left items in the attic
text_en: Omar had been meaning to check the attic ever since he moved in. One afternoon, he brought a flashlight and a pair of work gloves. He stepped carefully on the beams, avoiding the insulation. Near the chimney, he found a wooden crate full of vinyl records. He pulled out an album and read the title, a jazz album from the seventies. He set it on the floor and flipped through more records, seeing various genres. A second crate contained a record player, dusty but intact. Omar carried the player down to the living room, thinking he might test it later. He returned for the records and placed them near the player.
text_zh: 奥马尔自从搬进来就一直想去看看阁楼。一天下午，他带了一个手电筒和一副工作手套。他小心地踩在横梁上，避开隔热层。在烟囱附近，他发现了一个装满黑胶唱片的木箱。他抽出一张专辑，读了标题，是一张七十年代的爵士专辑。他把它放在地板上，又翻看了更多唱片，看到了各种流派。第二个箱子里装着一台电唱机，虽然布满灰尘，但完好无损。奥马尔把电唱机搬到客厅，想着稍后可以试试。他又回来拿唱片，把它们放在电唱机旁边。

topic: A homeowner discovers previous residents left items in the attic
text_en: Paula was searching for a spare rug to place in the entryway. She went into the attic and scanned the floor. Under a pile of old blankets, she found a rolled-up area rug. She unrolled it partway and saw a pattern of geometric shapes in muted tones. Underneath the rug lay a stack of framed photographs. Paula picked one up and wiped the dust off the glass, revealing a portrait of a couple in formal attire. Another photo showed a group of children in front of a schoolhouse. She leaned the frames against the wall, thinking they must have belonged to the previous family. She gathered the rug and took it downstairs.
text_zh: 保拉正在寻找一块备用地毯放在门厅。她走进阁楼，扫视了一下地板。在一堆旧毯子下面，她发现了一块卷起的地毯。她展开一部分，看到上面有柔和色调的几何图案。地毯下面放着一叠装裱好的照片。保拉拿起一张，擦去玻璃上的灰尘，露出一对穿着正装的夫妇的肖像。另一张照片显示一群孩子在一所学校前面。她把相框靠在墙上，心想这些一定属于前一个家庭。她收起地毯，把它拿下了楼。

topic: A homeowner discovers previous residents left items in the attic
text_en: Leo climbed into the attic to find his winter coat, which he had packed away in a bin. He shifted several boxes until he found the one marked "Winter." Inside, he discovered a woman's wool coat and a pair of leather boots, items he did not recognize. He pulled the coat out and checked the pockets. In one pocket, he found a grocery list and a receipt from a local store, both dated from several months ago. Leo put them back and hung the coat on a hook near the attic entrance, planning to ask his landlord if they belonged to a previous tenant. He located his own coat underneath.
text_zh: 利奥爬进阁楼去找他的冬衣，他把它打包在一个箱子里。他挪动几个箱子，直到找到标有“冬季”的那个。在里面，他发现了一件女式羊毛外套和一双皮靴，这些物品他都不认识。他把外套拿出来，检查了口袋。在一个口袋里，他发现了一张购物清单和一张当地商店的收据，日期都是几个月前的。利奥把它们放回去，把外套挂在阁楼入口附近的钩子上，打算问房东这些是否属于前一位租户。他在下面找到了自己的外套。

topic: A homeowner discovers previous residents left items in the attic
text_en: Carla decided to organize the attic shelves, which were cluttered with old tools and paint cans. On one shelf, she spotted a cigar box. She opened it and found a collection of smooth stones, each with a name written on it in marker. There must have been a dozen or so, all different names. She lifted one out and read the writing, then placed it back. Next to the stones was a small notebook with a few pages of handwriting, describing a hiking trail and a list of supplies. Carla closed the box and put it back on the shelf. She resumed tidying the other items, leaving the box as it was.
text_zh: 卡拉决定整理阁楼的架子，上面堆满了旧工具和油漆罐。在一个架子上，她发现了一个雪茄盒。她打开它，发现里面有一堆光滑的石头，每块上面都用记号笔写着一个名字。大概有十几块，名字各不相同。她拿起一块，读了上面的字，然后放了回去。石头旁边是一个小笔记本，上面有几页手写的文字，描述了一条徒步路线和一份补给清单。卡拉合上盒子，把它放回架子上。她继续整理其他物品，让盒子保持原样。

topic: A homeowner discovers previous residents left items in the attic
text_en: Ben pulled down the attic stairs and went up, looking for an old backpack. He checked behind a stack of cardboard boxes and found a duffel bag. Unzipping it, he saw a collection of cassette tapes, each labeled with a band name and a date. He picked one up and turned it over, reading the track list on the case insert. Some of the labels were written in a neat hand, others in a scrawl. Ben slid the tape back into the bag and zipped it shut. He put the bag on a shelf, thinking he might mention it to the previous owner if he saw them at the annual neighborhood garage sale.
text_zh: 本拉下阁楼楼梯，走上去，寻找一个旧背包。他检查了一堆纸板箱后面，发现了一个行李袋。拉开拉链，他看到一堆盒式磁带，每盘都标有乐队名称和日期。他拿起一盘，翻过来，读了盒内插页上的曲目列表。有些标签字迹工整，有些则潦草。本把磁带放回袋子里，拉上拉链。他把袋子放在架子上，想着如果他在一年一度的邻里旧货出售会上见到前房主，可能会提一下这件事。

topic: A homeowner discovers previous residents left items in the attic
text_en: Angela went into the attic to retrieve a box of books she had stored there. She found the box near the far wall, but next to it sat a small, locked chest. She tried the lid, but it wouldn't open. She looked around the attic for a key, checking the pockets of an old coat and a drawer in a filing cabinet. She found a set of small keys on a ring. She tried them one by one until the lock clicked. Inside, she found a collection of handwritten recipes, a few sepia-toned photographs, and a piece of lace folded in a handkerchief. Angela looked at the photographs, then closed the chest and took it to the kitchen to show her husband.
text_zh: 安吉拉走进阁楼，去取她存放在那里的一箱书。她在远墙附近找到了箱子，但旁边放着一个小型上锁的箱子。她试着打开盖子，但打不开。她在阁楼里寻找钥匙，检查了一件旧外套的口袋和文件柜的一个抽屉。她找到了一串小钥匙。她一把一把地试，直到锁咔哒一声打开。里面，她发现了一叠手写食谱、几张棕褐色调的照片，以及一块叠在手帕里的蕾丝。安吉拉看了看照片，然后合上箱子，把它拿到厨房给丈夫看。

topic: Someone finds an unsigned birthday card in their mailbox
text_en: Maya sorted through the mail on her way inside, bills and catalogs in one hand. At the bottom was a birthday card, the envelope plain and unmarked. She opened it while standing in the hallway. The front had a generic floral design, and inside was a handwritten message wishing her a good birthday. There was no signature. She flipped the card over, checked the envelope again, but found no clue. She set it on the kitchen counter beside her keys and began opening the rest of the mail. Later, she moved it to a drawer with other cards.
text_zh: 玛雅在进屋的路上整理邮件，一手拿着账单和目录。最下面是一张生日贺卡，信封朴素且没有标记。她站在门厅里打开了它。正面是普通的鲜花图案，里面有一条手写的祝福她生日快乐的信息。没有签名。她把贺卡翻过来，又检查了一遍信封，但没有找到任何线索。她把它放在厨房台面上，旁边是她的钥匙，然后开始打开其余的邮件。后来，她把它和其他卡片一起放进了抽屉。

topic: Someone finds an unsigned birthday card in their mailbox
text_en: After bringing in the mail, Tom noticed a single card among the envelopes. It was addressed to him, but there was no return address. He opened it while walking to the living room. The card had a picture of a birthday cake and a simple message inside. He checked the signature line, but it was blank. He looked at the postmark, but it was smudged. He set the card on the coffee table and picked up the newspaper. He thought about calling his sister, but he wasn't sure if she had sent it. He left it on the table and went to make lunch.
text_zh: 汤姆取回邮件后，注意到信封中有一张单独的贺卡。它是寄给他的，但没有回信地址。他一边走向客厅一边打开它。贺卡上有一张生日蛋糕的图片，里面有一条简单的信息。他检查了签名栏，但那里是空白的。他看了看邮戳，但已经模糊不清了。他把贺卡放在咖啡桌上，拿起了报纸。他想过给他姐姐打电话，但不确定是不是她寄的。他把它留在桌子上，去做午饭了。

topic: Someone finds an unsigned birthday card in their mailbox
text_en: Ben found the card wedged between a utility bill and a grocery flyer. The envelope had his name and address in neat cursive, but no return address. He opened it at the kitchen table, reading the standard birthday greeting and a line about hoping he had a nice day. No name at the bottom. He turned the card over, then looked inside the envelope once more. He placed it on the table and finished sorting the rest of the mail, then left it there while he went to make lunch.
text_zh: 本发现那张贺卡夹在了一张水电费账单和一张杂货店传单之间。信封上有他名字和地址，字迹是整齐的草书，但没有回信地址。他在厨房桌子上打开了它，读着标准的生日祝福和一句希望他今天过得愉快的话。底部没有名字。他把贺卡翻过来，然后又往信封里看了一眼。他把它放在桌子上，整理完其余的邮件，然后把它留在那里，去做午饭了。

topic: Someone finds an unsigned birthday card in their mailbox
text_en: Marta pulled the mail from the box, noticing a card with no return address among the bills. She opened it in the kitchen, reading a generic birthday message signed only with a looping initial. She flipped it over, checking for a name, but the envelope was blank. She set it on the counter, thinking it might be from a neighbor or a coworker who forgot to sign it. After a moment, she placed it on the fridge with a magnet, deciding she'd ask around later. Then she went back to sorting the rest of the mail.
text_zh: 玛尔塔从信箱里取出邮件，在账单中注意到一张没有回信地址的贺卡。她在厨房里打开了它，读着一条普通的生日祝福，只签了一个潦草的首字母。她把它翻过来，寻找名字，但信封是空白的。她把它放在台面上，想着可能是哪位邻居或同事忘记签名了。过了一会儿，她用磁铁把它贴在冰箱上，决定稍后再去问问。然后她又回去整理其余的邮件了。

topic: Someone finds an unsigned birthday card in their mailbox
text_en: Mara collected the mail from the box at the end of her driveway, sorting through bills and a catalog until she noticed a cream-colored envelope with no return address. Inside was a card with a simple floral design on the front. The message read, "Hope your day is as lovely as you are," but there was no signature. She turned it over, checking for any hidden writing, then set it on the kitchen counter beside the fruit bowl. She wondered who might have sent it, but her mind soon drifted to the laundry that needed folding. The card remained there for the rest of the afternoon.
text_zh: 玛拉从车道尽头的信箱里取回邮件，在账单和一份目录中翻找，直到她注意到一个奶油色的信封，没有回信地址。里面是一张贺卡，正面有简单的花卉图案。信息写着：“希望你今天过得和你一样可爱”，但没有签名。她把它翻过来，检查是否有任何隐藏的文字，然后把它放在厨房台面上，水果碗旁边。她想知道是谁寄来的，但她的思绪很快就飘到了需要叠的衣物上。那张贺卡整个下午都留在那里。

topic: Someone finds an unsigned birthday card in their mailbox
text_en: After unlocking the front door, Leo flipped through the stack of envelopes in his hand. A small card with a watercolor sunset on the front caught his attention. He opened it while walking to the living room. The inside read, "Wishing you a wonderful birthday," with no name attached. He checked the postmark, which was local, but that offered no clues. He placed the card on the coffee table and went to the kitchen to start dinner. Later, he noticed it again and thought about asking his neighbors, but decided it wasn't worth the effort.
text_zh: 利奥打开前门后，翻看着手里的一叠信封。一张正面印有水彩日落的小贺卡引起了他的注意。他一边走向客厅一边打开它。里面写着：“祝你生日快乐”，没有署名。他检查了邮戳，是本地的，但这并没有提供什么线索。他把贺卡放在咖啡桌上，去厨房开始做晚饭。后来，他又注意到了它，想过去问问邻居，但觉得不值得费那个劲。

topic: Someone finds an unsigned birthday card in their mailbox
text_en: Marta sorted the mail on the kitchen counter, bills and flyers going into separate piles. At the bottom was a card in a cream envelope with her name written in neat, unfamiliar handwriting. There was no return address. She opened it and found a simple birthday greeting, signed only with a small drawing of a flower. She turned the card over, checked the envelope again, and set it on the windowsill. Later, she mentioned it to her neighbor while watering the plants. The neighbor had no idea who sent it. Marta shrugged and put the card on the shelf with the others.
text_zh: 玛尔塔在厨房台面上整理邮件，账单和传单分成几堆。最下面是一张装在奶油色信封里的贺卡，上面用整齐而陌生的笔迹写着她的名字。没有回信地址。她打开它，发现是一句简单的生日祝福，只签了一个小花的小图案。她翻过贺卡，又检查了一遍信封，然后把它放在窗台上。后来，她在浇花时向邻居提起了这件事。邻居也不知道是谁寄来的。玛尔塔耸耸肩，把贺卡和其他卡片一起放在了架子上。

topic: Someone finds an unsigned birthday card in their mailbox
text_en: Tom walked back from the mailbox, the mail held loosely in his hand. Among the usual flyers was a bright yellow envelope. He opened it there on the porch. The card had a cartoon balloon on the front and read, "Another year older, another year better!" with no signature. He flipped through the envelope for any other clue, but there was nothing. He tucked the card under his arm and went inside, setting it on the bookshelf. He wondered if his sister had sent it, but she usually signed her cards. He continued with his afternoon chores.
text_zh: 汤姆从信箱走回来，手里松松地拿着邮件。在常见的传单中，有一个亮黄色的信封。他在门廊上就打开了它。贺卡正面有一个卡通气球，上面写着：“又长一岁，更好一岁！”没有签名。他在信封里翻了翻，寻找其他线索，但什么也没有。他把贺卡夹在胳膊下，走进屋里，把它放在书架上。他想知道是不是他姐姐寄的，但她通常会在卡片上签名。他继续做下午的家务。

topic: Someone finds an unsigned birthday card in their mailbox
text_en: Rebecca was getting the mail when she saw a card with her name written in a neat hand. She opened it right at the mailbox. The card had a picture of a cup of coffee. Inside, it said, "Hope your birthday is as good as a fresh cup of coffee." No signature. She looked around the street, but there was no one there. She put the card in her bag and walked back to her house. She set it on the table by the door, next to her keys, and went to get a glass of water.
text_zh: 丽贝卡正在取邮件，看到一张写着她名字、字迹工整的贺卡。她就在信箱旁打开了它。贺卡上有一杯咖啡的图片。里面写着：“希望你生日像一杯新鲜咖啡一样美好。”没有签名。她环顾了一下街道，但那里没有人。她把贺卡放进包里，走回了家。她把它放在门口的桌子上，紧挨着她的钥匙，然后去拿了一杯水。

topic: Someone finds an unsigned birthday card in their mailbox
text_en: Nina collected the mail from the box and noticed a pastel envelope with no return address. She opened it while waiting for the kettle to boil. The card showed a bouquet of wildflowers, and the inside read, "Thinking of you on your birthday." There was no name. She examined the handwriting, which seemed neat but unfamiliar. She placed the card on the windowsill above the sink. As she poured her tea, she considered whether it might be from a coworker or a distant relative. She made a mental note to mention it to her partner later, but then got caught up in a phone call.
text_zh: 妮娜从信箱里取出邮件，注意到一个没有回信地址的淡色信封。她在等水壶烧开时打开了它。贺卡上是一束野花，里面写着：“在你生日时想念你。”没有名字。她仔细看了看笔迹，似乎很工整但并不熟悉。她把贺卡放在水槽上方的窗台上。倒茶时，她考虑着是否可能是同事或远房亲戚寄来的。她默默记下稍后要和伴侣提一下，但随后就忙于接电话了。

topic: Someone finds an unsigned birthday card in their mailbox
text_en: After work, Daniel collected his mail from the lobby box. Among the usual envelopes was a thick, cream-colored card with his name in cursive. No stamp, no postmark, no return address. He opened it in the elevator. Inside was a birthday message and a hand-drawn star. He didn't recognize the handwriting. At home, he placed it on the table and asked his roommate if he knew anything. His roommate didn't. Daniel left the card on the table and went to make dinner, glancing at it once more before turning on the stove.
text_zh: 下班后，丹尼尔从大厅信箱里取了他的邮件。在平常的信封中，有一张厚实的奶油色卡片，上面用草书写着他的名字。没有邮票，没有邮戳，没有回信地址。他在电梯里打开了它。里面是一条生日祝福和一颗手绘的星星。他不认识那笔迹。回到家，他把卡片放在桌子上，问室友是否知道什么。室友不知道。丹尼尔把卡片留在桌子上，去做晚饭，在打开炉子前又瞥了它一眼。

topic: Someone finds an unsigned birthday card in their mailbox
text_en: Alicia brought the mail inside and set it on the kitchen table. A card with a pastel envelope stood out among the bills. She opened it, finding a picture of a birthday cake with candles. The message read, "Wishing you all the best on your special day," but there was no signature. She turned the card over and looked at the back, but it was blank. She placed it on the fridge with a magnet. As she started preparing lunch, she thought about her friends and family, trying to recall if anyone had mentioned sending something. She decided she might ask about it later.
text_zh: 艾丽西娅把邮件拿进屋里，放在厨房桌子上。一张淡彩色信封的卡片在账单中格外显眼。她打开它，发现里面是一张画着蜡烛的生日蛋糕的图片。信息上写着：“祝你在这个特别的日子里一切顺利，”但没有签名。她把卡片翻过来看背面，但背面是空白的。她用磁铁把它贴在冰箱上。当她开始准备午餐时，她想着她的朋友和家人，试图回忆是否有人提到过寄了什么东西。她决定稍后可能会问一下这件事。

topic: Someone finds an unsigned birthday card in their mailbox
text_en: Lena sorted through the stack of mail on the kitchen counter—bills, a catalog, a postcard from her dentist. At the bottom was a small white envelope with no return address, just her name in neat handwriting. She slid her finger under the flap and pulled out a card with a simple flower illustration on the front. Inside, a short message wished her a good birthday. She checked the signature line; it was blank. Lena turned the envelope over, looking for any clue. She set it by her keys and finished reviewing the rest of the mail, then later took the card upstairs to her desk.
text_zh: 莉娜在厨房台面上整理着那堆邮件——账单、一本目录、一张牙医寄来的明信片。最底下是一个白色的小信封，没有回信地址，只有她名字的整齐笔迹。她用指头滑过封口，抽出一张正面有简单花朵插图的卡片。里面，一条简短的留言祝她生日快乐。她检查了签名栏；是空白的。莉娜把信封翻过来，寻找任何线索。她把它放在钥匙旁边，继续查看其余的邮件，然后后来把卡片拿到楼上的书桌上。

topic: Someone finds an unsigned birthday card in their mailbox
text_en: Tom picked up his mail and noticed a small card with his name on it. He opened it right there by the curb. It had a picture of a balloon and a handwritten note wishing him well on his birthday. There was no signature, just a squiggle. He looked around the street, but no one was nearby. He took the card inside and put it on the counter. He asked his wife if she had put it there. She hadn't. Tom shrugged, placed it in the drawer with other cards, and went to check on the laundry.
text_zh: 汤姆拿起他的邮件，注意到一张上面有他名字的小卡片。他就在路边打开了它。上面有一张气球的图片和一张手写的便条，祝他生日快乐。没有签名，只有一个潦草的笔迹。他环顾街道，但附近没有人。他把卡片拿进屋里，放在柜台上。他问他妻子是否把它放在那里。她没有。汤姆耸耸肩，把它和其他卡片一起放进抽屉里，然后去查看洗衣情况。

topic: Someone finds an unsigned birthday card in their mailbox
text_en: Jordan came back from the mailbox, flipping through the envelopes. One with a floral pattern caught his eye. He opened it in the kitchen. The card had a message that read, "Wishing you a day filled with laughter and love," but no signature. He checked the envelope again, but there was nothing to identify the sender. He placed the card on the counter and continued with his morning routine, making coffee and checking his phone. The card sat there, a small mystery he didn't spend much time on, but he didn't throw it away either.
text_zh: 乔丹从邮箱回来，翻着信封。一个带有花卉图案的信封引起了他的注意。他在厨房里打开了它。卡片上有一条信息，写着：“祝你充满欢笑和爱的一天，”但没有签名。他又检查了信封，但没有任何能识别寄件人的信息。他把卡片放在柜台上，继续他的早晨例行公事，煮咖啡，看手机。卡片就放在那里，一个小谜团，他没有花太多时间，但也没有扔掉它。

topic: Someone finds an unsigned birthday card in their mailbox
text_en: Elena collected the mail from her front porch. A plain white envelope with her name printed in block letters caught her eye. She opened it in the kitchen. Inside was a birthday card with a cartoon cat and a message that read "Have a great day!" It was unsigned. She looked at the envelope again, but there was no clue. She set the card on the fridge and mentioned it to her brother on the phone later. He said he hadn't sent it. Elena left it there and went to water her plants.
text_zh: 埃琳娜从前门廊取了邮件。一个上面用印刷体写着她的名字的白色信封引起了她的注意。她在厨房里打开了它。里面是一张生日卡片，上面有一只卡通猫，信息写着“祝你今天愉快！”没有签名。她又看了看信封，但没有任何线索。她把卡片放在冰箱上，后来在电话里向她的哥哥提起了这件事。他说他没有寄。埃琳娜把它留在那里，去给她的植物浇水。

topic: Someone finds an unsigned birthday card in their mailbox
text_en: Marcus sorted through his mail in the hallway. There was a small envelope with his name written in pencil. He opened it and found a birthday card with a simple design of balloons and confetti. The message was short: "Wishing you a good one." There was no signature. He looked at the back of the card, but it was blank. He put it back in the envelope and placed it on the table. Later, he asked his coworker if she had sent anything. She said no. He left the card on the table and went to bed.
text_zh: 马库斯在走廊里整理他的邮件。有一个小信封，上面用铅笔写着他的名字。他打开它，发现一张生日卡片，上面有简单的气球和五彩纸屑的设计。信息很短：“祝你过得好。”没有签名。他看了看卡片的背面，但它是空白的。他把它放回信封里，放在桌子上。后来，他问他的同事是否寄了什么东西。她说没有。他把卡片留在桌子上，去睡觉了。

topic: Someone finds an unsigned birthday card in their mailbox
text_en: Aisha found the card in her mailbox after returning from work. The envelope was light blue, with her name written in a loopy script. Inside was a birthday greeting with a picture of a cake. It was unsigned. She looked at the envelope for a return address, but there was none. She brought it inside and placed it on the coffee table. She asked her friend who was visiting if she knew anything about it. Her friend didn't. Aisha put the card on the shelf and sat down to watch TV.
text_zh: 艾莎下班回来后，在邮箱里发现了那张卡片。信封是浅蓝色的，上面用潦草的笔迹写着她的名字。里面是一张生日祝福，有一张蛋糕的图片。没有签名。她看了看信封，找回信地址，但没有。她把它带进屋里，放在咖啡桌上。她问来访的朋友是否知道这件事。她的朋友不知道。艾莎把卡片放在架子上，坐下来看电视。

topic: Someone finds an unsigned birthday card in their mailbox
text_en: Greg collected his mail and noticed a small envelope with his name on it. He opened it in the garage. The card inside had a picture of a sailboat and a message saying "Hope your day goes well." There was no signature. He checked the envelope again, but it was plain white with no postmark. He put the card on the workbench and continued sorting his tools. Later, he asked his sister if she had sent it. She said she hadn't. Greg left the card on the workbench and went inside for lunch.
text_zh: 格雷格收集了他的邮件，注意到一个小信封，上面有他的名字。他在车库里打开了它。里面的卡片上有一张帆船的图片，信息说“希望你今天过得好。”没有签名。他又检查了信封，但它是纯白色的，没有邮戳。他把卡片放在工作台上，继续整理他的工具。后来，他问他姐姐是否寄了它。她说她没有。格雷格把卡片留在工作台上，进去吃午饭。

topic: Someone finds an unsigned birthday card in their mailbox
text_en: Nora picked up her mail and saw a small, square envelope with her name written in red ink. She opened it while walking back to her apartment. The card inside had a picture of a sunflower and a note that said "Thinking of you on your birthday." It wasn't signed. She looked at the envelope again, but there was no clue. She placed the card on her desk and continued unpacking groceries. Later, she mentioned it to her mother on the phone. Her mother hadn't sent it. Nora left the card on the desk and finished putting away the food.
text_zh: 诺拉拿起她的邮件，看到一个小方形的信封，上面用红墨水写着她的名字。她走回公寓时打开了它。里面的卡片上有一朵向日葵的图片和一张便条，写着“在你生日时想着你。”没有签名。她又看了看信封，但没有任何线索。她把卡片放在书桌上，继续整理杂货。后来，她在电话里向她的母亲提起了这件事。她的母亲没有寄。诺拉把卡片留在书桌上，把食物收好。

topic: Someone discovers a hidden room in their new house
text_en: Maya was unpacking boxes in the hallway when she noticed a small seam in the wallpaper. She pressed on it, and a section of the wall swung inward, revealing a narrow staircase. She flicked on her phone's light and stepped down into a dusty room with old wooden shelves. The shelves held jars of preserved fruit and a stack of letters tied with twine. She picked up one letter and saw it was addressed to a woman she didn't recognize. Maya set the letter back and walked upstairs to continue unpacking, leaving the door ajar.
text_zh: 玛雅正在走廊里拆箱时，注意到墙纸上有一条细缝。她按了一下，墙壁的一部分向内转动，露出一段狭窄的楼梯。她打开手机的手电筒，走下楼梯，进入一个布满灰尘的房间，里面有旧木架子。架子上放着几罐腌制水果和一叠用细绳捆着的信。她拿起一封信，看到收信人是一位她不认识的女人。玛雅把信放回去，走上楼继续拆箱，让那扇门半开着。

topic: Someone discovers a hidden room in their new house
text_en: When Mia moved into the old craftsman house, she spent her first weekend cleaning. In the hallway closet, behind a stack of paint cans, she noticed a small seam in the wall. Pressing on it, a panel gave way, revealing a narrow staircase leading down. She grabbed her phone for light and descended. The room was dusty, filled with old wooden crates and a workbench. A few tools lay rusted on the surface. She ran her hand along the bench, leaving a trail in the dust. After a few minutes, she went back upstairs, leaving the panel open for now.
text_zh: 米娅搬进那栋老式工匠风格的房子后，第一个周末都在打扫。在走廊的壁橱里，在一堆油漆罐后面，她注意到墙上有一条细缝。她按了一下，一块镶板松开了，露出一段通往下面的狭窄楼梯。她拿起手机照明，走了下去。房间里布满灰尘，堆满了旧木箱和一张工作台。台面上放着几件生锈的工具。她用手沿着工作台摸了一下，在灰尘中留下了一道痕迹。几分钟后，她回到楼上，暂时让那块镶板开着。

topic: Someone discovers a hidden room in their new house
text_en: Elena was cleaning the pantry when she found a false back behind a shelf. She pulled it away and discovered a narrow room with a low ceiling. It contained an old desk and a chair. On the desk was a ledger with handwritten entries and a brass key. Elena opened the ledger and saw dates and names, but she didn't recognize any of them. She closed the ledger and placed the key on top. She left the room and went back to cleaning the pantry, leaving the false back open.
text_zh: 埃琳娜正在清理食品储藏室时，发现一个架子后面有一个假背板。她把它拉开，发现了一个天花板很低的狭窄房间。里面有一张旧书桌和一把椅子。书桌上放着一本手写账本和一把黄铜钥匙。埃琳娜打开账本，看到了日期和名字，但她一个也不认识。她合上账本，把钥匙放在上面。她离开房间，回去继续清理食品储藏室，让假背板开着。

topic: Someone discovers a hidden room in their new house
text_en: Ethan had just unpacked the last box in his new apartment. While adjusting a bookshelf, he noticed the back wall didn't quite meet the floor. He knelt and found a loose baseboard. Pulling it aside, he saw a small crawlspace. He crawled in with a flashlight, finding a tiny room with a single chair and a stack of old newspapers. The air was stale. He picked up one paper, the date from decades ago. He put it back and crawled out, brushing dust off his knees. He replaced the baseboard loosely, planning to check the rest of the space later.
text_zh: 伊桑刚在新公寓里拆完最后一个箱子。在调整书架时，他注意到后墙和地板之间没有完全贴合。他跪下来，发现了一块松动的踢脚板。他把它拉开，看到了一个小爬行空间。他用手电筒爬了进去，发现了一个小房间，里面有一把椅子和一叠旧报纸。空气很闷。他拿起一份报纸，日期是几十年前的。他把它放回去，爬了出来，拍掉膝盖上的灰尘。他松松地装回踢脚板，打算稍后检查其余空间。

topic: Someone discovers a hidden room in their new house
text_en: Nina was exploring the basement of her new house when she noticed a brick that was slightly different in color. She tapped it, and it moved. She pulled it out, revealing a small keyhole. After searching, she found a key hanging on a nail nearby. She inserted it and a section of the wall swung open, revealing a small room with shelves lined with jars of preserved fruits and vegetables. Labels with faded handwriting covered them. She stepped inside, the floor creaking under her. After a moment, she closed the door and went back upstairs to finish unpacking.
text_zh: 尼娜正在探索新房子的地下室时，注意到一块颜色略有不同的砖。她敲了敲，它动了。她把它拉出来，露出一个小钥匙孔。经过一番搜寻，她发现附近钉子上挂着一把钥匙。她把它插进去，墙壁的一部分打开了，露出一个小房间，架子上摆满了装着腌制水果和蔬菜的罐子。标签上的字迹已经褪色。她走进去，地板在她脚下吱吱作响。过了一会儿，她关上门，回到楼上继续拆箱。

topic: Someone discovers a hidden room in their new house
text_en: As Tom was hanging a picture in the living room, his drill hit something solid behind the drywall. He cut a small hole and peered in, finding a wooden door frame. He widened the opening and discovered a door. It opened into a small room with a built-in desk and a typewriter. The desk had some papers, yellowed with age. He read a few lines—notes about a garden. The room smelled of old paper and dust. He left the door open and continued with his picture, deciding to sort through the papers another day.
text_zh: 汤姆正在客厅挂画时，他的钻头碰到了干墙后面的某个坚硬物体。他切了一个小洞，往里看，发现了一个木门框。他扩大了开口，发现了一扇门。门通向一个小房间，里面有嵌入式书桌和一台打字机。书桌上放着一些泛黄的纸张。他读了几行——是关于花园的笔记。房间里弥漫着旧纸和灰尘的气味。他让门开着，继续挂画，决定改天再整理那些纸张。

topic: Someone discovers a hidden room in their new house
text_en: While cleaning out the attic of her new house, Priya moved a stack of old suitcases and noticed a trapdoor in the floor. She lifted it, revealing a ladder leading down. She climbed into a small, finished space with a bed and a nightstand. A lamp sat on the nightstand, unplugged. She plugged it in and turned it on, casting a warm glow. The room felt lived-in, with a few books on the floor. She sat on the bed for a moment, then climbed back up, leaving the trapdoor open.
text_zh: 普里亚在打扫新房子的阁楼时，挪开了一堆旧行李箱，注意到地板上有扇活板门。她把它掀开，露出一架通往下面的梯子。她爬进了一个小而装修过的空间，里面有一张床和一个床头柜。床头柜上放着一盏台灯，没有插电。她插上电源，打开灯，发出温暖的光芒。房间感觉有人住过，地板上有几本书。她在床上坐了一会儿，然后爬了上去，让活板门开着。

topic: Someone discovers a hidden room in their new house
text_en: Marcus was checking the water heater in the utility closet when he noticed a small door at the back, almost hidden by pipes. He squeezed past them and turned the knob. The door opened into a narrow room with a workbench and a pegboard covered in tools. A half-finished wooden chair sat in the corner, clamped to the bench. Dust covered everything. He picked up a chisel and examined it, then set it down. He closed the door and went back to his original task, making a mental note to explore further.
text_zh: 马库斯正在杂物间检查热水器时，注意到后面有一扇小门，几乎被管道遮住了。他挤过管道，转动了门把手。门通向一个狭窄的房间，里面有一张工作台和一个挂满工具的钉板。角落里放着一把半成品木椅，被夹在工作台上。所有东西都覆盖着灰尘。他拿起一把凿子检查了一下，然后放下。他关上门，回到原来的任务，心里记着要再探索一下。

topic: Someone discovers a hidden room in their new house
text_en: Maya was unpacking boxes in the bedroom of her new house when she noticed a small seam in the wall behind the closet. She ran her fingers along it and felt a slight give. With a bit of effort, she pushed, and a narrow door swung open, revealing a dusty staircase leading down. She hesitated, then grabbed a flashlight from her bag. The stairs creaked under her weight. At the bottom, she found a small room with old shelves lined with jars and a worn wooden table. She picked up a jar, wiped it clean, and set it back down. Then she climbed upstairs to continue unpacking.
text_zh: 玛雅正在新房子的卧室里拆箱时，注意到壁橱后面的墙上有一条细缝。她用手指沿着它摸了一下，感觉有点松动。她稍微用力一推，一扇窄门打开了，露出一段布满灰尘的楼梯，通往下面。她犹豫了一下，然后从包里拿出手电筒。楼梯在她的重量下吱吱作响。在底部，她发现了一个小房间，旧架子上摆满了罐子，还有一张破旧的木桌。她拿起一个罐子，擦干净，然后放回去。然后她爬上楼继续拆箱。

topic: Someone discovers a hidden room in their new house
text_en: Liam was installing a shelf in the bedroom closet when he noticed a seam in the wall. He ran his fingers along it and found a latch. He lifted it, and a small door swung open. Inside was a narrow space with a few hooks and a shelf. On the shelf sat a box of old photographs. He picked one up—a family picnic from long ago. He flipped through a few more, then placed them back. He closed the door and finished installing the shelf, leaving the latch as it was.
text_zh: 利亚姆正在卧室壁橱里安装搁板时，注意到墙上有一条缝。他沿着它摸了摸，找到了一个闩锁。他抬起它，一扇小门打开了。里面是一个狭窄的空间，有几个挂钩和一个架子。架子上放着一盒旧照片。他拿起一张——很久以前的一次家庭野餐。他又翻了几张，然后放了回去。他关上门，继续安装搁板，让闩锁保持原样。

topic: Someone discovers a hidden room in their new house
text_en: Ethan had just moved into the old house on Elm Street. While hanging a picture in the hallway, he knocked on the wall and heard a hollow sound. He tapped around until he found a loose panel. Pulling it aside, he discovered a small, dark space behind it. Inside were a few dusty books and a faded photograph. He took the photo out to look at it, then placed it back carefully. He slid the panel closed, making sure it fit snugly, and went back to hanging his picture. The hallway looked the same as before, but he knew what was behind the wall now.
text_zh: 伊桑刚搬进榆树街的那栋老房子。在走廊挂画时，他敲了敲墙，听到空洞的声音。他四处敲击，直到发现一块松动的镶板。他将其拉开，发现后面有一个狭小、黑暗的空间。里面有几本落满灰尘的书和一张褪色的照片。他拿出照片看了看，然后小心地放回去。他滑上镶板，确保它严丝合缝，然后回去继续挂画。走廊看起来和以前一样，但他现在知道墙后面有什么了。

topic: Someone discovers a hidden room in their new house
text_en: When Ben moved into the ranch house, he noticed a strange bump in the hallway floor. He pulled up the carpet and found a wooden plug. He removed it, revealing a small compartment. Inside was a rolled-up blueprint and a key. The blueprint showed a room not on the current floor plan. He searched the walls and found a hidden door in the study, unlocked with the key. It led to a small office with a desk and a filing cabinet. He opened a drawer, finding old receipts. He closed it and left the door ajar.
text_zh: 本搬进牧场式住宅时，注意到走廊地板有一处奇怪的凸起。他掀起地毯，发现一个木塞。他将其取下，露出一个小隔间。里面有一卷蓝图和一把钥匙。蓝图显示了一个当前平面图上没有的房间。他搜查了墙壁，在书房发现了一扇隐藏的门，用钥匙打开了。门后是一间小办公室，里面有一张桌子和一个文件柜。他打开一个抽屉，发现了一些旧收据。他关上抽屉，让门半开着。

topic: Someone discovers a hidden room in their new house
text_en: When Rachel bought the house, the realtor mentioned it had been renovated several times. She didn't think much of it until she noticed a draft coming from under the stairs. She knelt down and saw a small, almost invisible door. It was painted to match the wall. She pulled it open and found a crawl space filled with old boxes and a bicycle with flat tires. She crawled in a little way, touching the dusty boxes, then backed out. She closed the door and stood up, brushing off her knees. She made a mental note to go through the boxes later.
text_zh: 瑞秋买下这栋房子时，房地产经纪人提到它已经翻新过好几次了。她没太在意，直到她注意到楼梯下方有股穿堂风。她蹲下身子，看到一扇几乎看不见的小门。门被漆成与墙壁相匹配的颜色。她拉开门，发现一个爬行空间，里面堆满了旧箱子，还有一辆轮胎瘪了的自行车。她稍微爬进去一点，摸了摸那些布满灰尘的箱子，然后退了出来。她关上门，站起来，拍了拍膝盖上的灰尘。她心里记下稍后要翻看那些箱子。

topic: Someone discovers a hidden room in their new house
text_en: After moving into the cottage, Daniel was exploring the basement when he noticed a brick that seemed slightly out of place. He pressed it, and a section of the wall slid back, revealing a small room. It was empty except for a single chair and a stack of old newspapers on the floor. He stepped inside and looked around, then picked up one of the newspapers and glanced at the date. He put it back and walked out, leaving the secret door open for a moment before pushing it shut. He went upstairs to make a phone call about the house's history.
text_zh: 搬进小屋后，丹尼尔正在探索地下室，这时他注意到一块砖似乎有点错位。他按了一下，墙壁的一部分滑开，露出一个小房间。房间里空荡荡的，只有一把椅子和地板上的一叠旧报纸。他走进去环顾四周，然后拿起其中一份报纸，瞥了一眼日期。他把它放回去，走了出去，让那扇暗门开了一会儿，然后才把它推上。他上楼去打电话询问这栋房子的历史。

topic: Someone discovers a hidden room in their new house
text_en: Laura was cleaning the spare bedroom when she noticed the floorboards near the window were loose. She pried one up and found a shallow compartment beneath it. Inside was a metal box with a rusted latch. She lifted the box out and set it on the bed. The latch opened with a little effort, revealing old letters tied with string and a small key. She untied the string and read the first letter, then retied it and placed the box back in the compartment. She replaced the floorboard, making sure it was level, and continued dusting the room.
text_zh: 劳拉正在打扫客房，这时她注意到窗户附近的地板条松动了。她撬起一块，发现下面有一个浅隔间。里面有一个金属盒子，带有一个生锈的闩锁。她把盒子拿出来，放在床上。闩锁稍微用点力就打开了，露出用绳子捆着的旧信和一把小钥匙。她解开绳子，读了第一封信，然后重新系好，把盒子放回隔间。她放回地板条，确保它平整，然后继续打扫房间。

topic: Someone discovers a hidden room in their new house
text_en: Tom was inspecting the attic of his new house when he noticed a small door in the far corner, half-hidden behind a stack of boxes. He moved the boxes aside and opened the door. Behind it was a narrow passage that led to a tiny room with a slanted ceiling. The room contained a small desk and a lamp. He sat down in the chair for a moment, then got up and looked through the desk drawers. They were empty. He closed the door and went back downstairs to the living room, where he resumed sorting through his moving boxes.
text_zh: 汤姆正在检查新房子的阁楼，这时他注意到远处角落里有一扇小门，半掩在一堆箱子后面。他把箱子移开，打开了门。门后是一条狭窄的通道，通向一个带有倾斜天花板的小房间。房间里有一张小桌子和一盏灯。他在椅子上坐了一会儿，然后站起来，翻了翻书桌抽屉。抽屉是空的。他关上门，回到楼下的客厅，继续整理他的搬家箱子。

topic: Someone discovers a hidden room in their new house
text_en: While painting the living room, Priya noticed a faint outline of a door on the wall. She scraped away some paint and found a handle. She turned it, and the door opened into a small, dark space. She used her phone's flashlight to see. It was a tiny room with a sink and a counter, like an old kitchenette. The faucet was rusty, and the counter was dusty. She touched the sink and then wiped her hand on her jeans. She closed the door and decided to ask the previous owner about it. She picked up her paintbrush and continued painting.
text_zh: 普里亚在粉刷客厅时，注意到墙上有一扇门的模糊轮廓。她刮掉一些油漆，发现了一个把手。她转动把手，门开进一个狭小、黑暗的空间。她用手机的手电筒照亮。那是一个小房间，有水槽和台面，像一个小厨房。水龙头生锈了，台面上积满灰尘。她摸了摸水槽，然后在牛仔裤上擦了擦手。她关上门，决定去问问前房主。她拿起画笔，继续粉刷。

topic: Someone discovers a hidden room in their new house
text_en: Jake was in the garage, looking for a hammer, when he noticed a large cabinet pushed against the back wall. He moved it aside and saw a door behind it. He opened the door and found a small workshop with tools hanging on the walls and a workbench in the center. There was a layer of dust over everything. He picked up a wrench, wiped it off, and put it back. He looked around for a few minutes, then closed the door and pushed the cabinet back into place. He found the hammer on a shelf and went back inside the house.
text_zh: 杰克在车库里找锤子时，注意到一个大柜子靠在后墙上。他把它移到一边，看到后面有一扇门。他打开门，发现一个小工作间，墙上挂着工具，中间有一个工作台。所有东西上都有一层灰尘。他拿起一把扳手，擦干净，然后放了回去。他环顾了几分钟，然后关上门，把柜子推回原位。他在架子上找到了锤子，然后回到了屋里。

topic: Someone discovers a hidden room in their new house
text_en: Sofia was putting away groceries in the pantry when she noticed a small gap in the back panel. She pulled at it, and the panel came off, revealing a narrow staircase. She climbed up and found a small room under the eaves, with a window that looked out over the backyard. The room was mostly empty, except for a small table and a chair. She sat in the chair and looked out the window for a while, then stood up and went back down the stairs. She replaced the panel and finished putting away the groceries.
text_zh: 索菲亚正在食品储藏室里放杂货，这时她注意到后面板有一个小缝隙。她拉了拉，面板脱落，露出一段狭窄的楼梯。她爬上去，发现屋檐下有一个小房间，有一扇窗户，可以俯瞰后院。房间几乎是空的，只有一张小桌子和一把椅子。她在椅子上坐了一会儿，望着窗外，然后站起来，走下楼梯。她放回面板，继续放好杂货。

topic: Someone discovers a hidden room in their new house
text_en: Mark was measuring the walls of the study to plan where to put his bookshelves when he noticed a section of the wall that didn't match the rest. He tapped it, and it sounded different. He pushed on it, and it swung inward. Behind it was a small room with a desk and a chair, and the walls were lined with built-in bookshelves. He stepped inside and ran his hand along the shelves. They were dusty but solid. He walked around the room, then stepped out and closed the door. He continued measuring the outer wall, noting the dimensions on his paper.
text_zh: 马克正在测量书房的墙壁，计划把书架放在哪里，这时他注意到墙壁的一部分与其余部分不匹配。他敲了敲，声音不同。他推了一下，门向内摆开。后面是一个小房间，里面有一张桌子和一把椅子，墙壁上排列着内置书架。他走进去，用手沿着书架划过。书架布满灰尘，但很结实。他在房间里走了一圈，然后走出来，关上门。他继续测量外墙，在纸上记下尺寸。

topic: Two strangers realize they've been dating the same person
text_en: Maya was at the coffee shop when a woman at the next table mentioned Alex's name. She looked over, and the woman smiled. "You know Alex?" Maya asked. The woman nodded. "We've been seeing each other for a few months." Maya stirred her latte, watching the foam swirl. "I've been dating Alex too," she said. They compared details—the same favorite restaurant, the same weekend trips. The woman's phone buzzed; it was Alex texting. Maya pulled out her own phone, showing the same message. They sat in silence, the coffee growing cold between them.
text_zh: 玛雅在咖啡店时，邻桌的一位女士提到了亚历克斯的名字。她看过去，那位女士微笑着。“你认识亚历克斯？”玛雅问。那位女士点点头。“我们交往几个月了。”玛雅搅动着拿铁，看着泡沫旋转。“我也一直在和亚历克斯约会，”她说。她们对比了细节——同样的最喜欢的餐厅，同样的周末旅行。那位女士的手机响了；是亚历克斯发来的短信。玛雅拿出自己的手机，显示着同样的信息。她们沉默地坐着，咖啡在她们之间渐渐变凉。

topic: Two strangers realize they've been dating the same person
text_en: At a friend's barbecue, Liam struck up a conversation with a man holding a burger. They talked about their jobs, their neighborhoods, and eventually, dating. "I'm seeing someone named Casey," the man said. Liam paused, his burger halfway to his mouth. "I'm seeing Casey too." The man laughed, then saw Liam's expression. "Wait, you're serious?" They compared notes—the same apartment building, the same habit of leaving notes. Casey had told each of them they were the only one. They both looked toward the grill, where Casey was laughing with someone else.
text_zh: 在朋友的烧烤聚会上，利亚姆和一个拿着汉堡的男人攀谈起来。他们聊了工作、居住的社区，最后聊到了约会。“我在和一个叫凯西的人约会，”那人说。利亚姆停顿了一下，汉堡举到嘴边。“我也在和凯西约会。”那人笑了，然后看到利亚姆的表情。“等等，你是认真的？”他们对比了信息——同一栋公寓楼，同样留便条的习惯。凯西曾告诉他们每个人，对方是唯一。他们都看向烤架那边，凯西正和别人笑着。

topic: Two strangers realize they've been dating the same person
text_en: Priya was at a bookstore when she overheard a man telling the clerk about a date with someone named Jordan. She recognized the story—the same movie, the same joke. She approached him. "Sorry, but I think we're dating the same person." He looked at her, puzzled. They exchanged details, and it became clear. Jordan had been seeing both of them. Priya put back the book she was holding. "Well," she said, "that explains some things." The man nodded, and they stood in the aisle, neither knowing what to say next.
text_zh: 普里亚在书店时，无意中听到一个男人对店员说起和一个叫乔丹的人约会的事。她认出了那个故事——同一部电影，同一个笑话。她走近他。“抱歉，但我想我们在和同一个人约会。”他困惑地看着她。他们交换了细节，事情变得清楚了。乔丹一直在同时和他们两人约会。普里亚把手里拿的书放回去。“嗯，”她说，“这解释了一些事情。”男人点点头，他们站在过道里，都不知道接下来该说什么。

topic: Two strangers realize they've been dating the same person
text_en: At the farmers market, Dana stopped at a stall selling handmade pottery. A woman beside her picked up the same glazed mug. They laughed, and Dana noticed the woman's bracelet—a silver chain with a tiny compass charm, identical to the one her boyfriend Mark wore. "Where did you get that?" Dana asked. The woman smiled. "My boyfriend gave it to me. He travels a lot for work." Dana's stomach tightened. "Mark?" The woman's smile faded. "You know Mark?" They stared at each other, the mug forgotten between them, as the market bustled on around them.
text_zh: 在农贸市场，达娜在一个卖手工陶器的摊位前停下。她旁边的女人拿起同一个釉面马克杯。她们笑了，达娜注意到那女人的手镯——一条银色链子，带着一个小小的指南针吊坠，和她男朋友马克戴的一模一样。“你从哪里得到的？”达娜问。那女人微笑着。“我男朋友给我的。他经常出差。”达娜的胃一紧。“马克？”那女人的笑容消失了。“你认识马克？”她们互相盯着对方，马克杯被遗忘在她们之间，市场在她们周围熙熙攘攘。

topic: Two strangers realize they've been dating the same person
text_en: Jonas was waiting for his takeout when a man he didn't recognize sat across from him. "You're Jonas, right? I'm Marcus. We need to talk about Dana." Jonas frowned. "Dana?" Marcus nodded. "My girlfriend. Or so I thought. She mentioned you, said you were just a friend from work." Jonas felt a strange heaviness in his chest. He had been seeing Dana for several weeks. She had told him she was single. Marcus sighed, rubbing his forehead. "I guess we've both been fooled." Jonas looked at his takeout bag, then back at Marcus. He didn't know what to believe. He picked up his bag and stood. "I need to go." Marcus nodded. "Yeah, me too."
text_zh: 乔纳斯在等他的外卖时，一个他不认识的男人坐在他对面。“你是乔纳斯，对吧？我是马库斯。我们需要谈谈达娜。”乔纳斯皱起眉头。“达娜？”马库斯点点头。“我的女朋友。或者我以为是。她提到过你，说你只是工作上的朋友。”乔纳斯感到胸口有一种奇怪的沉重感。他已经和达娜交往了几个星期。她告诉他她是单身。马库斯叹了口气，揉着额头。“我想我们都被骗了。”乔纳斯看了看他的外卖袋，又看了看马库斯。他不知道该相信什么。他拿起袋子站起来。“我得走了。”马库斯点点头。“是啊，我也是。”

topic: Two strangers realize they've been dating the same person
text_en: At the farmer's market, Ben reached for a jar of honey at the same moment as another man. They both laughed and stepped back.
