The man introduced himself as David, and they chatted about the weather. Later, Ben saw David at the bakery section, and they exchanged a few words again. Ben mentioned that he was meeting his girlfriend, Anna, for lunch. David's expression shifted slightly. He said that his girlfriend was also named Anna. Ben pulled out his phone to show a photo, and David showed his own. The same smiling face looked back at them from both screens.
text_zh: 在农贸市场，本伸手去拿一罐蜂蜜，同时另一个男人也伸手去拿。他们都笑了，退了回去。那人自我介绍叫大卫，他们聊了聊天气。后来，本在面包区看到大卫，他们又交谈了几句。本提到他要和女朋友安娜一起吃午饭。大卫的表情微微变了。他说他的女朋友也叫安娜。本拿出手机展示一张照片，大卫也展示了他的。两张屏幕上，同一张笑脸看着他们。

topic: Two strangers realize they've been dating the same person
text_en: Jake was helping his sister move when he saw a photo on her mantel. It was a picture of his girlfriend, Emma, with his sister's roommate, Chris. He asked about it. His sister said Chris had been dating Emma for a year. Jake felt his jaw tighten. He knew Emma had been with him for almost the same amount of time. He didn't say anything at first, just stared at the photo. Later, he called Chris. They met for a drink, comparing stories. The reality of the situation settled over them like a heavy blanket.
text_zh: 杰克在帮妹妹搬家时，看到她壁炉架上的一张照片。那是他女朋友艾玛和他妹妹的室友克里斯的合影。他问起这件事。他妹妹说克里斯和艾玛已经约会一年了。杰克感到下巴绷紧了。他知道艾玛和他在一起的时间也差不多。他起初什么也没说，只是盯着照片。后来，他打电话给克里斯。他们见面喝了一杯，对比了各自的故事。现实的真相像一条沉重的毯子笼罩着他们。

topic: Two strangers realize they've been dating the same person
text_en: While waiting for a bus, Emily overheard a man talking on his phone. He was telling someone he'd see them later, and he mentioned a movie they'd seen together. Emily recognized the movie. It was the one she'd seen with her boyfriend, Mark. She turned and saw the man was Mark's friend, David. She introduced herself. David's face fell. He said he was talking to his girlfriend, who was also named Emily. They realized they were both dating Mark. They stood in awkward silence, the bus pulling up and leaving without them.
text_zh: 在等公交车时，艾米丽无意中听到一个男人在打电话。他告诉某人晚点见，并提到他们一起看过的一部电影。艾米丽认出了那部电影。那是她和男朋友马克一起看过的。她转过身，看到那个男人是马克的朋友大卫。她做了自我介绍。大卫的脸色沉了下来。他说他正在和他的女朋友通话，她也叫艾米丽。他们意识到他们都在和马克约会。他们尴尬地沉默着，公交车来了又走了，没有载他们。

topic: Two strangers realize they've been dating the same person
text_en: At a party, Kevin met a woman who mentioned she was dating a man named Mike. Kevin said he knew Mike, and they started talking. The woman described Mike's apartment, the one with the blue door and the cat. Kevin felt a chill. That was his Mike. He mentioned the cat's name, and the woman nodded. They both fell silent. They had been seeing the same person. They looked at each other, then at the crowd around them, feeling a strange mix of confusion and something else they couldn't name.
text_zh: 在一个派对上，凯文遇到了一个女人，她提到她在和一个叫迈克的男人约会。凯文说他认识迈克，他们开始交谈。那个女人描述了迈克的公寓，那个有蓝色门和猫的公寓。凯文感到一阵寒意。那是他的迈克。他提到猫的名字，那个女人点了点头。他们都沉默了。他们一直在和同一个人约会。他们看着对方，然后看着周围的人群，感到一种奇怪的困惑和另一种他们无法名状的情绪的混合。

topic: Two strangers realize they've been dating the same person
text_en: At the coffee shop, Maya recognized the woman from the photos on Daniel's phone. They both reached for the same cup. The barista looked between them, then back at the counter. Maya's hand pulled back. The other woman, Claire, did the same. They exchanged a brief glance. Maya mentioned the weekend trip Daniel had planned. Claire mentioned the same cabin. Maya stirred her coffee slowly, watching the cream swirl. Claire checked her phone. They sat in silence for a moment, each holding their own cup, before Maya asked what time Daniel usually called her.
text_zh: 在咖啡店，玛雅认出了丹尼尔手机照片里的那个女人。她们同时伸手去拿同一个杯子。咖啡师看看她们两个，又看看柜台。玛雅的手缩了回去。另一个女人，克莱尔，也缩回了手。她们短暂地交换了一个眼神。玛雅提到丹尼尔计划的周末旅行。克莱尔提到了同一个小屋。玛雅慢慢地搅动咖啡，看着奶油旋转。克莱尔看了看手机。她们沉默地坐了一会儿，各自握着自己的杯子，然后玛雅问丹尼尔通常什么时候给她打电话。

topic: Two strangers realize they've been dating the same person
text_en: Tom was at the gym, finishing his workout, when a man approached him. "Hey, you're Tom, right? I'm Ryan. I think we have something in common." Tom wiped his face with a towel. "What's that?" Ryan smiled, but it didn't reach his eyes. "We're both seeing Jess." Tom stopped. "What?" Ryan nodded. "She's been coming over to my place for weeks. Said she was single." Tom thought about Jess, about their dates, about how she always seemed to have a reason not to introduce him to her friends. "I don't believe you," Tom said. Ryan pulled out his phone, showing a text conversation. Tom read it, seeing familiar phrases. He handed the phone back. "I guess we've both been fooled," Ryan said. Tom didn't reply.
text_zh: 汤姆正在健身房完成他的锻炼，这时一个男人走近他。“嘿，你是汤姆，对吧？我是瑞安。我想我们有些共同点。”汤姆用毛巾擦了擦脸。“什么共同点？”瑞安笑了笑，但笑意未达眼底。“我们都在和杰丝约会。”汤姆停住了。“什么？”瑞安点了点头。“她来我这儿好几个星期了。她说她是单身。”汤姆想到了杰丝，想到了他们的约会，想到了她似乎总有理由不把他介绍给她的朋友。“我不信，”汤姆说。瑞安掏出手机，展示了一段短信对话。汤姆读着，看到了熟悉的措辞。他把手机递了回去。“我想我们都被骗了，”瑞安说。汤姆没有回答。

topic: Two strangers realize they've been dating the same person
text_en: Elena was browsing the shelves at the bookstore when she overheard a man asking the clerk about a novel she had recommended to her boyfriend, Marcus. She glanced over and saw the man holding the same edition. She approached him and said that Marcus had enjoyed that book. The man looked puzzled and said his partner's name was Marcus as well. They compared details, and the man showed her a photo of Marcus at a concert. Elena recognized the jacket Marcus had worn when he said he was visiting his brother. They stood in the aisle, the fluorescent lights humming overhead.
text_zh: 埃琳娜正在书店浏览书架，这时她无意中听到一个男人向店员询问一本她推荐给男友马库斯的小说。她瞥了一眼，看到那个男人拿着同一个版本。她走近他，说马库斯很喜欢那本书。那个男人显得困惑，说他的伴侣也叫马库斯。他们比较了细节，那个男人给她看了一张马库斯在音乐会上的照片。埃琳娜认出了马库斯说去看望哥哥时穿的那件夹克。他们站在过道里，头顶的荧光灯嗡嗡作响。

topic: Two strangers realize they've been dating the same person
text_en: During a work break, Chris walked to the coffee cart and saw a woman he didn't know wearing a bracelet he had given to his girlfriend, Dana. He asked about it. The woman said it was a gift from her boyfriend, whom she called Dan. Chris mentioned that his girlfriend's name was Dana, and the woman's eyes widened. They talked for a few minutes, comparing details about where Dan and Dana said they spent their weekends. Chris mentioned the cabin by the lake, and the woman nodded. They both looked at the bracelet, then at each other, and Chris realized the coffee was getting cold in his hand.
text_zh: 工作休息时，克里斯走到咖啡车旁，看到一个不认识的女士戴着他送给女友达娜的手链。他问起这件事。那位女士说这是她男朋友送的礼物，她叫他丹。克里斯提到他女朋友的名字是达娜，那位女士睁大了眼睛。他们聊了几分钟，比较了丹和达娜说他们周末度过的地点的细节。克里斯提到了湖边的木屋，那位女士点了点头。他们都看了看手链，然后互相看了看，克里斯意识到手中的咖啡已经凉了。

topic: Two strangers realize they've been dating the same person
text_en: During a break at a class, a man named Daniel asked a woman named Sophie about her weekend. She said she'd gone to a concert with her boyfriend. Daniel asked which concert. She named a band. Daniel felt a twist. He'd been at that same concert with his girlfriend. They described their partners to each other. Sophie's boyfriend wore a red hat. Daniel's girlfriend wore a red hat too. They looked at each other, the classroom noise fading. They had been with the same person, just on different sides of the crowd.
text_zh: 课间休息时，一个叫丹尼尔的男子问一个叫苏菲的女子周末过得怎么样。她说她和男朋友去听了一场音乐会。丹尼尔问是哪场音乐会。她说出了一个乐队的名字。丹尼尔感到一阵揪心。他和女朋友也去了那场音乐会。他们互相描述了各自的伴侣。苏菲的男朋友戴着一顶红帽子。丹尼尔的女朋友也戴着一顶红帽子。他们看着对方，教室里的噪音渐渐消失。他们曾和同一个人在一起，只是站在人群的不同侧。

topic: Two strangers realize they've been dating the same person
text_en: Ella was at the grocery store, picking out apples, when a woman approached her. "Excuse me, are you Ella? I'm Rachel. I'm dating a man named Ben." Ella looked at her. "Ben?" Rachel nodded. "He's been coming to my apartment for months. He said he was single." Ella felt a knot in her stomach. She had been seeing Ben for a while. He had told her the same thing. Rachel looked at her. "I found your number in his phone. I called it, and you answered." Ella remembered a missed call from an unknown number. "That was you?" Rachel nodded. "I thought you should know." Ella looked at the apples in her basket. "I don't know what to say." Rachel shrugged. "Neither do I." Ella put the apples back.
text_zh: 艾拉正在杂货店挑苹果，这时一个女人走近她。“打扰一下，你是艾拉吗？我是瑞秋。我在和一个叫本的男人约会。”艾拉看着她。“本？”瑞秋点了点头。“他来我公寓好几个月了。他说他是单身。”艾拉感到胃里打了个结。她和本交往已有一段时间。他也跟她说了同样的话。瑞秋看着她。“我在他手机里找到了你的号码。我打了过去，你接了。”艾拉想起有一个未接来电，号码不熟悉。“那是你？”瑞秋点了点头。“我想你应该知道。”艾拉看着篮子里的苹果。“我不知道该说什么。”瑞秋耸了耸肩。“我也不知道。”艾拉把苹果放了回去。

topic: Two strangers realize they've been dating the same person
text_en: Owen was at a bar, waiting for his drink, when a woman tapped his shoulder. "You're Owen, right? I'm Claire. I'm seeing a man named David." Owen turned to face her. "David?" Claire nodded. "He's been my boyfriend for a while. He mentioned you, said you were a colleague. But I saw a message on his phone from you that was clearly romantic." Owen felt a pang. He had been dating David for a month. David had said he was unattached. "What did the message say?" Owen asked. Claire quoted it. Owen recognized his own words. "I see," he said quietly. Claire looked at him. "I think we've both been misled." Owen picked up his drink, not tasting it. "Yeah, maybe."
text_zh: 欧文正在酒吧等他的饮料，这时一个女人拍了拍他的肩膀。“你是欧文，对吧？我是克莱尔。我在和一个叫大卫的男人交往。”欧文转过身面对她。“大卫？”克莱尔点了点头。“他是我男朋友有一阵子了。他提到过你，说你是同事。但我看到他手机里有一条你发来的信息，明显是浪漫的。”欧文感到一阵刺痛。他和大卫约会已经一个月了。大卫说过他没有伴侣。“那条信息说了什么？”欧文问。克莱尔引述了那条信息。欧文认出了自己的话。“我明白了，”他轻声说。克莱尔看着他。“我想我们都被误导了。”欧文拿起饮料，没有尝出味道。“是啊，也许吧。”

topic: Two strangers realize they've been dating the same person
text_en: At a coffee shop, Jenna waited for her latte. A woman nearby was on the phone, laughing. "Yes, I'll see you tonight, Alex." Jenna glanced over, and the woman's phone background caught her eye—a photo of a man with his arm around the woman. Jenna recognized him instantly. It was Alex, the man she'd been seeing for months. She stepped closer. "Excuse me," she said. The woman looked up, still smiling. "Sorry, did you say something?" Jenna pointed at the phone. "That's Alex. My Alex." The woman's smile vanished. "Your Alex?" They stood in silence as the barista called Jenna's name.
text_zh: 在咖啡店里，珍娜等着她的拿铁。附近一个女人正在打电话，笑着。“是的，我今晚见你，亚历克斯。”珍娜瞥了一眼，那个女人的手机背景吸引了她的注意——一张男人搂着那个女人的照片。珍娜立刻认出了他。那是亚历克斯，她交往了几个月的人。她走近一步。“打扰一下，”她说。那个女人抬起头，仍然微笑着。“抱歉，你说了什么吗？”珍娜指着手机。“那是亚历克斯。我的亚历克斯。”那个女人的笑容消失了。“你的亚历克斯？”她们沉默地站着，这时咖啡师叫了珍娜的名字。

topic: Two strangers realize they've been dating the same person
text_en: Liam was at the laundromat, folding clothes, when a man sat next to him. "You're Liam, right? I'm Kevin. I think we need to talk about Rachel." Liam paused. "Rachel?" Kevin nodded. "She's been my girlfriend for a while. She said she was single." Liam felt a tightness in his chest. He had been seeing Rachel for weeks. She had said the same thing. "I found your number in her phone," Kevin said. "I called it, and you answered." Liam remembered a call from an unknown number. "That was you?" Kevin nodded. "I thought you should know." Liam looked at the shirt he was folding. "I don't know what to say." Kevin shrugged. "Neither do I." Liam set the shirt down.
text_zh: 利亚姆正在自助洗衣店叠衣服，这时一个男人坐在他旁边。“你是利亚姆，对吧？我是凯文。我想我们需要谈谈瑞秋。”利亚姆停顿了一下。“瑞秋？”凯文点了点头。“她是我女朋友有一阵子了。她说她是单身。”利亚姆感到胸口发紧。他和瑞秋约会已经几个星期了。她也说了同样的话。“我在她手机里找到了你的号码，”凯文说。“我打了过去，你接了。”利亚姆想起有一个来自陌生号码的电话。“那是你？”凯文点了点头。“我想你应该知道。”利亚姆看着手里正在叠的衬衫。“我不知道该说什么。”凯文耸了耸肩。“我也不知道。”利亚姆把衬衫放下。

topic: Two strangers realize they've been dating the same person
text_en: Hannah was at a farmers market when a man with a basket of vegetables stopped next to her. "You're Hannah, aren't you? I'm Mark. I'm seeing a woman named Emily." Hannah looked at him. "Emily?" Mark nodded. "She's been coming to my place for months. She said she was single." Hannah felt a pang. She had been dating Emily for a while. Emily had said the same thing. "I found your number in her phone," Mark said. "I called it, and you answered." Hannah remembered a missed call. "That was you?" Mark nodded. "I thought you should know." Hannah looked at the tomatoes in her basket. "I don't know what to say." Mark shrugged. "Neither do I." Hannah put the tomatoes back.
text_zh: 汉娜在农贸市场时，一个男人提着一篮蔬菜在她旁边停下。“你是汉娜，对吧？我是马克。我在和一个叫艾米丽的女人交往。”汉娜看着他。“艾米丽？”马克点了点头。“她来我这儿好几个月了。她说她是单身。”汉娜感到一阵刺痛。她和艾米丽约会已有一段时间。艾米丽也说了同样的话。“我在她手机里找到了你的号码，”马克说。“我打了过去，你接了。”汉娜想起有一个未接来电。“那是你？”马克点了点头。“我想你应该知道。”汉娜看着篮子里的西红柿。“我不知道该说什么。”马克耸了耸肩。“我也不知道。”汉娜把西红柿放了回去。

topic: Two strangers realize they've been dating the same person
text_en: Jordan was at a bar with colleagues when a woman approached and asked if he knew Mike. Jordan said Mike was his boyfriend. The woman said she was also dating Mike. They compared stories: the same restaurant, the same playlist, the same joke about the cat. Jordan finished his drink and said he had to go. Outside, the evening air was cool. He walked toward the bus stop, then stopped and turned back. He went inside again and found the woman still at the bar. He asked if she wanted to get coffee sometime, to talk more. She said yes.
text_zh: 乔丹和同事在酒吧时，一个女人走近他，问他是否认识迈克。乔丹说迈克是他的男朋友。那个女人说她也和迈克在约会。他们比较了各自的故事：同一家餐厅，同一个播放列表，同一个关于猫的笑话。乔丹喝完饮料，说他得走了。外面，傍晚的空气很凉爽。他走向公交车站，然后停下来，转过身。他再次走进去，发现那个女人还在酒吧。他问她是否想找个时间喝杯咖啡，多聊聊。她说好。

topic: A person finds a hidden letter in a used book
text_en: Margaret was sorting through a box of donated paperbacks when a folded sheet slipped from a novel about a seaside town. She opened it and found a short note written in a neat hand, dated years ago, mentioning a meeting at a café that no longer existed. The note was signed with an initial. Margaret turned it over, but the back was blank. She placed it back inside the book and set the book on the shelf with the others. Later, she mentioned the note to her colleague, who said it was probably just an old bookmark.
text_zh: 玛格丽特正在整理一箱捐赠的平装书时，一张折叠的纸从一本关于海滨小镇的小说中滑落。她打开它，发现是一张简短的字条，字迹工整，日期是多年前，提到在一个已不存在的咖啡馆见面。字条上只签了一个首字母。玛格丽特把它翻过来，但背面是空白的。她把字条放回书里，把书和其他书一起放在书架上。后来，她向同事提到了这张字条，同事说那可能只是一个旧书签。

topic: A person finds a hidden letter in a used book
text_en: At the used bookshop, Daniel picked up a worn copy of a travel memoir. When he flipped through it, a small envelope fell out. The flap was unsealed, and inside was a letter written on thin paper. It talked about a trip to the mountains and mentioned a specific trail and a waterfall. Daniel read it twice, then looked around the shop. He handed the book and letter to the owner, who shrugged and said people left all sorts of things. Daniel bought the book and kept the letter in the envelope.
text_zh: 在二手书店，丹尼尔拿起一本磨损的旅行回忆录。当他翻阅时，一个小信封掉了出来。封口没有封上，里面是一封写在薄纸上的信。信中提到一次山区旅行，并提到一条具体的小径和一个瀑布。丹尼尔读了两遍，然后环顾了一下书店。他把书和信交给店主，店主耸耸肩说人们会留下各种各样的东西。丹尼尔买下了这本书，并把信留在信封里。

topic: A person finds a hidden letter in a used book
text_en: Lena found the letter between pages of a poetry collection she had borrowed from the library. It was a single page, typed, with a few lines about a lost dog and a request to call a phone number if found. The number had an old area code. Lena read it while standing by the returns shelf. She considered calling, but the number was likely disconnected. She put the letter back in the book and returned it. That evening, she mentioned it to her roommate, who said it was probably a prank.
text_zh: 莉娜在她从图书馆借的一本诗集中发现了那封信。那是一页纸，打印的，上面有几行关于一只走失的狗的文字，并请求如果找到就拨打一个电话号码。号码是旧区号。莉娜站在还书架旁读着信。她考虑过打电话，但号码很可能已经停机了。她把信放回书里，然后归还了书。那天晚上，她向室友提起了这件事，室友说那可能是个恶作剧。

topic: A person finds a hidden letter in a used book
text_en: Maya was sorting through a box of used books she had bought at a library sale when she noticed a folded piece of paper sticking out from the pages of an old novel. She pulled it out carefully, smoothing the creases. It was a handwritten letter, dated from several decades ago, addressed to a woman named Eleanor. The writer mentioned a train ride they had taken together and a promise to meet again. Maya read it twice, then placed it back between the pages where she had found it. She set the book on her nightstand, thinking she might mention it to her sister later.
text_zh: 玛雅正在整理一箱她在图书馆义卖会上买的旧书时，注意到一张折叠的纸从一本旧小说的书页间露出来。她小心地把它抽出来，抚平折痕。那是一封手写的信，日期是几十年前，写给一位名叫埃莉诺的女士。写信人提到他们一起坐过一次火车，并承诺再次见面。玛雅读了两遍，然后把它放回她发现它的书页之间。她把书放在床头柜上，想着以后可能会跟姐姐提起这件事。

topic: A person finds a hidden letter in a used book
text_en: While waiting for his coffee to cool, Daniel flipped through a secondhand book he had picked up from a street vendor. A thin envelope slipped out and landed on the table. He opened it, finding a letter written in neat cursive. It was from a man to his brother, describing a summer job and asking about family news. The letter had no envelope, just the paper, folded in thirds. Daniel read it once, then tucked it back inside the book. He finished his coffee and left the book on the table when he headed out.
text_zh: 在等咖啡冷却的时候，丹尼尔翻阅了一本他从街头小贩那里买来的二手书。一个薄薄的信封滑了出来，落在桌子上。他打开它，发现一封用整齐的草书写成的信。信是一个男人写给他兄弟的，描述了一份暑期工作，并询问家里的消息。信没有信封，只有纸，折成三折。丹尼尔读了一遍，然后把它塞回书里。他喝完咖啡，离开时把书留在了桌子上。

topic: A person finds a hidden letter in a used book
text_en: Maya was sorting through a box of old novels at a yard sale when she picked up a weathered copy of a travel memoir. As she flipped through the pages, a folded letter slipped out and landed on the grass. She unfolded it, reading a note written in neat handwriting, dated years ago. It mentioned a meeting place and a time, but the rest was vague. Maya looked around, but no one seemed to be watching. She tucked the letter back into the book and placed it in her bag, deciding to read it more fully later. She paid the seller and walked home, the letter's words lingering in her mind.
text_zh: 玛雅正在庭院旧货出售会上整理一箱旧小说时，拿起一本破旧的旅行回忆录。当她翻阅书页时，一封折叠的信滑了出来，落在草地上。她展开信，读着用整齐笔迹写的字条，日期是多年前。信中提到一个见面地点和时间，但其余内容含糊不清。玛雅环顾四周，但似乎没有人在看。她把信塞回书里，放进包里，决定稍后再仔细阅读。她付钱给卖家，走回家，信中的话语在她脑海中萦绕。

topic: A person finds a hidden letter in a used book
text_en: At the library's annual book sale, Daniel picked up a thick history book. When he opened it to check for any markings, a small envelope fell out. Inside was a letter from someone named Claire, thanking a person named Tom for a lovely evening. It was written in a casual, friendly tone, mentioning a walk in the park and a shared meal. Daniel read it twice, then placed it back inside the book. He bought the book for a dollar and took it home, setting it on his desk. He wasn't sure what to make of the letter, but he left it where it was.
text_zh: 在图书馆的年度书展上，丹尼尔拿起一本厚厚的历史书。当他打开书检查是否有标记时，一个小信封掉了出来。里面是一封来自一个叫克莱尔的人的信，感谢一个叫汤姆的人度过了一个愉快的夜晚。信以随意友好的语气写成，提到在公园散步和共享一餐。丹尼尔读了两遍，然后把它放回书里。他花了一美元买下这本书，带回家放在书桌上。他不确定该怎么看待这封信，但他把它留在原处。

topic: A person finds a hidden letter in a used book
text_en: While cleaning out her late aunt's apartment, Rosa found a box of paperback mysteries. In one of them, a letter was tucked between the pages. It was addressed to her aunt from a former colleague, discussing a project they had worked on together. The letter mentioned some difficulties but also a sense of accomplishment. Rosa read it, noting the date and the colleague's name. She set the book aside, planning to keep it with her aunt's other personal papers. The letter gave her a small glimpse into a part of her aunt's life she hadn't known about.
text_zh: 在清理已故姑妈的公寓时，罗莎发现了一箱平装本推理小说。在其中一本里，一封信夹在书页之间。信是写给姑妈的，来自一位前同事，讨论了他们曾一起参与的一个项目。信中提到了困难，但也提到了成就感。罗莎读了信，注意到日期和同事的名字。她把书放在一边，打算把它和姑妈的其他私人文件放在一起。这封信让她得以一窥姑妈生活中她所不知道的一部分。

topic: A person finds a hidden letter in a used book
text_en: Liam was browsing a secondhand shop and found a copy of a classic novel he'd been meaning to read. As he checked the pages, a folded note fell out. It was a short message from a parent to a child, reminding them to pick up milk and bread on the way home. The handwriting was slightly rushed. Liam smiled briefly, then put the note back inside the book. He bought the novel and left the shop. Later, while reading, he came across the note again and left it in place, thinking it was a small piece of someone else's daily life.
text_zh: 利亚姆在逛一家二手店时，发现了一本他一直想读的经典小说。当他检查书页时，一张折叠的纸条掉了出来。那是一封简短的信息，从父母写给孩子的，提醒他们回家路上买牛奶和面包。笔迹略显潦草。利亚姆微微一笑，然后把纸条放回书里。他买下小说，离开了商店。后来，在阅读时，他又看到了那张纸条，并把它留在原处，想着这是别人日常生活的一小部分。

topic: A person finds a hidden letter in a used book
text_en: At a used bookstore, Priya found an old poetry anthology. When she opened it, a letter slipped out from between the pages. It was written by a woman to her sister, describing a recent trip to the coast. She mentioned the weather, the food, and a long walk on the beach. Priya read the letter, noticing the careful handwriting. She put it back in the book and decided to buy it. When she got home, she placed the book on her shelf, the letter still inside, a quiet reminder of an unknown traveler.
text_zh: 在一家二手书店，普里亚发现了一本旧诗集。当她打开时，一封信从书页间滑落。信是一位女士写给妹妹的，描述了最近一次去海边的旅行。她提到了天气、食物和在沙滩上长时间散步。普里亚读了信，注意到那工整的笔迹。她把信放回书里，决定买下它。回到家后，她把书放在书架上，信还在里面，静静地提醒着一位不知名的旅人。

topic: A person finds a hidden letter in a used book
text_en: James was helping a friend move and came across a box of books that were destined for donation. He picked up a guide to birdwatching and flipped through it. A letter fell out, written in pencil, from a person thanking a neighbor for feeding their cat while they were away. It was brief and practical, with a note about the cat's favorite spot. James read it, then returned it to the book. He put the book in the donation box and continued helping with the move, the letter's simple message fading from his thoughts.
text_zh: 詹姆斯在帮朋友搬家时，发现了一箱准备捐赠的书。他拿起一本观鸟指南，随手翻了翻。一封信掉了出来，是用铅笔写的，写信人感谢邻居在他们外出期间帮忙喂猫。信的内容简短而实际，还提到了猫最喜欢的角落。詹姆斯读完后，把信放回了书里。他把书放进捐赠箱，继续帮忙搬家，信里简单的话语渐渐从他的思绪中淡去。

topic: A person finds a hidden letter in a used book
text_en: At a library sale, Lena picked up a worn copy of a gardening manual. Later that evening, while flipping through the pages, a folded envelope slipped out. The handwriting was neat and dated from years ago, addressed to someone named Margaret. Inside was a short note about meeting at a café to discuss plans for a community garden. Lena read it twice, then placed it back between the pages. She thought about the people who might have owned the book before her. She set the manual on her nightstand and finished her tea before getting ready for bed.
text_zh: 在一次图书馆义卖会上，莉娜拿起一本破旧的园艺手册。当晚晚些时候，她翻阅书页时，一个折叠的信封滑了出来。字迹工整，日期是多年前的，收信人是一位名叫玛格丽特的人。里面是一张简短的便条，提到要在咖啡馆见面，讨论社区花园的计划。莉娜读了两遍，然后把它放回书页之间。她想着这本书以前可能属于谁。她把手册放在床头柜上，喝完茶，然后准备上床睡觉。

topic: A person finds a hidden letter in a used book
text_en: During a quiet afternoon, Marcus sorted through boxes of books he had inherited from his uncle. In a dusty volume of poetry, he found a letter written on thin paper. The sender mentioned a train journey and hoped to see the recipient soon. The names were unfamiliar, and the date was from several decades earlier. Marcus read the letter slowly, then folded it and tucked it into the book's front cover. He placed the book on a shelf with the others and went to make a sandwich. The letter stayed where it was.
text_zh: 在一个安静的下午，马库斯整理着从叔叔那里继承来的一箱箱书。在一本布满灰尘的诗集里，他发现了一封写在薄纸上的信。写信人提到了一次火车旅行，并希望很快见到收信人。名字很陌生，日期是几十年前的。马库斯慢慢地读着信，然后把它折好，塞进书的前封面里。他把书和其他书一起放在书架上，然后去做了一个三明治。信就留在那里。

topic: A person finds a hidden letter in a used book
text_en: While cleaning out a spare room, Priya came across a box of old novels. She picked up a thick mystery and noticed a corner of paper sticking out from the pages. It was a handwritten letter from a woman to her brother, describing a recent move and asking about family news. The postmark was faded. Priya read it and then put it back, closing the book. She continued sorting through the box, setting aside a few books to keep and others to donate. The letter remained in the mystery, unseen.
text_zh: 在清理一间闲置房间时，普里亚发现了一箱旧小说。她拿起一本厚厚的悬疑小说，注意到书页间露出一角纸。那是一封手写的信，是一位女士写给弟弟的，描述了最近的一次搬家，并询问家里的消息。邮戳已经褪色。普里亚读完后，把信放回去，合上了书。她继续整理箱子，挑出几本要保留的书，其他的则准备捐赠。那封信仍然留在悬疑小说里，无人看见。

topic: A person finds a hidden letter in a used book
text_en: At a secondhand bookstore, Tom bought a biography of a famous explorer. That night, while reading in bed, he found a letter tucked near the middle of the book. It was written in a flowing script and talked about a recent holiday by the sea. The author mentioned a friend who had not written back. Tom examined the letter for a moment, then placed it on his bedside table. He went back to reading the biography. In the morning, he put the letter back inside the book and left it on the shelf.
text_zh: 在一家二手书店，汤姆买了一本著名探险家的传记。那天晚上，他在床上阅读时，在书的中部附近发现了一封信。信是用流畅的笔迹写的，谈到了最近一次在海边的假期。写信人提到一位朋友没有回信。汤姆端详了一会儿信，然后把它放在床头柜上。他继续读传记。早上，他把信放回书里，然后把书放在书架上。

topic: A person finds a hidden letter in a used book
text_en: While on a lunch break, Marcus wandered into a thrift store and found a book on photography. As he flipped through it, a small envelope fell out. Inside was a letter from a man to his wife, mentioning a planned weekend trip and a camera he wanted to buy. It was written in a warm, casual style. Marcus read it, then returned it to the book. He decided to buy the book, and on his way back to work, he thought about the letter, wondering if the couple ever took that trip.
text_zh: 午休时，马库斯走进一家旧货店，发现一本关于摄影的书。他翻阅时，一个小信封掉了出来。里面是一封丈夫写给妻子的信，提到计划中的周末旅行和他想买的一台相机。信的风格温暖而随意。马库斯读完后，把信放回书里。他决定买下这本书，在回公司的路上，他想着那封信，不知道那对夫妇是否真的进行了那次旅行。

topic: A person finds a hidden letter in a used book
text_en: Maya was sorting through a box of donated novels at the library when a thin envelope slipped from between the pages of a worn mystery. The paper was yellowed, and the handwriting was neat and small. She opened it, reading a few lines about a train trip and a meeting that had been postponed. The letter was unsigned, and the name of the recipient was not mentioned. Maya folded it back carefully and placed it inside the book, then returned the novel to the shelf for the next reader. She continued sorting the remaining books without giving the letter much further thought.
text_zh: 玛雅正在图书馆整理一箱捐赠的小说，一个薄薄的信封从一本破旧的悬疑小说的书页间滑落。纸张已经泛黄，字迹工整而细小。她打开信封，读了几行关于一次火车旅行和一次被推迟的会面的内容。信没有署名，也没有提到收信人的名字。玛雅小心地把它折好，放回书里，然后把小说放回书架，留给下一位读者。她继续整理剩下的书，没有再过多地想那封信。

topic: A person finds a hidden letter in a used book
text_en: In a hotel room, Ben found a book on the nightstand left by a previous guest. He opened it to the first chapter and noticed a letter used as a bookmark. It was from a traveler to a friend back home, describing the city they were visiting and the food they had tried. The letter was written on hotel stationery. Ben read it, then left it in the book. He set the book aside and unpacked his suitcase, the letter's description of the city making him think about his own plans.
text_zh: 在一家酒店房间里，本发现床头柜上有一本前一位客人留下的书。他打开第一章，注意到一封信被用作书签。那是一位旅行者写给家乡朋友的，描述了他们在游览的城市和尝试过的食物。信写在酒店的信纸上。本读完后，把信留在书里。他把书放在一边，打开行李箱，信中关于城市的描述让他思考起自己的计划。

topic: A person finds a hidden letter in a used book
text_en: Rachel was at a flea market and bought a box of old books for a few dollars. When she got home, she started going through them. In a collection of essays, she found a letter. It was from a person to a former classmate, mentioning a reunion and asking if they still lived in the same town. The letter was brief and ended with a question. Rachel read it, then put it back in the book. She set the book on a shelf with the others, not sure what to do with it.
text_zh: 瑞秋在跳蚤市场花几美元买了一箱旧书。回到家后，她开始翻阅。在一本散文集中，她发现了一封信。信是一位老同学写给另一位同学的，提到了一次聚会，并询问对方是否还住在同一个镇上。信很简短，结尾是一个问题。瑞秋读完后，把信放回书里。她把书和其他书一起放在书架上，不知道该拿它怎么办。

topic: A person finds a hidden letter in a used book
text_en: While unpacking a box of secondhand books from an estate sale, Paul found a folded note tucked into the spine of a cookbook. It was a short list of ingredients for a pie, written in pencil, with a small sketch of a pie dish in the corner. The handwriting was unfamiliar, and there was no date or name. He read it twice, then set it aside on the kitchen counter. He picked up the cookbook and flipped through a few pages, then put it on the shelf with the others. The note remained on the counter until he later used it to jot down a phone number.
text_zh: 在拆开一箱从遗产拍卖会上买来的二手书时，保罗发现一张折叠的便条塞在一本食谱的书脊里。那是一张用铅笔写的馅饼配料清单，角落里还画了一个小小的馅饼盘草图。笔迹很陌生，没有日期或名字。他读了两遍，然后把它放在厨房台面上。他拿起食谱，翻了几页，然后把它和其他书一起放在书架上。那张便条一直留在台面上，直到后来他用它记了一个电话号码。

topic: A college student discovers their roommate has been reading their journal
text_en: Maya came back from her morning class to find the room empty. Her journal lay on her desk, slightly askew, a pen resting on top of it that she didn't remember leaving there. She picked it up, flipped through the pages. The last entry she'd written was about her weekend trip. A corner of the page was folded down, something she never did. She put the journal back in its usual spot and started gathering her laundry. When her roommate returned with lunch, Maya asked about the weather outside. They talked about an upcoming assignment. Maya noticed her roommate's eyes flick to the desk once, then away.
text_zh: 玛雅从早课上回来，发现房间空无一人。她的日记本放在书桌上，微微歪斜，上面放着一支她不记得自己留下的笔。她拿起日记本，翻了几页。她写的最后一篇是关于周末旅行的。有一页的角被折了起来，她从不这样做。她把日记本放回原位，开始收拾要洗的衣服。当室友带着午餐回来时，玛雅问起外面的天气。她们聊起了一个即将到来的作业。玛雅注意到室友的目光扫向书桌一次，然后又移开了。

topic: A college student discovers their roommate has been reading their journal
text_en: Ethan walked into the dorm room and saw his roommate, Leo, sitting at his desk, quickly closing a book. Ethan recognized the cover—it was his journal, the one with the dark blue cover he kept in his drawer. Leo turned, smiled, and said something about a study group. Ethan walked over to his own desk and opened his laptop. He noticed the drawer was slightly open. He didn't say anything. Later that evening, while Leo was in the shower, Ethan moved the journal to the bottom of his backpack. He left it there and went to get dinner with a friend.
text_zh: 伊桑走进宿舍房间，看到室友利奥坐在书桌前，迅速合上一本书。伊桑认出了封面——那是他的日记本，深蓝色封面，他一直放在抽屉里。利奥转过身，微笑着说了些关于学习小组的事。伊桑走到自己的书桌前，打开笔记本电脑。他注意到抽屉微微开着。他什么也没说。那天晚上晚些时候，趁利奥在洗澡，伊桑把日记本移到背包底部。他把它留在那里，然后和朋友去吃晚饭。

topic: A college student discovers their roommate has been reading their journal
text_en: Priya was lying on her bed, scrolling through her phone, when her roommate, Jenna, came in and went straight to her desk. Priya had been writing in her journal earlier and had left it out. Jenna picked it up, looked at the cover, then put it down. Priya saw her do it. She didn't say anything. Jenna started talking about a chemistry test they had coming up. Priya responded, but her mind was on the journal. After Jenna left for her afternoon lab, Priya opened the journal to the last page she'd written. It looked the same. She closed it and put it in her drawer.
text_zh: 普里亚躺在床上刷手机时，室友珍娜走进来，径直走向她的书桌。普里亚之前一直在写日记，把它留在了外面。珍娜拿起日记本，看了看封面，然后放下。普里亚看到了她的动作。她什么也没说。珍娜开始谈论她们即将到来的化学考试。普里亚回应着，但心思却在日记本上。珍娜离开去上下午的实验课后，普里亚打开日记本翻到她写的最后一页。看起来和原来一样。她合上日记本，把它放进抽屉里。

topic: A college student discovers their roommate has been reading their journal
text_en: Alex had a routine of writing in his journal every night before bed. One evening, he came back from the bathroom to find his roommate, Sam, standing near his desk, holding the journal. Sam quickly placed it back and said he was looking for a charger. Alex nodded and climbed into his bunk. He lay there for a while, listening to Sam's music. The next morning, Alex took the journal with him to the library and read through the last few entries. Nothing was missing. He wrote a new entry about the library's quiet atmosphere, then slipped the journal into his coat pocket.
text_zh: 亚历克斯有每晚睡前写日记的习惯。一天晚上，他从浴室回来，发现室友萨姆站在他的书桌旁，手里拿着日记本。萨姆迅速把它放回去，说他在找充电器。亚历克斯点点头，爬上自己的床铺。他躺了一会儿，听着萨姆的音乐。第二天早上，亚历克斯带着日记本去了图书馆，翻阅了最后几篇。什么也没少。他写了一篇关于图书馆安静氛围的新日记，然后把日记本塞进了外套口袋。

topic: A college student discovers their roommate has been reading their journal
text_en: Rachel noticed that her journal had been moved. She kept it between some textbooks on her shelf, and now it was on top. She picked it up and opened it to a random page. There was a faint crease in the spine, as if it had been opened wide. Her roommate, Dana, was at her own desk, wearing headphones. Rachel put the journal back, slightly differently, and started working on her laptop. Later, Dana took off her headphones and asked Rachel if she wanted to order pizza. Rachel said sure. While they ate, Rachel watched Dana's hands, but Dana didn't go near the journal.
text_zh: 瑞秋注意到她的日记本被移动过。她把它放在书架上的几本教科书之间，现在它却在最上面。她拿起日记本，随手翻开一页。书脊上有一道淡淡的折痕，好像被大幅打开过。她的室友达娜正戴着耳机坐在自己的书桌前。瑞秋把日记本放回去，位置稍有不同，然后开始用笔记本电脑工作。后来，达娜摘下耳机，问瑞秋要不要点披萨。瑞秋说好。她们吃的时候，瑞秋观察着达娜的手，但达娜没有靠近日记本。

topic: A college student discovers their roommate has been reading their journal
text_en: Jordan's journal was a plain black notebook he'd had for years. He came back from a run to find it on his bed, not on his desk where he'd left it. His roommate, Chris, was sitting at his own desk, typing. Jordan picked up the journal and put it back on his desk. Chris didn't look up. Jordan took a shower and then sat down to study. He noticed a small coffee ring on the desk near the journal, but his coffee was on the other side. He wiped it off with his sleeve. He didn't mention it to Chris.
text_zh: 乔丹的日记本是一个朴素的黑色笔记本，他已经用了好几年。他跑步回来发现它躺在床上，而不是他离开时放的书桌上。他的室友克里斯正坐在自己的书桌前打字。乔丹拿起日记本，放回书桌上。克里斯没有抬头。乔丹洗了个澡，然后坐下来学习。他注意到日记本旁边的书桌上有一个小小的咖啡渍，但他的咖啡在另一边。他用袖子擦掉了。他没有向克里斯提起这件事。

topic: A college student discovers their roommate has been reading their journal
text_en: Lena had been writing about her day in her journal when her roommate, Tara, came back from class. Lena closed the journal and put it under her pillow. Tara sat on her own bed and started talking about a professor's lecture. Lena listened, responding occasionally. When Tara went to the bathroom, Lena took the journal out and saw that the ribbon bookmark was now sticking out at a different page than she'd left it. She opened to that page. It was an entry from a few days ago about a disagreement with a friend. She closed it and put it in her backpack.
text_zh: 莉娜正在写关于她一天的日记时，室友塔拉下课回来了。莉娜合上日记本，把它放在枕头下。塔拉坐在自己的床上，开始谈论一位教授的讲座。莉娜听着，偶尔回应。塔拉去洗手间时，莉娜拿出日记本，发现丝带书签现在露出的页码和她离开时不同。她翻到那一页。那是几天前写的一篇关于与朋友分歧的日记。她合上日记本，把它放进背包里。

topic: A college student discovers their roommate has been reading their journal
text_en: Marcus kept his journal in a desk drawer. One afternoon, he reached for it and found it wasn't in its usual spot. He searched the drawer, then the desk top. His roommate, Ben, was on his bed, reading a textbook. Marcus asked if Ben had seen it. Ben said no, without looking up. Marcus found it a few minutes later under a stack of papers. He opened it, checking the pages. He didn't see any marks. He put it back in the drawer, this time at the bottom. He went back to his homework, occasionally glancing at Ben.
text_zh: 马库斯把日记本放在书桌抽屉里。一天下午，他伸手去拿，发现它不在平常的位置。他翻了翻抽屉，又找了桌面。他的室友本正躺在床上看教科书。马库斯问本有没有看到。本没有抬头，说没有。几分钟后，马库斯在一叠文件下找到了它。他打开日记本，检查了页面。他没有看到任何标记。他把它放回抽屉，这次放在最下面。他继续做作业，偶尔瞥一眼本。

topic: A college student discovers their roommate has been reading their journal
text_en: Sophie was in the middle of writing a long entry about her summer plans when her roommate, Emily, walked in. Sophie closed the journal and put it aside. Emily sat down and started telling Sophie about a call with her mom. Sophie listened, nodding. When Emily left for a club meeting, Sophie opened the journal again. The pen she'd been using was now on the floor near Emily's side of the room. She picked it up and continued writing, but she kept the journal in her lap for the rest of the evening.
text_zh: 苏菲正在写一篇关于她暑假计划的長篇日记，这时室友艾米丽走了进来。苏菲合上日记本，把它放在一边。艾米丽坐下来，开始告诉苏菲她和她妈妈通电话的事。苏菲听着，点点头。艾米丽去参加社团会议后，苏菲又打开了日记本。她一直在用的笔现在掉在艾米丽那边的地板上。她捡起笔继续写，但那天晚上剩下的时间里，她一直把日记本放在膝盖上。

topic: A college student discovers their roommate has been reading their journal
text_en: Daniel came back to his dorm after a late class to find his roommate, Kyle, asleep at his desk, with Daniel's journal open in front of him. Daniel stood in the doorway for a moment. He walked over and gently closed the journal. Kyle stirred but didn't wake. Daniel took the journal and put it in his backpack. He sat on his bed and looked at Kyle's sleeping form. The next morning, Kyle didn't mention it. Daniel didn't either. He carried the backpack with him all day, even to the cafeteria.
text_zh: 丹尼尔下晚课后回到宿舍，发现室友凯尔趴在书桌上睡着了，丹尼尔的日记本摊开在他面前。丹尼尔在门口站了一会儿。他走过去，轻轻合上日记本。凯尔动了动，但没有醒。丹尼尔拿起日记本，放进背包里。他坐在床上，看着凯尔熟睡的身影。第二天早上，凯尔没有提起这件事。丹尼尔也没有。他一整天都背着那个背包，甚至去食堂也带着。

topic: A college student discovers their roommate has been reading their journal
text_en: Ava was looking for her favorite pen and opened her roommate's drawer by accident. Inside, she saw her own journal, the one she thought she'd lost a week ago. She pulled it out. It had a few new dog-eared pages. Her roommate, Chloe, wasn't in the room. Ava opened to the dog-eared pages. They were entries about Chloe's birthday party, which Ava hadn't attended. She put the journal back exactly where she'd found it and closed the drawer. When Chloe came back, Ava asked about the party. Chloe described it. Ava nodded, then went back to her own desk.
text_zh: 艾娃正在找她最喜欢的笔，不小心打开了室友的抽屉。在里面，她看到了自己的日记本，那本她以为一周前丢失的日记本。她把它拿出来。上面有几页新的折角页。她的室友克洛伊不在房间里。艾娃翻到折角页。那是关于克洛伊生日派对的记录，艾娃没有参加那个派对。她把日记本放回原处，关上了抽屉。克洛伊回来后，艾娃问起派对的事。克洛伊描述了派对。艾娃点了点头，然后回到自己的书桌前。

topic: A college student discovers their roommate has been reading their journal
text_en: Noah had a habit of writing in his journal at the campus coffee shop. One day, he left it on the table while he went to order a refill. When he came back, his roommate, Tyler, was sitting there, holding the journal. Tyler said he'd just arrived and saw it. Noah took it and put it in his bag. They walked back to the dorm together, talking about a video game. That night, Noah checked the journal. The page he'd been writing on was now blank, as if he hadn't written anything. He looked at the blank page for a while, then closed the journal.
text_zh: 诺亚习惯在校园咖啡店写日记。一天，他去续杯时把日记本留在了桌上。当他回来时，他的室友泰勒正坐在那里，手里拿着日记本。泰勒说他刚到，看到了它。诺亚接过日记本，放进包里。他们一起走回宿舍，聊着一个电子游戏。那天晚上，诺亚检查了日记本。他正在写的那一页现在是空白的，好像他什么都没写过。他盯着空白页看了一会儿，然后合上了日记本。

topic: A college student discovers their roommate has been reading their journal
text_en: Isabella noticed her journal was on the floor near her roommate's bed. She picked it up and brushed off the dust. Her roommate, Olivia, was watching a show on her laptop. Isabella sat on her own bed and opened the journal to the last entry. It was about a difficult conversation with her parents. She closed it and put it on her nightstand. Olivia paused the show and asked Isabella if she wanted to watch something together. Isabella said she had homework. She opened her textbook, but her eyes kept drifting to the journal.
text_zh: 伊莎贝拉注意到她的日记本在室友床边的地板上。她捡起来，掸去灰尘。她的室友奥利维亚正在笔记本电脑上看节目。伊莎贝拉坐在自己的床上，翻开日记本，看到最后一篇。那是关于与父母一次艰难对话的记录。她合上日记本，把它放在床头柜上。奥利维亚暂停了节目，问伊莎贝拉是否想一起看点什么。伊莎贝拉说她有作业。她打开课本，但目光却不断飘向日记本。

topic: A college student discovers their roommate has been reading their journal
text_en: Lucas was in the middle of a phone call with his sister when he walked into his room. His roommate, Jake, was at his desk, with Lucas's journal open. Lucas ended the call quickly. Jake looked up and said he was looking for a piece of paper. Lucas pointed to the printer. Jake took a sheet and handed the journal back. Lucas took it without saying anything. He sat on his bed and opened it. The page he'd been writing on was about his sister. He closed it and put it in his bag. He didn't write again that day.
text_zh: 卢卡斯正和姐姐通电话，走进房间时，他的室友杰克正坐在书桌前，卢卡斯的日记本摊开着。卢卡斯迅速结束了通话。杰克抬起头，说他在找一张纸。卢卡斯指了指打印机。杰克拿了一张纸，把日记本递了回去。卢卡斯什么也没说，接了过来。他坐在床上，翻开日记本。他正在写的那一页是关于他姐姐的。他合上日记本，放进包里。那天他没有再写。

topic: A college student discovers their roommate has been reading their journal
text_en: Mia kept her journal in a small lockbox, but the lock was broken. She came back from class to find the box open, the journal on top of her desk. Her roommate, Zoe, was nowhere in sight. Mia picked up the journal and opened it. The pages were in order. She closed it and put it back in the box, but she didn't close the lid. When Zoe came back, Mia asked if she'd seen anyone in the room. Zoe said no. Mia nodded and started making dinner. She left the journal out on the desk for the rest of the night.
text_zh: 米娅把日记本放在一个小锁箱里，但锁坏了。她下课回来发现箱子开着，日记本放在书桌上。她的室友佐伊不见踪影。米娅拿起日记本，翻开看了看。页面顺序正常。她合上日记本，放回箱子里，但没有盖上盖子。佐伊回来后，米娅问她是否看到有人进过房间。佐伊说没有。米娅点了点头，开始做晚饭。那天晚上剩下的时间里，她把日记本留在了书桌上。

topic: A college student discovers their roommate has been reading their journal
text_en: Ethan's roommate, Lucas, was always borrowing things without asking. One evening, Ethan found his journal on Lucas's bed, under a textbook. He picked it up and opened it. There was a bookmark in it that Ethan didn't own. He removed the bookmark and put it on Lucas's desk. He took the journal back to his own side. The next day, Lucas asked if Ethan had seen his bookmark. Ethan said he'd seen it on his desk. Lucas thanked him. Ethan didn't mention the journal. He started keeping it in his backpack.
text_zh: 伊桑的室友卢卡斯总是未经允许就借东西。一天晚上，伊桑在卢卡斯的床上，一本教科书下面，发现了自己的日记本。他捡起来，翻开。里面有一个不是伊桑的书签。他取出书签，放在卢卡斯的书桌上。他把日记本拿回自己那边。第二天，卢卡斯问伊桑有没有看到他的书签。伊桑说他在书桌上看到了。卢卡斯道了谢。伊桑没有提起日记本的事。他开始把日记本放在背包里。

topic: A college student discovers their roommate has been reading their journal
text_en: Grace was writing in her journal when her roommate, Lily, came in and flopped onto her bed. Grace closed the journal and put it on her lap. Lily started talking about a guy she'd met in class. Grace listened, making small comments. When Lily got up to go to the bathroom, Grace put the journal under her pillow. She heard Lily come back and go to her own desk. Grace lay on her bed, staring at the ceiling. She didn't take the journal out again until after Lily had fallen asleep.
text_zh: 格蕾丝正在写日记，这时她的室友莉莉进来，扑到床上。格蕾丝合上日记本，放在腿上。莉莉开始说起她在课上遇到的一个男生。格蕾丝听着，偶尔插几句。莉莉起身去洗手间时，格蕾丝把日记本塞到枕头下。她听到莉莉回来，走到自己的书桌前。格蕾丝躺在床上，盯着天花板。直到莉莉睡着后，她才再次拿出日记本。

topic: A college student discovers their roommate has been reading their journal
text_en: Owen came back from the gym to find his roommate, Max, sitting on the floor, flipping through a notebook. Owen recognized it as his journal. Max looked up, said he thought it was his own notebook, and tossed it back. Owen caught it. He opened it to the page where he'd been writing. It was about his workouts. He closed it and put it on his desk. He didn't say anything else. The next morning, he moved the journal to a different spot in his bag. He didn't mention it to Max.
text_zh: 欧文从健身房回来，发现室友马克斯坐在地板上，翻着一本笔记本。欧文认出那是他的日记本。马克斯抬起头，说他以为那是自己的笔记本，然后把日记本扔了回去。欧文接住了。他翻到他正在写的那一页。那是关于他的锻炼的。他合上日记本，放在书桌上。他什么也没说。第二天早上，他把日记本移到包里另一个位置。他没有向马克斯提起这件事。

topic: A college student discovers their roommate has been reading their journal
text_en: Hannah had a journal she wrote in every few days. She came back from a weekend trip to find it on her desk, open to a page she'd written before she left. Her roommate, Emma, was unpacking her own bag. Hannah closed the journal and put it in her drawer. Emma said the trip was fun. Hannah agreed. They talked about the places they'd seen. Later, when Emma went to dinner, Hannah opened the drawer. The journal was still there. She took it out and read the page. It was about feeling homesick. She put it back and went to join Emma.
text_zh: 汉娜有一本日记，每隔几天写一次。她周末旅行回来，发现日记本在书桌上，翻到她离开前写的那一页。她的室友艾玛正在整理自己的包。汉娜合上日记本，放进抽屉。艾玛说旅行很有趣。汉娜表示同意。她们聊起了去过的地方。后来，艾玛去吃晚饭时，汉娜打开抽屉。日记本还在那里。她拿出来，读了那一页。那是关于想家的。她把它放回去，然后去找艾玛。

topic: A college student discovers their roommate has been reading their journal
text_en: David's journal was a gift from his mother. He kept it on his bookshelf. One day, he noticed it was sticking out slightly from the row of books. He pulled it out and opened it. A receipt fell out from a store he'd never been to. He picked it up and looked at it. It was dated a few days ago. He put the receipt back in the journal and returned it to the shelf. His roommate, Aaron, was at his desk. David asked Aaron if he'd been to that store. Aaron said he hadn't. David nodded and sat down to study.
text_zh: 大卫的日记本是母亲送的礼物。他把它放在书架上。一天，他注意到它从书堆里稍微突出来。他把它抽出来，翻开。一张他从未去过的商店的收据掉了出来。他捡起来看了看。日期是几天前。他把收据放回日记本里，放回书架。他的室友亚伦正在书桌前。大卫问亚伦是否去过那家商店。亚伦说没有。大卫点了点头，坐下来学习。

topic: Someone receives a package intended for the previous tenant
text_en: The package was sitting by the front door when Dana got home from work. The label had the previous tenant's name on it, but the address was correct. Dana carried it inside and set it on the kitchen counter. It was a medium-sized box, fairly light. She wondered if the forwarding order had expired. She thought about calling the property manager, but it was late. Instead, she wrote a note with the previous tenant's name and the date, and taped it to the box. Then she put it in the hall closet, where she kept things she needed to deal with later.
text_zh: 达娜下班回家时，包裹就放在前门旁边。标签上是前租客的名字，但地址是正确的。达娜把它拿进屋里，放在厨房台面上。这是一个中等大小的盒子，相当轻。她想知道转寄订单是否已经过期。她想过给物业经理打电话，但时间已晚。于是，她写了一张纸条，上面写着前租客的名字和日期，然后贴在盒子上。接着，她把它放进走廊的壁橱里，那里放着她需要稍后处理的东西。

topic: Someone receives a package intended for the previous tenant
text_en: Maya picked up the envelope from the mat. It was addressed to someone named Elise, who had lived there before. The return address was a clinic across town. Maya placed it on the table by the door. She had been getting a few pieces of mail for Elise over the past month. She usually left them in a pile. Today, she sorted through the pile and noticed most were bills. She put the new envelope with the others. Maybe the mail would stop eventually, she thought, as she went to make dinner.
text_zh: 玛雅从门垫上捡起信封。收件人是一个叫艾莉丝的人，她以前住在这里。寄件地址是城对面的一家诊所。玛雅把它放在门边的桌子上。过去一个月里，她陆续收到几封寄给艾莉丝的邮件。她通常把它们堆在一起。今天，她翻看了那堆邮件，注意到大部分是账单。她把新信封和其他邮件放在一起。也许邮件最终会停止吧，她一边想着，一边去做晚饭。

topic: Someone receives a package intended for the previous tenant
text_en: The delivery driver handed over a long, narrow box. The name on it was not hers. Liam signed for it anyway, because the driver was in a hurry. He put the box in the corner of the living room. It had a return label from an art supply store. He didn't know anyone who would send him art supplies. The previous tenant had moved out months ago. He left the box where it was and went back to reading. A few days later, he saw it still there and moved it near the door to return to sender.
text_zh: 快递员递过来一个长而窄的盒子。上面的名字不是她的。利亚姆还是签收了，因为快递员很匆忙。他把盒子放在客厅的角落里。上面有来自一家美术用品店的退货标签。他不认识会给他寄美术用品的人。前租客几个月前就搬走了。他把盒子留在原处，继续看书。几天后，他看到它还在那里，就把它移到门边，准备退回给寄件人。

topic: Someone receives a package intended for the previous tenant
text_en: Priya found a padded envelope leaning against the door. It was addressed to the prior occupant. She brought it inside to keep it from getting wet. The return address was a relative's home in another state. She put it on the bookshelf with the other misdelivered mail. She thought about calling the management office to see if they had a forwarding address. She decided to wait and see if more mail came. For now, she just wanted to finish unpacking the kitchen boxes. She set the envelope aside and continued.
text_zh: 普里亚发现一个加衬垫的信封靠在门上。收件人是之前的住户。她把它拿进屋里，以免被淋湿。寄件地址是另一个州的一位亲戚家。她把它和其他误投的邮件一起放在书架上。她想过给管理处打电话，看看他们是否有转寄地址。她决定等等看是否还有更多邮件。目前，她只想赶紧拆完厨房的箱子。她把信封放在一边，继续干活。

topic: Someone receives a package intended for the previous tenant
text_en: Ethan was pulling into the driveway when he saw the delivery truck pull away. A small box sat on the porch. The label showed a name he didn't recognize. He picked it up and felt a slight weight. Inside the house, he placed it on the dining table. He considered opening it, but it wasn't his. He called the phone number on the return label. No one answered. He left a message explaining the situation. Then he put the box on a shelf in the garage, out of the way, and went about his evening.
text_zh: 伊桑开车进车道时，看到快递卡车开走了。门廊上放着一个小盒子。标签上是一个他不认识的名字。他捡起来，感觉有点分量。进屋后，他把它放在餐桌上。他考虑过打开它，但这不是他的东西。他拨打了退货标签上的电话号码。没人接听。他留了一条语音信息说明情况。然后他把盒子放在车库的架子上，不碍事的地方，然后继续过他的晚上。

topic: Someone receives a package intended for the previous tenant
text_en: Maya pulled the cardboard box from the porch, its label bearing a name she didn't recognize. The previous tenant, a man she'd never met, had left no forwarding address. She set it on the kitchen counter, running her fingers along the tape. The package was light, and the corners were worn. She thought about opening it, but it wasn't hers. Instead, she placed it on the shelf by the door, next to a stack of old mail. A week later, it was still there, gathering dust. Maya occasionally glanced at it, wondering if she'd ever know what it contained.
text_zh: 玛雅从门廊上拿起纸板箱，标签上是一个她不认识的名字。前租客，一个她从未见过的男人，没有留下转寄地址。她把它放在厨房台面上，手指沿着胶带划过。包裹很轻，边角已经磨损。她想过打开它，但这不是她的东西。于是，她把它放在门边的架子上，旁边是一叠旧邮件。一周后，它还在那里，积满了灰尘。玛雅偶尔会瞥一眼，想知道自己是否有一天会知道里面装了什么。

topic: Someone receives a package intended for the previous tenant
text_en: A courier knocked and handed over a box that was clearly for the previous tenant. The sender was a pharmacy. Jordan took it and set it on the entryway floor. The previous tenant had left no forwarding address. Jordan thought about calling the pharmacy to let them know, but the customer service line was probably long. He put the box on the top shelf of the coat closet. He made a mental note to deal with it if more packages came. Then he closed the closet door and went to check on the laundry.
text_zh: 快递员敲门，递过来一个显然是给前租客的盒子。寄件人是一家药店。乔丹接过来，放在门厅地板上。前租客没有留下转寄地址。乔丹想过给药店打电话告知他们，但客服电话可能很长。他把盒子放在衣帽间的最上层架子上。他暗自记下，如果还有更多包裹，再处理。然后他关上壁橱门，去查看洗衣情况。

topic: Someone receives a package intended for the previous tenant
text_en: Sofia saw the box on the doorstep when she returned from her run. It was a cardboard box, sealed with tape. The name on the label was not hers. She picked it up and carried it inside. She placed it on the kitchen table next to her keys. The return address was a book club she had never heard of. She wondered if the previous tenant had ordered something before moving. She left it there while she made lunch. After eating, she moved it to the shelf by the door and went back to her day.
text_zh: 索菲亚跑步回来时看到门阶上的盒子。那是一个纸板箱，用胶带封着。标签上的名字不是她的。她捡起来，拿进屋里。她把它放在厨房桌子上，旁边是她的钥匙。寄件地址是一个她从未听说过的读书俱乐部。她想知道前租客是不是在搬家前订了什么东西。她做午饭时把它留在那里。吃完饭后，她把它移到门边的架子上，然后继续过她的一天。

topic: Someone receives a package intended for the previous tenant
text_en: Carlos found the package behind the porch chair. It must have been left earlier. The label was for someone named Martinez. He didn't know any Martinez. He brought it in and put it on the floor of his study. It was a large box, but not heavy. He thought about opening it to see if there was a way to return it, but it wasn't his to open. He called the leasing office. They said they would check their records. He hung up and left the box in the study, where it stayed for a while.
text_zh: 卡洛斯在门廊椅子后面发现了那个包裹。它一定是早些时候被留下的。标签上是一个叫马丁内斯的人。他不认识任何叫马丁内斯的人。他把它拿进来，放在书房的 地板上。那是一个大盒子，但不重。他考虑过打开看看是否有办法退回，但这不是他的东西，不能打开。他给租赁办公室打了电话。他们说会查一下记录。他挂了电话，把盒子留在书房里，在那里放了一段时间。

topic: Someone receives a package intended for the previous tenant
text_en: The mailman handed over a thick envelope along with the usual bills. The envelope was addressed to the person who used to live there. Lena put it on the counter. She had been getting a few things for that person, mostly catalogs. This one felt more important, with a handwritten address. She thought about writing "Return to Sender" on it and putting it in a mailbox. But she wasn't sure if that was the right thing. She set it aside with the other mail and went to pay her own bills.
text_zh: 邮递员递过来一个厚厚的信封，还有平时的账单。信封是寄给以前住在那里的那个人的。莉娜把它放在柜台上。她一直收到那个人的一些东西，大多是目录。这个感觉更重要，地址是手写的。她想过在上面写“退回寄件人”，然后放进邮箱。但她不确定这样做是否正确。她把它和其他邮件放在一边，然后去付自己的账单。

topic: Someone receives a package intended for the previous tenant
text_en: A package was left on the doorstep, and the label had the previous tenant's name. The sender was a grocery delivery service. Hannah carried it inside and set it on the counter. It felt cool, like it might contain perishables. She opened the box, since the contents might spoil. Inside were a few items of food. She didn't know what to do with them. She put the perishable items in the fridge to keep them from going bad. She left the rest in the box. She figured the previous tenant would not come back for it.
text_zh: 一个包裹被留在了门阶上，标签上写着前租户的名字。寄件人是一家杂货配送服务公司。汉娜把它拿进屋里，放在柜台上。包裹摸起来很凉，可能装有易腐物品。她打开了盒子，因为里面的东西可能会变质。里面是一些食品。她不知道该怎么处理它们。她把易腐物品放进冰箱以防变质。她把剩下的留在盒子里。她猜想前租户不会回来取它。

topic: Someone receives a package intended for the previous tenant
text_en: Ben was at his desk when the doorbell rang. He opened the door to find a package leaning against the frame. The name on it was someone he had never met. The sender was a hardware store. He brought it inside and put it on the floor by the entrance. He thought about checking with the landlord, but he didn't have the number handy. He left it there for the day. The next morning, he saw it again and moved it to the garage, where it would be out of the way.
text_zh: 本正坐在书桌前，门铃响了。他打开门，发现一个包裹靠在门框上。上面的名字是他从未见过的人。寄件人是一家五金店。他把包裹拿进屋里，放在入口处的地板上。他考虑过联系房东，但手边没有号码。他把它放在那里一整天。第二天早上，他又看到了它，把它搬到了车库，那里不会碍事。

topic: Someone receives a package intended for the previous tenant
text_en: The box was on the welcome mat when Olivia came home. It was addressed to the previous resident. The label was printed, and the return address was a company she didn't recognize. She picked it up and felt something shift inside. She carried it to the living room and placed it on the coffee table. She considered calling the company, but it was after hours. She decided to wait. She put the box on a chair in the corner, where it wouldn't be in the way. She went to prepare dinner.
text_zh: 奥利维亚回家时，盒子就在门垫上。收件人是前一位住户。标签是打印的，寄件地址是一家她不认识的公司。她拿起盒子，感觉里面有东西在动。她把它拿到客厅，放在咖啡桌上。她考虑过给公司打电话，但已经过了营业时间。她决定等一等。她把盒子放在角落的椅子上，这样就不会碍事。然后她去准备晚餐。

topic: Someone receives a package intended for the previous tenant
text_en: Mara found the box on the doormat when she got home from work. The label had the previous tenant's name printed neatly above her own address. She carried it inside and set it on the kitchen counter, turning it over to read the return address. A bookstore downtown. She hadn't ordered anything recently. The box was light, and when she shook it gently, something slid back and forth inside. She put it on the shelf by the door, planning to mention it to the landlord next time she saw him. For now, it could wait.
text_zh: 玛拉下班回家时，在门垫上发现了盒子。标签上整齐地印着前租户的名字，上面是她自己的地址。她把它拿进屋里，放在厨房柜台上，翻过来看寄件地址。是市中心的一家书店。她最近没有订购任何东西。盒子很轻，她轻轻摇晃时，里面有东西来回滑动。她把它放在门边的架子上，打算下次见到房东时提一下。现在，可以等等。

topic: Someone receives a package intended for the previous tenant
text_en: Liam found the package propped against his door when he came home from work. The name on it was a woman's, one he didn't know. He carried it inside, placing it on the dining table. The box was heavier than he expected, and he wondered what could be inside. He thought about contacting the landlord to ask about the previous tenant, but it seemed like too much effort. Instead, he put it in the closet with his winter coats, where it would be out of the way. He closed the door, telling himself he'd deal with it later, though he wasn't sure when that would be.
text_zh: 利亚姆下班回家时，发现包裹靠在门上。上面是一个女人的名字，他不认识。他把它拿进屋里，放在餐桌上。盒子比他预期的要重，他好奇里面可能是什么。他考虑过联系房东询问前租户的事，但似乎太麻烦了。于是，他把它放进衣柜里，和冬衣放在一起，这样就不会碍事。他关上门，告诉自己以后再处理，尽管他不确定那是什么时候。

topic: Someone receives a package intended for the previous tenant
text_en: Priya picked up the envelope from the doormat, addressed to a former occupant of her flat. The handwriting was neat, and there was no return address. She held it for a moment, feeling the weight of it. It was probably a bill or a bank statement, something important to someone else. She thought about forwarding it, but she didn't have the person's new address. She slid it into the drawer of the hall table, among other stray papers. Every now and then, she'd open the drawer for something else and see it there, a small reminder of a life she knew nothing about.
text_zh: 普里亚从门垫上捡起信封，收件人是她公寓的前住户。字迹工整，没有寄件地址。她拿了一会儿，感受着它的重量。这可能是账单或银行对账单，对别人来说很重要。她想过转寄，但没有那个人的新地址。她把它滑进大厅桌子的抽屉里，和其他散落的文件放在一起。偶尔，她会打开抽屉找别的东西，看到它，一个她一无所知的生活的小小提醒。

topic: Someone receives a package intended for the previous tenant
text_en: The package was waiting by the front door when Alex came back from a walk. It was a flat, rectangular box. The name on it was not his. The sender was a photography studio. He picked it up and took it inside. He placed it on the desk in the spare room. He wondered if the previous tenant had ordered prints and forgotten them. He didn't know what to do. He left it there. A few days later, he saw it and thought about it again. He still didn't do anything with it.
text_zh: 亚历克斯散步回来时，包裹正等着他。那是一个扁平的矩形盒子。上面的名字不是他的。寄件人是一家摄影工作室。他拿起它，带进屋里。他把它放在备用房间的桌子上。他好奇前租户是否订购了照片却忘了。他不知道该怎么办。他把它留在那里。几天后，他看到了它，又想了想。他仍然没有处理它。

topic: Someone receives a package intended for the previous tenant
text_en: Tina found a padded mailer in her mailbox. It was too big for the slot, so the mail carrier had left it sticking out. It was addressed to the previous tenant. The return address was a bank. She pulled it out and brought it inside. She set it on the kitchen table. She had been getting a lot of mail for the previous tenant. She had a pile of it in the corner. She added this to the pile. She thought about going to the post office, but she wasn't sure it would help. She went back to her chores.
text_zh: 蒂娜在邮箱里发现了一个气泡信封。它太大，塞不进邮箱，所以邮递员把它留在了外面。收件人是前租户。寄件地址是一家银行。她把它拿出来，带进屋里。她把它放在厨房桌子上。她一直收到前租户的邮件。她在角落里堆了一堆。她把这个加到那堆里。她想过要去邮局，但不确定是否有用。她继续做家务。

topic: Someone receives a package intended for the previous tenant
text_en: A box was on the doorstep when Daniel got home. It was a large, heavy box. The label was for the previous tenant. The sender was a furniture store. He managed to drag it inside. He put it in the hallway, where it blocked part of the walkway. He thought about opening it to see if there was a return slip, but it wasn't his. He called the store's customer service. They said they would look into it. He left the box in the hallway for a few days until he heard back.
text_zh: 丹尼尔回家时，一个盒子在门阶上。那是一个又大又重的盒子。标签是前租户的。他设法把它拖进屋里。他把它放在走廊里，挡住了部分通道。他打开它，看看有没有退货单，但这不是他的。他打电话给商店的客服。他们说会调查。他把盒子放在走廊里几天，直到收到回复。

topic: Someone receives a package intended for the previous tenant
text_en: The package was sitting on the porch, and the label had a name that was unfamiliar. The sender was a specialty food company. Laura brought it in and set it on the dining table. The box was cold to the touch. She thought it might contain something that needed refrigeration. She opened it to check. Inside were some jars and a cold pack. She put the jars in the fridge to keep them from spoiling. She left the rest on the table. She didn't know what else to do with it.
text_zh: 包裹放在门廊上，标签上的名字很陌生。劳拉把它拿进屋里，放在餐桌上。盒子摸起来很凉。她打开它，看看里面有什么。里面是一些罐子和一个冷包。她把罐子放进冰箱以防变质。她把剩下的留在桌子上。她不知道还能怎么处理。

topic: A coach has to cut a player from the team
text_en: The gym was quiet after practice, the only sound the hum of the ventilation system. Coach Miriam set down her clipboard and looked at the young woman standing before her. "I'm making some changes to the roster," she said, her voice even. "We need to go in a different direction for the season. Your spot on the team is being cut." The player nodded, her face unreadable. Miriam handed her a folder with the necessary paperwork. "You've improved a lot this year," she added. "I'll write a recommendation if you want to try out elsewhere." The player took the folder and left. Miriam watched her go, then returned to her office to update the roster list.
text_zh: 训练结束后，体育馆里很安静，只有通风系统的嗡嗡声。教练米里亚姆放下写字板，看着站在她面前的年轻女子。“我要对名单做一些调整，”她说，语气平稳。“这个赛季我们需要走不同的方向。你的队伍位置被裁掉了。”球员点了点头，脸上毫无表情。米里亚姆递给她一个装有必要文件的文件夹。“你今年进步很大，”她补充道。“如果你想尝试其他地方，我会写推荐信。”球员接过文件夹，离开了。米里亚姆看着她离去，然后回到办公室更新名单。

topic: A coach has to cut a player from the team
text_en: David waited until the parking lot had emptied before asking Alex to stay behind. They sat on the bench near the equipment shed. "I've been watching you all season," David began, rubbing the back of his neck. "You have a good attitude, but the team needs a different balance. I'm letting you go." Alex looked down at his shoes, then back up. "Okay," he said. "Thanks for the chance." He stood and walked to his car without another word. David gathered the stray balls from the field, then locked the shed. The sky was getting dark as he drove home.
text_zh: 大卫等到停车场空了才请亚历克斯留下。他们坐在器材棚附近的長椅上。“我整个赛季都在观察你，”大卫开口，揉了揉后颈。“你态度很好，但球队需要不同的平衡。我要让你离开。”亚历克斯低头看着自己的鞋子，然后又抬起头。“好的，”他说。“谢谢给我机会。”他站起来，一言不发地走向他的车。大卫从场上捡起散落的球，然后锁上器材棚。他开车回家时，天色渐暗。

topic: A coach has to cut a player from the team
text_en: Marta set the clipboard on the gym bench and looked across the court where the girls were finishing their drills. She had been watching Lena all season, noting her footwork, her passes, the way she hesitated before shooting. The roster needed to shrink, and Lena's name had been at the bottom of Marta's list for weeks. After practice, she asked Lena to stay behind. They sat on the bleachers while Marta explained the decision, keeping her voice even. Lena nodded, gathered her bag, and walked out. Marta picked up the clipboard and wrote a note for the next practice.
text_zh: 玛尔塔把写字板放在体育馆的长凳上，看着球场对面女孩们正在完成训练。她整个赛季都在观察莉娜，注意她的步法、传球，以及她在投篮前犹豫的样子。名单需要缩减，而莉娜的名字几周来一直排在玛尔塔名单的底部。训练结束后，她请莉娜留下。她们坐在看台上，玛尔塔解释了决定，语气保持平稳。莉娜点了点头，收拾好包，走了出去。玛尔塔拿起写字板，为下次训练写了一张便条。

topic: A coach has to cut a player from the team
text_en: Marcus had called the meeting for early morning, before classes. He stood by the bleachers as the players trickled in. When everyone was present, he spoke. "This is never easy, but I have to make a change. Sarah, you're off the team." Sarah blinked, her face going still. "But I've been training hard," she said. Marcus acknowledged her effort. "It's about team composition, not your work ethic." He gave her a list of other teams in the area that might need players. Sarah took the paper, folded it, and walked away. The rest of the players looked at each other, then at Marcus, who picked up his clipboard and began the practice.
text_zh: 马库斯把会议安排在清晨，上课之前。他站在看台旁，球员们陆续到来。当所有人都到场时，他开口了。“这从来都不容易，但我必须做出改变。莎拉，你被移出队伍了。”莎拉眨了眨眼，脸上一片平静。“但我一直在努力训练，”她说。马库斯承认了她的努力。“这关乎团队构成，而不是你的工作态度。”他给了她一份该地区可能需要球员的其他队伍名单。莎拉接过纸，折好，走开了。其余的球员面面相觑，然后看着马库斯，他拿起写字板，开始了训练。

topic: A coach has to cut a player from the team
text_en: The office was small, with posters of past teams on the walls. Coach Linda held the signed letter in her hand. "I'm sorry, Tom, but we're not renewing your place on the squad." Tom sat across from her, his cap on his lap. "Is there anything I could do?" he asked. Linda shook her head. "The decision's final. It's not about performance alone." She slid a brochure across the desk. "There's a community league that starts next month." Tom glanced at it, then placed it in his pocket. He stood up, shook her hand, and left. Linda filed the letter and made a note in her calendar.
text_zh: 办公室很小，墙上贴着过去队伍的海报。教练琳达手里拿着签好的信。“对不起，汤姆，我们不会续签你的队伍名额。”汤姆坐在她对面，帽子放在膝盖上。“有什么我能做的吗？”他问。琳达摇了摇头。“决定是最终的。这不仅仅关乎表现。”她推过一张宣传册。“有一个社区联赛下个月开始。”汤姆瞥了一眼，然后放进了口袋。他站起来，和她握了握手，离开了。琳达把信归档，并在日历上做了记录。

topic: A coach has to cut a player from the team
text_en: After a lengthy practice, Coach Nguyen asked Elena to stay behind. The other players had already headed to the showers. Nguyen sat on the bench, motioning for Elena to join him. "I've been thinking about the lineup," he said. "We have to make cuts to stay competitive. You're one of them." Elena stared at the floor. "I thought I was doing well," she said. Nguyen nodded. "You were. But the numbers don't work for everyone." He offered to help her find another team. Elena thanked him, her voice flat. She left her practice gear on the bench and walked out. Nguyen collected the gear and placed it in the lost-and-found bin.
text_zh: 长时间的训练后，阮教练请埃琳娜留下。其他球员已经去洗澡了。阮坐在长凳上，示意埃琳娜坐到他旁边。“我一直在考虑阵容，”他说。“为了保持竞争力，我们必须进行裁减。你是其中之一。”埃琳娜盯着地板。“我以为我做得很好，”她说。阮点了点头。“你确实做得很好。但名额对每个人来说都不够。”他主动提出帮她找另一支队伍。埃琳娜感谢了他，声音平淡。她把训练装备留在长凳上，走了出去。阮收拾好装备，放进了失物招领箱。

topic: A coach has to cut a player from the team
text_en: Coach Patricia had been dreading this conversation all week, but now it was time. She found Kevin in the locker room, packing his bag. "Kevin, I need to talk to you." He zipped his bag and turned to face her. "I'm cutting you from the team," she said. Kevin's expression didn't change. "Okay," he said. "Can I still come to the games?" Patricia was taken aback. "Sure, you're welcome to." He nodded and left. Patricia stood there for a moment, then went to her office to finalize the roster. The locker room was empty except for the echo of the door swinging shut.
text_zh: 帕特里夏教练整个星期都在害怕这次谈话，但现在时候到了。她在更衣室里找到凯文，他正在收拾包。“凯文，我需要和你谈谈。”他拉上包的拉链，转身面对她。“我要把你从队伍中裁掉，”她说。凯文的表情没有变化。“好的，”他说。“我还能来看比赛吗？”帕特里夏吃了一惊。“当然，欢迎你来。”他点了点头，离开了。帕特里夏在那里站了一会儿，然后去办公室敲定名单。更衣室里空荡荡的，只有门关上的回声。

topic: A coach has to cut a player from the team
text_en: Coach Ramirez reviewed the roster on his clipboard before practice. He had to cut one player before the weekend tournament, and the decision weighed on him. After the drills, he asked Marcus to stay behind. They stood by the equipment shed while the rest of the team headed to the locker room. Ramirez explained that the squad was full and that Marcus would be released. Marcus nodded and picked up his bag. Ramirez offered to help him find another team in the area. Marcus said he would think about it. They shook hands, and Marcus walked toward the parking lot.
text_zh: 拉米雷斯教练在训练前查看了写字板上的名单。他必须在周末锦标赛前裁掉一名球员，这个决定让他感到沉重。训练结束后，他请马库斯留下。他们站在器材棚旁，而其他队员则前往更衣室。拉米雷斯解释说队伍已满，马库斯将被释放。马库斯点了点头，拿起他的包。拉米雷斯主动提出帮他找该地区的另一支队伍。马库斯说他会考虑。他们握了握手，马库斯走向停车场。

topic: A coach has to cut a player from the team
text_en: It was a rainy Tuesday when Coach Allen asked for a private word with Jess. They stood under the awning outside the gym. "I have to tell you," Allen said, "you're not going to be on the team this year." Jess hugged her notebook to her chest. "I really wanted this," she said. Allen acknowledged that. "I know. But we have limited spots, and I have to choose based on the team's needs." He suggested she could join the intramural league. Jess nodded, thanked him, and walked into the rain. Allen watched her go, then went back inside to dry off.
text_zh: 那是一个下雨的星期二，艾伦教练请求与杰丝私下谈谈。他们站在体育馆外的雨棚下。“我必须告诉你，”艾伦说，“你今年不会在队伍里了。”杰丝把笔记本抱在胸前。“我真的很想加入，”她说。艾伦承认了这一点。“我知道。但我们的名额有限，我必须根据队伍的需求来选择。”他建议她可以加入校内联赛。杰丝点了点头，感谢了他，然后走进了雨中。艾伦看着她离去，然后回到里面擦干身体。

topic: A coach has to cut a player from the team
text_en: Coach Bennett had scheduled individual meetings with each player. When it was Ryan's turn, Bennett got straight to the point. "Ryan, I'm cutting you from the roster." Ryan had been expecting a discussion about his role, not this. "Why?" he asked. Bennett explained that the team needed more speed on the wings. Ryan considered this. "I can work on that," he said. Bennett shook his head. "It's not a training issue. It's a fit issue." Ryan stood up, took his jacket, and left without another word. Bennett noted in his log that the conversation was complete.
text_zh: 贝内特教练安排了与每位球员的单独会面。轮到瑞安时，贝内特开门见山。“瑞安，我要把你从名单上裁掉。”瑞安原本期待的是关于他角色的讨论，而不是这个。“为什么？”他问。贝内特解释说队伍在边路需要更多速度。瑞安考虑了一下。“我可以在这方面努力，”他说。贝内特摇了摇头。“这不是训练问题。这是适配问题。”瑞安站起来，拿起夹克，一言不发地离开了。贝内特在他的日志中记录谈话已完成。

topic: A coach has to cut a player from the team
text_en: The cafeteria was mostly empty at that hour. Coach Silva sat across from Dana, a folder on the table between them. "I've made some decisions about the team," she said. "You're not going to be on it." Dana looked at the folder, then at Silva. "I didn't see this coming," she said. Silva nodded. "I understand. It's a hard call." She opened the folder and pointed to a list of other teams. "These are still accepting players." Dana took the list, folded it, and put it in her pocket. "Thanks," she said. She stood and left the cafeteria. Silva closed the folder and finished her coffee.
text_zh: 那个时间点，自助餐厅里几乎空无一人。席尔瓦教练坐在达娜对面，两人之间的桌上放着一个文件夹。“我对球队做了一些决定，”她说。“你不会在名单上了。”达娜看了看文件夹，又看了看席尔瓦。“我没料到会这样，”她说。席尔瓦点了点头。“我理解。这是个艰难的决定。”她打开文件夹，指着一份其他球队的名单。“这些队还在招人。”达娜接过名单，折好，放进了口袋。“谢谢，”她说。她站起来，离开了自助餐厅。席尔瓦合上文件夹，喝完了咖啡。

topic: A coach has to cut a player from the team
text_en: Practice had ended, and the players were leaving. Coach Morgan called out to Luis, who was heading for the door. "Luis, wait up." Luis turned around. Morgan walked over, speaking quietly. "I'm making changes to the squad. You won't be part of it." Luis looked at the floor, then back at Morgan. "Is there anything I can do?" Morgan shook his head. "It's not about you personally. It's about the team's needs." Luis nodded slowly. "Okay. I understand." He left without another word. Morgan watched him go, then went to the office to update the roster on the wall.
text_zh: 训练结束了，球员们正在离开。摩根教练叫住了正朝门口走去的路易斯。“路易斯，等一下。”路易斯转过身来。摩根走过去，低声说道。“我要对球队阵容做些调整。你不会在其中了。”路易斯看了看地板，又看向摩根。“我能做点什么吗？”摩根摇了摇头。“这不是针对你个人。是球队的需要。”路易斯慢慢点了点头。“好的。我明白了。”他没再多说一句话就离开了。摩根看着他离去，然后走进办公室去更新墙上的名单。

topic: A coach has to cut a player from the team
text_en: Coach Patel had written the new roster on a piece of paper, but he wanted to tell each player in person. He found Hannah in the library, studying. "Hannah, can we step outside?" They went into the hallway. "I'm cutting you from the team," Patel said. Hannah looked at him, her eyes steady. "I've been trying my best," she said. Patel agreed. "You have. But the team needs a different skill set." He handed her a letter explaining the decision. Hannah took it, read it, and put it in her bag. "Thank you for telling me directly," she said. Patel nodded and returned to the library to find the next player.
text_zh: 帕特尔教练已经把新名单写在了一张纸上，但他想当面告诉每个球员。他在图书馆找到了正在学习的汉娜。“汉娜，我们能出去一下吗？”他们走到走廊里。“我要把你从球队裁掉，”帕特尔说。汉娜看着他，目光坚定。“我一直都在尽我最大的努力，”她说。帕特尔表示同意。“你确实尽力了。但球队需要不同的技能组合。”他递给她一封解释这一决定的信。汉娜接过信，读了一遍，然后放进了包里。“谢谢你直接告诉我，”她说。帕特尔点了点头，回到图书馆去找下一个球员。

topic: A coach has to cut a player from the team
text_en: The gym was closed for maintenance, so Coach Adams held the meeting in the park. He sat on a bench with Chris beside him. "I've got some news," Adams began. "You're not on the team anymore." Chris looked out at the empty field. "I guess I saw it coming," he said. Adams raised an eyebrow. "Why?" Chris shrugged. "I haven't been playing well lately." Adams said it was more about the team's direction. They sat in silence for a moment. Then Chris stood up. "I'll pick up my stuff tomorrow." He walked away. Adams stayed on the bench, watching the clouds move.
text_zh: 体育馆因维修关闭了，所以亚当斯教练把会议安排在公园里。他坐在长椅上，克里斯坐在他旁边。“我有消息要告诉你，”亚当斯开口说。“你不在球队里了。”克里斯望着空旷的场地。“我想我预料到了，”他说。亚当斯挑了挑眉毛。“为什么？”克里斯耸了耸肩。“我最近打得不好。”亚当斯说这更多是关于球队的方向。他们沉默地坐了一会儿。然后克里斯站了起来。“我明天来拿我的东西。”他走开了。亚当斯留在长椅上，看着云彩移动。

topic: A coach has to cut a player from the team
text_en: Coach Foster had been avoiding this conversation, but the season was starting soon. She caught up with Priya after practice. "Priya, I need to talk to you." They walked to the side of the field. "I'm cutting you from the team," Foster said. Priya's face went blank. "Why?" she asked. Foster explained the need for more players in a different position. Priya listened, then asked if she could still practice with the team sometimes. Foster said that might be possible, but not officially. Priya thanked her and left. Foster returned to the field to lead the next drill.
text_zh: 福斯特教练一直在回避这次谈话，但赛季很快就要开始了。训练结束后她赶上了普丽娅。“普丽娅，我需要和你谈谈。”他们走到场地边上。“我要把你从球队裁掉，”福斯特说。普丽娅的脸变得毫无表情。“为什么？”她问道。福斯特解释了需要更多不同位置的球员。普丽娅听着，然后问她是否还能偶尔和球队一起训练。福斯特说那也许可以，但不是正式的。普丽娅向她道谢后离开了。福斯特回到场地带领下一项训练。

topic: A coach has to cut a player from the team
text_en: It was a warm evening, and the team was having a light practice. Coach Ellis called over to Jordan, who was doing stretches. "Jordan, come here a second." Jordan walked over. Ellis put a hand on his shoulder. "I have to let you go from the team." Jordan stopped stretching. "Oh," he said. "I thought I was doing okay." Ellis said he was, but the team needed a different lineup. Jordan nodded. "Alright. Thanks for telling me." He went to the bench, gathered his things, and left. Ellis watched him go, then blew his whistle to resume practice.
text_zh: 那是一个温暖的傍晚，球队正在进行轻松的训练。埃利斯教练叫住了正在做拉伸的乔丹。“乔丹，过来一下。”乔丹走了过去。埃利斯把手放在他的肩膀上。“我得让你离开球队了。”乔丹停止了拉伸。“哦，”他说。“我以为我做得还不错。”埃利斯说他确实做得不错，但球队需要不同的阵容。乔丹点了点头。“好的。谢谢你告诉我。”他走到长椅旁，收拾好自己的东西，离开了。埃利斯看着他离去，然后吹响哨子继续训练。

topic: A coach has to cut a player from the team
text_en: Coach Ramirez had scheduled a phone call with each cut player. When she called Aisha, Aisha answered on the first ring. "Hi, Coach." Ramirez got straight to the point. "Aisha, I'm not putting you on the team this season." There was a pause. "Can I ask why?" Aisha said. Ramirez explained the need for more experience at the position. Aisha said she understood. Ramirez offered to write a recommendation for another team. Aisha said that would be helpful. They ended the call with a plan to meet later. Ramirez hung up and dialed the next number on her list.
text_zh: 拉米雷斯教练安排了与每位被裁球员的电话通话。当她打电话给艾莎时，艾莎第一声铃响就接了。“嗨，教练。”拉米雷斯开门见山。“艾莎，这个赛季我不会把你放进球队名单。”电话那头停顿了一下。“我能问为什么吗？”艾莎说。拉米雷斯解释了该位置需要更多经验。艾莎说她理解。拉米雷斯提出可以为她写一封推荐信给另一支球队。艾莎说那会很有帮助。他们以约定稍后见面结束了通话。拉米雷斯挂断电话，拨打了名单上的下一个号码。

topic: A coach has to cut a player from the team
text_en: The locker room was empty when Coach Turner came in. He found Sam putting on his shoes. "Sam, I need to talk to you." Sam looked up. "Sure." Turner sat down on the bench opposite. "I'm making a change. You're off the team." Sam stopped tying his shoe. "I've been here for a while," he said. Turner nodded. "I know. It's a hard decision." Sam finished tying his shoe and stood up. "I'll miss it," he said. Turner said he was welcome to come by anytime. Sam nodded and left. Turner sat in the locker room for a few minutes before heading to his office.
text_zh: 特纳教练进来时，更衣室里空无一人。他看到山姆正在穿鞋。“山姆，我需要和你谈谈。”山姆抬起头。“好的。”特纳在对面长椅上坐下。“我要做一个调整。你不在球队里了。”山姆停下了系鞋带的动作。“我在这里待了一段时间了，”他说。特纳点了点头。“我知道。这是个艰难的决定。”山姆系好鞋带，站了起来。“我会想念这里的，”他说。特纳说他随时欢迎他过来。山姆点了点头，离开了。特纳在更衣室里坐了几分钟，然后才走向办公室。

topic: A coach has to cut a player from the team
text_en: Coach Miller had put up a notice about individual meetings. When it was Taylor's turn, Miller closed the door. "Taylor, I have to tell you that you're not on the team this year." Taylor's face showed no reaction. "I figured it might be something like that," she said. Miller asked why. Taylor said she hadn't been playing as well as she could. Miller said it was more about the team's composition. Taylor accepted that. "Will you still be at the games?" Miller asked. Taylor shrugged. "Maybe." She left the office. Miller made a note on the meeting list and moved to the next name.
text_zh: 米勒教练贴出了一张关于个别会谈的通知。轮到泰勒时，米勒关上了门。“泰勒，我必须告诉你，今年你不在球队名单上。”泰勒脸上没有任何反应。“我猜可能是这样的事，”她说。米勒问为什么。泰勒说她最近打得没有她能做到的那么好。米勒说这更多是关于球队的构成。泰勒接受了这一点。“你还会来看比赛吗？”米勒问道。泰勒耸了耸肩。“也许吧。”她离开了办公室。米勒在会谈名单上做了个记号，然后转向下一个名字。

topic: A coach has to cut a player from the team
text_en: Coach Brooks waited until the end of practice to speak with Ethan. The other players had already left. "Ethan, stay back a moment." Ethan put down his water bottle. Brooks took a deep breath. "I'm cutting you from the team." Ethan looked at him, his expression unchanged. "Okay," he said. "Is there anything I should know?" Brooks said it was about team needs. Ethan nodded. "I'll get my stuff tomorrow." He picked up his water bottle and walked to the exit. Brooks watched him leave, then turned off the lights and locked the gym.
text_zh: 布鲁克斯教练等到训练结束才和伊桑谈话。其他球员已经离开了。“伊桑，留一下。”伊桑放下水瓶。布鲁克斯深吸了一口气。“我要把你从球队裁掉。”伊桑看着他，表情没有变化。“好的，”他说。“有什么我需要知道的吗？”布鲁克斯说这是关于球队的需要。伊桑点了点头。“我明天来拿我的东西。”他拿起水瓶，走向出口。布鲁克斯看着他离开，然后关掉灯，锁上了体育馆。

topic: Someone learns their favorite author plagiarized their stories
text_en: Marta had been collecting the author's books for years, and the latest novel felt familiar. She recognized a scene from her own unpublished manuscript, the one she'd shared at a workshop. She checked the author's acknowledgments; no mention of her. She set the book aside and made dinner, then returned to it, rereading the passage. It was the same, almost word for word. She thought about the workshop she'd attended, the small group, and who else had been there. She closed the book and placed it on the shelf, not sure what to do next.
text_zh: 玛尔塔多年来一直在收集这位作者的书，最新的小说让她感觉似曾相识。她认出了其中一幕出自她自己未发表的手稿，那是在一个写作工作坊上分享过的。她查看了作者的致谢部分，没有提到她。她把书放在一边去做晚饭，然后又回来重新阅读那段文字。几乎是一字不差。她回想起参加过的那个工作坊，那个小团体，以及还有谁在场。她合上书，把它放在书架上，不确定接下来该怎么办。

topic: Someone learns their favorite author plagiarized their stories
text_en: Liam was a devoted fan of a mystery writer. He collected all his books and even attended a signing. One evening, he stumbled upon an obscure blog that analyzed old pulp magazines. A story from decades ago had the same detective, the same dialogue, and the same solution. Liam read through both stories carefully, noting the borrowed phrases. He set his book aside and looked out the window. He thought about the author he had followed for so long, then picked up his phone and scrolled through his messages, not sure what to do next.
text_zh: 利亚姆是一位悬疑作家的忠实粉丝。他收集了他所有的书，甚至参加过签售会。一天晚上，他偶然发现一个分析旧时低俗杂志的冷门博客。一篇几十年前的故事有着相同的侦探、相同的对话和相同的谜底。利亚姆仔细阅读了两个故事，注意到了那些被借用的短语。他把书放在一边，望向窗外。他想起了自己追随了这么久的作家，然后拿起手机，翻阅着信息，不确定接下来该怎么办。

topic: Someone learns their favorite author plagiarized their stories
text_en: Elena had always admired Marcus Webb's novels, especially the way he described coastal towns. She was reading his latest book when a passage about a lighthouse keeper's daughter felt achingly familiar. It was nearly identical to a story she had written years ago for a workshop. She set the book down and walked to her desk, pulling out the old folder. She compared the paragraphs side by side. The names were changed, but the dialogue was the same. She closed the folder and sat for a while, looking out the window, then put the book back on the shelf.
text_zh: 埃琳娜一直很欣赏马库斯·韦伯的小说，尤其是他对沿海城镇的描写。她在读他的最新作品时，一段关于灯塔看守人女儿的文字让她感到痛心地熟悉。这几乎与她多年前为一个工作坊写的故事一模一样。她放下书，走到书桌前，翻出那个旧文件夹。她将段落并排比较。名字改了，但对话是一样的。她合上文件夹，坐了一会儿，望着窗外，然后把书放回了书架。

topic: Someone learns their favorite author plagiarized their stories
text_en: Daniel had collected every book by his favorite author, a man named Julian Croft. He was in the middle of a new release, a mystery set in a small town. He reached a chapter where a character found a hidden letter in a piano bench. Daniel stopped. He had written that exact scene for a creative writing class years ago. He remembered the teacher's comments. He went to his storage box and found the old manuscript. The wording was almost verbatim. He read a few more pages and noticed other similarities. He closed the book and placed it on the coffee table.
text_zh: 丹尼尔收藏了他最喜欢的作家朱利安·克罗夫特的所有书。他正在读一本新出版的小说，背景是小镇的悬疑故事。他读到一个章节，其中一个人物在钢琴凳里发现了一封隐藏的信。丹尼尔停了下来。这正是他多年前在创意写作课上写过的场景。他记得老师的评语。他走到储物箱前，找到了旧手稿。措辞几乎是逐字逐句的。他又读了几页，发现了其他相似之处。他合上书，把它放在咖啡桌上。

topic: Someone learns their favorite author plagiarized their stories
text_en: Maya loved the poetic style of her favorite writer, Rachel Stone. She was reading a collection of short stories when one story about a woman who collected abandoned keys seemed too familiar. Maya had written a similar piece for her blog last year. She pulled up her post and compared the descriptions. The sequence of events matched closely. She scrolled through the rest of the collection and found another story that mirrored a piece she had submitted to a literary magazine. She turned off her laptop and stared at the bookshelf, then picked up a different book to read.
text_zh: 玛雅喜欢她最喜欢的作家雷切尔·斯通的诗歌风格。她在读一本短篇小说集时，其中一篇关于一个收集废弃钥匙的女人的故事似乎太熟悉了。玛雅去年在自己的博客上写过类似的作品。她调出她的帖子，比较了描述。事件顺序非常接近。她浏览了文集的其余部分，发现了另一篇与她投给文学杂志的作品相似的故事。她关上笔记本电脑，盯着书架，然后拿起另一本书来读。

topic: Someone learns their favorite author plagiarized their stories
text_en: Tom was a devoted fan of the author Lila Hart. Her new novel featured a protagonist who worked in a secondhand bookstore and found a diary hidden in a cookbook. Tom recognized the plot instantly. It was from a story he had shared in an online writing forum. He remembered the replies he received. He logged into the forum and found his old post, then compared the key scenes. The names were different, but the structure and dialogue were nearly identical. He closed the browser and sat back in his chair, then got up to make a sandwich.
text_zh: 汤姆是作家莉拉·哈特的忠实粉丝。她的新小说主角在一家二手书店工作，在一本烹饪书中发现了一本日记。汤姆立刻认出了这个情节。这来自他在一个在线写作论坛上分享的故事。他记得收到的回复。他登录论坛，找到了自己的旧帖子，然后比较了关键场景。名字不同，但结构和对话几乎相同。他关上浏览器，靠回椅子里，然后起身去做了一个三明治。

topic: Someone learns their favorite author plagiarized their stories
text_en: Priya had read all of Victor Hale's novels. His latest book, a historical drama, described a woman who sewed messages into quilts.
