Priya had written that concept for a short story contest years ago. She had the rejection email still in her inbox. She opened her saved document and read it again. The plot details were the same, including the specific pattern of stitches. She put her laptop aside and looked at the book on her nightstand. She then picked it up and placed it in the drawer, closing it slowly.
text_zh: 普里娅读过维克多·黑尔的所有小说。他最新的历史剧作品描述了一个女人把信息缝进被子里。普里娅多年前为一场短篇小说比赛写过这个构思。她的收件箱里还留着那封退稿邮件。她打开保存的文档，又读了一遍。情节细节相同，包括具体的针脚图案。她把笔记本电脑放在一边，看着床头柜上的书。然后她拿起它，放进抽屉里，慢慢关上。

topic: Someone learns their favorite author plagiarized their stories
text_en: Alex was halfway through a new novel by his favorite writer, Sarah Bennett. The book featured a character who solved puzzles left by an estranged uncle. Alex paused. He had written a very similar story for a local writing group. He had the printed copy in a folder. He found it and compared the opening chapters. The uncle's letters were almost identical. He read further and saw more parallels. He put the folder back and continued reading the book for a while, then set it down and went to water the plants.
text_zh: 亚历克斯读到他最喜欢的作家莎拉·贝内特的新小说读到一半。这本书讲述了一个角色解开疏远的叔叔留下的谜题。亚历克斯停了下来。他曾经为当地一个写作小组写过非常相似的故事。他有一份打印稿放在文件夹里。他找到它，比较了开头的章节。叔叔的信几乎一模一样。他继续读下去，看到了更多的相似之处。他把文件夹放回去，继续读了一会儿书，然后放下书，去浇花了。

topic: Someone learns their favorite author plagiarized their stories
text_en: Nina admired the clean prose of her favorite author, David Lin. She was reading his recent essay collection when one piece about growing up near a train station felt too close to a personal essay she had published in a small magazine. She found the old issue and compared the passages. The descriptions of the stationmaster and the waiting room were the same. She placed the magazine on the table and looked at the book. She then closed it and left it on the couch, walking into the kitchen to start dinner.
text_zh: 尼娜欣赏她最喜欢的作家大卫·林的简洁文风。她在读他最近的散文集时，其中一篇关于在火车站附近长大的文章感觉和她在一本小杂志上发表的一篇个人随笔太接近了。她找到那本旧杂志，比较了段落。关于站长和候车室的描述一模一样。她把杂志放在桌子上，看着那本书。然后她合上书，把它留在沙发上，走进厨房开始做晚饭。

topic: Someone learns their favorite author plagiarized their stories
text_en: Chris had been a fan of the thriller writer J. D. Monroe for years. His new book had a scene where a detective finds a clue in a jar of pickles. Chris remembered writing that exact scene for a writing prompt. He searched his old emails and found the prompt and his response. The dialogue was nearly the same. He read the rest of the chapter and noticed other borrowed elements. He closed the email and the book, then went to his bookshelf to see if any other novels had similar passages.
text_zh: 克里斯多年来一直是惊悚小说作家J·D·门罗的粉丝。他的新书中有一个场景是侦探在一罐泡菜里发现线索。克里斯记得自己为一个写作提示写过完全相同的场景。他搜索了自己的旧电子邮件，找到了提示和他的回复。对话几乎相同。他读完了章节的其余部分，注意到其他被借用的元素。他关掉邮件和书，然后走到书架前，看看是否还有其他小说有类似的段落。

topic: Someone learns their favorite author plagiarized their stories
text_en: Marta had just finished the last chapter of the new novel by her favorite author, a writer she had followed for years. As she closed the book, a familiar passage caught her eye—a description of a rainy street that she was sure she had read before, in an old anthology. She pulled the dusty volume from her shelf and found the same scene, word for word. She set the books side by side on the table and started comparing further paragraphs. Her tea went cold as she turned pages. The afternoon passed quietly. She gathered a few more of the author's books and began checking them against the anthology, noting the matches on a scrap of paper.
text_zh: 玛尔塔刚刚读完她最喜欢的作者的新小说的最后一章，这位作者她已经追随多年。合上书时，一段熟悉的段落引起了她的注意——一段对雨街的描写，她确信自己以前在一本旧选集里读过。她从书架上抽出那本布满灰尘的书，发现了同样的场景，一字不差。她把两本书并排放在桌子上，开始比较更多的段落。她翻页时茶都凉了。下午静静地过去了。她又收集了几本这位作者的书，开始对照选集检查，在一张废纸上记下相同之处。

topic: Someone learns their favorite author plagiarized their stories
text_en: Lena received the literary magazine in the mail and settled into her armchair to read the latest short story from her preferred writer. The plot drew her in immediately, yet the phrasing felt oddly familiar. Halfway through, she recognized a sequence of events from a lesser-known collection she had borrowed from the library. She fetched the old book and placed it on the kitchen counter beside the magazine. She read both stories in full, then again, marking lines that were nearly identical. She left them open on the counter and went to make dinner, occasionally glancing over at the pages, her attention repeatedly returning to the overlapping sentences.
text_zh: 莉娜收到了邮寄来的文学杂志，在扶手椅里安顿下来，阅读她偏爱的作家的最新短篇小说。情节立刻吸引了她，但措辞却感觉异常熟悉。读到一半时，她认出了从图书馆借来的一本不太知名的选集中的一系列事件。她取来那本旧书，放在厨房台面上，紧挨着杂志。她把两个故事完整地读了一遍，然后又读了一遍，标记出几乎相同的行句。她把它们摊开放在台面上，去做晚饭，偶尔瞥一眼那些书页，注意力反复回到那些重叠的句子上。

topic: Someone learns their favorite author plagiarized their stories
text_en: Marina had finished the latest novel by her favorite author during her lunch break, and the plot felt uncomfortably familiar. It followed a cartographer who discovered a hidden city beneath a glacier, a story she had submitted to a small press years ago. She pulled up her old manuscript and compared passages, finding whole paragraphs nearly identical. Marina set her phone down and stared at her apartment wall. Her friend called later to ask about dinner, and Marina said she was busy, though she spent the evening rereading her own chapters instead.
text_zh: 玛丽娜在午休时间读完了她最喜欢的作家的最新小说，情节感觉不舒服地熟悉。它讲述了一位制图师发现冰川下隐藏城市的故事，这是她多年前投稿给一家小型出版社的故事。她调出旧手稿进行比较，发现整段整段几乎完全相同。玛丽娜放下手机，盯着公寓的墙壁。她的朋友后来打电话来问晚餐的事，玛丽娜说她很忙，尽管她整个晚上都在重读自己的章节。

topic: Someone learns their favorite author plagiarized their stories
text_en: Ethan noticed that the new short story collection included a piece about a lighthouse keeper who traded memories for supplies. It matched a story he had posted on an old forum under a pseudonym. He scrolled through the forum thread, confirming the dates, then checked the author's acknowledgments page for any mention of him. There was none. Ethan closed his laptop and went to the kitchen to make coffee. When his roommate asked about the collection, Ethan said it was fine and placed it on the shelf with the others.
text_zh: 伊桑注意到新的短篇小说集里有一篇关于灯塔看守人用记忆换取补给的故事。这与他曾在一个旧论坛上以化名发布的故事相符。他滚动浏览论坛帖子，确认了日期，然后检查了作者的致谢页，看是否有提到他。没有。伊桑合上笔记本电脑，去厨房煮咖啡。当室友问起这本选集时，伊桑说还不错，然后把它和其他书一起放到了书架上。

topic: Someone learns their favorite author plagiarized their stories
text_en: Priya listened to the audiobook during her commute, and the chapter about a beekeeper who could hear the thoughts of flowers was almost exactly like the piece she had written for a creative writing workshop. She remembered the feedback from the instructor, who had praised her original idea. Priya replayed the chapter twice, noting the same phrasing and the same quirky dialogue. When she reached her office, she turned off the car and sat for a moment. Then she gathered her bag and walked inside, attending her meetings as usual.
text_zh: 普里娅在通勤途中听有声书，关于一个能听到花朵思想的养蜂人的章节几乎和她为创意写作工作坊写的作品一模一样。她记得导师的反馈，导师曾称赞她原创的想法。普里娅重放了两遍那个章节，注意到相同的措辞和同样古怪的对话。到达办公室后，她关掉汽车，坐了一会儿。然后她拿起包走进去，像往常一样参加会议。

topic: Someone learns their favorite author plagiarized their stories
text_en: Greg was a fan of a comic book writer. He was at a convention and saw a panel about the history of comics. The panelist mentioned an old comic that had a similar storyline to the writer's famous run. Greg found a reprint of the old comic and read it, noticing the same villain and plot twists. He brought it to the writer's booth and asked about it. The writer said they had never seen it, but Greg wasn't sure. He left the convention with the comic, thinking about the similarities.
text_zh: 格雷格是一位漫画作家的粉丝。他在一个漫展上，看到了一个关于漫画历史的座谈会。座谈嘉宾提到了一部旧漫画，其故事情节与那位作家的著名连载相似。格雷格找到那部旧漫画的再版，读了起来，注意到同样的反派和情节转折。他把它带到作家的展位前询问。作家说他们从未见过，但格雷格不确定。他带着那本漫画离开了漫展，思考着这些相似之处。

topic: Someone learns their favorite author plagiarized their stories
text_en: Gabriel's favorite science-fiction writer had a new series out, and he was enjoying the second book when a description of an alien planet reminded him of a novella from a magazine he'd read years ago. He found the back issue in a box in his garage. The planetary system, the climate, even the names of the species were the same. Gabriel spread the issues and the novel on his workbench, checking passages against each other. He used a highlighter to mark matching text. The garage light hummed as he worked. When he was done, he put the novel on the shelf but left the magazine on the bench for the time being.
text_zh: 加布里埃尔最喜欢的科幻作家出了一套新系列，他正在享受第二本书时，一段对外星行星的描述让他想起多年前在一本杂志上读过的中篇小说。他在车库的一个箱子里找到了那期过刊。行星系统、气候，甚至物种的名字都相同。加布里埃尔把杂志和小说摊在工作台上，逐段对照检查。他用荧光笔标记匹配的文本。车库的灯嗡嗡作响，他继续工作。完成后，他把小说放回书架，但暂时把杂志留在了工作台上。

topic: Someone learns their favorite author plagiarized their stories
text_en: Kevin had always admired the way Daniel Marsh wrote about small-town life. When he saw the new novel at the bookstore, he bought it immediately, eager to read it over the weekend. As he turned the pages, he recognized passages—his own descriptions of the diner, the way he'd written about the old bridge. He drove to his studio and pulled out his old notebooks, comparing his drafts to the printed text. The sentences were there, almost verbatim. He closed the book and sat for a long while, staring at his shelves of Daniel Marsh novels that had inspired him.
text_zh: 凯文一直钦佩丹尼尔·马什描写小镇生活的方式。当他在书店看到新小说时，立即买了下来，渴望在周末阅读。翻页时，他认出了段落——他自己对餐馆的描写，他写旧桥的方式。他开车去工作室，拿出旧笔记本，将草稿与印刷文本进行比较。那些句子都在，几乎逐字相同。他合上书，坐了很久，盯着那些曾给他灵感的丹尼尔·马什的小说书架。

topic: Someone learns their favorite author plagiarized their stories
text_en: Lena had sent her story to a contest months ago; the rejection letter was still tucked in a drawer. When the famous author's new collection arrived at the library, she leafed through it and found a story that was hers—the same small town, the same unusual name for the bakery. She checked the copyright page, then borrowed a copy to compare. Her sister asked what she was doing, and Lena said she was just checking something. She read her original side by side with the printed pages, noticing where the author had made small changes. She closed the book and placed it on the table for now.
text_zh: 莉娜几个月前把她的故事寄给了一个比赛；拒绝信还塞在抽屉里。当那位著名作家的新选集到达图书馆时，她翻阅了一下，发现一个故事是她的——同样的小镇，面包店同样不寻常的名字。她检查了版权页，然后借了一本进行比较。她姐姐问她在做什么，莉娜说她只是在查点东西。她将她的原稿与印刷页面并排阅读，注意到作者做了小改动的地方。她合上书，暂时把它放在桌子上。

topic: Someone learns their favorite author plagiarized their stories
text_en: Peter was a collector of first editions. He found a rare book by a famous author at an estate sale. Inside was a letter from an earlier writer mentioning that the author had borrowed ideas from them. Peter read the letter and then the book, noticing the similarities. He placed the letter back inside the book and put it on his shelf. He thought about the author's legacy, then went to his computer to see if anyone else had mentioned the letter, but he found no record. He sat back, thinking about the secret he had uncovered.
text_zh: 彼得是初版书的收藏家。他在一次遗产拍卖会上发现了一本著名作家的稀有书籍。里面有一封早期作家的信，提到那位作家从他们那里借用了想法。彼得读了信，然后读了书，注意到相似之处。他把信放回书里，放在书架上。他思考着那位作家的遗产，然后去电脑前查看是否有人提到过那封信，但没有找到任何记录。他坐回去，思考着他发现的秘密。

topic: Someone discovers their teenager has a secret social media account
text_en: Maya found her son's tablet on the kitchen counter, still lit with a notification from an app she didn't recognize. She tapped it and saw a profile with a handle she'd never heard. The posts were mostly memes and complaints about homework, but there were also photos of him with friends at places he said he wasn't going. She set the tablet down and walked to the living room, where he was doing homework. She asked about the app. He shrugged and said it was just for fun. She didn't push further, but she kept thinking about the photos.
text_zh: 玛雅在厨房台面上发现了儿子的平板电脑，屏幕还亮着，显示着一个她不认识的应用程序的通知。她点了一下，看到一个她从未听过的用户名的个人资料。帖子大多是表情包和对家庭作业的抱怨，但也有他和朋友们的照片，那些地方他说过他不会去。她把平板电脑放下，走到客厅，他正在那里做作业。她问起那个应用程序。他耸耸肩，说只是为了好玩。她没有再追问，但一直在想那些照片。

topic: Someone discovers their teenager has a secret social media account
text_en: The tablet on the coffee table lit up with a message. David glanced at it, expecting a school notification, but the sender name was unfamiliar. It was addressed to his daughter, using a nickname she only used at home. He picked up the tablet and scrolled, finding a profile with photos she hadn't shared with him. He saw posts about her weekend plans and a few comments from friends he didn't know. He put the tablet down, screen facing the table. Later, he asked her about her weekend plans, and she gave a vague answer. He didn't bring up the tablet.
text_zh: 咖啡桌上的平板电脑亮起一条消息。大卫瞥了一眼，以为是学校通知，但发件人的名字很陌生。消息是发给他女儿的，用的是她只在家里用的昵称。他拿起平板电脑，滚动屏幕，发现一个她没给他看过的照片的个人资料。他看到关于她周末计划的帖子，以及一些他不认识的朋友的评论。他把平板电脑放下，屏幕朝下。后来，他问她周末有什么计划，她给出了一个含糊的回答。他没有提起平板电脑。

topic: Someone discovers their teenager has a secret social media account
text_en: Daniel was looking through the family computer's browser history to find a recipe he'd saved. Instead, he found visits to a social site under a username that wasn't his. He clicked on it and saw his daughter's face on the profile picture. The posts were about her daily life, but some mentioned parties and people he didn't know. He closed the browser and went to her room. She was reading. He asked if she had an account he didn't know about. She said yes, but it was private. He nodded and left, wondering what she meant by private.
text_zh: 丹尼尔正在查看家用电脑的浏览器历史记录，想找一个他保存过的食谱。结果，他发现了一个用户名不是他的社交网站的访问记录。他点击进去，看到个人资料照片上是他女儿的脸。帖子是关于她的日常生活的，但有些提到了聚会和他不认识的人。他关闭浏览器，去了她的房间。她正在看书。他问她是否有一个他不知道的账户。她说是的，但那是私密的。他点点头，离开了，心里想着她说的私密是什么意思。

topic: Someone discovers their teenager has a secret social media account
text_en: Marta noticed her son's phone buzzing at odd hours, always face-down on the kitchen counter. One evening, while clearing the table, she picked it up to hand it to him and saw a notification from an account name she didn't recognize. Later that night, she opened her own laptop and typed the handle into a search bar. The profile had a few photos of her son, none recent, and posts about school that were vague. She closed the browser and went to bed, thinking she might mention it to him in the morning, though she hadn't decided what she would say.
text_zh: 玛尔塔注意到儿子的手机在奇怪的时间嗡嗡作响，总是屏幕朝下放在厨房台面上。一天晚上，在收拾桌子时，她拿起手机递给他，看到一个她不认识的账户名的通知。那天深夜，她打开自己的笔记本电脑，在搜索栏里输入了那个用户名。个人资料里有几张她儿子的照片，都不是近期的，还有一些关于学校的模糊帖子。她关闭浏览器，上床睡觉，想着早上可能会跟他提一下，虽然她还没决定要说什么。

topic: Someone discovers their teenager has a secret social media account
text_en: On a Sunday afternoon, Tom was looking for a screwdriver in the garage. He opened a toolbox and found a tablet underneath some rags. It wasn't the family tablet. He turned it on. The screen showed a social media feed for his son, with posts about music and jokes. He saw a comment thread about a school event. Tom closed the tablet and put it back where he found it. He found the screwdriver in another drawer. That night, he asked his son if he had seen the family's spare tablet. His son said no.
text_zh: 一个星期天下午，汤姆在车库里找螺丝刀。他打开一个工具箱，在抹布下面发现了一个平板电脑。那不是家里的平板电脑。他打开它。屏幕上显示的是他儿子的社交媒体信息流，有关于音乐和笑话的帖子。他看到一条关于学校活动的评论串。汤姆合上平板电脑，把它放回原处。他在另一个抽屉里找到了螺丝刀。那天晚上，他问儿子有没有见过家里备用的平板电脑。儿子说没有。

topic: Someone discovers their teenager has a secret social media account
text_en: While paying a household bill, Leo glanced at his daughter's discarded tablet and noticed a social app open with a username he'd never heard her use. He finished his task, then sat down and tapped the profile. It contained short captions under pictures of her friends and places he didn't recognize. He set the tablet down and went to fold laundry in the other room. Later, he asked her about her day, and she gave a usual answer. He didn't bring up the account, but he remembered the name, thinking he might look again sometime.
text_zh: 在支付家庭账单时，利奥瞥了一眼女儿丢弃的平板电脑，注意到一个社交应用开着，用户名是他从未听她用过的。他完成手头的事情，然后坐下来点击那个个人资料。里面有一些简短说明，配着他朋友和地方的图片，他都不认识。他把平板电脑放下，去另一个房间叠衣服。后来，他问她今天过得怎么样，她给出了平常的回答。他没有提起那个账户，但记住了那个名字，想着以后可能还会再看一眼。

topic: Someone discovers their teenager has a secret social media account
text_en: While looking for a charger in the living room, Marcus found a phone wedged between the couch cushions. It had a case he didn't recognize. He picked it up and saw a notification from a social media app. The profile picture was of his daughter, but the username was unfamiliar. He opened the app and saw a few posts, mostly about movies and friends. He put the phone back between the cushions. Later, he asked his daughter if she'd seen his charger. She said she hadn't. He didn't mention the phone.
text_zh: 在客厅找充电器时，马库斯发现沙发垫之间夹着一部手机。手机壳他不认识。他拿起手机，看到一个社交应用的通知。个人资料照片是他女儿，但用户名很陌生。他打开应用，看到一些帖子，大多是关于电影和朋友的。他把手机放回垫子之间。后来，他问女儿有没有看到他的充电器。她说没有。他没有提起手机。

topic: Someone discovers their teenager has a secret social media account
text_en: The family computer was acting up, so Priya went to the browser history to find a troubleshooting page. She saw a long list of visits to a social media site she didn't know. The profile name was her son's, but the email address was different from the one they had on file for him. She cleared the history and ran a disk cleanup. When her son came in, she told him the computer was slow and she'd cleared some files. He thanked her and sat down to use it. She left the room.
text_zh: 家用电脑出了点问题，所以普里亚去浏览器历史记录里找故障排除页面。她看到一长串访问一个她不认识的社交媒体网站的记录。个人资料名字是她儿子的，但电子邮件地址与他们存档的不同。她清除了历史记录，并运行了磁盘清理。当儿子进来时，她告诉他电脑很慢，她清理了一些文件。他谢了她，坐下来使用电脑。她离开了房间。

topic: Someone discovers their teenager has a secret social media account
text_en: Priya was sorting through mail at the kitchen table when her daughter's phone lit up beside her. A message preview showed a reply to a post from an account Priya had never seen. She finished sorting the envelopes, then picked up the phone and opened the profile. It had a few pictures of her daughter's friends and some short comments. Priya put the phone back and continued with her tasks. That evening, she asked her daughter how school was going, and the conversation moved along as usual. The account name stayed in her mind, but she didn't mention it.
text_zh: 普里亚正在厨房桌子上整理邮件，这时女儿的手机在旁边亮了起来。一条消息预览显示了对一个普里亚从未见过的账户的帖子的回复。她整理完信封，然后拿起手机打开个人资料。里面有几张女儿朋友的照片和一些简短评论。普里亚把手机放回去，继续做她的事情。那天晚上，她问女儿学校怎么样，谈话像往常一样进行。那个账户名留在她脑海里，但她没有提起。

topic: Someone discovers their teenager has a secret social media account
text_en: Marcus was paying bills on his laptop when he noticed a browser tab open to a social media profile. He clicked on it and saw his daughter's name, but the profile picture was of a place he didn't recognize. The posts were about a trip she'd supposedly taken last summer, but she'd been home then. He closed the tab and later asked her about it. She said it was an old account she'd made for a game. He didn't believe her, but he didn't push. He just wondered why she'd lie.
text_zh: 马库斯正在笔记本电脑上支付账单，这时他注意到一个浏览器标签页打开着一个社交媒体个人资料。他点击进去，看到女儿的名字，但个人资料照片是一个他不认识的地方。帖子是关于她去年夏天据称去的一次旅行，但那时她在家。他关闭了标签页，后来问她这件事。她说那是一个她为游戏创建的旧账户。他不相信她，但没有追问。他只是想知道她为什么撒谎。

topic: Someone discovers their teenager has a secret social media account
text_en: The family tablet was left on the kitchen table. Laura picked it up to check the weather and saw that the user profile was different from the usual one. It was her daughter's name, but with a different last name. She tapped on it and saw a feed with posts about art and music. There were comments from people she didn't recognize. She switched back to the main profile and checked the weather. When her daughter came home, Laura asked if she had been using the tablet. Her daughter said she had, for homework.
text_zh: 家庭平板电脑被留在厨房桌子上。劳拉拿起它查看天气，发现用户资料与平时不同。上面是她女儿的名字，但姓氏不同。她点击进去，看到一条关于艺术和音乐的动态。有一些她不认识的人的评论。她切换回主资料并查看了天气。当女儿回家时，劳拉问她是否用过平板电脑。女儿说她用过，是为了做作业。

topic: Someone discovers their teenager has a secret social media account
text_en: While looking for a book in his son's room, Daniel noticed a stack of printed pages on the desk. They were screenshots of a social media profile. The profile had his son's first name and a different last name. The posts were about hobbies and friends. Daniel looked at the pages for a moment, then put them back under a notebook. He found the book he was looking for. Later, he asked his son if he had printed anything recently. His son said he hadn't. Daniel nodded and left the room.
text_zh: 在儿子房间找书时，丹尼尔注意到书桌上有一叠打印出来的页面。那是社交媒体资料的截图。资料上有他儿子的名字和一个不同的姓氏。帖子是关于爱好和朋友的。丹尼尔看了这些页面一会儿，然后把它们放回笔记本下面。他找到了他要找的书。后来，他问儿子最近是否打印过什么东西。儿子说没有。丹尼尔点了点头，离开了房间。

topic: Someone discovers their teenager has a secret social media account
text_en: At work, Grace received a friend request from an account that had her daughter's photo as the profile picture. The name was unfamiliar. She clicked on the profile and saw it was private, but the bio mentioned her daughter's school. She ignored the request. That evening, she asked her daughter if she knew of any accounts using her photos. Her daughter said no. Grace said she saw a strange request and just wanted to make sure. Her daughter said it was probably a scam. Grace went back to her laptop.
text_zh: 在工作中，格蕾丝收到一个好友请求，来自一个用她女儿照片作为头像的账户。名字不熟悉。她点击进入个人资料，发现是私密的，但简介提到了她女儿的学校。她忽略了该请求。那天晚上，她问女儿是否知道有账户使用她的照片。女儿说不知道。格蕾丝说她看到了一个奇怪的请求，只是想确认一下。女儿说那可能是诈骗。格蕾丝回到她的笔记本电脑前。

topic: Someone discovers their teenager has a secret social media account
text_en: While cleaning out the car, Victor found a phone under the passenger seat. It was his son's, but not the one he usually used. The screen was locked, but a notification showed a message from a social media app. The sender's name was someone Victor didn't know. He put the phone in the glove compartment. When his son came out to help, Victor asked if he had left his phone in the car. His son said no. Victor said he found one and put it away. His son looked at the glove compartment but didn't open it.
text_zh: 清理汽车时，维克多在副驾驶座下发现了一部手机。那是他儿子的，但不是他通常用的那部。屏幕是锁定的，但一条通知显示来自社交媒体应用的消息。发件人的名字是维克多不认识的人。他把手机放在手套箱里。当儿子出来帮忙时，维克多问他是否把手机落在车里了。儿子说没有。维克多说他在车里发现了一部手机并收了起来。儿子看了看手套箱，但没有打开。

topic: Someone discovers their teenager has a secret social media account
text_en: Jenna found her son's old phone in a drawer while looking for a charger. It turned on and showed a notification from an app. She opened it and saw a profile with his name, but the posts were from a time when he'd been at camp. They showed him at a party with older kids. She put the phone back and didn't mention it. That evening, she asked him about his time at camp. He said it was fine. She wanted to ask more, but she didn't know how to bring it up without admitting she'd looked.
text_zh: 詹娜在抽屉里找充电器时发现了儿子的旧手机。手机开机后显示一条来自某个应用的通知。她打开它，看到一个有他名字的资料，但帖子来自他在夏令营的时候。帖子显示他和年龄较大的孩子一起参加派对。她把手机放回去，没有提起。那天晚上，她问他夏令营过得怎么样。他说挺好的。她想问更多，但不知道如何开口而不承认自己看过手机。

topic: Someone discovers their teenager has a secret social media account
text_en: During a quiet afternoon, Tom found his son's old laptop left open on the couch. A social media page was visible, with a username Tom didn't recognize. He read a few posts, mostly about sports and music, and saw some photos of his son with people he didn't know. Tom closed the laptop and placed it on the desk. Later, he mentioned to his wife that their son seemed to have an account they hadn't known about. She shrugged and said teenagers did that sometimes. Tom nodded and went back to reading the newspaper, leaving the laptop where it was.
text_zh: 在一个安静的下午，汤姆发现儿子的旧笔记本电脑开着放在沙发上。一个社交媒体页面可见，用户名汤姆不认识。他读了几条帖子，大多是关于体育和音乐的，还看到一些儿子和他不认识的人的照片。汤姆合上笔记本电脑，把它放在书桌上。后来，他向妻子提到儿子似乎有一个他们不知道的账户。她耸耸肩说青少年有时会这样。汤姆点了点头，继续看报纸，把笔记本电脑留在原处。

topic: Someone discovers their teenager has a secret social media account
text_en: Elena was unpacking groceries when her son's phone slid off the counter and landed at her feet. The screen showed a notification from a profile with a nickname she'd never heard. She picked up the phone, set it on the table, and continued putting away food. After she finished, she sat down and looked at the account, scrolling through a few posts about classes and weekend plans. She recognized some of the names in the comments. She put the phone back and started dinner. When her son came in, she asked him to wash the vegetables, and he did. Neither mentioned the phone.
text_zh: 埃琳娜正在整理杂货时，儿子的手机从柜台上滑落，掉在她脚边。屏幕显示一条来自一个她从未听过的昵称的资料的通知。她捡起手机，放在桌子上，继续收拾食物。完成后，她坐下来查看账户，滚动浏览了几条关于课程和周末计划的帖子。她认出评论中的一些名字。她把手机放回去，开始做晚饭。儿子进来时，她让他洗蔬菜，他照做了。两人都没有提到手机。

topic: Someone discovers their teenager has a secret social media account
text_en: While looking for a stamp in the desk drawer, Frank found a small notebook. It was his daughter's, and it contained a list of usernames and passwords for various sites. Most were for games, but one was for a social media site he didn't recognize. He closed the notebook and put it back. He found the stamps in another drawer. Later, he asked his daughter if she had any accounts that required passwords. She said she had a few for games. He said okay and went to mail a letter.
text_zh: 在书桌抽屉里找邮票时，弗兰克发现了一个小笔记本。那是他女儿的，里面列出了各种网站的用户名和密码。大多数是游戏的，但有一个是他不认识的社交媒体网站。他合上笔记本，放回原处。他在另一个抽屉里找到了邮票。后来，他问女儿是否有需要密码的账户。她说她有几个游戏的。他说好的，然后去寄信了。

topic: Someone discovers their teenager has a secret social media account
text_en: The family's Wi-Fi router had a parental control app. While checking the usage logs, Beth noticed a lot of traffic to a social media site during school hours. The device listed was her daughter's phone. She looked at the site's name and didn't recognize it. She turned off the router and went to bed. The next morning, she asked her daughter if she had been on her phone during class. Her daughter said she hadn't. Beth said the router showed some activity. Her daughter shrugged and said it must have been a glitch.
text_zh: 家里的Wi-Fi路由器有一个家长控制应用。在检查使用日志时，贝丝注意到上课时间有大量流量流向一个社交媒体网站。列出的设备是她女儿的手机。她看了看网站名称，不认识。她关掉路由器，上床睡觉。第二天早上，她问女儿是否在课堂上用手机。女儿说没有。贝丝说路由器显示了一些活动。女儿耸耸肩说那一定是故障。

topic: Someone discovers their teenager has a secret social media account
text_en: During a quiet evening, Paula was scrolling through her own social media feed when she saw a comment from an account that had her daughter's profile picture but a different name. The comment was on a post about a local event. She clicked on the account and saw a few posts, mostly about hobbies and school. She didn't mention it to her daughter, but she kept the account in mind. The next day, she noticed her daughter using her phone more often than usual, and she wondered about the connection.
text_zh: 在一个安静的晚上，保拉正在浏览自己的社交媒体动态，她看到一条来自一个账户的评论，该账户使用她女儿的头像但名字不同。评论是关于一个本地活动的帖子。她点击进入该账户，看到几条帖子，大多是关于爱好和学校的。她没有向女儿提起，但记住了这个账户。第二天，她注意到女儿比平时更频繁地使用手机，她想知道其中的联系。

topic: Two friends plan separate birthday parties on the same day
text_en: Mara and Jenna had been friends since college, and both had birthdays in the same week. This year, they each decided to throw a party on Saturday without checking with the other. Mara booked a small room at a local cafe and ordered a cake with her name on it. Jenna planned a backyard barbecue and bought decorations. When they finally spoke on Thursday, Jenna mentioned the barbecue. Mara paused, realizing the date. She said she had already reserved the cafe. They agreed to figure something out later, but neither changed their plans. Saturday arrived with both events on the calendar.
text_zh: 玛拉和珍娜从大学起就是朋友，她们的生日都在同一周。今年，她们各自决定在周六举办派对，而没有互相商量。玛拉在当地一家咖啡馆订了一个小房间，并订了一个写有她名字的蛋糕。珍娜计划在后院烧烤，并买了装饰品。当她们终于在周四通话时，珍娜提到了烧烤。玛拉停顿了一下，意识到日期冲突。她说她已经预订了咖啡馆。她们同意稍后再想办法，但谁也没有改变计划。周六到来时，两个活动都排在了日程上。

topic: Two friends plan separate birthday parties on the same day
text_en: Leo had reserved the back room of a pizzeria for his birthday. His friend Sam had reserved the same room for his own party on the same day. When Leo arrived early, he found Sam already there, arranging a banner. They stared at each other for a moment, then Leo said, "Well, this is a thing." They decided to share the space, each keeping their own cake and guests. The room was a bit crowded, but people mingled. Leo spent most of the evening talking with his friends, occasionally nodding to Sam's side. At the end, they helped each other clean up.
text_zh: 利奥为他的生日预订了披萨店的包间。他的朋友萨姆在同一天为自己的派对预订了同一个房间。利奥提前到达时，发现萨姆已经在那里布置横幅了。他们面面相觑了一会儿，然后利奥说：“嗯，这可真是巧了。”他们决定共用这个空间，各自保留自己的蛋糕和客人。房间有点拥挤，但人们互相交流。利奥大部分时间都在和朋友们聊天，偶尔向萨姆那边点头致意。最后，他们互相帮忙打扫卫生。

topic: Two friends plan separate birthday parties on the same day
text_en: Priya and her friend Ravi had planned separate gatherings for their birthdays, both on the same day. Priya had booked a park pavilion, and Ravi had booked the same pavilion for the afternoon. When Priya arrived with her decorations, she found Ravi's family already there. They exchanged apologetic looks and then decided to combine the picnics. The children played together, and the adults shared food. Priya and Ravi took turns cutting their cakes. It wasn't what either had imagined, but the afternoon passed pleasantly, with both groups mingling and the birthday songs happening one after another.
text_zh: 普里亚和她的朋友拉维为他们的生日分别计划了聚会，都在同一天。普里亚预订了一个公园凉亭，拉维也预订了同一个凉亭，时间是下午。当普里亚带着装饰品到达时，发现拉维的家人已经在那里了。他们交换了歉意的眼神，然后决定合并野餐。孩子们一起玩耍，大人们分享食物。普里亚和拉维轮流切蛋糕。这虽然不是他们各自想象的样子，但下午过得很愉快，两个群体互相交流，生日歌一首接一首地唱。

topic: Two friends plan separate birthday parties on the same day
text_en: Diego and Sam were roommates who shared a birthday month. Diego wanted a quiet dinner with a few friends, so he made reservations at his favorite Italian place. Sam, however, had been planning a larger get-together at a nearby park for weeks. He sent out invites and bought a piñata. On the morning of the day, Diego saw the park setup on Sam's phone. He mentioned his dinner reservation. Sam looked at the calendar and realized the overlap. They each went ahead with their own plans, splitting the guest list between them.
text_zh: 迭戈和萨姆是室友，他们的生日在同一个月。迭戈想和几个朋友安静地吃顿饭，于是在他最喜欢的意大利餐厅订了位。然而，萨姆几周来一直在计划在附近公园举办一个更大的聚会。他发出了邀请，并买了一个皮纳塔。当天早上，迭戈在萨姆的手机上看到了公园布置。他提到了自己的晚餐预订。萨姆看了看日历，意识到日期重叠了。他们各自按自己的计划进行，把客人名单分开了。

topic: Two friends plan separate birthday parties on the same day
text_en: Aisha had planned a dinner party at her apartment for her birthday. Her friend Samira had also planned a dinner party at her own place on the same day. They talked on the phone in the morning, each mentioning final preparations. Only later did they realize the date matched. They considered rescheduling one, but both had guests already committed. They decided to go ahead separately, each hosting her own party. Aisha cooked her favorite dishes, and her guests arrived on time. She spent the evening serving food and chatting. Samira texted her a photo of her cake, and Aisha replied with a photo of hers.
text_zh: 艾莎计划在她的公寓为她的生日举办一个晚宴。她的朋友萨米拉也计划在同一天在她自己家举办晚宴。她们早上通了电话，各自提到最后的准备工作。直到后来她们才意识到日期相同。她们考虑改期其中一个，但双方都有客人已经确定要来。她们决定各自分开举办，各自主持自己的派对。艾莎做了她最喜欢的菜，客人们准时到达。她整晚都在上菜和聊天。萨米拉给她发了一张她蛋糕的照片，艾莎也回了一张她的蛋糕照片。

topic: Two friends plan separate birthday parties on the same day
text_en: Carlos and his friend Miguel had each booked a lane at a bowling alley for their birthdays, both for the same evening. Carlos arrived with his coworkers and saw Miguel's family at the next lane. They high-fived and decided to keep their reservations, but move the lanes closer. They played a few frames together, then split back to their own groups. Carlos focused on his game, enjoying the competitive banter with his friends. Miguel did the same. At the end, they exchanged birthday wishes and went their separate ways, each satisfied with how the evening had turned out.
text_zh: 卡洛斯和他的朋友米格尔各自为他们的生日预订了保龄球馆的一条球道，都是在同一个晚上。卡洛斯和同事们到达时，看到米格尔的家人在隔壁球道。他们击掌庆祝，并决定保留预订，但把球道移近一些。他们一起打了几局，然后又各自回到自己的小组。卡洛斯专注于比赛，享受着与朋友们的竞争性调侃。米格尔也是如此。最后，他们互致生日祝福，然后各自离开，都对晚上的结果感到满意。

topic: Two friends plan separate birthday parties on the same day
text_en: Hannah and her friend Grace had both planned beach picnics for their birthdays on the same day. Hannah arrived at the usual spot and saw Grace's blanket already spread. They laughed about it and set up their picnics side by side. Each had brought her own food and decorations. They shared some snacks and took photos of each other's groups. Hannah played frisbee with her friends, Grace went for a walk with hers. In the evening, they both lit candles on their cakes and sang for each other. The sunset was nice, and they packed up together.
text_zh: 汉娜和她的朋友格蕾丝都计划在同一天为她们的生日举办海滩野餐。汉娜到达常去的地点，看到格蕾丝的毯子已经铺好了。她们对此大笑，然后把野餐并排摆好。每个人都带了自己的食物和装饰品。她们分享了一些零食，并互相给对方的团体拍照。汉娜和朋友们玩飞盘，格蕾丝和她的朋友们去散步。晚上，她们都在蛋糕上点燃蜡烛，互相唱歌。日落很美，她们一起收拾东西。

topic: Two friends plan separate birthday parties on the same day
text_en: Priya and her brother Ravi shared the same birthday. This year, Priya decided to host a brunch at her apartment for her coworkers. Ravi, meanwhile, had arranged a game night at his place with his old school friends. Neither told the other about the specific time. On the day, Priya was arranging pastries when Ravi called to ask if she could pick up extra chairs. She said she was busy until afternoon. Ravi said his guests were coming at noon. Priya realized the conflict but had already prepared food. She wished him well and hung up, continuing to set the table.
text_zh: 普里亚和她的兄弟拉维同一天生日。今年，普里亚决定在她的公寓为同事们举办早午餐。与此同时，拉维安排在他的住处和旧校友们玩游戏之夜。两人都没有告诉对方具体时间。当天，普里亚正在摆放糕点时，拉维打电话问她能否带些额外的椅子过来。她说她忙到下午。拉维说他的客人中午到。普里亚意识到冲突，但已经准备好了食物。她祝他一切顺利，然后挂了电话，继续摆桌子。

topic: Two friends plan separate birthday parties on the same day
text_en: Mara and Jenna had chosen the same Saturday for their birthday get-togethers months earlier, each unaware of the overlap. On the morning of the event, Mara reviewed her guest list and noticed Jenna's name, realizing the conflict. She called Jenna, who answered with a similar concern. They agreed to split the day, with Mara hosting a brunch and Jenna an evening gathering. Mara rearranged her table settings and adjusted the menu, then sent a quick text to their mutual friends explaining the revised plan. By noon, the first guests arrived, and Mara welcomed them warmly, keeping the conversation light and easy.
text_zh: 玛拉和珍娜几个月前就选择了同一个周六来举办她们的生日聚会，两人都没有意识到日期重叠。活动当天早上，玛拉检查了她的客人名单，注意到珍娜的名字，意识到冲突。她打电话给珍娜，珍娜接电话时也有类似的担忧。她们同意把这一天分开，玛拉举办早午餐，珍娜举办晚间聚会。玛拉重新调整了餐桌布置和菜单，然后给共同的朋友们发了一条简短的信息，解释修改后的计划。中午时分，第一批客人到了，玛拉热情地欢迎他们，让谈话保持轻松愉快。

topic: Two friends plan separate birthday parties on the same day
text_en: Tomas and his cousin Marta both had birthdays on the same day. Tomas planned a fishing trip with his uncles, leaving early in the morning. Marta arranged a family dinner at her house in the evening. They assumed the other knew about the plans. On the day, Tomas came back from fishing in the afternoon and found a message from Marta asking him to bring dessert. He realized the dinner was that evening. He had already eaten with the uncles but said he would stop by later. Marta's dinner went ahead as planned, and Tomas arrived after the main course, just in time for cake.
text_zh: 托马斯和他的表妹玛尔塔同一天生日。托马斯计划和叔叔们去钓鱼，一大早就出发了。玛尔塔安排晚上在她家举行家庭晚宴。他们都以为对方知道这些计划。当天下午，托马斯钓鱼回来，发现玛尔塔发来一条信息，让他带甜点来。他意识到晚宴就在当晚。他已经和叔叔们吃过饭了，但他说稍后会过去。玛尔塔的晚宴按计划进行，托马斯在主菜之后到达，正好赶上吃蛋糕。

topic: Two friends plan separate birthday parties on the same day
text_en: Nina and her friend Rachel had each planned a movie marathon at home for their birthdays, both on the same day. They talked on the phone in the morning and discovered the overlap. They decided to have a joint marathon at Rachel's place, since she had a bigger TV. They combined their snack supplies and movie lists. Nina brought her favorite films, Rachel contributed hers. They spent the afternoon watching, pausing only to eat and discuss scenes. When the cake came out, they both blew out the candles together. It was a long day, but they got through most of the list.
text_zh: 尼娜和她的朋友瑞秋各自计划在家举办电影马拉松来庆祝生日，而且都在同一天。早上她们通电话时发现了这个重叠。她们决定在瑞秋家联合举办马拉松，因为她的电视更大。她们合并了零食供应和电影清单。尼娜带来了她最喜欢的电影，瑞秋贡献了她的。她们花了整个下午观看，只在吃东西和讨论场景时暂停。当蛋糕端出来时，她们一起吹灭了蜡烛。这是漫长的一天，但她们看完了大部分清单。

topic: Two friends plan separate birthday parties on the same day
text_en: Omar and his friend Tariq had both rented a small party room at a community center for their birthday parties, both for the same afternoon. Omar arrived first and set up his decorations. Tariq came in with his own supplies and stopped short. They looked at the room, then at each other. They decided to share the space, each keeping his own table. The room was large enough for both groups. Omar played music from his playlist, Tariq brought his own speaker. They took turns hosting games. By the end, the room was a mix of both parties, and everyone seemed to have a good time.
text_zh: 奥马尔和他的朋友塔里克都在社区中心租了一个小派对房间来举办生日派对，而且都是同一个下午。奥马尔先到，布置好了他的装饰。塔里克带着自己的用品进来，突然停住了。他们看了看房间，又看了看对方。他们决定共用这个空间，各自保留自己的桌子。房间足够大，能容纳两个团体。奥马尔播放他播放列表里的音乐，塔里克带来了自己的扬声器。他们轮流主持游戏。到最后，房间成了两个派对的混合体，每个人似乎都玩得很开心。

topic: Two friends plan separate birthday parties on the same day
text_en: Sofia and her friend Elena had each planned a cooking party for their birthdays, both on the same evening. Sofia had invited friends to her apartment to make pasta; Elena had invited hers to make pizza. They discovered the conflict when they texted about grocery lists. They decided to combine the events at Sofia's place, since her kitchen was bigger. Everyone pitched in, and they made both pasta and pizza. Sofia showed her friends how to roll dough, Elena taught her sauce recipe. They ate together, and both women received small gifts. The kitchen was a mess, but they all helped clean up.
text_zh: 索菲亚和她的朋友埃琳娜各自计划在同一个晚上举办烹饪派对来庆祝生日。索菲亚邀请了朋友到她的公寓做意大利面；埃琳娜邀请了朋友做披萨。当她们发短信讨论购物清单时发现了冲突。她们决定把活动合并到索菲亚家，因为她的厨房更大。每个人都参与进来，既做了意大利面也做了披萨。索菲亚向朋友们展示如何擀面团，埃琳娜教她的酱汁配方。她们一起吃饭，两位女士都收到了小礼物。厨房一片狼藉，但她们都帮忙清理了。

topic: Two friends plan separate birthday parties on the same day
text_en: Liam had been planning his birthday barbecue for weeks, and his friend Sam had mentioned a small dinner party on the same date. Neither had checked the other's calendar, so when Liam called Sam to confirm a time, Sam said, 'I'm having people over that night.' They both paused, then Liam suggested they combine efforts. Sam agreed, and they decided to host a joint cookout at a nearby park. Liam took charge of the grill, while Sam brought sides and drinks. The afternoon passed with games and conversation, and by evening, the group had naturally split into smaller clusters, everyone enjoying the shared celebration without fuss.
text_zh: 利亚姆已经计划他的生日烧烤好几个星期了，他的朋友萨姆提到在同一天有一个小型晚宴。两人都没有查看对方的日历，所以当利亚姆打电话给萨姆确认时间时，萨姆说：“那天晚上我邀请了人来家里。”他们都停顿了一下，然后利亚姆建议他们联合起来。萨姆同意了，他们决定在附近的公园举办联合烧烤。利亚姆负责烤架，萨姆带来了配菜和饮料。下午在游戏和交谈中度过，到了晚上，人群自然地分成更小的群体，每个人都毫无拘束地享受共同的庆祝活动。

topic: Two friends plan separate birthday parties on the same day
text_en: Paula and her friend Monica had both planned to visit a local art museum on their birthdays, as they each loved the current exhibit. They ran into each other at the ticket counter. They decided to tour together, since they had similar taste. They walked through the galleries, pausing to discuss the paintings. Paula preferred the modern wing, Monica liked the classical. They split up for a while, then met for lunch at the museum café. They each had a small dessert to celebrate. They exchanged birthday wishes and agreed it had been a nice way to spend the day.
text_zh: 宝拉和她的朋友莫妮卡都计划在生日那天参观当地的艺术博物馆，因为她们都喜欢当前的展览。她们在售票处偶遇。她们决定一起参观，因为她们品味相似。她们走过画廊，停下来讨论画作。宝拉更喜欢现代馆，莫妮卡喜欢古典馆。她们分开了一段时间，然后在博物馆咖啡馆见面吃午餐。她们各自吃了一个小甜点来庆祝。她们互致生日祝福，并一致认为这是度过这一天的一种好方式。

topic: Two friends plan separate birthday parties on the same day
text_en: Maya and Priya had been friends since college, and their birthdays fell on the same date. This year, each had quietly planned separate gatherings. Maya booked a small room at a local café and invited a handful of close colleagues. Priya arranged a backyard barbecue with her extended family. They hadn't discussed it, each assuming the other would want their own celebration. On the morning of the day, Maya texted Priya about the café reservation. Priya replied with details of her barbecue. They agreed to meet for coffee afterward, each attending their own event first. The day proceeded with both parties going smoothly.
text_zh: 玛雅和普里亚从大学起就是朋友，她们的生日在同一天。今年，她们各自悄悄计划了单独的聚会。玛雅在当地一家咖啡馆订了一个小房间，邀请了几位关系密切的同事。普里亚安排了一个后院烧烤，邀请了她的大家庭。她们没有讨论过这件事，都以为对方想要自己的庆祝活动。当天早上，玛雅给普里亚发短信说咖啡馆的预订。普里亚回复了她烧烤的细节。她们同意之后见面喝咖啡，各自先参加自己的活动。这一天顺利进行，两个派对都进展顺利。

topic: Two friends plan separate birthday parties on the same day
text_en: Tina and her friend Laura had both planned a karaoke night at a bar for their birthdays, both on the same evening. Tina arrived with her group and saw Laura with hers. They waved and decided to share the stage, taking turns picking songs. Tina sang her favorite ballad, Laura did a duet with a friend. They cheered for each other's performances. The bar was busy, but they managed to get enough turns. At the end of the night, the bartender brought out a small cake with candles for both of them. They blew them out together and then sang one last song as a group.
text_zh: 蒂娜和她的朋友劳拉都计划在酒吧举办卡拉OK之夜来庆祝生日，而且都在同一个晚上。蒂娜和她的团队到达时看到了劳拉和她的团队。她们挥手致意，决定共用舞台，轮流选歌。蒂娜唱了她最喜欢的民谣，劳拉和朋友合唱了一首。她们为彼此的表演欢呼。酒吧很忙，但她们设法得到了足够多的机会。晚上结束时，酒保端出一个带蜡烛的小蛋糕给她们俩。她们一起吹灭蜡烛，然后作为团体唱了最后一首歌。

topic: Two friends plan separate birthday parties on the same day
text_en: Tom and his friend Sarah had both promised their families separate birthday dinners on the same Sunday. Tom only realized the overlap when Sarah mentioned her reservation at a restaurant he had also booked. He called her, and they laughed about the coincidence. They considered swapping times, but both had relatives who preferred their current slots. So they decided to keep their own plans and simply wish each other well over the phone. Tom drove to his parents' place, where his mother had prepared his favorite meal. He ate, chatted with his siblings, and later texted Sarah a photo of his dessert. She replied with a picture of her own cake.
text_zh: 汤姆和他的朋友莎拉都答应过家人在同一个周日举办单独的生日晚餐。汤姆直到莎拉提到她在一家他也预订过的餐厅的预订时才意识到重叠。他打电话给她，他们对这个巧合大笑。他们考虑过交换时间，但双方都有亲戚更喜欢他们当前的时间段。所以他们决定保留各自的计划，只是通过电话互相祝福。汤姆开车去他父母家，他母亲准备了他最喜欢的饭菜。他吃了饭，和兄弟姐妹聊天，后来给莎拉发了一张他甜点的照片。她回复了一张她自己蛋糕的照片。

topic: Two friends plan separate birthday parties on the same day
text_en: Rosa and her friend Carmen had both planned a spa day for their birthdays, booking the same salon and the same time slot. Rosa arrived for her massage and saw Carmen in the waiting area. They laughed and decided to share the appointment, taking turns with the treatments. Rosa had a facial, Carmen had a manicure. They chatted in the lounge between services. They each got a small gift from the staff. Afterward, they went for coffee and compared notes on their treatments. They agreed it had been a relaxing way to spend their birthdays, even if it wasn't what either had originally planned.
text_zh: 罗莎和她的朋友卡门都计划在生日那天做水疗，预订了同一家沙龙和同一个时间段。罗莎来做按摩时看到卡门在等候区。她们笑了，决定共用预约，轮流做护理。罗莎做了面部护理，卡门做了美甲。她们在服务间隙在休息室聊天。她们各自从工作人员那里得到了一份小礼物。之后，她们去喝咖啡，比较了护理心得。她们一致认为这是度过生日的一种放松方式，即使这不是她们原本计划的。

topic: Two friends plan separate birthday parties on the same day
text_en: Rosa and her best friend Mei had both scheduled their birthday parties for the same Saturday evening, each assuming the other knew. When Rosa sent out invitations, she noticed Mei's name on the list and realized the conflict. She called Mei, who said, 'Oh no, I already sent mine too.' They decided to merge their guest lists and host a combined party at Rosa's apartment. Rosa prepared a punch bowl, and Mei brought a tray of sandwiches. Their friends mingled, moving between the kitchen and living room. At one point, both women stood near the window, watching the group laugh and talk, and Rosa remarked that the party felt bigger than either had planned. Mei agreed, and they continued circulating among their guests.
text_zh: 罗莎和她最好的朋友梅都把自己的生日派对安排在同一个周六晚上，都以为对方知道。当罗莎发出邀请时，她注意到名单上有梅的名字，意识到了冲突。她打电话给梅，梅说：“哦不，我也已经发出去了。”她们决定合并宾客名单，在罗莎的公寓举办联合派对。罗莎准备了一大碗潘趣酒，梅带来了一盘三明治。她们的朋友们混在一起，在厨房和客厅之间穿梭。有一次，两个女人都站在窗边，看着大家欢笑交谈，罗莎说这个派对感觉比她们任何一个人计划的都要大。梅同意，她们继续在宾客中穿梭。

topic: A musician hears their song being performed by someone else
text_en: Maya was walking through the farmer's market when she heard a familiar melody. A young woman with a guitar was playing a song Maya had written years ago. She stood by a stall of tomatoes, listening. The woman sang the chorus slightly differently, stretching a note that Maya had always kept short. Maya watched the small crowd gather. When the song ended, the woman smiled and thanked everyone. Maya picked up a tomato, paid for it, and continued her walk. She thought about how the song had taken on a life of its own, shaped by someone else's voice. It was a strange feeling, but she didn't dwell on it. She had plans to meet a friend for lunch.
text_zh: 玛雅正穿过农贸市场，这时她听到了一段熟悉的旋律。一个拿着吉他的年轻女子正在弹唱一首玛雅多年前写的歌。她站在一个卖西红柿的摊位旁听着。那个女子唱副歌时稍有不同，拉长了一个玛雅总是唱得很短的音符。玛雅看着一小群人聚拢过来。歌曲结束时，女子微笑着向大家道谢。玛雅拿起一个西红柿，付了钱，继续她的散步。她想着这首歌如何有了自己的生命，被别人的声音所塑造。那是一种奇怪的感觉，但她没有多想。她计划和朋友见面吃午饭。

topic: A musician hears their song being performed by someone else
text_en: Ethan sat in the waiting room of the auto repair shop. From the speaker above the door, a soft acoustic version of a song he had recorded with his band started playing. He recognized the chord progression immediately, though the arrangement was stripped down. The singer was a woman, her voice lower than his. She sang the lyrics clearly, and Ethan found himself mouthing along. The receptionist tapped her fingers on the desk. When the song ended, a commercial for a local furniture store came on. Ethan picked up a magazine and flipped through it. He wondered if anyone else in the room knew who had written the song. His car was ready, and he paid the bill.
text_zh: 伊桑坐在汽车修理店的等候区。门上方扬声器里开始播放一首他和他乐队录制过的歌曲的轻柔原声版本。他立刻认出了和弦进行，尽管编曲被简化了。歌手是位女性，声音比他的低。她清晰地唱着歌词，伊桑发现自己跟着默唱。前台小姐用手指敲着桌面。歌曲结束时，播出了一个本地家具店的广告。伊桑拿起一本杂志翻看。他想着房间里是否还有其他人知道这首歌是谁写的。他的车修好了，他付了账单。

topic: A musician hears their song being performed by someone else
text_en: Nadia was browsing in a used bookstore when she heard a piano piece drifting from the back room. It was a composition she had written for her grandmother's memorial. She recognized the gentle left-hand pattern and the rising melody. The pianist played it slower than she had, giving it a more somber tone. Nadia walked toward the back room and saw an older man at an upright piano, a stack of sheet music beside him. He played the final chord and paused. She turned away and continued browsing the shelves. She found a book of poetry she had been looking for. At the counter, she paid and left without mentioning the music.
text_zh: 纳迪亚正在一家二手书店浏览，这时她听到从后屋传来一段钢琴曲。那是她为祖母的追悼会写的一首曲子。她认出了轻柔的左手伴奏型和上扬的旋律。钢琴家弹得比她慢，赋予了它更忧郁的基调。纳迪亚走向后屋，看到一位年长的男子在立式钢琴前，旁边放着一叠乐谱。他弹完最后一个和弦，停了下来。她转过身，继续浏览书架。她找到了一本她一直在找的诗集。在柜台付了钱，她离开了，没有提及那音乐。

topic: A musician hears their song being performed by someone else
text_en: Liam was jogging along the river path when he heard a busker playing a song he had written for a school project. The busker, a middle-aged man with a harmonica, played the main riff and sang the verses with a gravelly voice. Liam slowed to a walk. The song had been about a summer trip with his cousins. The busker's version was faster, more upbeat. A few people tossed coins into his open guitar case. Liam stood for a moment, then continued his run. He thought about how the song had been a class assignment, not something he had planned to share widely. He turned up the path toward the bridge.
text_zh: 利亚姆正沿着河边小路慢跑，这时他听到一个街头艺人弹唱一首他为学校项目写的歌。那个街头艺人是个中年男子，带着口琴，弹着主旋律，用沙哑的嗓音唱着主歌。利亚姆放慢速度，改为步行。这首歌是关于他和表兄弟们的一次夏日旅行。街头艺人的版本更快，更欢快。几个人往他打开的吉他盒里扔硬币。利亚姆站了一会儿，然后继续跑步。他想着这首歌原本只是课堂作业，并不是他打算广泛分享的东西。他转向通往桥的小路。

topic: A musician hears their song being performed by someone else
text_en: Priya was waiting for her coffee at a small café when she heard a song she had written in college. It was playing through the café's speakers, a cover by a band she didn't recognize. The original was a quiet ballad, but this version had a driving drumbeat and electric guitar. She listened to the lyrics, which she remembered writing in a notebook during a late-night study session. The song was about a lost key, a metaphor she had been proud of. The barista called her name. She picked up her latte and sat by the window. The song ended and another one began. She stirred her coffee and watched the rain.
text_zh: 普里亚正在一家小咖啡馆等她的咖啡，这时她听到一首她在大学时写的歌。这首歌通过咖啡馆的扬声器播放，是一个她不认识的乐队的翻唱版本。原曲是一首安静的民谣，但这个版本有强劲的鼓点和电吉他。她听着歌词，她记得那是在一次深夜学习时在笔记本上写的。这首歌是关于一把丢失的钥匙，一个她曾引以为豪的隐喻。咖啡师叫了她的名字。她拿起拿铁，坐在窗边。歌曲结束，另一首开始。她搅拌着咖啡，看着雨。

topic: A musician hears their song being performed by someone else
text_en: Owen was in a department store, looking for a new belt, when he heard a song he had composed for a friend's wedding. The melody came through the store's overhead speakers, a soft piano version. He recognized the part he had written for the bride's walk down the aisle. The arrangement was simpler than his original, with only piano and a light string section. Owen held a belt in his hand, checking the size. The song continued as he walked to the checkout. The cashier scanned his purchase. He heard the final notes as he left the store. He put the belt in his bag and headed to his car.
text_zh: 欧文在一家百货商店里找一条新皮带，这时他听到一首他为朋友的婚礼创作的歌曲。旋律从商店的头顶扬声器传来，是一个轻柔的钢琴版本。他认出了他为新娘走红毯时写的部分。编曲比他的原版更简单，只有钢琴和轻量的弦乐部分。欧文手里拿着一条皮带，检查尺寸。他走向收银台时，歌曲还在继续。收银员扫描了他的购买物品。他离开商店时听到了最后的音符。他把皮带放进包里，走向他的车。

topic: A musician hears their song being performed by someone else
text_en: Grace was at a community pool, watching her niece swim. From a portable speaker on the deck, a song she had recorded with her old band started playing. It was a rock song about a road trip. The version playing was a live recording, with a crowd cheering in the background. Grace recognized her own guitar part, though the mix was different. Her niece splashed to the edge of the pool. Grace waved. The song ended and a pop song came on. She put on her sunglasses and leaned back in her chair. She thought about the recording session, which had been in a small studio downtown.
text_zh: 格蕾丝在社区游泳池，看着她侄女游泳。从甲板上的便携音箱里，开始播放一首她和她的老乐队录制的歌曲。那是一首关于公路旅行的摇滚歌曲。播放的版本是现场录音，背景有人群欢呼声。格蕾丝认出了自己的吉他部分，尽管混音不同。她侄女溅着水花游到池边。格蕾丝挥了挥手。歌曲结束，一首流行歌曲开始播放。她戴上太阳镜，靠在椅子上。她想起了那次录音，是在市中心的一个小录音棚里。

topic: A musician hears their song being performed by someone else
text_en: Daniel was in an elevator at his office building. The elevator music was a jazz arrangement of a song he had written for a friend's short film. The original was a simple acoustic tune, but this version had a saxophone and a walking bass line. Daniel recognized the melody, though the rhythm was swung differently. He rode to the fifth floor, where the doors opened. He stepped out and walked to his cubicle. He sat down at his desk and opened his laptop. The song had been a side project, not something he had promoted. He checked his email and started on a report.
text_zh: 丹尼尔在他办公楼的电梯里。电梯音乐是一首他为朋友的短片创作的歌曲的爵士改编版。原曲是一首简单的原声曲调，但这个版本有萨克斯风和行走低音线。丹尼尔认出了旋律，尽管节奏的摇摆方式不同。他乘电梯到五楼，门开了。他走出去，走向他的隔间。他在办公桌前坐下，打开笔记本电脑。那首歌只是一个副业项目，不是他推广过的东西。他查看了电子邮件，开始写报告。

topic: A musician hears their song being performed by someone else
text_en: Sofia was in a grocery store, picking out avocados, when she heard a song she had written for a talent show in high school. It was playing through the store's sound system, a country version with a fiddle. The original was a pop song with a synth beat. She remembered practicing the lyrics in her bedroom. The version playing had different instrumentation but the same chorus. She put the avocados in her cart and moved to the produce section. The song faded out and an advertisement for a sale came on. She continued down the aisle, checking her list for the rest of the items.
text_zh: 索菲亚在一家杂货店里挑选牛油果，这时她听到一首她为高中才艺表演写的歌。这首歌通过商店的音响系统播放，是一个带小提琴的乡村版本。原曲是一首带合成器节拍的流行歌曲。她记得在卧室里练习歌词的情景。播放的版本乐器不同，但副歌一样。她把牛油果放进购物车，走到农产品区。歌曲淡出，一个促销广告开始播放。她继续沿着过道走，检查清单上剩下的物品。

topic: A musician hears their song being performed by someone else
text_en: Marcus was sitting in a park, eating a sandwich, when he heard a familiar tune from a nearby bandstand. A small group was playing a song he had written for his brother's birthday. The arrangement was for a brass band, with a tuba and trumpets. Marcus recognized the main melody, though the tempo was quicker. The band played through the chorus, and a few people clapped. Marcus finished his sandwich and threw the wrapper in a trash can. He watched the band for another minute, then stood up and walked toward the playground. He had promised to push his nephew on the swings.
text_zh: 马库斯坐在公园里吃三明治，这时他听到附近音乐台传来一段熟悉的曲调。一个小团体正在演奏一首他为哥哥生日写的歌。编曲是铜管乐队版本，有大号和喇叭。马库斯认出了主旋律，尽管速度更快。乐队演奏了副歌，几个人鼓了掌。马库斯吃完三明治，把包装纸扔进垃圾桶。他又看了一会儿乐队，然后站起来走向游乐场。他答应过要推他侄子荡秋千。

topic: A musician hears their song being performed by someone else
text_en: Ava was in a bookstore café, reading a novel, when she heard a song she had written for a local charity event. It was playing from the café's speaker, a stripped-down version with just a voice and a guitar. The singer was a man, his voice different from hers. He sang the lyrics about a lighthouse and the sea. Ava turned a page in her book, but she listened. The song ended, and the café returned to its usual ambient noise. She took a sip of her tea and continued reading. She had written the song quickly, not expecting it to be played anywhere else.
text_zh: 艾娃在一家书店咖啡馆里读小说时，听到了一首她为当地慈善活动写的歌。这首歌正从咖啡馆的扬声器里播放出来，是一个精简版，只有人声和吉他。歌手是个男人，声音和她不同。他唱着关于灯塔和大海的歌词。艾娃翻了一页书，但她听着。歌曲结束了，咖啡馆恢复了平常的环境噪音。她抿了一口茶，继续阅读。她当时很快就写好了这首歌，没想到它会在别处播放。

topic: A musician hears their song being performed by someone else
text_en: Leo was in a laundromat, folding his clothes, when he heard a song he had recorded for a demo tape years ago. It was playing from a radio on the counter. The version was a remix, with electronic beats and a synthesized melody. Leo recognized his own vocal track, though it was pitched higher. He folded a shirt and placed it in his basket. The song had been part of an album that never got released. He listened to the chorus, which he remembered writing in a single afternoon. The song ended and a news bulletin came on. He picked up his basket and left.
text_zh: 利奥在一家自助洗衣店叠衣服时，听到了一首他多年前为试听带录制的歌。这首歌正从柜台上的收音机里播放出来。这个版本是混音版，有电子节拍和合成旋律。利奥认出了自己的声轨，尽管音调被调高了。他叠好一件衬衫，放进篮子里。这首歌原本是一张从未发行的专辑的一部分。他听着副歌，记得自己是在一个下午写出来的。歌曲结束后，播报了一条新闻简报。他拿起篮子离开了。

topic: A musician hears their song being performed by someone else
text_en: Hannah was at a bus stop, waiting for her ride, when she heard a song she had written for her mother's birthday. A young man was playing it on a guitar across the street. He sang the lyrics about a garden and a porch swing. Hannah watched him from the bench. He played the final chord and adjusted his cap. The bus arrived, and she got on. She found a seat by the window. She thought about how the song had been a private gift, not something she had intended to share. The bus pulled away, and she looked out at the passing buildings.
text_zh: 汉娜在公交车站等车时，听到了一首她为母亲生日写的歌。一个年轻男人正在街对面弹着吉他唱这首歌。他唱着关于花园和门廊秋千的歌词。汉娜坐在长椅上看着他。他弹完最后一个和弦，调整了一下帽子。公交车来了，她上了车。她找了个靠窗的座位坐下。她想着这首歌本是私人礼物，并非她有意分享的东西。公交车开动了，她望着窗外掠过的建筑。

topic: A musician hears their song being performed by someone else
text_en: Nathan was in a hardware store, looking for a new drill bit, when he heard a song he had composed for a school play. It was playing over the store's speakers, a choral version with a full choir. The original was a solo piano piece. Nathan recognized the melody, which had been the theme for the main character. He walked to the drill section and picked up a box. The choir sang the final notes, and the song faded into a commercial. He took the drill bit to the counter and paid. He drove home and started working on a shelf.
text_zh: 内森在一家五金店寻找新的钻头时，听到了一首他为学校戏剧创作的曲子。这首歌正通过商店的扬声器播放，是一个有完整合唱团的合唱版本。原曲是钢琴独奏。内森认出了这段旋律，它曾是主角的主题曲。他走到钻头区，拿起一盒钻头。合唱团唱完最后的音符，歌曲淡出，接着是广告。他把钻头拿到柜台付了款。他开车回家，开始做一个架子。

topic: A musician hears their song being performed by someone else
text_en: Isabel was at a train station, waiting for her platform to be announced. From the station's speakers, a song she had written for a friend's art show started playing. It was an ambient piece with soft synthesizers. The version playing was slightly different, with a deeper bass line. Isabel recognized the melody, which she had based on a photograph of a city skyline. She listened as the song played, then the announcer called her train. She picked up her bag and walked to the platform. She found a seat by the window and put in her headphones, listening to a podcast.
text_zh: 伊莎贝尔在火车站等待她的站台被广播通知。车站的扬声器里开始播放一首她为朋友的画展写的歌。那是一首带有柔和合成器的氛围音乐。播放的版本略有不同，贝斯线更深沉。伊莎贝尔认出了这段旋律，她是以一张城市天际线的照片为基础创作的。她听着歌曲播放，然后广播员通知了她的列车。她拿起包走向站台。她找了个靠窗的座位坐下，戴上耳机，听起了播客。

topic: A musician hears their song being performed by someone else
text_en: Elena was in a pharmacy, picking up a prescription, when she heard a song she had written for her father's retirement party. It was playing through the store's speakers, a soft rock version with a guitar solo. Elena recognized the lyrics, which mentioned a toolbox and a workbench. She waited at the counter while the pharmacist checked her name. The song played on, and she tapped her foot slightly. She took her prescription and walked out. The song was still playing as she got into her car. She set the bag on the passenger seat and started the engine.
text_zh: 埃琳娜在一家药店取处方药时，听到了一首她为父亲退休派对写的歌。这首歌正通过商店的扬声器播放，是一个带有吉他独奏的软摇滚版本。埃琳娜认出了歌词，其中提到了工具箱和工作台。她在柜台前等着，药剂师核对了她的名字。歌曲继续播放，她轻轻用脚打着拍子。她拿了处方药走了出去。她上车时，歌曲还在播放。她把袋子放在副驾驶座上，发动了引擎。

topic: A musician hears their song being performed by someone else
text_en: Tom was in a barbershop, getting a haircut, when he heard a song he had written for a podcast intro. It was a short jingle, but the version playing was a full-length song with lyrics. The barber hummed along as he trimmed. Tom recognized the melody, which he had composed on a keyboard. The lyrics were different from his original, which had only been a few seconds long. The song ended and a different track began. Tom looked at himself in the mirror. The barber finished and brushed the hair off his shoulders. Tom paid and left.
text_zh: 汤姆在一家理发店理发时，听到了一首他为播客开场白写的歌。那是一段简短的广告歌，但播放的版本是一首完整的歌曲，带有歌词。理发师一边修剪一边哼着。汤姆认出了这段旋律，他是在键盘上创作的。歌词和他原来的不同，原来的只有几秒钟长。歌曲结束后，另一首曲子开始了。汤姆看着镜子里的自己。理发师剪完了，拂去他肩上的头发。汤姆付了钱离开了。

topic: A musician hears their song being performed by someone else
text_en: Maya was stacking clean plates when the faint sound of piano drifted through the open kitchen window. She paused, towel in hand, listening. The melody was unmistakable—her own composition, the one she had recorded last winter. Through the neighbor's window, she could see a young woman at the keyboard, playing the piece with a steady, careful rhythm. Maya finished drying the plate and set it down. She recognized the phrasing, the small hesitation before the chorus. She turned back to the sink, letting the music continue in the background as she wiped the counter.
text_zh: 玛雅正在叠干净的盘子，这时一阵微弱的钢琴声从敞开的厨房窗户飘进来。她停下来，手里拿着毛巾，倾听着。旋律清晰可辨——是她自己的作品，去年冬天录制的那首。透过邻居的窗户，她看到一个年轻女人在键盘前，以稳定而仔细的节奏弹奏着这首曲子。玛雅擦干盘子，放了下来。她认出了乐句，副歌前的小停顿。她转身回到水槽边，让音乐在背景中继续，同时擦拭着台面。

topic: A musician hears their song being performed by someone else
text_en: Victor was in a coffee shop, writing in his notebook, when he heard a song he had written for a documentary about a fishing village. It was playing through the shop's speakers, a folk version with a banjo. Victor recognized the melody, which he had based on a recording of waves. The banjo played a solo, and then the vocals came in. The lyrics were about a boat and a net. Victor wrote a few lines in his notebook. The song ended and the barista called out a name. He closed his notebook and took a sip of his coffee.
text_zh: 维克多在一家咖啡店里写笔记时，听到了一首他为一部关于渔村的纪录片写的歌。这首歌正通过店里的扬声器播放，是一个带有班卓琴的民谣版本。维克多认出了这段旋律，他是以海浪的录音为基础创作的。班卓琴独奏了一段，然后人声进来了。歌词是关于一条船和一张渔网。维克多在笔记本上写了几行字。歌曲结束了，咖啡师叫了一个名字。他合上笔记本，抿了一口咖啡。

topic: A musician hears their song being performed by someone else
text_en: Jonah stood at the back of the small café, waiting for his order. A guitarist sat on a stool near the window, playing through a set of familiar tunes. Then the opening notes of a song Jonah had written years ago began. He recognized the chord progression and the particular strumming pattern. He picked up his coffee from the counter and walked toward the door, passing close enough to hear the lyrics clearly. The guitarist played it slightly faster than Jonah usually did. He stepped outside, the door closing behind him, and the music faded as he walked down the street.
text_zh: 乔纳站在小咖啡馆的后面，等着他的订单。一位吉他手坐在窗边的凳子上，弹奏着一组熟悉的曲调。然后，乔纳多年前写的一首歌的开头音符响了起来。他认出了和弦进行和特定的扫弦模式。他从柜台拿起咖啡，走向门口，经过时能清楚地听到歌词。吉他手弹得比乔纳通常的速度稍快一些。他走出门外，门在他身后关上，音乐随着他沿街走去而逐渐消失。

topic: A person finds old photos that contradict family stories
text_en: While sorting through a box of kitchen linens, Lena found a small envelope tucked inside a tea towel. Inside were several photographs from a seaside holiday. One showed her grandmother standing beside a man who was not her grandfather. The date on the back placed it years before her grandparents' marriage. Lena put the photos back in the envelope and set it on the counter. Later, she mentioned it to her mother, who glanced at the image and said only that people had many friends then. Lena placed the envelope in her own drawer without asking more.
text_zh: 在整理一盒厨房亚麻布时，莉娜发现一个信封塞在一条茶巾里。里面是几张海边度假的照片。其中一张显示她的祖母站在一个不是她祖父的男人旁边。背面的日期表明这比祖父母结婚早了好几年。莉娜把照片放回信封，放在柜台上。后来，她向母亲提起这件事，母亲瞥了一眼照片，只说那时候人们有很多朋友。莉娜把信封放进自己的抽屉，没有再问。

topic: A person finds old photos that contradict family stories
text_en: Marco was cleaning out his late uncle's garage when he discovered a shoebox of old photographs. One photo showed his uncle in military uniform, but the insignia matched a branch of service that family stories always said he had never joined. Marco held the picture up to the light and looked at the back, but there was no caption. He put it in his jacket pocket and later showed it to his father. His father studied it for a moment, then said the uniform could have belonged to a friend. Marco placed the photo back in the shoebox and returned it to the shelf.
text_zh: 马可正在清理他已故叔叔的车库时，发现了一个装满旧照片的鞋盒。一张照片显示他的叔叔穿着军装，但徽章属于一个家族故事中从未提及他加入的兵种。马可把照片举到光下，看了看背面，但没有说明文字。他把它放进夹克口袋，后来给父亲看。父亲端详了一会儿，然后说制服可能是朋友的。马可把照片放回鞋盒，放回架子上。

topic: A person finds old photos that contradict family stories
text_en: Priya was helping her mother sort through old albums when she came across a picture of her parents at a beach resort. Her mother had always told her they spent their honeymoon in the mountains. The photo had a date that was several months before their wedding. Priya pointed it out to her mother, who looked at it briefly and said they must have taken a trip earlier that year. Priya turned the photo over, but there was no writing on the back. She slid it back into the album sleeve and continued turning pages.
text_zh: 普里亚正在帮母亲整理旧相册时，发现了一张父母在海滨度假胜地的照片。母亲总是告诉她，他们的蜜月是在山区度过的。照片上的日期比他们的婚礼早几个月。普里亚把它指给母亲看，母亲看了一眼，说他们那年早些时候一定去旅行过。普里亚把照片翻过来，但背面没有字。她把它滑回相册套中，继续翻页。

topic: A person finds old photos that contradict family stories
text_en: While clearing out a closet, Tom found a cigar box with black-and-white photos. One showed his grandfather standing next to a woman in a wedding dress. The family story was that his grandfather had married only once, and his grandmother was that woman. But the woman in the photo looked different from his grandmother's younger pictures. Tom brought the box to his aunt, who laughed and said the woman was a cousin who had borrowed the dress for a studio portrait. Tom nodded and put the box back on the shelf.
text_zh: 在清理壁橱时，汤姆发现了一个装有黑白照片的雪茄盒。一张显示他的祖父站在一个穿婚纱的女人旁边。家族故事说他的祖父只结过一次婚，他的祖母就是那个女人。但照片中的女人看起来与他祖母年轻时的照片不同。汤姆把盒子带给他的姑妈，她笑着说那个女人是一个借了裙子拍影楼照的表亲。汤姆点点头，把盒子放回架子上。

topic: A person finds old photos that contradict family stories
text_en: Elena was unpacking a box of books from her childhood home when a folded photograph fell out. It showed her father as a young man, standing in front of a shop that she had never heard mentioned. The sign above the door had a name that was not her family's. She asked her father about it that evening. He glanced at the photo and said he had worked there one summer during college. Elena had always been told he spent those summers on a farm. She put the photo on the bookshelf and went back to unpacking.
text_zh: 埃琳娜正在从童年家中搬来的书箱里拆包时，一张折叠的照片掉了出来。它显示她的父亲年轻时站在一家她从未听过的商店前。门上的招牌有一个不是她家姓氏的名字。那天晚上她问父亲这件事。他瞥了一眼照片，说他在大学期间的一个夏天在那里工作过。埃琳娜一直被告知那些夏天他在农场度过。她把照片放在书架上，继续拆包。

topic: A person finds old photos that contradict family stories
text_en: Marta was sorting through a box of her father's belongings when she found a photo of him in a military uniform. The family had always said he was too young to serve in the war, that he'd spent those years working on the farm. But there he was, standing beside a barracks with other young men, the date faintly written on the back. She turned the photo over a few times, then placed it on the table. Later, she mentioned it to her mother, who glanced at it briefly and said the uniform must have belonged to a cousin. Marta nodded and put the photo back in the box.
text_zh: 玛尔塔在整理父亲遗物时，发现了一张他穿军装的照片。家人总是说他太年轻，没有参战，那些年他在农场工作。但他就在那里，站在营房旁，和其他年轻人在一起，背面模糊地写着日期。她把照片翻了几次，然后放在桌子上。后来，她向母亲提起，母亲瞥了一眼，说制服一定是表亲的。玛尔塔点点头，把照片放回盒子里。

topic: A person finds old photos that contradict family stories
text_en: While cleaning out the garage, Daniel came across an old shoebox filled with photographs. One picture showed his grandfather standing next to a fishing boat, a catch hanging from the dock. Daniel's father had always said his grandfather never went fishing, claiming he hated the water. Daniel looked at the photo for a long moment, then placed it back in the box. He continued sorting through the garage, moving boxes and old tools. Later, he mentioned the photo to his father, who just shrugged and said the man in the picture might be someone else. Daniel didn't press the matter.
text_zh: 在清理车库时，丹尼尔发现了一个装满照片的旧鞋盒。一张照片显示他的祖父站在一艘渔船旁，码头上挂着渔获。丹尼尔的父亲总是说他的祖父从不钓鱼，声称他讨厌水。丹尼尔看了照片很久，然后把它放回盒子里。他继续整理车库，搬动箱子和旧工具。后来，他向父亲提起照片，父亲只是耸耸肩，说照片里的人可能是别人。丹尼尔没有追问。

topic: A person finds old photos that contradict family stories
text_en: Rita found an envelope of photos in a drawer of the desk she had inherited from her uncle. One photo showed her uncle in a military uniform, standing in front of a barracks. Her mother had often said her uncle never served in the military because of a medical condition. Rita looked at the photo, noting the insignia on the uniform. She put the envelope back in the drawer and closed it. Later, she asked her mother about it, but her mother insisted the photo must be of a friend. Rita didn't argue. She simply left the envelope where she found it and went back to her chores.
text_zh: 丽塔在从叔叔那里继承的书桌抽屉里发现了一个信封，里面装着照片。一张照片显示她的叔叔穿着军装，站在营房前。她的母亲常说叔叔因为健康问题从未服过兵役。丽塔看着照片，注意到制服上的徽章。她把信封放回抽屉，关上。后来，她问母亲这件事，但母亲坚持说照片一定是朋友的。丽塔没有争辩。她只是把信封留在原处，继续做家务。

topic: A person finds old photos that contradict family stories
text_en: Luis was helping his mother clean out the spare room when he found a photo album under a stack of old blankets. The album contained pictures of his parents on a vacation to a lake, years before he was born. His mother had always told him they never took vacations, always working to save money. Luis turned the pages slowly, seeing his parents smiling by the water. He closed the album and placed it back under the blankets. His mother came in and asked what he was doing. He said he was just tidying up. He didn't bring up the photos.
text_zh: 路易斯正在帮母亲清理空房间时，在一堆旧毯子下发现了一本相册。相册里有他父母在湖边度假的照片，那是在他出生前几年。母亲总是告诉他他们从不度假，总是工作攒钱。路易斯慢慢翻页，看到父母在水边微笑。他合上相册，放回毯子下。母亲进来问他做什么。他说他只是整理一下。他没有提起照片。

topic: A person finds old photos that contradict family stories
text_en: Elena was unpacking boxes in her new apartment when she found a small tin containing photographs. One showed her father as a young man, playing guitar on a stage. Her family had always said her father never played any instrument, claiming he had no musical talent. Elena studied the picture, noticing the guitar and the microphone. She put the tin back in the box and continued unpacking. When her father visited later, she didn't mention the photo. She just showed him the apartment and asked about his day. The tin stayed in the box, stored in a closet.
text_zh: 埃琳娜在新公寓拆箱时，发现了一个装着照片的小铁盒。一张显示她的父亲年轻时在舞台上弹吉他。家人总是说她的父亲从不演奏任何乐器，声称他没有音乐天赋。埃琳娜仔细看照片，注意到吉他和麦克风。她把铁盒放回箱子，继续拆包。后来父亲来访时，她没有提起照片。她只是带他看公寓，问他今天过得怎么样。铁盒留在箱子里，存放在壁橱里。

topic: A person finds old photos that contradict family stories
text_en: Tom was going through his grandmother's old chest when he found a photo of her standing next to a race car. The family story was that she had never been interested in cars, always taking the bus. Tom looked at the photo, seeing the number on the car door and her confident stance. He placed the photo back in the chest and closed the lid. He finished sorting through the chest, setting aside items to keep and items to donate. He didn't mention the photo to anyone, deciding it was probably from a carnival or a fair. He moved on to the next task.
text_zh: 汤姆正在翻祖母的旧箱子，发现了一张她站在一辆赛车旁的照片。家里的说法是她对汽车从不感兴趣，总是坐公交车。汤姆看着照片，看到了车门上的号码和她自信的姿态。他把照片放回箱子里，合上了盖子。他整理完箱子，把要保留的东西和要捐赠的东西分开。他没有向任何人提起这张照片，认为那可能是狂欢节或集市上的照片。他继续做下一件事。

topic: A person finds old photos that contradict family stories
text_en: Nina found a box of slides in her father's study. She held one up to the light and saw a picture of her mother skiing down a snowy slope. Her mother had always said she never learned to ski, preferring warm climates. Nina looked through a few more slides, all showing the same scene. She put the slides back in the box and returned it to the shelf. Later, she asked her mother about it, but her mother laughed and said it must be a friend. Nina didn't pursue it. She went back to her book, leaving the box on the shelf.
text_zh: 尼娜在父亲的书房里发现了一盒幻灯片。她拿起一张对着光看，看到一张母亲在雪坡上滑雪的照片。母亲总是说她从没学过滑雪，更喜欢温暖的气候。尼娜又看了几张幻灯片，都是同样的场景。她把幻灯片放回盒子里，放回架子上。后来，她问起母亲这件事，但母亲笑着说那一定是朋友。尼娜没有追问。她回去看书，把盒子留在架子上。

topic: A person finds old photos that contradict family stories
text_en: Carlos was cleaning the attic when he found a photo of his uncle shaking hands with a famous politician. His family had always said his uncle was never involved in politics, staying away from public life. Carlos looked at the photo, noting the date on the back. He put the photo back in the box and continued cleaning. He didn't mention it to his parents, thinking it might be a staged photo or a coincidence. He finished the attic and went downstairs for lunch. The photo remained in the box, forgotten for the time being.
text_zh: 卡洛斯在打扫阁楼时发现了一张叔叔与一位著名政治家握手的照片。家人总是说叔叔从不参与政治，远离公共生活。卡洛斯看着照片，注意到背面的日期。他把照片放回盒子里，继续打扫。他没有向父母提起这件事，心想那可能是摆拍或巧合。他打扫完阁楼，下楼吃午饭。照片留在盒子里，暂时被遗忘了。

topic: A person finds old photos that contradict family stories
text_en: Sofia was looking through her mother's old jewelry box when she found a photograph tucked behind the velvet lining. It showed her mother in a ballet costume, posed in a dance studio. Her mother had always said she never took dance lessons, being too clumsy. Sofia looked at the photo, seeing the pointe shoes and the tutu. She placed the photo back behind the lining and closed the box. She didn't ask her mother about it, feeling it might be a private matter. She continued looking through the other items, then put the box away.
text_zh: 索菲亚在翻看母亲的首饰盒时，在天鹅绒衬里后面发现了一张照片。照片上母亲穿着芭蕾舞服，在舞蹈室里摆着姿势。母亲总是说她从没上过舞蹈课，因为太笨拙。索菲亚看着照片，看到了足尖鞋和芭蕾舞裙。她把照片放回衬里后面，合上盒子。她没有问母亲这件事，觉得那可能是私事。她继续看其他东西，然后把盒子收好。

topic: A person finds old photos that contradict family stories
text_en: Mark was helping his father clean the basement when he found a photo of his grandfather with a group of people in front of a large tent. His father had always said his grandfather never went camping, hating the outdoors. Mark looked at the photo, seeing the tents and the trees in the background. He handed the photo to his father, who looked at it briefly and then put it aside without comment. They continued cleaning, moving boxes and old furniture. Mark didn't ask any questions, and the photo was eventually placed in a pile of items to be kept.
text_zh: 马克在帮父亲打扫地下室时，发现了一张祖父和一群人在一个大帐篷前的照片。父亲总是说祖父从不去露营，讨厌户外活动。马克看着照片，看到了背景中的帐篷和树木。他把照片递给父亲，父亲看了一眼，然后没说什么就放在一边。他们继续打扫，搬箱子和旧家具。马克没有问任何问题，照片最终被放在了一堆要保留的物品里。

topic: A person finds old photos that contradict family stories
text_en: Julia found a stack of photographs in a book she borrowed from her aunt. One photo showed her aunt at a cooking class, holding a chef's hat. Her aunt had always said she never cooked, always ordering takeout. Julia looked at the photo, seeing the kitchen and the other students. She put the photo back in the book and returned it to the shelf. Later, she mentioned it to her aunt, who said the photo was from a friend's party. Julia nodded and changed the subject. She continued reading the book, though she glanced at the shelf occasionally.
text_zh: 朱莉娅在从姑姑那里借来的一本书里发现了一叠照片。其中一张照片显示姑姑在烹饪课上，手里拿着一顶厨师帽。姑姑总是说她从不做饭，总是点外卖。朱莉娅看着照片，看到了厨房和其他学生。她把照片放回书里，放回架子上。后来，她向姑姑提起这件事，姑姑说那张照片是朋友聚会时拍的。朱莉娅点点头，转移了话题。她继续看书，尽管偶尔会瞥一眼书架。

topic: A person finds old photos that contradict family stories
text_en: Peter was going through his mother's old papers when he found a photo of her in a laboratory coat, holding a beaker. His mother had always said she never worked in a lab, being more of an office person. Peter looked at the photo, seeing the equipment and the labels on the shelves. He put the photo back in the pile and continued sorting. He didn't mention it to his mother, thinking it might be from a school project or a tour. He finished the papers and moved on to other boxes. The photo stayed in the pile, mixed with other documents.
text_zh: 彼得在翻看母亲的文件时，发现了一张她穿着实验室工作服、拿着烧杯的照片。母亲总是说她从没在实验室工作过，更像是个办公室人员。彼得看着照片，看到了设备和架子上的标签。他把照片放回文件堆里，继续整理。他没有向母亲提起这件事，心想那可能是学校项目或参观时拍的。他整理完文件，继续处理其他箱子。照片留在文件堆里，和其他文件混在一起。

topic: A person finds old photos that contradict family stories
text_en: Elena discovered a stack of old photographs in a drawer while cleaning out her grandmother's house. One showed her grandfather standing next to a woman who was not her grandmother, both of them smiling at a seaside resort. The family story had always been that he never traveled anywhere except to visit relatives. Elena studied the picture for a while, noting the style of clothing and the backdrop. She set it aside with the others and continued sorting through the kitchen items. When her aunt arrived later, Elena handed her the photograph without comment, and her aunt simply placed it in her purse.
text_zh: 埃琳娜在打扫祖母的房子时，在一个抽屉里发现了一叠旧照片。其中一张显示祖父站在一个不是祖母的女人旁边，两人在海滨度假胜地微笑着。家里的说法一直是他除了探亲外从不去任何地方旅行。埃琳娜仔细看了一会儿照片，注意到服装风格和背景。她把它和其他照片放在一边，继续整理厨房用品。后来姑姑来了，埃琳娜把照片递给她，没有说什么，姑姑只是把它放进了钱包里。

topic: A person finds old photos that contradict family stories
text_en: While unpacking boxes from the attic, Paul came across a photograph of his mother at a racetrack, holding a winning ticket. His family had often recounted how she never gambled or enjoyed such outings. He looked at the image, then at the back, where someone had written a name and a date. He set it on the shelf near the other family pictures. That evening, he asked his father about it, but his father just shrugged and said it must have been a joke. Paul left the photograph where it was and went back to unpacking the rest of the boxes.
text_zh: 保罗在从阁楼搬下来的箱子里翻找时，发现了一张母亲在赛马场拿着中奖彩票的照片。家人经常讲述她从不赌博或不喜欢这种外出活动。他看了看照片，又看了看背面，有人在那里写了一个名字和日期。他把它放在架子上，靠近其他家庭照片。那天晚上，他问父亲这件事，但父亲只是耸耸肩，说那一定是个玩笑。保罗把照片留在原处，继续打开其余的箱子。

topic: A person finds old photos that contradict family stories
text_en: Laura was helping her mother sort through old family photos for a reunion. She found one of her mother in a graduation gown, but the background was a different university than the one her mother always said she attended. Laura looked at the photo, seeing the building and the banner. She showed it to her mother, who said it must be from a friend's graduation. Laura nodded and placed the photo in a pile to keep. They continued sorting, and the photo was eventually put into an album. Laura didn't bring it up again.
text_zh: 劳拉正在帮母亲整理旧家庭照片，为聚会做准备。她发现了一张母亲穿着毕业礼服的照片，但背景是另一所大学，而不是母亲一直说的那所。劳拉看着照片，看到了建筑物和横幅。她拿给母亲看，母亲说那一定是朋友的毕业典礼。劳拉点点头，把照片放在要保留的一堆里。她们继续整理，照片最终被放进了相册。劳拉没有再提起这件事。

topic: A student discovers their teacher follows them on social media
text_en: Maya was scrolling through her feed when she noticed a familiar profile picture. Her history teacher, Mr. Alvarez, had liked her post about a local art exhibit. She paused, then tapped his profile. His account was public, filled with photos of his dog and hiking trips. She scrolled back to her own posts, noticing he had liked a few others from the past month. She put her phone down and picked up her notebook, flipping to the page where she had written down the homework. She wrote a reminder to check her privacy settings later, then continued reviewing her notes for the next day's class.
text_zh: 玛雅正在刷信息流时，注意到一个熟悉的头像。她的历史老师阿尔瓦雷斯先生赞了她关于当地艺术展的帖子。她停顿了一下，然后点开了他的主页。他的账户是公开的，满是他的狗和徒步旅行的照片。她翻回自己的帖子，注意到他过去一个月还赞了其他几个。她放下手机，拿起笔记本，翻到她记作业的那一页。她写了一条提醒，打算稍后检查隐私设置，然后继续复习第二天的课程笔记。

topic: A student discovers their teacher follows them on social media
text_en: Jonah saw the notification while waiting for his coffee. His English teacher, Ms. Chen, had started following him. He clicked on her profile, seeing a mix of book recommendations and family photos. He scrolled through his own posts, wondering if any of them were inappropriate. He had posted a meme about homework last week. He shrugged, put his phone in his pocket, and picked up his coffee. He walked to his next class, thinking about the essay due Friday. He made a mental note to keep his posts a bit more school-appropriate, just in case.
text_zh: 乔纳在等咖啡时看到了通知。他的英语老师陈老师开始关注他了。他点开她的主页，看到的是书籍推荐和家庭照片的混合。他翻看自己的帖子，想知道是否有任何不当的内容。他上周发了一个关于作业的梗图。他耸耸肩，把手机放进口袋，拿起咖啡。他走向下一节课，想着周五要交的论文。他默默记下，要让自己的帖子更符合学校规范一些，以防万一。

topic: A student discovers their teacher follows them on social media
text_en: Priya was in the library when she saw the notification. Her math teacher, Mr. Thompson, had followed her on Instagram. She glanced at his profile, which was mostly pictures of his garden and his cat. She didn't post much herself, just a few photos of her paintings and some study memes. She wondered if he had found her account through the class group. She closed the app and returned to her textbook, solving the next problem. She didn't think much more about it, but she did decide to make her account private later that evening.
text_zh: 普里亚在图书馆时看到了通知。她的数学老师汤普森先生在Instagram上关注了她。她瞥了一眼他的主页，主要是他的花园和猫的照片。她自己发帖不多，只有几张画作和一些学习梗图。她想知道他是不是通过班级群找到她的账户的。她关掉应用，回到课本，解下一道题。她没有多想，但确实决定当晚晚些时候把账户设为私密。

topic: A student discovers their teacher follows them on social media
text_en: Liam was eating lunch when he noticed that his science teacher, Mrs. Patel, had followed him on Twitter. He scrolled through her timeline, which was full of science articles and retweets about space. He had tweeted about a video game the other day. He wondered if she would see his occasional complaints about homework. He finished his sandwich and put his phone away. He had a lab report to finish, so he headed to the library. He didn't change anything about his account, but he was a bit more mindful about what he posted.
text_zh: 利亚姆吃午饭时注意到他的科学老师帕特尔夫人在Twitter上关注了他。他翻看她的时间线，满是科学文章和关于太空的转发。他前几天发过一条关于电子游戏的推文。他想知道她会不会看到他偶尔对作业的抱怨。他吃完三明治，把手机收起来。他有一份实验报告要完成，所以去了图书馆。他没有改变账户的任何设置，但发帖时更加注意了。

topic: A student discovers their teacher follows them on social media
text_en: Sofia was in her room when she saw the follow request from her Spanish teacher, Señora García. She accepted it, then looked at her profile. It was full of photos of her travels and her family. Sofia's own account was mostly pictures of her friends and her dog. She scrolled through her posts, making sure there was nothing too embarrassing. She saw a photo from a party last month, but it was just her and her friends smiling. She put her phone down and started her homework, thinking about the upcoming oral exam.
text_zh: 索菲亚在房间里看到了来自她的西班牙语老师加西亚夫人的关注请求。她接受了，然后看了看她的主页。上面满是她的旅行和家人照片。索菲亚自己的账户大多是朋友和她的狗的照片。她翻看自己的帖子，确保没有太尴尬的内容。她看到一张上个月派对上的照片，但只有她和朋友们微笑。她放下手机，开始做作业，想着即将到来的口语考试。

topic: A student discovers their teacher follows them on social media
text_en: Ethan was checking his notifications when he saw that his history teacher, Mr. Brooks, had followed him on Instagram.
