He clicked on the profile, seeing a mix of historical memes and photos of his kids. Ethan's account was mostly about his skateboarding and his band. He wondered if Mr. Brooks would see the video of him falling off his skateboard. He laughed a little, then continued scrolling. He had a paper to write, so he opened his laptop and started researching. He didn't think about the follow again until later that night.
text_zh: 伊桑查看通知时，看到他的历史老师布鲁克斯先生在Instagram上关注了他。他点开主页，看到历史梗图和孩子们的照片。伊桑的账户主要是关于滑板和乐队的。他想知道布鲁克斯先生会不会看到他滑板摔倒的视频。他笑了笑，然后继续滑动。他有一篇论文要写，所以打开笔记本电脑开始研究。直到那天晚上晚些时候，他才再次想起这次关注。

topic: A student discovers their teacher follows them on social media
text_en: Ava was in the cafeteria when she noticed that her art teacher, Ms. Rivera, had followed her on social media. She tapped the notification, seeing Ms. Rivera's profile filled with her own artwork and photos of her studio. Ava's account was a mix of her sketches and photos of her cat. She felt a slight flutter, thinking maybe Ms. Rivera had seen her art in class and wanted to see more. She scrolled through her posts, making sure her sketches were presentable. She then put her phone away and joined her friends at the table.
text_zh: 艾娃在食堂时注意到她的艺术老师里维拉女士在社交媒体上关注了她。她点开通知，看到里维拉女士的主页满是她的艺术作品和工作室照片。艾娃的账户是她的素描和猫的照片的混合。她感到一阵轻微的激动，想着也许里维拉女士在课堂上看到了她的艺术，想看到更多。她翻看自己的帖子，确保素描看起来不错。然后她放下手机，加入朋友们的桌子。

topic: A student discovers their teacher follows them on social media
text_en: Noah was in his room when he saw that his physics teacher, Mr. Kim, had followed him on Twitter. He clicked on the profile, which was mostly retweets of science news and occasional posts about his dog. Noah's timeline was full of jokes and memes, some of which were about school. He scrolled through his recent posts, wondering if any were too edgy. He saw one about a pop quiz that was a bit sarcastic. He shrugged and closed the app. He had a problem set to finish, so he turned to his textbook.
text_zh: 诺亚在房间里看到他的物理老师金先生在Twitter上关注了他。他点开主页，主要是科学新闻的转发和偶尔关于他的狗的帖子。诺亚的时间线满是笑话和梗图，其中一些是关于学校的。他翻看最近的帖子，想知道是否有太出格的。他看到一条关于突击测验的帖子，有点讽刺。他耸耸肩，关掉了应用。他有一组题要完成，所以转向课本。

topic: A student discovers their teacher follows them on social media
text_en: Isabella was scrolling through her feed when she saw that her English teacher, Mr. Davis, had liked one of her posts. She tapped his profile, seeing a mix of book quotes and photos of his garden. Her account was mostly about her poetry and her daily life. She noticed he had liked a few of her poems. She felt a small sense of recognition, but then she remembered he was her teacher. She continued scrolling, then put her phone down to read a chapter for class. She didn't change anything about her account.
text_zh: 伊莎贝拉刷信息流时，看到她的英语老师戴维斯先生赞了她的一条帖子。她点开他的主页，看到书籍语录和花园照片的混合。她的账户主要是关于她的诗歌和日常生活。她注意到他赞了她的几首诗。她感到一丝被认可的感觉，但随后她想起他是她的老师。她继续滑动，然后放下手机，读一章课内内容。她没有改变账户的任何设置。

topic: A student discovers their teacher follows them on social media
text_en: Mason was in the school library when he saw the notification. His biology teacher, Mrs. Nguyen, had followed him on Instagram. He looked at her profile, which was full of plant photos and her kids. His own account was mostly about his hiking trips and his dog. He scrolled through his posts, making sure there were no embarrassing photos. He saw one from a party, but it was just him and his friends. He put his phone away and continued working on his lab report. He didn't think much about it.

topic: An employee discovers the company is being sold
text_en: Maya was sorting through the supply cabinet when her supervisor called her into the office. The news came out in a steady stream: the company had accepted an offer from a larger firm. Maya listened, nodded, and asked about the timeline. Back at her desk, she opened the spreadsheet she had been working on and continued entering the figures. The cursor blinked steadily. She noticed her hand was steady on the mouse. At the end of the day, she packed her bag and walked to the train, thinking about how the office might look different in a few months.
text_zh: 玛雅正在整理储物柜时，她的主管叫她进办公室。消息源源不断地传来：公司已接受了一家更大公司的收购要约。玛雅听着，点了点头，询问了时间安排。回到办公桌前，她打开一直在处理的电子表格，继续输入数据。光标稳定地闪烁。她注意到自己的手稳稳地放在鼠标上。一天结束时，她收拾好包，走向火车，想着几个月后办公室可能会变得不同。

topic: An employee discovers the company is being sold
text_en: During the team meeting, the regional manager mentioned the acquisition almost in passing. Liam sat with his coffee cooling beside him, watching the slide that showed the new logo. He wrote down a few notes about the transition dates. After the meeting, he returned to his cubicle and finished drafting the client email he had started earlier. He proofread it twice, then sent it. On the way out, he saw the CEO’s office door was closed, and he remembered the boxes stacked in the hallway, waiting for the moving crew.

text_en: Priya was reviewing the quarterly reports when the email arrived from HR. The subject line read: "Company Update." She clicked it and read the announcement about the sale. In the break room, she poured herself a glass of water and saw a colleague doing the same. They exchanged a brief nod. She returned to her desk and continued her work until the end of the shift.

topic: An employee discovers the company is being sold
text_en: The notice was posted on the bulletin board near the time clock. Daniel read it while waiting for his shift to start. The company was being acquired by a competitor. He folded the paper back and pinned it up. During his break, he called his wife to mention it, keeping the conversation brief. Back on the floor, he stocked the shelves as usual. The warehouse hummed with the same sounds. At the end of the day, he clocked out and walked to his car, the announcement still folded in his pocket.
text_zh: 通知贴在考勤钟附近的公告栏上。丹尼尔在等待轮班开始时读了它。公司将被一家竞争对手收购。他把纸折好，重新钉上去。休息时，他给妻子打了个电话，简短地提了一下。回到工作区，他像往常一样整理货架。仓库里响着同样的声音。一天结束时，他打卡下班，走向自己的车，那份公告还折在口袋里。

text_en: Elena was in the middle of a phone call with a client when her manager motioned her over. She finished the call and then heard the news: the company was being sold. She wrote down the date of the official announcement. After the manager left, she returned to her desk and checked the schedule for the next week. The tasks were unchanged. She updated her calendar and then went to the printer to collect a document. As she walked back, she noticed the office was quiet, but the usual sounds of typing continued.
text_zh: 埃琳娜正在和客户通电话时，她的经理示意她过去。她结束通话后，听到了这个消息：公司要被出售了。她记下了正式公告的日期。经理离开后，她回到办公桌前，查看了下周的日程安排。任务没有变化。她更新了日历，然后去打印机取了一份文件。走回来时，她注意到办公室很安静，但通常的打字声还在继续。

She adjusted the colors and text alignment, then saved the file. She sent it to the client for feedback. Later, she saw the CEO walking through the office, but she didn't stop to talk. She returned to her desk.
text_zh: 消息来自一位看到内部公告的同事的群聊。格蕾丝阅读了消息，然后去公司门户网站确认。她阅读了官方声明，并记下了过渡日期。然后她关闭门户网站，继续处理她正在做的设计稿。她调整了颜色和文本对齐方式，然后保存了文件。她将其发送给客户以征求反馈。后来，她看到首席执行官走过办公室，但没有停下来交谈。她回到了自己的办公桌。

topic: An employee discovers the company is being sold
text_en: During the lunch break, a supervisor came to the cafeteria and announced the sale. Tom looked up from his sandwich and listened. The supervisor answered a few questions and left. Tom finished his lunch and went back to his desk. He had a stack of invoices to process, and he worked through them one by one. He noticed the office was a little quieter, but the phones still rang. At the end of the day, he turned off his computer and walked home, the announcement replaying in his mind as he passed the familiar streets.
text_zh: 午休期间，一位主管来到自助餐厅宣布了出售消息。汤姆从三明治上抬起头来倾听。主管回答了几个问题后离开。汤姆吃完午餐，回到办公桌前。他有一堆发票要处理，便逐一处理。他注意到办公室比平时安静了一些，但电话仍然响着。一天结束时，他关掉电脑，走回家，经过熟悉的街道时，公告在他脑海中回放。

topic: An employee discovers the company is being sold
text_en: Maya glanced at the email from the regional office while sipping her morning coffee. The subject line read 'Company Update' and the attached document outlined a merger with a larger firm. She scrolled through the details, noting the timeline for the transition and the assurances about job stability. Her desk phone rang, and she answered it, speaking with a vendor about an upcoming shipment. After hanging up, she returned to the document, rereading the section about new management. She saved a copy to her personal drive, then stood to attend the weekly team meeting, leaving the email open on her screen.
text_zh: 玛雅一边喝着早晨的咖啡，一边瞥了一眼地区办公室发来的电子邮件。主题行写着“公司更新”，附件概述了与一家更大公司的合并。她滚动浏览细节，注意到过渡时间线和关于工作稳定性的保证。桌上的电话响了，她接听，与供应商讨论即将到来的发货。挂断电话后，她回到文档，重新阅读关于新管理层的部分。她将副本保存到个人驱动器，然后起身参加每周团队会议，让电子邮件在屏幕上保持打开状态。

topic: An employee discovers the company is being sold
text_en: The announcement was made on the intercom. Nathan stopped what he was doing and listened. The company was being acquired. He went back to his workbench and resumed assembling the parts. The rhythm of the work was familiar. At the break, he went to the vending machine and got a soda. A coworker asked if he thought anything would change. Nathan shrugged and said they would have to wait and see. He drank his soda and returned to the bench. The shift ended, and he clocked out, walking to his motorcycle.
text_zh: 公告通过内部广播系统发布。内森停下手中的工作倾听。公司正在被收购。他回到工作台继续组装零件。工作的节奏很熟悉。休息时，他去自动售货机买了一瓶汽水。一位同事问他是否认为会有任何变化。内森耸耸肩说他们只能等着瞧。他喝完汽水，回到工作台。班次结束，他打卡下班，走向他的摩托车。

topic: An employee discovers the company is being sold
text_en: The letter was on his desk when he returned from a meeting. It was from the executive team, outlining the sale. David read it and then placed it in the tray. He then reviewed the project notes for the next client call. He made a few edits and prepared the agenda. The call went as planned. After the call, he wrote a summary and sent it to the team. He then looked at the letter again, but only for a moment. He filed it in the cabinet and continued with the day's work.
text_zh: 他开会回来时，信在他的桌子上。信来自执行团队，概述了出售事宜。大卫读了信，然后把它放在托盘中。随后他审阅了下次客户电话会议的项目笔记。他做了几处修改，并准备了议程。电话会议按计划进行。电话会议结束后，他写了总结并发送给团队。然后他再次看了看那封信，但只是一会儿。他把它归档在文件柜里，继续当天的工作。

topic: An employee discovers the company is being sold
text_en: The news was shared during the department meeting. Laura listened as the manager explained the sale. She asked about the timeline, and the manager said the details were still being worked out. Laura returned to her cubicle and opened the spreadsheet. She checked the formulas and updated the data. She then printed the report and placed it in the inbox. She saw a colleague walking by and asked if they had heard the news. They said yes and continued. Laura went back to her desk and started on the next task.
text_zh: 消息在部门会议上分享。劳拉听着经理解释出售事宜。她询问了时间表，经理说细节仍在敲定中。劳拉回到自己的隔间，打开电子表格。她检查了公式并更新了数据。然后她打印了报告，放入收件箱。她看到一位同事走过，问他们是否听到了消息。他们说是的，然后继续走。劳拉回到办公桌，开始下一个任务。

topic: An employee discovers the company is being sold
text_en: The announcement was on the company intranet. Kevin clicked the link and read the statement. It said the company had agreed to be acquired. He closed the browser and went back to the code he was writing. He debugged a function and ran the tests. The tests passed. He committed the changes and updated the task tracker. At lunch, he ate at his desk and scrolled through the news feed. He saw the article about the sale and skimmed it. He then closed the browser and worked on the next feature until the end of the day.
text_zh: 公告在公司内网上发布。凯文点击链接阅读了声明。声明说公司已同意被收购。他关闭浏览器，回到正在编写的代码。他调试了一个函数并运行测试。测试通过。他提交了更改并更新了任务追踪器。午餐时，他在办公桌前吃饭，浏览新闻源。他看到了关于出售的文章并略读了一下。然后他关闭浏览器，继续开发下一个功能直到一天结束。

topic: An employee discovers the company is being sold
text_en: The memo was placed in her mailbox. Nina picked it up along with other mail and read it on the way to her desk. The company was being sold. She put the memo in her bag and sat down. She opened the customer service logs and started responding to the pending tickets. She worked through them one by one. At one point, a supervisor came by to ask if she had any questions about the announcement. Nina said she didn't. The supervisor nodded and left. Nina continued with the tickets and finished them before the end of her shift.
text_zh: 备忘录放在她的邮箱里。妮娜连同其他邮件一起取出，在走向办公桌的路上阅读。公司将被出售。她把备忘录放进包里，坐了下来。她打开客户服务日志，开始回复待处理的工单。她逐一处理。有一次，一位主管过来问她是否对公告有任何疑问。妮娜说没有。主管点点头离开了。妮娜继续处理工单，在轮班结束前完成了。

topic: A person accidentally sends a text to the wrong recipient
text_en: Maya had typed a quick message to her sister about the party, but as she hit send, she realized the name on top of the chat was her boss. She stared at the screen, reading the words about the office playlist. Her thumb hovered over the message, but it was already delivered. She put the phone face down on the kitchen counter and picked up her coffee. The message sat there, sent to the wrong place. She took a sip and then opened the phone again, but there was no reply yet. She scrolled back to the top of the chat to confirm the contact.
text_zh: 玛雅给姐姐打了一条关于聚会的简短消息，但按下发送键时，她意识到聊天顶部的名字是她的老板。她盯着屏幕，读着关于办公室播放列表的文字。她的拇指悬停在消息上，但消息已经发送了。她把手机屏幕朝下放在厨房台面上，拿起咖啡。消息就那样待在那里，发错了地方。她喝了一口，然后又打开手机，但还没有回复。她滚动到聊天顶部确认联系人。

topic: A person accidentally sends a text to the wrong recipient
text_en: Liam was texting his friend about their weekend plans, but his phone auto-corrected the name and he sent it to his neighbor instead. The message said, "I'll bring the chips and the good dip." He noticed the mistake when the neighbor replied with a thumbs up. Liam looked at the screen, then typed a quick apology. The neighbor sent back, "No problem." Liam put the phone in his pocket and went to find his keys. He would have to be more careful with the contact list next time. He left the house to run his errands.
text_zh: 利亚姆正在给朋友发短信讨论周末计划，但手机自动更正了名字，他把短信发给了邻居。消息说：“我会带薯片和好蘸酱。”当邻居回复一个大拇指时，他注意到了错误。利亚姆看了看屏幕，然后快速打了一条道歉。邻居回复：“没问题。”利亚姆把手机放进口袋，去找钥匙。下次他得更加小心联系人列表。他离开家去办差事。

topic: A person accidentally sends a text to the wrong recipient
text_en: Maya typed a quick message to her neighbor about picking up the mail while she was away. She pressed send and continued packing her suitcase. A few minutes later, her phone buzzed with a reply from her colleague, who had received the text by mistake. Maya read the response and realized the mix-up. She wrote back a brief apology and clarified that the message was meant for someone else. Then she returned to folding her clothes and checking her travel list. The evening went on as usual, with Maya finishing her packing and setting out her keys by the door.
text_zh: 玛雅给邻居发了一条简短消息，关于她外出时帮忙取邮件。她按下发送键，继续收拾行李箱。几分钟后，她的手机嗡嗡响，是同事的回复，同事误收了这条短信。玛雅读了回复，意识到搞错了。她简短道歉，并澄清消息是发给别人的。然后她继续叠衣服，检查旅行清单。晚上照常进行，玛雅收拾好行李，把钥匙放在门边。

topic: A person accidentally sends a text to the wrong recipient
text_en: Ethan was in a meeting, and he wanted to remind his colleague about the report. He pulled out his phone and typed a short note, but he sent it to the client instead. The client responded, "I think you meant this for someone else." Ethan looked at the screen and then at the meeting agenda. He wrote back, "Yes, my apologies." He put the phone away and turned his attention back to the speaker. The report was still due, but he would handle that after the meeting. The mistaken text was already done.
text_zh: 伊桑正在开会，他想提醒同事关于报告的事。他掏出手机打了一条简短便条，但发给了客户。客户回复：“我想你是想发给别人吧。”伊桑看了看屏幕，又看了看会议议程。他回复：“是的，抱歉。”他把手机收起来，把注意力转回发言人。报告仍然要交，但他会等会议结束后处理。错发的短信已经发出去了。

topic: A person accidentally sends a text to the wrong recipient
text_en: Daniel was at the grocery store when he remembered to tell his sister about the family dinner on Sunday. He typed out the details and sent the text, then continued down the aisle comparing brands of pasta sauce. His phone chimed with a reply from an old coworker, who had received the message instead. Daniel looked at the screen, realized his mistake, and sent a quick note to the coworker explaining the error. He then forwarded the original text to his sister. After finishing his shopping, he headed home and unpacked the bags without giving the mix-up much more thought.
text_zh: 丹尼尔在杂货店时，想起要告诉姐姐周日家庭聚餐的事。他打出细节并发送短信，然后继续在过道里比较意大利面酱的品牌。他的手机响起，是前同事的回复，对方误收了消息。丹尼尔看了看屏幕，意识到错误，给同事发了一条简短说明，解释错误。然后他把原始短信转发给姐姐。买完东西后，他回家，把袋子放好，没有多想这个乌龙。

topic: A person accidentally sends a text to the wrong recipient
text_en: Priya sat at her desk during lunch and texted her friend about meeting for coffee after work. She mentioned the usual café and a time that suited her. A moment later, a response came from her landlord, who had gotten the message by mistake. Priya blinked at the screen and then replied with an apology, explaining that the text was intended for someone else. She sent a new message to her friend with the same details. After that, she ate her sandwich and scrolled through a few news articles until her break ended.
text_zh: 普里亚午餐时坐在桌前，给朋友发短信约下班后喝咖啡。她提到常去的咖啡馆和合适的时间。过了一会儿，房东回复了，房东误收了消息。普里亚眨眨眼看着屏幕，然后回复道歉，解释短信是发给别人的。她给朋友发了一条新消息，内容相同。之后，她吃了三明治，浏览了几篇新闻文章，直到休息结束。

topic: A person accidentally sends a text to the wrong recipient
text_en: Ethan was walking his dog in the park when he remembered to ask his brother about borrowing a ladder for the weekend. He pulled out his phone and typed the question, then hit send without checking the recipient. A reply came from a former classmate, who was puzzled by the request. Ethan glanced at the screen, recognized the error, and sent a brief apology along with an explanation. He then messaged his brother properly. The dog tugged at the leash, and Ethan continued their walk around the pond before heading back home.
text_zh: 伊桑在公园遛狗时，想起要问哥哥借梯子过周末。他掏出手机打出问题，没检查收件人就按了发送。一位前同学回复，对请求感到困惑。伊桑瞥了一眼屏幕，意识到错误，发了一条简短道歉和解释。然后他正确地把消息发给了哥哥。狗拽着牵引绳，伊桑继续绕着池塘散步，然后回家。

topic: A person accidentally sends a text to the wrong recipient
text_en: Laura was in the middle of preparing dinner when she thought to text her mother about the recipe for the casserole. She typed the ingredients she needed and sent the message. Her phone rang a few minutes later with a reply from her dentist's office, which had received the text by mistake. Laura read the response and realized what had happened. She wrote back a short apology and sent the correct message to her mother. She then went back to stirring the pot and checking the oven, the mix-up already fading from her attention.
text_zh: 劳拉正在准备晚餐，想到要给妈妈发短信问砂锅菜的食谱。她打出需要的食材并发送消息。几分钟后，手机响了，是牙医诊所的回复，对方误收了短信。劳拉读了回复，意识到发生了什么。她回了一条简短道歉，并把正确的消息发给妈妈。然后她回去搅拌锅子，检查烤箱，乌龙已经从她的注意力中淡去。

topic: A person accidentally sends a text to the wrong recipient
text_en: Maya typed a quick reply to her colleague about the project timeline, but as she pressed send, she noticed the contact name was her sister's. She stared at the screen for a moment, then reread the message. It mentioned a meeting and some data files. She wondered if her sister would be puzzled by it. Maya set the phone down on the kitchen counter and picked up her coffee. She thought about sending a follow-up to clarify, but she wasn't sure what to say. She decided to wait and see if her sister replied.
text_zh: 玛雅给同事打了一条关于项目时间表的简短回复，但按下发送键时，她注意到联系人名字是姐姐的。她盯着屏幕看了一会儿，然后重读了消息。消息提到一个会议和一些数据文件。她想知道姐姐会不会感到困惑。玛雅把手机放在厨房台面上，拿起咖啡。她考虑发一条后续消息澄清，但不确定该说什么。她决定等等看姐姐是否回复。

topic: A person accidentally sends a text to the wrong recipient
text_en: Maya had typed a quick message to her sister about picking up groceries on the way home. She pressed send and slipped the phone into her coat pocket. A few minutes later, she pulled it out to check the time and saw a reply from a colleague. The message had gone to the wrong thread. She read the colleague's response, which was brief and polite, then wrote back a short apology. She reopened the correct conversation and retyped the grocery list, making sure the recipient's name was right this time. Then she continued down the street toward the store.
text_zh: 玛雅给姐姐打了一条简短消息，关于回家路上买杂货。她按下发送键，把手机滑进外套口袋。几分钟后，她掏出手机看时间，看到同事的回复。消息发错了对话。她读了同事的回复，简短而礼貌，然后回了一条简短道歉。她重新打开正确的对话，重新输入购物清单，这次确保收件人的名字正确。然后她继续沿街走向商店。

topic: A person accidentally sends a text to the wrong recipient
text_en: James was in the hardware store when he thought to tell his wife about the paint color he had picked out. He typed the name of the shade and the brand, then sent the message. A response came from his bank, which had received the text by mistake. James stared at the screen for a second, then replied with a brief apology. He sent the correct message to his wife and walked over to the checkout counter with the paint can in his hand. He paid and drove home, the mix-up not coming up again.
text_zh: 詹姆斯在五金店时，想到要告诉妻子他挑选的油漆颜色。他输入了色调名称和品牌，然后发送了消息。他的银行回复了一条消息，银行误收到了这条短信。詹姆斯盯着屏幕看了一秒钟，然后简短地回复了道歉。他把正确的消息发给了妻子，手里拿着油漆罐走向收银台。他付了款，开车回家，这次混淆没有再被提起。

topic: A person accidentally sends a text to the wrong recipient
text_en: Liam was texting his neighbor about borrowing a ladder for the afternoon. He finished the message and hit send, then set the phone aside while he made lunch. When he picked it up again, there was a reply from an old college friend who lived in another state. The friend had responded with a puzzled comment about the ladder. Liam realized he had selected the wrong contact. He sent a quick correction to the friend and then forwarded the original message to the neighbor. After that, he ate his sandwich and checked his email.
text_zh: 利亚姆正在给邻居发短信，想借梯子用一下午。他写完消息并按下发送，然后把手机放在一边去做午饭。当他再次拿起手机时，看到一位住在另一个州的大学老友回复了。那位朋友对梯子的事回复了一条困惑的评论。利亚姆意识到他选错了联系人。他给朋友快速发了一条更正，然后把原始消息转发给了邻居。之后，他吃了三明治，查看了电子邮件。

topic: A person accidentally sends a text to the wrong recipient
text_en: Ethan was texting his mother about a family gathering, but he accidentally sent the message to his boss. The text said, "I'll bring the salad and a cake." He realized the mistake when he saw the name at the top. His boss would likely be confused. Ethan put the phone down and looked out the window. He thought about sending a correction, but he didn't know how to phrase it. He decided to wait until his boss said something. He picked up his book and tried to read, but the thought lingered.
text_zh: 伊桑正在给母亲发短信，谈论家庭聚会的事，但他不小心把消息发给了老板。短信内容是：“我会带沙拉和蛋糕。”当他看到顶部的名字时，他意识到了错误。他的老板可能会感到困惑。伊桑放下手机，望向窗外。他考虑发一条更正，但不知道如何措辞。他决定等老板先开口。他拿起书试图阅读，但那个念头一直萦绕在心头。

topic: A person accidentally sends a text to the wrong recipient
text_en: Priya meant to text her brother about their parents' anniversary dinner. She wrote the message and sent it without looking closely at the screen. A short while later, she noticed a reply from a former coworker. The coworker asked if Priya had meant to send that to someone else. Priya typed back a brief explanation and apologized for the mix-up. She then copied the message into the correct conversation with her brother. She put the phone on the table and went back to folding laundry, glancing at the screen occasionally in case another reply came through.
text_zh: 普里娅本想给哥哥发短信，谈论父母的结婚纪念日晚餐。她写了消息，没有仔细看屏幕就发送了。过了一会儿，她注意到一位前同事的回复。同事问普里娅是不是发错了人。普里娅简短地回复了解释，并为混淆道歉。然后她把消息复制到了与哥哥的正确对话中。她把手机放在桌子上，回去叠衣服，偶尔瞥一眼屏幕，以防又有回复。

topic: A person accidentally sends a text to the wrong recipient
text_en: Tom was in the garage sorting through tools when he thought to ask his friend about the best way to fix a leaky faucet. He typed the question and sent the text. A reply came from his doctor's office, which had received the message by mistake. Tom read the response and recognized the error. He sent a brief apology and explained the situation. He then messaged his friend with the same question. He picked up a wrench and continued organizing the workbench, the mix-up not occupying his thoughts for long.
text_zh: 汤姆在车库里整理工具时，想到要问朋友修理漏水水龙头的最佳方法。他输入了问题并发送了短信。他的医生办公室回复了一条消息，他们误收到了这条消息。汤姆读了回复，意识到了错误。他发送了简短的道歉并解释了情况。然后他给朋友发了同样的问题。他拿起扳手，继续整理工作台，这次混淆没有在他脑海中停留太久。

topic: A person accidentally sends a text to the wrong recipient
text_en: Ethan was messaging his roommate about a leaky faucet in the kitchen. He typed the details and hit send, then placed the phone on the desk while he gathered his keys. When he picked it up, he saw a response from his aunt. She had replied with a concerned question about the plumbing. Ethan realized he had chosen her name instead of his roommate's. He wrote back to his aunt, explaining it was a mistake, and then sent the original message to the correct person. He pocketed the phone and headed out to run his errands.
text_zh: 伊桑正在给室友发短信，谈论厨房里漏水的水龙头。他输入了详细信息并按下发送，然后把手机放在桌子上，同时收拾钥匙。当他拿起手机时，看到姑姑的回复。她回复了一个关于管道问题的关切询问。伊桑意识到他选择了她的名字而不是室友的。他给姑姑回复，解释这是个错误，然后把原始消息发给了正确的人。他把手机放进口袋，出门去办事。

topic: A person accidentally sends a text to the wrong recipient
text_en: Nina sent a text to her friend about meeting for coffee later in the week. She finished the message and pressed send, then continued sorting through her mail. A few minutes later, her phone buzzed with a reply from a dentist's office. The receptionist had received the coffee invitation and responded with a polite note that they didn't schedule appointments by text. Nina realized she had sent it to the wrong number. She apologized briefly and then sent the message again to her friend. She set the phone down and opened the next envelope.
text_zh: 尼娜给朋友发了一条短信，谈论本周晚些时候见面喝咖啡。她写完消息并按下发送，然后继续整理邮件。几分钟后，她的手机嗡嗡作响，收到牙医诊所的回复。接待员收到了咖啡邀请，并礼貌地回复说他们不通过短信安排预约。尼娜意识到她发错了号码。她简短地道歉，然后再次把消息发给了朋友。她放下手机，打开下一个信封。

topic: A person accidentally sends a text to the wrong recipient
text_en: Omar was texting his cousin about borrowing a car for the weekend. He typed the request and sent it, then put the phone in his bag. When he checked later, there was a reply from a former supervisor. The supervisor had responded with a short comment about the car request. Omar saw that he had picked the wrong contact. He replied to the supervisor with an apology and clarified the mistake. Then he resent the message to his cousin. He zipped his bag and walked to the bus stop, keeping the phone in his hand.
text_zh: 奥马尔正在给表弟发短信，谈论周末借车的事。他输入了请求并发送，然后把手机放进包里。当他稍后查看时，看到一位前主管的回复。主管对借车请求回复了一条简短的评论。奥马尔发现自己选错了联系人。他回复主管道歉并澄清了错误。然后他把消息重新发给了表弟。他拉上包的拉链，走向公交车站，手里拿着手机。

topic: A person accidentally sends a text to the wrong recipient
text_en: Ava sent a text to her husband about picking up a prescription on his way home. She wrote the message and pressed send without checking the contact list. A while later, she got a reply from a neighbor. The neighbor said she thought Ava had the wrong person. Ava looked at the screen and saw the mistake. She typed a quick apology and then sent the original message to her husband. She placed the phone on the counter and continued preparing dinner, occasionally glancing at the screen in case he replied.
text_zh: 艾娃给丈夫发了一条短信，让他回家路上取药。她写了消息，没有检查联系人列表就按下了发送。过了一会儿，她收到邻居的回复。邻居说她以为艾娃发错了人。艾娃看了看屏幕，看到了错误。她快速输入了道歉，然后把原始消息发给了丈夫。她把手机放在柜台上，继续准备晚餐，偶尔瞥一眼屏幕，以防他回复。

topic: A person accidentally sends a text to the wrong recipient
text_en: Maya had typed a quick message to her sister about picking up dinner, but the name at the top of the chat showed her coworker, not her sister. She stared at the screen for a moment, reading the words again. The message mentioned a specific restaurant and a time. She tapped the back arrow and saw the conversation list. Her thumb hovered over the chat, but there was no way to unsend it. She closed the app and placed the phone on the table. After a minute, she opened it again and typed a short apology to her coworker, then went back to folding the laundry.
text_zh: 玛雅给姐姐打了一条简短的消息，关于取晚餐的事，但聊天顶部的名字显示的是她的同事，而不是姐姐。她盯着屏幕看了一会儿，又读了一遍那些字。消息提到了一个具体的餐厅和时间。她点击了返回箭头，看到了对话列表。她的拇指悬停在聊天上，但无法撤回。她关闭了应用，把手机放在桌子上。一分钟后，她又打开它，给同事输入了一条简短的道歉，然后回去叠衣服。

topic: A person's longtime hobby becomes their child's obsession
text_en: Margaret had kept a meticulous garden journal for years, recording planting dates and weather patterns. Her daughter, Lena, now spent every afternoon with the journal, copying the notes into her own notebook and asking Margaret to identify every plant in the yard. Margaret would point out the roses and the tomatoes, and Lena would write it all down. One evening, Lena asked if she could take the journal to school for show-and-tell. Margaret said yes, and reminded her to be careful with it. Lena nodded, already planning which pages to show her class.
text_zh: 玛格丽特多年来一直精心记录着一本园艺日志，记下种植日期和天气模式。她的女儿莉娜现在每天下午都花时间翻阅这本日志，把笔记抄进自己的笔记本里，并请玛格丽特辨认院子里的每一种植物。玛格丽特会指出玫瑰和西红柿，莉娜则会把它们都写下来。一天晚上，莉娜问她能否把日志带到学校去参加展示与讲述活动。玛格丽特答应了，并提醒她要小心保管。莉娜点了点头，心里已经在盘算要给全班同学看哪些页了。

topic: A person's longtime hobby becomes their child's obsession
text_en: Ellen had spent years tending her rose garden, pruning and feeding each bush with care. Her daughter, Mia, now followed her outside every afternoon, carrying her own small watering can. Ellen showed her how to check for aphids and where to cut dead blooms. They worked side by side in the warm soil, Mia asking endless questions about soil and sunlight. Ellen found herself planning their gardening sessions around Mia's school schedule. The garden grew fuller, with Mia's favorite pink roses blooming near the back fence. Ellen was glad to share the work, even if her own quiet time had become a shared routine.
text_zh: 艾伦多年来一直精心照料着她的玫瑰园，细心修剪、施肥每一丛玫瑰。她的女儿米娅现在每天下午都会跟着她到户外，带着自己的小浇水壶。艾伦教她如何检查蚜虫，以及在哪里剪掉枯萎的花朵。她们在温暖的土壤里并肩劳作，米娅不停地问关于土壤和阳光的问题。艾伦发现自己开始根据米娅的学校作息来安排她们的园艺时间。花园变得更加茂盛，米娅最喜欢的粉色玫瑰在后篱笆附近盛开着。艾伦很高兴能分享这份工作，即使她原本独处的安静时光已经变成了共同的日常。

topic: A person's longtime hobby becomes their child's obsession
text_en: Ellen had been knitting sweaters for her family for years. Her granddaughter, Mia, had recently become fascinated with the process, sitting next to Ellen and watching the needles move. Ellen gave her a ball of yarn and a pair of beginner needles, and Mia tried to cast on, the loops slipping off. Ellen showed her again, patiently, and Mia tried once more. They spent the afternoon like that, Ellen working on a sleeve and Mia attempting her own small square. Mia asked if she could have her own project bag, and Ellen said she would look for one.
text_zh: 艾伦多年来一直为家人织毛衣。她的孙女米娅最近对这个过程着了迷，坐在艾伦旁边看着织针来回移动。艾伦给了她一团毛线和一副初学者用的织针，米娅试着起针，但线圈总是滑落。艾伦耐心地又示范了一次，米娅又试了一次。她们就这样度过了一个下午，艾伦织着袖子，米娅则尝试织她自己的小方块。米娅问她能不能有自己的手工包，艾伦说她会去找一个。

topic: A person's longtime hobby becomes their child's obsession
text_en: Paul had collected stamps since he was a boy, sorting them into albums by country and era. His daughter, Claire, had begun to ask about the stamps, wanting to know where each one was from. Paul would pull out a magnifying glass and show her the tiny details, and Claire would study them carefully. She started her own small collection, using the stamps Paul gave her from duplicates. One afternoon, she asked if she could help him sort the latest batch. Paul said yes, and showed her how to organize them by postmark.
text_zh: 保罗从小就收集邮票，按国家和年代把它们分类装进集邮册里。他的女儿克莱尔开始询问这些邮票，想知道每一枚来自哪里。保罗会拿出放大镜给她看细微的细节，克莱尔则会仔细研究。她开始收集自己的小收藏，用的是保罗从重复的邮票中给她的那些。一天下午，她问他能否帮忙整理最新的一批邮票。保罗答应了，并教她如何按邮戳分类。

topic: A person's longtime hobby becomes their child's obsession
text_en: Ruth played the piano every evening after dinner. Her son, Daniel, had started sitting on the bench beside her, watching her hands move across the keys. Ruth taught him the names of the notes, and Daniel would practice finding middle C. He asked if he could take lessons, and Ruth said she would look into it. That night, Daniel stayed at the piano after Ruth finished, pressing the keys one by one. Ruth listened from the kitchen as she washed the dishes, hearing the same note repeated over and over.
text_zh: 露丝每天晚饭后都会弹钢琴。她的儿子丹尼尔开始坐在她旁边的琴凳上，看着她的双手在琴键上移动。露丝教他认识音符的名称，丹尼尔则练习找到中央C。他问她能否去上钢琴课，露丝说她会去了解一下。那天晚上，露丝弹完后，丹尼尔留在钢琴旁，一个键一个键地按着。露丝在厨房洗碗时听着，听到同一个音符一遍又一遍地重复。

topic: A person's longtime hobby becomes their child's obsession
text_en: For years, Daniel had assembled model ships in his workshop, carefully fitting tiny planks and painting hulls. His son, Leo, had started joining him after school, sitting on a stool and sorting the small parts. Daniel taught him how to read the instructions and use the glue sparingly. They built a schooner together over several weekends, Leo handling the sails while Daniel shaped the masts. The workshop now held Leo's own half-finished projects on a separate shelf. Daniel enjoyed the company, though he sometimes missed working alone late into the night. The hobby had become something they shared.
text_zh: 多年来，丹尼尔一直在他的工作室里组装模型船，小心地安装细小的木板并给船体上漆。他的儿子利奥放学后开始加入他，坐在凳子上整理小零件。丹尼尔教他如何阅读说明书以及如何节省地使用胶水。他们花了几个周末一起建造了一艘双桅纵帆船，利奥负责处理船帆，丹尼尔则塑造桅杆。现在工作室的另一个架子上放着利奥自己未完成的项目。丹尼尔很享受这份陪伴，尽管他有时会怀念独自工作到深夜的时光。这个爱好已经变成了他们共同分享的事情。

topic: A person's longtime hobby becomes their child's obsession
text_en: Helen had kept a scrapbook of pressed flowers for years, each page labeled with the flower's name and where it was found. Her grandson, Leo, had started helping her press new specimens, carefully laying them between the pages of a heavy book. Helen showed him how to arrange the petals, and Leo would spend a long time getting it just right. He asked if he could have his own scrapbook. Helen said they could get one the next time they went to the store. Leo continued to adjust a petal, his brow furrowed.
text_zh: 海伦多年来一直保存着一本压花剪贴簿，每一页都标有花的名称和发现地点。她的孙子利奥开始帮她压制新的标本，小心地把它们夹在一本厚书的书页之间。海伦教他如何整理花瓣，利奥会花很长时间把它弄到恰到好处。他问她能否拥有自己的剪贴簿。海伦说他们下次去商店时可以买一本。利奥继续调整一片花瓣，眉头紧锁。

topic: A person's longtime hobby becomes their child's obsession
text_en: Robert had built model ships for decades, the shelves in his study lined with finished vessels. His son, Ben, had taken an interest, asking to watch Robert glue the tiny masts and rig the sails. Robert gave Ben an old model to practice on, and Ben spent his afternoons carefully painting the hull. He asked if he could start a new model from a kit. Robert said they could pick one out together. Ben held the paintbrush, waiting for the next instruction. Robert showed him how to thin the paint.
text_zh: 罗伯特几十年来一直在制作模型船，书房里的架子上摆满了完成的船只。他的儿子本对此产生了兴趣，要求看罗伯特粘贴细小的桅杆和装配船帆。罗伯特给了本一个旧模型让他练习，本每天下午都仔细地给船体上漆。他问能否从套件开始制作一个新模型。罗伯特说他们可以一起挑选一个。本拿着画笔，等待下一个指示。罗伯特教他如何稀释油漆。

topic: A person's longtime hobby becomes their child's obsession
text_en: For years, Marcus had spent his evenings restoring vintage watches. His daughter Lena had always watched from the kitchen table, but recently she had started asking to help. Tonight, she had spread the tiny gears across a cloth, her small fingers carefully sorting each piece. Marcus showed her how to hold the tweezers, how to align the spring. She listened intently, repeating the motions until they felt natural. When he glanced at the clock, he realized the hour had grown late. Lena looked up, still focused on the mechanism. He quietly gathered the tools, letting her finish the task on her own.
text_zh: 多年来，马库斯一直把晚上的时间花在修复古董手表上。他的女儿莉娜总是在厨房桌旁看着，但最近她开始主动要求帮忙。今晚，她把微小的齿轮摊在一块布上，用她的小手指仔细地分类每一个零件。马库斯教她如何拿镊子，如何对齐弹簧。她专注地听着，反复练习这些动作，直到感觉自然。当他瞥了一眼时钟，发现时间已经很晚了。莉娜抬起头，仍然专注于那个机械装置。他悄悄收拾好工具，让她自己完成这项任务。

topic: A person's longtime hobby becomes their child's obsession
text_en: Raymond had practiced woodworking for decades, shaping chairs and shelves in his garage. His daughter, Claire, had taken an interest, watching him sand and varnish. He let her use the smaller tools, showing her how to measure and mark the wood. They built a birdhouse together, Claire choosing the paint color and hammering the nails with his guidance. The garage now had a corner with her tools and projects. Raymond appreciated her enthusiasm, though he sometimes had to remind her to finish one piece before starting another. The craft had become a family activity.
text_zh: 雷蒙德从事木工几十年，在车库里制作椅子和架子。他的女儿克莱尔对此产生了兴趣，看着他打磨和上漆。他让她使用较小的工具，教她如何测量和标记木材。他们一起建造了一个鸟舍，克莱尔选择油漆颜色，并在他的指导下钉钉子。车库现在有一个角落放着她的工具和项目。雷蒙德很欣赏她的热情，尽管他有时不得不提醒她完成一件作品后再开始另一件。这门手艺已经成为一项家庭活动。

topic: A person's longtime hobby becomes their child's obsession
text_en: Derek's workshop was filled with model airplanes he had built over decades, each one carefully assembled and painted. His daughter Elena grew up watching him sand wings and apply decals. When she was in high school, she started joining him on weekends, asking to build her own kits. He taught her how to read the instructions and use the tools. She became meticulous, often staying at the bench longer than he did. One Saturday, she finished a replica of a vintage biplane, holding it up for him to inspect. He turned it over in his hands, checking the seams and paint lines, then nodded and placed it on the shelf beside his own models.
text_zh: 德里克的车间里摆满了他在几十年间制作的飞机模型，每一架都是精心组装并上漆的。他的女儿埃琳娜从小看着他打磨机翼、贴贴花。她上高中时，开始在周末加入他，要求自己制作模型套件。他教她如何阅读说明书和使用工具。她变得一丝不苟，常常在操作台前待得比他更久。一个星期六，她完成了一架老式双翼飞机的复制品，举起来让他检查。他把它在手中翻来覆去，检查接缝和漆线，然后点了点头，把它放在自己模型旁边的架子上。

topic: A person's longtime hobby becomes their child's obsession
text_en: Harold had kept a detailed birdwatching journal for years, noting species and migration patterns. His niece, Ava, had started joining him on his morning walks, binoculars around her neck. He taught her to identify birds by their calls and flight patterns, pointing out a warbler in the bushes. Ava began keeping her own list, checking off each new bird they saw. They visited the park regularly, Harold carrying a thermos while Ava held the field guide. He was glad to share his knowledge, even if the walks were slower now. The hobby had become a shared interest.
text_zh: 哈罗德多年来一直记着详细的观鸟日志，记录物种和迁徙模式。他的侄女艾娃开始加入他的晨间散步，脖子上挂着双筒望远镜。他教她通过叫声和飞行模式识别鸟类，指出灌木丛中的一只莺。艾娃开始记自己的清单，每看到一种新鸟就勾选掉。他们定期去公园，哈罗德提着保温瓶，艾娃拿着野外指南。他很高兴能分享自己的知识，即使现在走得慢了些。这个爱好已成为共同的兴趣。

topic: A person's longtime hobby becomes their child's obsession
text_en: Phyllis had kept a vegetable garden for years, tending tomatoes, peppers, and herbs with steady routine. Her grandson Marcus visited each summer and helped with watering and weeding. This year, he arrived with a notebook full of sketches and questions about soil and planting schedules. He followed her through the rows, noting how she pinched back basil and staked the tomato plants. He asked if he could start his own small plot in the corner. She gave him a few seedlings and showed him how to space them. He checked on them every morning before breakfast, and she found herself checking his plants too, noting their progress alongside her own.
text_zh: 菲利斯多年来一直打理菜园，按部就班地照料着番茄、辣椒和香草。她的孙子马库斯每年夏天来访，帮忙浇水和除草。今年，他带来了一本满是素描和关于土壤与种植时间问题的笔记本。他跟着她走过菜畦，注意她如何掐薄荷和给番茄搭架。他问能否在角落开一小块自己的地。她给了他几株幼苗，并教他如何拉开间距。他每天早饭前都去查看他的植物，而她也发现自己会去查看他的，记录它们的长势，和自己的作物比较进度。

topic: A person's longtime hobby becomes their child's obsession
text_en: Vincent had restored old bicycles in his spare time, finding frames and replacing parts. His daughter, Nina, had started helping him, handing him tools and learning the names of components. He taught her how to adjust brakes and true a wheel, letting her take apart a rusty hub. They worked on a vintage bike together, Nina stripping the paint and choosing a new color. The garage was now cluttered with her projects as well. Vincent appreciated her involvement, though he sometimes had to stop her from taking things apart too quickly. The hobby had become a joint venture.
text_zh: 文森特在业余时间翻新旧自行车，找车架、换零件。他的女儿妮娜开始帮他干活，给他递工具，学习各种部件的名称。他教她如何调刹车、校车轮，还让她拆开一个生锈的花鼓。他们一起组装了一辆老式自行车，妮娜给车架打磨刮漆，挑选新颜色。车库现在也堆满了她的各种项目。文森特欣赏她的参与，尽管有时他得拦着她别太急于拆东西。这个爱好已成为两人合作的工程。

topic: A person's longtime hobby becomes their child's obsession
text_en: Alan had been a hobbyist photographer for years, mostly shooting landscapes and street scenes with his old film camera. His daughter Zoe borrowed it for a school project and returned it with a roll of developed prints. She had photographed their neighborhood, focusing on doorways and shadows. She asked if she could keep using the camera. He showed her how to adjust aperture and shutter speed, and she began carrying it everywhere. One afternoon, she showed him a series of shots taken in the park at dusk, the light soft and uneven. He looked through them slowly, then handed the prints back and offered to take her to the camera store to choose her own film.
text_zh: 艾伦多年来一直是摄影爱好者，主要用旧胶片相机拍风景和街景。他的女儿佐伊借相机做学校作业，还回来时带了一卷洗好的照片。她拍的是自家附近街区，聚焦门廊和影子。她问能否继续用这台相机。他教她如何调节光圈和快门速度，她便开始相机不离身。一个下午，她给他看了一组黄昏时在公园拍的照片，光线柔和且不均。他慢慢翻看，然后把照片递回去，提出带她去相机店挑她自己的胶卷。

topic: A person's longtime hobby becomes their child's obsession
text_en: Carl had been carving wooden spoons for years, his whittling knife kept sharp and ready. His son, Ethan, had started to sit with him on the porch, using a small piece of soft wood and a blunt knife. Carl showed him how to hold the knife and make even strokes. Ethan would carve for a while, then show his progress. He asked if he could carve something for his mother. Carl said that was a good idea. Ethan went back to his piece, and Carl continued on his own spoon.
text_zh: 卡尔多年来一直手工雕刻木勺，他的雕刻刀总是磨得锋利、随时可用。他的儿子伊桑开始坐在门廊上陪他，用一块软木和一把钝刀。卡尔教他如何握刀、均匀下刀。伊桑刻一会儿，就拿给他看进展。他问能不能给妈妈刻点什么。卡尔说那是个好主意。伊桑回去接着刻，卡尔继续刻他自己的勺子。

topic: A person's longtime hobby becomes their child's obsession
text_en: Bernard had kept a vegetable garden for many years, planting tomatoes and beans each spring. His son, Theo, had started helping him dig and water, fascinated by the growing process. Bernard taught him how to tell when vegetables were ripe and how to pull weeds without disturbing the roots. They harvested together, Theo carrying the basket and sorting the produce. Theo now had his own small plot at the end of the rows, where he planted radishes and lettuce. Bernard was glad to share the work, even if his own rows were sometimes neglected. The garden had become a family project.
text_zh: 伯纳德多年来一直种菜，每年春天种番茄和豆角。他的儿子西奥开始帮忙挖土浇水，对生长过程十分着迷。伯纳德教他怎么看蔬菜熟了没有，以及怎么拔草又不伤根。他们一起采摘，西奥提着篮子，把收成分类。西奥现在在菜畦尽头有了一小块属于自己的地，种了樱桃萝卜和生菜。伯纳德很乐意分享这项工作，即使自己的菜畦有时被疏忽了。菜园已成为一个家共同的项目。

topic: A person's longtime hobby becomes their child's obsession
text_en: Ruth had quilted for years, her sewing room stacked with fabric scraps and half-finished blocks. Her daughter Naomi had always been around the fabric but never showed much interest until she found a box of vintage quilt patterns at a yard sale. She brought them home and spread them across the kitchen table, asking Ruth about each one. Ruth explained the different stitches and color combinations. Naomi started piecing a small sampler, borrowing Ruth's rotary cutter and cutting mat. She worked on it in the evenings, sometimes asking Ruth to help with a tricky seam. When the top was finished, Ruth helped her baste it, and they pinned the layers together on the living room floor.
text_zh: 鲁思多年来一直做拼布，她的缝纫室里堆满布头和做了一半的拼布块。她的女儿娜奥米总在布料间长大，但一直没显出太大兴趣，直到她在二手甩卖上发现了一盒复古拼布图纸。她把图纸带回家，摊在厨房桌上，向鲁思每个都问询。鲁思讲解不同的针法和色彩搭配。娜奥米开始拼一个小样布，借用鲁思的旋转裁刀和切割垫。她晚上做，有时请鲁思帮忙处理难缝的接缝。布面完成后，鲁思帮她绷被面，她们一起在客厅地板上把所有层别在一起。

topic: A person's longtime hobby becomes their child's obsession
text_en: George had collected coins since his own childhood, keeping them in albums and cataloging each find. His son Tyler discovered the collection while looking for a lost book and spent an afternoon sorting through the pennies and nickels. He asked George about the dates and mint marks, and George showed him how to use the magnifying glass to check for errors. Tyler began bringing home pocket change and inspecting it at the kitchen table. He started a small box of his own, separating wheat pennies from newer ones. George lent him an old album and helped him organize the coins by year. They sat together on weekends, comparing finds and arranging the pages.
text_zh: 乔治从自己小时候起就收集硬币，他把它们收藏在册子里，并编号记录每一枚的发现。他的儿子泰勒在找一本丢失的书时发现了这个收藏，花了一个下午把那些分币和镍币分类整理。他问乔治那些年份和铸币厂标记，乔治便教他用放大镜检查错版。泰勒开始把兜里的零钱带回来，在厨房桌上仔细查看。他开了自己的一个小盒子，把小麦分币和较新的分币分开。乔治借给他一本旧册子，帮他按年份整理硬币。他们周末坐在一起，比较彼此的收藏，整理页面。

topic: A person's longtime hobby becomes their child's obsession
text_en: Agnes had kept a scrapbook of pressed flowers for years, carefully preserving petals and leaves. Her grandson, Peter, had become interested, collecting his own specimens on walks. She showed him how to press them between pages and label them with the date and place. They made a scrapbook together, Peter arranging the flowers and writing the names. He now carried a small notebook to record his finds, and they compared notes each week. Agnes was glad to share her knowledge, even if the house was full of drying flowers. The hobby had become a shared pursuit.
text_zh: 艾格尼丝多年来一直收藏压花册，小心保存花瓣和叶子。她的孙子彼得对此产生了兴趣，散步时也会采集自己的标本。她教他怎么把花压在书页之间，并标注日期和地点。他们一起做了一本压花册，彼得摆放花朵，写名字。他现在随身带一个小笔记本记录他的发现，每周他们都互相交流笔记。艾格尼丝很乐意分享她的知识，即使屋子里堆满了正在干燥的花。这个爱好已成为共同的追求。

topic: Someone finds their parent's draft letter of resignation from decades ago
text_en: Marta found the letter while clearing out the attic for her parents' move to a smaller place. It was in a shoebox with old tax returns, and the typed page was dated decades ago. It was addressed to the head of the hospital where her father had worked as an administrator, and it stated his intention to resign, citing a desire to pursue other opportunities. Marta remembered her father had never left that job until retirement. She folded the letter and placed it back in the box, then continued sorting through the other papers.
text_zh: 玛尔塔在为她父母搬到更小的地方而清理阁楼时发现了这封信。它在一个装着旧纳税申报单的鞋盒里，这封打印的信件日期是几十年前的。信是写给她父亲曾担任行政主管的那家医院的院长的，信中表明了他辞职的意向，理由是希望寻求其他机会。玛尔塔记得她父亲从未离开过那份工作，一直干到退休。她把信叠好放回盒子里，然后继续整理其他文件。

topic: Someone finds their parent's draft letter of resignation from decades ago
text_en: While cleaning out the attic, Maya found a folder tucked behind an old photo album. Inside was a typed letter, dated decades earlier, from her father to his employer. It was a draft resignation, stating his intention to leave his position for reasons he hadn't yet specified. The letter was incomplete, with a blank line where the explanation should have been. Maya read it twice, noting the formal language and the way he'd crossed out a sentence about opportunities elsewhere. She placed the folder back where she found it, then continued sorting through the boxes of holiday decorations.
text_zh: 在清理阁楼时，玛雅在一个旧相册后面发现了一个文件夹。里面是一封她父亲写给雇主的打印信件，日期是几十年前的。这是一封辞职信草稿，表明他打算离开职位，但原因尚未具体说明。信是不完整的，在应该写解释的地方留着一行空白。玛雅读了两遍，注意到正式的语言，以及他划掉的那句关于其他地方机会的话。她把文件夹放回原处，然后继续整理那些装着节日装饰品的箱子。

topic: Someone finds their parent's draft letter of resignation from decades ago
text_en: Ethan was clearing out his mother's desk when he discovered an envelope with his father's handwriting. Inside was a resignation letter, written years before Ethan was born. It mentioned a desire to pursue a different career path, but the final paragraph was missing. The paper was yellowed and creased from being folded many times. Ethan remembered his father had always worked at the same company. He set the letter on the desk, wondering if his father had ever actually sent it. Then he went back to sorting the drawers, placing old bills and receipts into separate piles.
text_zh: 伊桑在清理他母亲的桌子时，发现了一个写有他父亲笔迹的信封。里面是一封辞职信，写于伊桑出生前几年。信中提到了寻求不同职业道路的愿望，但最后一段不见了。纸张因多次折叠而泛黄起皱。伊桑记得他父亲一直在同一家公司工作。他把信放在桌子上，想知道他父亲是否真的寄出过这封信。然后他继续整理抽屉，把旧账单和收据分成几堆。

topic: Someone finds their parent's draft letter of resignation from decades ago
text_en: In a box of old papers, Nora found a draft letter in her mother's handwriting. It was addressed to the head of the hospital where her mother had worked as a nurse. The letter said she was resigning due to a change in family circumstances, but the details were vague. Nora noticed the date was from the year her older brother was born. She remembered her mother had taken a few years off before returning to work. Nora folded the letter and put it in her pocket, planning to ask her mother about it later, then continued unpacking the box.
text_zh: 在一盒旧文件中，诺拉发现了一封她母亲笔迹的信件草稿。信是写给她母亲曾担任护士的那家医院的院长的。信中说她因家庭情况变化而辞职，但细节很模糊。诺拉注意到日期是她哥哥出生的那一年。她记得她母亲休息了几年后才回去工作。诺拉把信叠好放进口袋，打算稍后问母亲这件事，然后继续打开箱子。

topic: Someone finds their parent's draft letter of resignation from decades ago
text_en: Liam was going through his late father's study when he found a handwritten note in a desk drawer. It was a draft resignation from his job at the bank, stating he wished to pursue other interests. The letter wasn't signed and had several scratched-out lines. Liam recalled his father had mentioned once that he'd almost quit to start a business, but the family needed the steady income. Liam read the letter again, noticing the careful penmanship, then placed it back in the drawer with the other papers he hadn't yet sorted.
text_zh: 利亚姆在整理他已故父亲的书房时，在书桌抽屉里发现了一张手写的便条。这是一封从银行工作辞职的草稿，表明他希望追求其他兴趣。信没有签名，并且有几行被划掉了。利亚姆回忆起他父亲曾提到过，他差点辞职去创业，但家里需要稳定的收入。利亚姆又读了一遍信，注意到那工整的笔迹，然后把它放回抽屉里，和其他他还没整理的文件放在一起。

topic: Someone finds their parent's draft letter of resignation from decades ago
text_en: While clearing out the attic for a new storage arrangement, Marta came across a folder tucked behind a stack of old photo albums. Inside was a typed letter from her father, dated decades earlier, addressed to his employer. It was his resignation, but it had never been sent. She read through the formal paragraphs, noting the mention of a different career path he had considered. Marta placed the letter back in the folder and set it on the desk in the spare room. Later, she mentioned it to her brother, who shrugged and said he had never seen it before.
text_zh: 在清理阁楼以进行新的储物安排时，玛尔塔在一堆旧相册后面发现了一个文件夹。里面是一封她父亲写的打印信件，日期是几十年前的，写给他的雇主。这是他的一封辞职信，但从未寄出。她通读了那些正式的段落，注意到其中提到了他考虑过的另一条职业道路。玛尔塔把信放回文件夹里，放在备用房间的桌子上。后来，她向哥哥提起了这件事，哥哥耸耸肩说以前从未见过。

topic: Someone finds their parent's draft letter of resignation from decades ago
text_en: Oliver found a folder in the filing cabinet labeled "Personal" that contained a draft letter from his mother. It was addressed to her school district, stating her resignation from teaching due to a family matter. The letter was undated, but the paper looked old. Oliver remembered his mother had stopped teaching for a few years when he was small, then returned. He wondered what the family matter might have been, but he didn't dwell on it. He put the letter back in the folder and returned it to the cabinet, then went to make lunch.
text_zh: 奥利弗在文件柜里发现了一个标有“个人”的文件夹，里面装着他母亲的一封信件草稿。信是写给她所在的学区的，说明她因家庭事务辞去教职。信没有日期，但纸张看起来很旧。奥利弗记得他母亲在他小时候停止教学几年，然后又回来了。他想知道那个家庭事务可能是什么，但没有深究。他把信放回文件夹，放回柜子里，然后去做午饭了。

topic: Someone finds their parent's draft letter of resignation from decades ago
text_en: When cleaning the bookshelf, Chloe found a letter tucked inside an old novel. It was a draft resignation from her father, addressed to the company where he'd worked for years. The letter said he was leaving to take a position elsewhere, but the name of the new company was left blank. Chloe knew her father had once been offered a job in another state, but he'd turned it down. She read the letter, noting the formal tone, then placed it back in the book and returned it to the shelf.
text_zh: 在清理书架时，克洛伊发现了一封夹在一本旧小说里的信。这是她父亲的辞职信草稿，写给他工作多年的公司。信中说他要离开去别处任职，但新公司的名称是空白的。克洛伊知道她父亲曾有一次在另一个州得到工作机会，但他拒绝了。她读了信，注意到正式的语气，然后把信放回书里，放回书架。

topic: Someone finds their parent's draft letter of resignation from decades ago
text_en: Noah was sorting through boxes in the basement when he came across an envelope with his mother's name on it. Inside was a resignation letter from her job at the law firm, citing a desire to spend more time with her family. The letter was dated from the year Noah was born. His mother had worked part-time for a while after that, then went back full-time. Noah folded the letter, put it back in the envelope, and set it aside with the other documents he was keeping. He continued looking through the remaining boxes.
text_zh: 诺亚在地下室整理箱子时，发现了一个写有他母亲名字的信封。里面是一封她律师事务所工作的辞职信，信中表示希望花更多时间陪伴家人。信的日期是诺亚出生的那一年。他母亲在那之后做了一段时间的兼职，然后又回去做全职。诺亚把信叠好，放回信封里，和他保留的其他文件放在一起。他继续翻看剩下的箱子。

topic: Someone finds their parent's draft letter of resignation from decades ago
text_en: During a spring cleaning of the study, Daniel found an envelope in a drawer of his mother's old desk. It contained a draft of her resignation letter from a company she had left years ago. The letter was handwritten, with several crossed-out lines and a note in the margin about wanting more time for painting. Daniel read it twice, then put it back in the envelope. He left it on the desk and went to make lunch. That evening, he asked his father if he remembered it, but his father only recalled that she had changed jobs around then.
text_zh: 在春季大扫除书房时，丹尼尔在他母亲旧书桌的抽屉里发现了一个信封。里面装着她多年前离开的一家公司辞职信的草稿。信是手写的，有几行被划掉，页边空白处有一条关于想要更多时间画画的注释。丹尼尔读了两遍，然后把它放回信封里。他把它留在桌子上，然后去做午饭。那天晚上，他问他父亲是否记得这件事，但他父亲只记得她当时换了工作。

topic: Someone finds their parent's draft letter of resignation from decades ago
text_en: While looking for a lost book, Isaac found a letter in the back of a drawer. It was a draft resignation from his father, written on company letterhead. The letter stated he was resigning effective immediately, but there was no reason given. Isaac knew his father had been laid off once, but this seemed different. He read the letter, noticing the date was from a time when his parents were having financial difficulties. He put the letter back in the drawer, closed it, and went back to searching for his book.
text_zh: 在寻找一本丢失的书时，艾萨克在抽屉深处发现了一封信。那是他父亲写的一封辞职信草稿，用的是公司信纸。信中说他将立即辞职，但没有给出理由。艾萨克知道他父亲曾被解雇过一次，但这似乎不同。他读了信，注意到日期是在他父母经济困难的时候。他把信放回抽屉，关上抽屉，继续找他的书。

topic: Someone finds their parent's draft letter of resignation from decades ago
text_en: While sorting through boxes in the garage, Elena discovered a manila folder with her father's name on it. Inside was a draft of a resignation letter he had written to the factory where he had worked for many years. The letter mentioned plans to start a small repair shop, but it had never been mailed. Elena set the folder aside and continued sorting. Later, she showed it to her mother, who said she remembered him talking about that idea once. Elena returned the letter to the folder and placed it on a shelf in the hallway.
text_zh: 在整理车库里的箱子时，埃琳娜发现了一个写着父亲名字的牛皮纸文件夹。里面是一封他写给工作多年的工厂的辞职信草稿。信中提到了开一家小修理店的计划，但这封信从未寄出。埃琳娜把文件夹放在一边，继续整理。后来，她把它拿给母亲看，母亲说她记得他曾提过那个想法一次。埃琳娜把信放回文件夹，把它放在走廊的架子上。

topic: Someone finds their parent's draft letter of resignation from decades ago
text_en: Cleaning out a closet in the hallway, James found a shoebox containing old documents. Among them was a typed resignation letter from his mother, written to the bank where she had been employed. The letter was dated years before she actually left, and it referenced a desire to move to a coastal town. James read it and then put it back in the shoebox. He finished organizing the closet and later mentioned the letter to his sister. She said she had never heard about that plan and thought it might have been just a passing idea.
text_zh: 在清理走廊的壁橱时，詹姆斯发现了一个装着旧文件的鞋盒。其中有一封他母亲打字的辞职信，是写给她曾任职的银行的。信的日期比她实际离开早了好几年，信中提到了搬到沿海小镇的愿望。詹姆斯读了信，然后把它放回鞋盒。他整理完壁橱，后来向妹妹提到了这封信。她说她从未听说过那个计划，认为那可能只是一时的想法。

topic: Someone finds their parent's draft letter of resignation from decades ago
text_en: While unpacking after a move, Priya found a drawer in an old cabinet that contained a folder with her father's handwriting. Inside was a draft of a resignation letter to his university department. The letter spoke of pursuing independent research, but it had never been sent. Priya read it and then placed it back in the folder. She continued unpacking and later told her aunt about the discovery. Her aunt recalled that her father had often talked about leaving academia but never did. Priya left the folder on the cabinet and went back to arranging books.
text_zh: 搬家后整理物品时，普里亚在一个旧柜子的抽屉里发现了一个文件夹，上面有她父亲的笔迹。里面是一封写给他大学院系的辞职信草稿。信中提到了从事独立研究的计划，但这封信从未寄出。普里亚读了信，然后把它放回文件夹。她继续整理，后来把这一发现告诉了姑姑。姑姑回忆说，她父亲经常谈论离开学术界，但从未付诸行动。普里亚把文件夹留在柜子上，回去整理书籍。

topic: Someone finds their parent's draft letter of resignation from decades ago
text_en: While looking for a spare key in the kitchen drawer, Tom found an old envelope with his mother's name on it. It held a draft of her resignation letter from the hospital where she had worked as a nurse. The letter was dated years before she actually retired and mentioned a wish to open a small bakery. Tom read it and then put it back in the envelope. He placed it on the counter and went about his day. That evening, he asked his father about it, but his father only said she had talked about baking sometimes.
text_zh: 在厨房抽屉里找备用钥匙时，汤姆发现了一个写着母亲名字的旧信封。里面是她从曾担任护士的医院辞职的信的草稿。信的日期比她实际退休早了好几年，信中提到了开一家小面包店的愿望。汤姆读了信，然后把它放回信封。他把信封放在柜台上，继续过他的日子。那天晚上，他向父亲问起这件事，但父亲只说母亲有时会谈论烘焙。

topic: Someone finds their parent's draft letter of resignation from decades ago
text_en: During a routine cleaning of the bookshelf, Nina found a folded piece of paper tucked inside an old novel. It was a draft of her father's resignation letter from the law firm where he had been a partner. The letter was dated many years earlier and mentioned a plan to teach at a community college. Nina read it and then refolded it and put it back in the book. She continued dusting the shelves. Later, she mentioned it to her cousin, who said he had never heard that story. Nina left the book on the shelf.
text_zh: 在例行清理书架时，尼娜发现一本旧小说里夹着一张折叠的纸。那是她父亲从他曾担任合伙人的律师事务所辞职的信的草稿。信的日期早了很多年，信中提到了在社区大学教书的计划。尼娜读了信，然后重新折好放回书里。她继续掸书架上的灰尘。后来，她向表兄提到了这件事，表兄说他从未听说过那个故事。尼娜把书留在书架上。

topic: Someone finds their parent's draft letter of resignation from decades ago
text_en: While clearing out a storage unit, Marcus found a box of his mother's papers from her old job at a publishing company. Among them was a draft of a resignation letter she had written but never sent. The letter mentioned wanting to travel and write a novel. Marcus read it and then placed it back in the box with the other papers. He finished going through the box and took it to his car. Later, he mentioned the letter to his brother, who said their mother had often talked about writing but never did.
text_zh: 在清理一个储物间时，马库斯发现了一箱母亲在出版公司旧工作的文件。其中有一封她写了但从未寄出的辞职信草稿。信中提到了想旅行和写小说的愿望。马库斯读了信，然后把它放回装有其他文件的箱子里。他翻完箱子，把它拿到车上。后来，他向哥哥提到了这封信，哥哥说他们的母亲经常谈论写作，但从未付诸行动。

topic: Someone finds their parent's draft letter of resignation from decades ago
text_en: While organizing the garage, Sandra found a folder in a stack of old bills. Inside was a typed resignation letter from her father, addressed to the company where he had worked as an engineer. The letter was dated years before he actually left and mentioned a plan to start a consulting business. Sandra read it and then put it back in the folder. She continued organizing the garage and later told her mother about it. Her mother said she remembered him discussing that idea once, but he never acted on it.
text_zh: 在整理车库时，桑德拉在一堆旧账单中发现了一个文件夹。里面是一封她父亲打字的辞职信，收件人是他曾担任工程师的公司。信的日期比他实际离开早了好几年，信中提到了创办咨询公司的计划。桑德拉读了信，然后把它放回文件夹。她继续整理车库，后来把这件事告诉了母亲。母亲说她记得他曾讨论过那个想法一次，但他从未付诸行动。

topic: Someone finds their parent's draft letter of resignation from decades ago
text_en: While looking through a drawer in the dining room, Peter found an old envelope with his mother's handwriting. It contained a draft of her resignation letter from the school where she had taught. The letter was dated years before she retired and mentioned a desire to open a small bookstore. Peter read it and then put it back in the envelope. He placed it on the sideboard and went to help with dinner. Later, he asked his aunt about it, but she only said that his mother had always loved reading.
text_zh: 在翻看餐厅的抽屉时，彼得发现了一个有母亲笔迹的旧信封。里面是她从曾教书的学校辞职的信的草稿。信的日期比她退休早了好几年，信中提到了开一家小书店的愿望。彼得读了信，然后把它放回信封。他把信封放在餐具柜上，去帮忙做晚饭。后来，他向姑姑问起这件事，但她只说他的母亲一直很喜欢阅读。

topic: Someone finds their parent's draft letter of resignation from decades ago
text_en: While clearing out the home office, Rachel found a folder in the bottom of a filing cabinet. Inside was a draft of her father's resignation letter from the bank where he had worked for many years. The letter was dated decades earlier and mentioned a plan to move to a rural area and farm. Rachel read it and then put it back in the folder. She continued sorting through the cabinet and later mentioned the letter to her uncle. He said he remembered his brother talking about farming once, but it never came to anything.
text_zh: 在清理家庭办公室时，蕾切尔在文件柜底部发现了一个文件夹。里面是她父亲从工作多年的银行辞职的信的草稿。信的日期早了几十年，信中提到了搬到农村地区务农的计划。蕾切尔读了信，然后把它放回文件夹。她继续整理文件柜，后来向叔叔提到了这封信。他说他记得他的兄弟曾谈论过务农，但从未有任何结果。

topic: Someone receives an apology letter years after the incident
text_en: Marta found the envelope wedged behind a stack of old cookbooks while clearing out her mother's pantry. The handwriting on the front was familiar, though it took her a moment to place it—Daniel, from her first job at the bookstore. Inside, a single page apologized for the way he'd handled their disagreement about the missing cash register receipts. He wrote that he'd always regretted implying she was careless. Marta folded the letter and put it in her coat pocket. She finished sorting the shelves, then made a cup of tea and thought about that winter.
text_zh: 玛尔塔在清理母亲的食物储藏室时，在一叠旧食谱书后面发现了一个信封。信封上的笔迹很熟悉，但她花了一会儿才认出是谁的——丹尼尔，她第一份工作书店里的同事。里面只有一页纸，为他在处理他们关于收银机收据丢失的争执时的行为道歉。他写道，他一直后悔暗示她粗心大意。玛尔塔把信折好放进了外套口袋。她整理完架子，然后泡了一杯茶，想起了那个冬天。

topic: Someone receives an apology letter years after the incident
text_en: The letter came with a postmark from a town he'd only visited once. Ethan recognized the neat, slanted script immediately—it was from his old college roommate, who had stopped speaking to him after a misunderstanding about a shared research notebook. The apology explained that he'd been under pressure and had overreacted, and that he now understood Ethan hadn't taken the notes without permission. Ethan read it twice, then placed it on the desk beside his laptop. He answered a few emails and later mentioned the letter to his wife over dinner, briefly, before the conversation moved on.
text_zh: 这封信的邮戳来自一个他只去过一次的小镇。伊桑立刻认出了那整洁而倾斜的笔迹——是他大学时的室友写的，他们曾因一本共用研究笔记本的误会而不再说话。道歉信解释说，他当时压力很大，反应过度了，现在他明白了伊桑并没有未经允许拿走笔记。伊桑读了两遍，然后把信放在笔记本电脑旁边的桌子上。他回复了几封邮件，后来在晚餐时简短地向妻子提起了这封信，然后话题就转开了。

topic: Someone receives an apology letter years after the incident
text_en: Nina was reorganizing her desk drawer when she came across a sealed envelope with her name written in pencil. It was from a former coworker, someone she'd clashed with during a team project several years ago. The letter said he was sorry for the way he'd spoken to her in that meeting, and that he'd since realized she was only trying to meet the deadline. Nina slid the letter back into the envelope and tucked it into a folder of old paperwork. She continued sorting the drawer, then went to make coffee.
text_zh: 尼娜正在整理书桌抽屉时，发现了一个用铅笔写着她名字的密封信封。信来自一位前同事，几年前在一个团队项目中她曾与对方发生过冲突。信中说，他很抱歉在那次会议上对她说话的方式，他后来意识到她只是想赶上截止日期。尼娜把信滑回信封，塞进了一个装满旧文件的文件夹里。她继续整理抽屉，然后去煮咖啡。

topic: Someone receives an apology letter years after the incident
text_en: A plain white envelope sat on the doormat when Greg got home from work. Inside was a handwritten note from a neighbor who had moved away the previous year. The neighbor apologized for letting his dog dig up Greg's flower bed and for not replacing the plants before he left. He wrote that he'd meant to say something but the move had been chaotic. Greg read the note, folded it, and put it on the kitchen counter. He watered his remaining plants and later mentioned the letter to his sister on the phone.
text_zh: 格雷格下班回家时，门垫上放着一个普通的白色信封。里面是一封手写的便条，来自一位去年搬走的邻居。邻居为让他的狗挖了格雷格的花坛，以及搬走前没有补种植物而道歉。他写道，他本想说的，但搬家太混乱了。格雷格读了便条，折好，放在厨房台面上。他给剩下的植物浇了水，后来在电话里向姐姐提起了这封信。

topic: Someone receives an apology letter years after the incident
text_en: Maya found the envelope while sorting through a box of old bills. The handwriting on the front was familiar, though she hadn't seen it in years. Inside was a single page, apologizing for a harsh comment made at a mutual friend's party. She remembered the remark, and how it had stung at the time. Now, she read the words twice, noting the careful phrasing. She placed the letter on the kitchen counter and finished sorting the box. Later, she filed it with her other important papers, not entirely sure what to do with it, but deciding it was worth keeping.
text_zh: 玛雅在整理一盒旧账单时发现了这个信封。信封上的笔迹很熟悉，尽管她多年未见了。里面只有一页纸，为在一次共同朋友的聚会上说的一句刻薄话道歉。她记得那句话，以及当时它带来的刺痛。现在，她读了两遍，注意到措辞的谨慎。她把信放在厨房台面上，继续整理盒子。后来，她把它和其他重要文件放在一起，不完全确定该怎么处理，但觉得值得保留。

topic: Someone receives an apology letter years after the incident
text_en: Tom was going through his filing cabinet when he found an envelope with his name on it, tucked behind some old tax documents. It was from a former colleague who had left the company after a dispute over a project's direction. The letter said he was sorry for the way he'd criticized Tom's work in front of the team, and that he'd since realized his own frustration was misdirected. Tom read it, then put it in the recycling bin. He closed the drawer and went back to the task he'd been working on.
text_zh: 汤姆在翻文件柜时，发现了一个写着他名字的信封，塞在一些旧税务文件后面。信来自一位前同事，他在一次项目方向争议后离开了公司。信中说，他很抱歉在团队面前批评汤姆的工作，他后来意识到自己的沮丧是错位的。汤姆读了信，然后把它放进了回收箱。他关上抽屉，继续做他一直在做的事情。

topic: Someone receives an apology letter years after the incident
text_en: A letter arrived in the mail for Alicia, addressed in a careful cursive she recognized from her aunt's handwriting. But the return address was from an old friend from high school, someone she'd stopped talking to after a misunderstanding about a shared secret. The letter apologized for spreading a rumor and said she'd always felt bad about it. Alicia read the letter while standing in the kitchen, then put it on the counter. She continued preparing dinner and later mentioned it to her husband, who nodded but didn't have much to say.
text_zh: 一封信寄到了艾丽西亚手中，地址是用她认出的姑妈的笔迹写的，字迹工整的草书。但回信地址来自一位高中时的老朋友，一个因共享秘密的误会而不再说话的人。信中为散布谣言道歉，并说她一直为此感到难过。艾丽西亚站在厨房里读了信，然后把它放在台面上。她继续准备晚餐，后来向丈夫提起了这件事，丈夫点了点头，但没有多说什么。

topic: Someone receives an apology letter years after the incident
text_en: The letter arrived on a Tuesday, tucked between a catalog and a utility bill. It was from an old colleague, apologizing for taking credit for a project they'd worked on together. The apology was detailed, acknowledging the specific meeting where the credit was claimed. He read it while standing by the mailbox. He remembered the project well, and the awkward silence that had followed. He folded the letter and put it in his coat pocket. That evening, he mentioned it to his wife, who asked what he planned to do. He shrugged, saying he hadn't decided yet.
text_zh: 信是在一个星期二到的，夹在一本目录和一张水电费账单之间。信来自一位老同事，为在一个共同参与的项目中独占功劳而道歉。道歉很详细，指出了具体声称功劳的会议。他站在邮箱旁读了信。他清楚地记得那个项目，以及随之而来的尴尬沉默。他把信折好放进了外套口袋。那天晚上，他向妻子提起了这件事，妻子问他打算怎么办。他耸耸肩，说他还没决定。

topic: Someone receives an apology letter years after the incident
text_en: In the pile of mail was a cream-colored envelope with no return address. Inside, a note from a former neighbor apologized for not returning a borrowed ladder before moving away. The neighbor wrote that they'd found it in their garage and felt they should explain. The man pictured the ladder, which he'd replaced years ago. He hadn't thought about it in a long time. He read the apology, then set it aside. He went to the garage to check his tools, and saw the newer ladder hanging on the wall. He came back inside and tossed the letter into the recycling bin.
text_zh: 在一堆邮件中有一个奶油色的信封，没有回信地址。里面有一张便条，来自一位前邻居，为搬走前没有归还借的梯子而道歉。邻居写道，他们在车库里发现了梯子，觉得应该解释一下。那人想象着那把梯子，他多年前已经换掉了。他很久没有想起过它了。他读了道歉信，然后把它放在一边。他去车库检查工具，看到墙上挂着的新梯子。他回到屋里，把信扔进了回收箱。

topic: Someone receives an apology letter years after the incident
text_en: A letter from an old high school friend arrived, apologizing for not showing up to a planned study session before finals. The friend wrote that a family issue had come up, and they hadn't known how to explain it at the time. The woman read the note while making her morning coffee. She remembered waiting at the library, then studying alone. She finished making her coffee and sat down to read the rest of the mail. She considered writing back, but the address was old. She put the letter on the table, next to her mug.
text_zh: 一封来自高中老友的信到了，为期末考试前没有出现在计划的学习会上而道歉。朋友写道，当时家里出了点事，他们不知道该怎么解释。女人在煮晨间咖啡时读了便条。她记得在图书馆等待，然后独自学习。她煮完咖啡，坐下来读剩下的邮件。她考虑回信，但地址是旧的。她把信放在桌子上，旁边是她的杯子。

topic: Someone receives an apology letter years after the incident
text_en: The envelope was postmarked from a city he'd lived in years ago. Inside, a former roommate apologized for leaving without paying his share of the last utility bill. He wrote that he'd been in a difficult spot and had meant to settle it later. The man read the apology, recalling the final month in that apartment, the unpaid bill, and the awkward silence when they'd parted. He hadn't thought about it in years. He set the letter on the desk and went back to his work. Later, he filed it with his old receipts.
text_zh: 信封上的邮戳来自他多年前住过的一个城市。里面，一位前室友为没有支付最后一份水电费就离开而道歉。他写道，他当时处境困难，本打算以后再解决。那人读着道歉信，回忆起在那间公寓的最后一个月、未付的账单，以及他们分别时尴尬的沉默。他已经多年没有想过这件事了。他把信放在桌上，回去继续工作。后来，他把信和旧收据一起归档了。

topic: Someone receives an apology letter years after the incident
text_en: Maya found the envelope tucked between old utility bills while sorting through a drawer she rarely opened. The handwriting was familiar—Lena's looping cursive, unchanged after all these years. Inside, a single page explained the misunderstanding that had ended their friendship during their final semester of college. Lena wrote that she had finally understood what actually happened that afternoon, and she was sorry for the accusations she had made. Maya read the letter twice, then set it on the kitchen counter. She finished sorting the drawer, putting the bills in a recycling pile. Later, she would decide whether to write back.
text_zh: 玛雅在整理一个她很少打开的抽屉时，发现信封夹在旧水电费账单之间。笔迹很熟悉——莉娜那弯弯曲曲的草书，这么多年一直没变。里面，一页纸解释了那个在大学最后一个学期结束她们友谊的误会。莉娜写道，她终于明白了那天下午到底发生了什么，她为自己所做的指责感到抱歉。玛雅把信读了两遍，然后把它放在厨房台面上。她整理完抽屉，把账单放进回收堆。稍后，她会决定是否回信。

topic: Someone receives an apology letter years after the incident
text_en: A letter arrived from an old friend, apologizing for missing a wedding they were supposed to attend. The friend explained that a last-minute work trip had made it impossible. The man read the note while sitting on the porch. He remembered the wedding, and the empty seat at the reception. He also remembered that the friend had sent a gift, so the absence had never seemed like a slight. He finished reading, then put the letter on the side table. He went back to his coffee, which had grown lukewarm.
text_zh: 一封来自老朋友的信，为错过他们本应参加的婚礼而道歉。朋友解释说，最后一刻的出差使他无法参加。那人坐在门廊上读着信。他记得那场婚礼，以及招待会上那个空座位。他还记得朋友送过礼物，所以缺席从未显得像怠慢。他读完信，然后把信放在边桌上。他回去喝咖啡，咖啡已经变得温热了。

topic: Someone receives an apology letter years after the incident
text_en: Lena was clearing out her childhood bedroom when she found the letter in a shoebox of school papers. It was from her high school friend, who had stopped speaking to her after a misunderstanding about a shared project. The letter explained how sorry she was for not listening back then. Lena folded it and placed it back in the box, then went downstairs to help her mother with the garage sale. She didn't mention the letter to anyone, but she kept it in her purse for the rest of the day.
text_zh: 莉娜正在清理她童年的卧室时，在一个装满学校文件的鞋盒里发现了那封信。信来自她的高中朋友，她在一次共同项目的误会后不再和她说话。信里解释了她当时没有倾听是多么抱歉。莉娜把信折好，放回盒子里，然后下楼帮母亲处理车库拍卖。她没有向任何人提起这封信，但那天剩下的时间里，她一直把它放在钱包里。

topic: Someone receives an apology letter years after the incident
text_en: Jonas was going through his late father's desk when he discovered a letter addressed to him. The handwriting was his father's, but the date was from years ago, before they had stopped talking. The letter was an apology for not being more supportive of Jonas's career choice. Jonas read it slowly, then placed it back in the drawer. He finished sorting the desk, setting aside items to keep and items to donate. That evening, he mentioned the letter to his sister over the phone, but they didn't dwell on it.
text_zh: 乔纳斯在整理他已故父亲的书桌时，发现了一封写给他的信。笔迹是他父亲的，但日期是多年前，在他们停止交谈之前。信是为没有更支持乔纳斯的职业选择而道歉。乔纳斯慢慢地读着信，然后把它放回抽屉。他整理完书桌，把要保留和要捐赠的物品分开。那天晚上，他在电话里向妹妹提到了这封信，但他们没有深究。

topic: Someone receives an apology letter years after the incident
text_en: Priya was unpacking boxes from her recent move when she came across a letter from an old coworker. They had worked together on a project that went poorly, and the coworker had blamed her unfairly. The letter was an apology for that blame, explaining that he had been under pressure and had taken it out on her. Priya read it, then put it in the recycling pile. She continued unpacking, arranging her books on the shelf. Later, she told her partner about it, and they both agreed it was good to have an apology, even if late.
text_zh: 普里亚正在拆最近搬家时的箱子，偶然发现了一封来自一位老同事的信。他们曾一起参与一个进展不佳的项目，那位同事不公平地责怪了她。信是为那次指责道歉，解释说他当时压力很大，把气撒在了她身上。普里亚读了信，然后把它放进回收堆。她继续拆箱，把书排列在书架上。后来，她告诉了伴侣这件事，他们都同意，即使道歉晚了，有道歉也是好的。

topic: Someone receives an apology letter years after the incident
text_en: Ethan was looking for a spare charger in his closet when he found a box of letters from his college years. One was from his ex-girlfriend, apologizing for how she had ended things abruptly after a fight. She wrote that she had been immature and regretted not talking it through. Ethan read the letter, then put it back in the box with the others. He found the charger and plugged in his phone. He didn't feel any need to respond, but he left the box out on the shelf instead of putting it back in the closet.
text_zh: 伊桑在衣柜里找备用充电器时，发现了一盒大学时期的信件。其中一封来自他的前女友，为她在一次争吵后突然结束关系而道歉。她写道，她当时不成熟，后悔没有好好谈一谈。伊桑读了信，然后把它和其他信一起放回盒子里。他找到了充电器，给手机插上电。他觉得没有必要回复，但他把盒子放在架子上，而不是放回衣柜里。

topic: Someone receives an apology letter years after the incident
text_en: Aisha was cleaning her office when she found a letter in a folder of old receipts. It was from a former client who had left a negative review years ago, blaming her for a delay that wasn't her fault. The letter was an apology, explaining that he had later learned the fault lay elsewhere. Aisha read it, then filed it in the recycling bin. She tidied her desk, sharpened a pencil, and made a list for the afternoon. She didn't mention it to her colleagues, but she felt a small sense of closure.
text_zh: 艾莎在打扫办公室时，在一个旧收据文件夹里发现了一封信。信来自一位多年前留下负面评价的前客户，责怪她造成了一次并非她过错的延误。信是道歉，解释说后来他了解到过错在别处。艾莎读了信，然后把它归档到回收箱。她整理好桌子，削了一支铅笔，为下午列了一个清单。她没有向同事提起这件事，但她感到一种小小的了结。

topic: Someone receives an apology letter years after the incident
text_en: Tom was helping his mother sort through her attic when he found a letter from his old basketball coach. The coach had benched him during a championship game, and Tom had quit the team in frustration. The letter apologized for that decision, saying he had been too focused on strategy and not enough on the players. Tom read it, then folded it and put it in his pocket. He continued helping his mother, carrying boxes down the stairs. Later, he called his brother to talk about it, but they soon moved on to other topics.
text_zh: 汤姆在帮母亲整理阁楼时，发现了一封来自他老篮球教练的信。教练在一场冠军赛中让他坐冷板凳，汤姆一气之下退出了球队。信为那个决定道歉，说他当时太专注于战术，而没有足够关注球员。汤姆读了信，然后把它折好放进口袋。他继续帮母亲，把箱子搬下楼。后来，他打电话给哥哥谈论这件事，但他们很快转向了其他话题。

topic: Someone receives an apology letter years after the incident
text_en: The letter arrived in a cream-colored envelope with a return address in a town Daniel had left behind a decade ago. It was from his former supervisor, the man who had let him go after a project went sideways. The supervisor wrote that he had since reviewed the records and realized Daniel had followed the instructions he had been given, and that the failure had been a miscommunication from above. He apologized for the way things had ended. Daniel folded the letter and placed it on the stack of mail by the door. He picked up his keys and headed out to run errands, the letter still on his mind.
text_zh: 信装在一个奶油色的信封里，回信地址是丹尼尔十年前离开的一个小镇。信来自他的前主管，那个在一个项目出问题后让他离开的人。主管写道，他后来审查了记录，意识到丹尼尔遵循了给他的指示，失败是上层的沟通失误。他为事情结束的方式道歉。丹尼尔把信折好，放在门边的一堆邮件上。他拿起钥匙出门办事，心里还想着那封信。

topic: Two siblings discover different versions of their inheritance
text_en: Maya and her brother sat in the lawyer's office, each holding a folder. Their mother had left the house and its contents to them jointly, but the paperwork in front of them told different stories. Maya's copy listed the cottage and the land around it. Theo's copy described an apartment in the city and a set of stocks. They compared the documents, line by line, and found their mother's signature on both. The lawyer adjusted his glasses and said he would look into the discrepancy. Maya closed her folder and asked Theo if he wanted to get lunch. They walked out together, discussing what their mother might have intended.
text_zh: 玛雅和她的兄弟坐在律师办公室里，每人手里拿着一个文件夹。他们的母亲把房子及其中的物品共同留给了他们，但他们面前的文件却讲述了不同的故事。玛雅的那份列出了小屋及其周围的土地。西奥的那份描述的是一套城市公寓和一些股票。他们逐行比较了文件，发现两份文件上都有母亲的签名。律师调整了一下眼镜，说他会调查这个差异。玛雅合上文件夹，问西奥想不想去吃午饭。他们一起走了出去，讨论着母亲可能的意图。

topic: Two siblings discover different versions of their inheritance
text_en: Elena's brother called her over to the old filing cabinet. He held a will that left the house to him alone. Elena had found another will in the attic trunk, leaving everything to her. They stood in the hallway, papers in hand, looking at each other. The handwriting on both looked like their father's. Elena noticed the second will had a different notary stamp. Her brother shrugged and put his copy back in the drawer. Elena kept hers in her coat pocket. They agreed to wait until the estate lawyer returned from vacation before deciding what to do next.
text_zh: 埃琳娜的兄弟叫她到旧文件柜旁。他手里拿着一份遗嘱，把房子单独留给了他。埃琳娜在阁楼的箱子里发现了另一份遗嘱，把一切都留给了她。他们站在走廊里，手里拿着文件，面面相觑。两份文件上的笔迹看起来都像他们父亲的。埃琳娜注意到第二份遗嘱上的公证印章不同。她的兄弟耸耸肩，把他的那份放回了抽屉。埃琳娜把她的那份放进了外套口袋。他们同意等遗产律师度假回来后再决定下一步怎么做。

topic: Two siblings discover different versions of their inheritance
text_en: At the reading, the lawyer announced that the siblings would split the family bakery equally. But later, in the back office, the younger brother found a handwritten note from their father, tucked inside an old recipe book. It said the bakery should go entirely to him. His sister, meanwhile, had found a similar note in the basement, naming her as sole owner. They met outside on the sidewalk, each holding their note. Neither had expected this. They compared the handwriting and saw small differences in the loops of the letters. They folded the notes and walked to the corner café to talk it over.
text_zh: 在宣读遗嘱时，律师宣布兄弟姐妹将平分家庭面包店。但后来，在后屋办公室里，弟弟在一本旧食谱书里发现了一张父亲手写的便条。便条上说面包店应该完全归他。与此同时，他的姐姐在地下室里也发现了一张类似的便条，上面写着她是唯一的所有者。他们在外面的人行道上相遇，每人手里都拿着自己的便条。两人都没有预料到这一点。他们比较了笔迹，发现字母的环状部分有细微的差异。他们折好便条，走到街角的咖啡馆去商量这件事。

topic: Two siblings discover different versions of their inheritance
text_en: At the reading of their aunt's will, Celia and her brother each received a sealed envelope containing a map to a small plot of land. Celia's map had a red circle around a section near the river. Her brother's map had a red circle around a different section, further north. Both maps were labeled with their aunt's name and the same property description. They spread the maps on the kitchen table, tracing the roads with their fingers. The land was the same size on both, but the locations did not match. Celia noticed the river was drawn differently on her brother's copy. They decided to drive out to the property the following weekend to see which map was accurate.
text_zh: 在宣读他们姑妈的遗嘱时，西莉亚和她的兄弟每人收到一个密封的信封，里面装着一张通往一小块土地的地图。西莉亚的地图上，靠近河边的一个区域被红圈标出。她兄弟的地图上，更靠北的一个不同区域被红圈标出。两张地图上都标有他们姑妈的名字和相同的房产描述。他们把地图摊在厨房桌子上，用手指沿着道路描画。两块地在两张地图上大小相同，但位置却不匹配。西莉亚注意到她兄弟那份地图上的河流画法不同。他们决定下个周末开车去那块地看看哪张地图是准确的。

topic: Two siblings discover different versions of their inheritance
text_en: When their mother's safe was opened, it contained a single deed to a house in the neighboring town. The name on the deed was their mother's, but the property address was different in the copy that each sibling had been given. Lena's copy listed a house on Maple Street, while her brother's copy listed the same house on Oak Avenue. The signatures and dates were identical. They compared the documents side by side, checking the notary stamps. The stamps were also the same. Lena called the county recorder's office to verify the official listing. The clerk said the property was registered under the Maple Street address. Her brother folded his copy and put it in his jacket pocket, saying he would look into it later.
text_zh: 当他们母亲的保险柜被打开时，里面只有一张通往邻镇一所房子的地契。地契上的名字是他们母亲的，但每个兄弟姐妹拿到的那份副本上的房产地址却不同。莉娜的副本上写的是枫树街的一所房子，而她兄弟的副本上写的是同一所房子在橡树大道。签名和日期完全相同。他们并排比较了文件，检查了公证印章。印章也相同。莉娜打电话给县记录员办公室核实官方登记信息。办事员说该房产登记在枫树街地址下。她的兄弟折起他的副本，放进夹克口袋，说稍后会调查。

topic: Two siblings discover different versions of their inheritance
text_en: After their mother passed, the siblings went through her apartment. In the bedroom drawer, the older brother found a will naming him as the recipient of the antique clock collection.
