In the kitchen, the younger sister found a different will, giving her the same collection. They sat on the couch, each holding a will. The brother noted the date on his was older. The sister pointed out that hers had been notarized more recently. They placed both wills on the coffee table, side by side. Neither reached for the phone to call a lawyer just yet. They decided to make tea first.
text_zh: 母亲去世后，兄弟姐妹们翻遍了她的公寓。在卧室的抽屉里，哥哥发现了一份遗嘱，指定他为古董钟表收藏的继承人。在厨房里，妹妹发现了另一份遗嘱，把同样的收藏留给了她。他们坐在沙发上，每人手里拿着一份遗嘱。哥哥指出他那一份的日期更早。妹妹指出她那一份是最近公证的。他们把两份遗嘱并排放在咖啡桌上。两人都还没有伸手去打电话叫律师。他们决定先泡杯茶。

topic: Two siblings discover different versions of their inheritance
text_en: Rafael and his sister drove to their grandfather's farmhouse after the funeral. In the study, Rafael found a deed in the desk drawer, transferring the house to him. His sister, in the bedroom, found another deed, naming her as the owner. They met in the hallway, each holding their paper. Rafael looked at his sister's deed, then at his own. The signatures were similar but the dates were different. His sister mentioned that their grandfather had redone his will a few years ago. Rafael nodded and folded his deed. They walked out to the porch, where the afternoon sun was warm, and discussed what to do next.
text_zh: 葬礼后，拉斐尔和他的妹妹开车去了祖父的农舍。在书房里，拉斐尔在书桌抽屉里发现了一份地契，将房子转让给了他。他的妹妹在卧室里发现了另一份地契，上面写着她是所有者。他们在走廊里相遇，每人手里都拿着自己的文件。拉斐尔看了看妹妹的地契，又看了看自己的。签名相似，但日期不同。他的妹妹提到，他们的祖父几年前重新立过遗嘱。拉斐尔点了点头，折起了他的地契。他们走到门廊上，午后的阳光温暖，讨论着下一步该怎么做。

topic: Two siblings discover different versions of their inheritance
text_en: After their grandfather passed, his will mentioned a collection of vintage watches that was to be divided equally. When the siblings opened the storage unit, they found a glass case with several watches inside. Each watch had a small tag with a name. The tags were mixed up, with some names repeated and others missing. The siblings took turns examining the timepieces, checking the engravings on the backs. Some watches had initials that did not match any family member they knew. They placed the watches back in the case and decided to make an inventory later. For now, they locked the unit and went to get lunch at a nearby diner.
text_zh: 祖父去世后，他的遗嘱中提到一批古董手表要平分。当兄弟姐妹们打开储物单元时，他们发现了一个玻璃柜，里面有几块手表。每块手表上都有一个小标签，写着名字。标签被弄混了，有些名字重复，有些则缺失。兄弟姐妹们轮流检查这些手表，查看背面的刻字。有些手表上的首字母与他们认识的任何家庭成员都不匹配。他们把表放回柜子里，决定稍后做个清单。目前，他们锁上储物单元，去附近的一家小餐馆吃午饭。

topic: Two siblings discover different versions of their inheritance
text_en: The inheritance was a small bookshop, according to their uncle's letter. When Nina and her brother arrived at the address, they found a building that was clearly a bakery. The sign above the door read 'Golden Crust Bakery,' and the windows displayed loaves of bread. They went inside and asked the owner about the bookshop. The owner said she had owned the bakery for years and had never heard of a bookstore at that location. Nina showed her the letter, which included a photograph of the storefront. The photo showed a bookstore with the same address, but the building in the photo looked older. They thanked the owner and stepped outside, looking at the photo again before putting it away.
text_zh: 根据他们叔叔的信，遗产是一家小书店。当妮娜和她的兄弟到达那个地址时，他们发现了一栋显然是面包店的建筑。门上的招牌写着“金脆皮面包店”，窗户里陈列着面包。他们走进去，向店主询问书店的事。店主说她经营这家面包店多年，从未听说过那个位置有书店。妮娜给她看了那封信，信里附有一张店面照片。照片上显示的是一家书店，地址相同，但照片中的建筑看起来更旧。他们谢过店主，走到外面，又看了看照片，然后把它收了起来。

topic: Two siblings discover different versions of their inheritance
text_en: Their father's will left a plot of land to each of his children. The surveyor's report that accompanied the will described the land as being adjacent to the family farm. However, when the siblings drove to the farm, they found a new housing development had been built on the edge of the property. The land they were supposed to inherit was now occupied by a row of houses. They parked at the end of the street and looked at the houses, which all looked similar. Their father's map showed the plot as empty, with no buildings. They decided to speak to the developer who had built the houses to ask about the land's history.
text_zh: 他们父亲的遗嘱给每个孩子留了一块地。随遗嘱附上的测量员报告描述这块地与家庭农场相邻。然而，当兄弟姐妹们开车到农场时，他们发现一片新的住宅开发项目已经建在房产边缘。他们本应继承的土地现在被一排房子占据了。他们把车停在街尾，看着那些看起来都很相似的房子。他们父亲的地图显示这块地是空的，没有建筑物。他们决定去找建造这些房子的开发商，询问这块地的历史。

topic: Two siblings discover different versions of their inheritance
text_en: A letter from a distant relative informed the siblings that they were to receive a share of a family trust. The letter included a list of assets, which included a small apartment in the city. When they contacted the trustee, they were told the apartment had been sold several years ago. The trustee provided a copy of the sale record, which showed the property had been transferred to an unknown buyer. The siblings looked at the original letter again, which did not mention any sale. They asked the trustee for more details, but he said he did not have any additional information. They left the meeting and walked down the street, discussing what to do next.
text_zh: 一封来自远亲的信告知这对兄弟姐妹，他们将获得家族信托基金的一部分。信中附有一份资产清单，其中包括市内的一间小公寓。当他们联系受托人时，被告知该公寓已在几年前售出。受托人提供了一份销售记录的副本，显示该房产已转让给一位不知名的买家。兄弟姐妹再次查看原信，信中并未提及任何销售事宜。他们向受托人询问更多细节，但他说没有更多信息。他们离开会面地点，沿街走去，讨论下一步该怎么做。

topic: Two siblings discover different versions of their inheritance
text_en: The siblings gathered at their late uncle's house to sort through his belongings. The brother found a life insurance policy in the desk, naming him as the beneficiary. The sister found another policy in the coat closet, naming her. They sat on the stairs, each holding their document. The brother noticed that the policy he found had an earlier date. The sister saw that hers had a different beneficiary designation form. They put the policies back where they found them. The brother said they should ask the bank about which one was active. The sister agreed, and they went to the kitchen to find something to eat.
text_zh: 兄弟姐妹们聚集在已故叔叔的房子里，整理他的遗物。哥哥在书桌里发现了一份人寿保险单，指定他为受益人。姐姐在衣橱里发现了另一份保险单，指定她为受益人。他们坐在楼梯上，各自拿着自己的文件。哥哥注意到他发现的那份保单日期较早。姐姐看到她的那份有不同的受益人指定表格。他们把保单放回原处。哥哥说他们应该去银行询问哪一份是有效的。姐姐同意了，他们去厨房找点吃的。

topic: Two siblings discover different versions of their inheritance
text_en: Their grandmother's will mentioned a set of antique chairs that were to be shared. When the siblings went to her house, they found a dining room with several chairs, but they were not the ones described in the will. The will described chairs with carved wooden backs, but the chairs in the room had plain upholstered backs. They searched the rest of the house and found a few more chairs in the attic, which were closer to the description but still not exact. The siblings compared the will's description with the chairs they had found. They decided to ask their aunt, who had helped their grandmother with the will, if she knew what had happened to the original chairs.
text_zh: 他们祖母的遗嘱中提到一套古董椅子，由他们共同继承。当兄弟姐妹们去她家时，他们发现餐厅里有几把椅子，但并非遗嘱中描述的那些。遗嘱描述的是雕花木靠背的椅子，但房间里的椅子是素面软垫靠背。他们搜查了房子的其他地方，在阁楼里又发现了几把椅子，那些椅子更接近描述，但仍不完全吻合。兄弟姐妹们将遗嘱中的描述与他们找到的椅子进行了比较。他们决定去问曾帮助祖母立遗嘱的姑妈，看她是否知道原来那些椅子发生了什么。

topic: Two siblings discover different versions of their inheritance
text_en: The inheritance from their great-aunt was a portfolio of stocks and bonds, according to the lawyer's letter. When the siblings met with the lawyer, he showed them a folder with several documents. The documents listed companies that had gone bankrupt years ago. The lawyer explained that the portfolio had lost most of its value over time. The siblings looked at the certificates, which were printed with ornate designs and old company names. They asked if there were any other assets, but the lawyer said this was all that remained. They thanked him and left the office, carrying the folder with them.
text_zh: 根据律师的信件，他们从姑婆那里继承的遗产是一个股票和债券的投资组合。当兄弟姐妹们与律师会面时，他给他们看了一个装有几份文件的文件夹。这些文件列出了多年前已破产的公司。律师解释说，这个投资组合的价值随着时间的推移已经大幅缩水。兄弟姐妹们看着那些印有华丽图案和旧公司名称的证书。他们问是否还有其他资产，但律师说这就是剩下的全部了。他们谢过他，带着文件夹离开了办公室。

topic: Two siblings discover different versions of their inheritance
text_en: Their mother's will left a house to each of her children. The houses were described as being on the same street, but with different house numbers. When the siblings went to the street, they found that only one house existed. The other address was an empty lot with a for-sale sign. They checked the deed for the second property, which showed the lot as having a house on it. The siblings walked around the lot, looking at the grass and the sign. They decided to contact the real estate agent whose number was on the sign to ask about the history of the lot.
text_zh: 他们母亲的遗嘱留给每个孩子一栋房子。房子被描述为在同一条街上，但门牌号不同。当兄弟姐妹们来到那条街时，他们发现只有一栋房子存在。另一个地址是一块空地，上面有一个待售标志。他们查看了第二处房产的地契，上面显示该地块上有一栋房子。兄弟姐妹们绕着地块走了走，看着草地和标志。他们决定联系标志上号码的房地产经纪人，询问这块地的历史。

topic: Two siblings discover different versions of their inheritance
text_en: The will of their uncle specified that his collection of rare books should be split between his niece and nephew. When the siblings opened the crate in the attic, they found boxes of old paperbacks, not the leather-bound volumes they had expected. The will described a set of first editions, but the books in the boxes were common reprints. They sorted through the books, checking the publication dates on the copyright pages. Some of the dates were recent, while others were older but not matching the descriptions. They packed the books back into the boxes and decided to take them to a local antiquarian for an appraisal.
text_zh: 他们叔叔的遗嘱规定，他收藏的稀有书籍应由侄女和侄子平分。当兄弟姐妹们打开阁楼里的板条箱时，他们发现里面是几盒旧平装书，而不是他们预期的皮面精装书。遗嘱中描述的是一套初版书，但箱子里的书是普通的再版书。他们翻阅书籍，检查版权页上的出版日期。有些日期是最近的，而另一些则更早，但与描述不符。他们把书重新装回箱子里，决定把它们带给当地一位古籍书商估价。

topic: Two siblings discover different versions of their inheritance
text_en: After their father's death, the siblings discovered he had left a safety deposit box in their names. When they opened it, they found a single key and a note. The note said the key was to a storage unit, but it did not say which one. There was no name or address on the note. The siblings took the key to the bank manager, who said he had no record of which storage facility the key belonged to. They examined the key, which had a small tag with a number that had been scratched off. They decided to visit a few nearby storage facilities to see if the key fit any of their locks.
text_zh: 父亲去世后，兄弟姐妹们发现他以他们的名义留下了一个保险箱。当他们打开它时，发现了一把钥匙和一张纸条。纸条上说这把钥匙是开一个储物单元的，但没有说明是哪一个。纸条上没有名字或地址。兄弟姐妹们把钥匙拿给银行经理看，经理说他没有记录这把钥匙属于哪个储物设施。他们检查了钥匙，上面有一个小标签，标签上的号码已被刮掉。他们决定去附近的几家储物设施看看钥匙能否打开他们的锁。

topic: Two siblings discover different versions of their inheritance
text_en: Their aunt's will included a piece of jewelry that was to be given to each of her nieces. When the siblings opened the small box, they found a single necklace inside. The will described a necklace with a blue gemstone, but the necklace in the box had a green gemstone. The siblings looked at the will again, which clearly stated the stone was blue. They searched the box for any other items, but it was empty. They wondered if the necklace had been switched or if the will had been written incorrectly. They decided to ask their aunt's friend, who had been present when the will was made, if she remembered anything about the jewelry.
text_zh: 他们姑妈的遗嘱中包括一件珠宝，要送给她的每位侄女。当兄弟姐妹们打开小盒子时，他们发现里面只有一条项链。遗嘱描述的是一条带有蓝色宝石的项链，但盒子里的项链却有绿色宝石。兄弟姐妹们再次查看遗嘱，遗嘱明确写着石头是蓝色的。他们搜查了盒子，看看是否有其他物品，但盒子是空的。他们想知道项链是否被调换了，或者遗嘱是否写错了。他们决定去问姑妈的朋友，她在立遗嘱时在场，看她是否记得关于珠宝的任何事情。

topic: Two siblings discover different versions of their inheritance
text_en: Lena and her brother inherited their father's workshop. While cleaning, Lena found a letter in the tool chest, stating that the workshop was to be sold and the money donated. Her brother, in the back room, found a different letter, saying the workshop should stay in the family. They showed each other the letters. Lena's was typed; her brother's was handwritten. The handwriting matched their father's. Lena reread her letter, noticing a small correction in the date. Her brother folded his letter and placed it in his pocket. They stood in the dusty workshop, the tools hanging on the walls, and decided to wait until the weekend to look through the rest of the boxes.
text_zh: 莉娜和她的兄弟继承了父亲的工场。在打扫时，莉娜在工具箱里发现了一封信，信中说工场将被出售，所得款项将捐出。她的兄弟在里屋发现了另一封信，说工场应该留在家族内。他们互相给对方看了信。莉娜的信是打印的；她兄弟的信是手写的。笔迹与他们父亲的相符。莉娜重读了她的信，注意到日期上有一处小小的修改。她的兄弟折好信，放进了口袋。他们站在布满灰尘的工场里，工具挂在墙上，决定等到周末再把剩下的箱子翻一遍。

topic: Two siblings discover different versions of their inheritance
text_en: The siblings arrived at their mother's house to divide her belongings. The sister went to the bedroom, where she found a jewelry box with a note inside, saying the pearls were for her. The brother went to the study and found a similar note in a drawer, saying the pearls were for him. They met in the living room, each holding a note. The sister's note was written on stationery; the brother's on a scrap of paper. They compared the handwriting, which looked the same. The sister put her note in her purse. The brother set his on the mantel. They looked at the jewelry box, still closed, and decided to leave it until they could ask their aunt.
text_zh: 兄弟姐妹们来到母亲的房子，分配她的遗物。姐姐去了卧室，在那里她发现了一个首饰盒，里面有一张纸条，说珍珠是给她的。弟弟去了书房，在一个抽屉里发现了一张类似的纸条，说珍珠是给他的。他们在客厅见面，每人手里拿着一张纸条。姐姐的纸条写在信纸上；弟弟的写在一张碎纸片上。他们比较了笔迹，看起来是一样的。姐姐把纸条放进了钱包。弟弟把它放在壁炉架上。他们看着仍然关着的首饰盒，决定先放着，等能问过姑妈再说。

topic: A homeowner learns their house was a former crime scene
text_en: Marta moved into the bungalow on Maple Street last Saturday. While unpacking cookbooks, she found a folded newspaper clipping tucked behind the kitchen drawers. The headline mentioned a robbery and a former resident. She read the short article twice, then set it on the counter. That afternoon she continued arranging the living room furniture, pausing once to look at the clipping. Later, she placed it in a drawer with other papers she kept, thinking she might mention it to her neighbor sometime. The house felt like hers, even with that bit of history.
text_zh: 上周六，玛尔塔搬进了枫树街的平房。在整理烹饪书时，她在厨房抽屉后面发现了一张折叠的报纸剪报。标题提到了一起抢劫案和一位前住户。她读了两遍这篇短文，然后把它放在台面上。那天下午，她继续布置客厅家具，中途停下来看了一眼剪报。后来，她把它和其他她保留的文件一起放进了一个抽屉，想着也许什么时候可以跟邻居提一下。这栋房子感觉像是她的了，即使带着那段历史。

topic: A homeowner learns their house was a former crime scene
text_en: When Dana bought the old colonial, the realtor mentioned only that the previous owners had moved west. A month later, a neighbor brought over a plate of cookies and let slip that the house had once been the scene of a burglary gone wrong. Dana paused, holding the plate, and glanced at the living room where the television now sat. She thanked the neighbor and set the cookies on the counter. That evening, she rearranged a few framed photos on the mantel, then went upstairs to finish unpacking the boxes in the bedroom. The house felt the same as before.
text_zh: 当达娜买下那栋老殖民风格房子时，房产经纪人只提到前房主搬去了西部。一个月后，一位邻居端来一盘饼干，无意中透露这栋房子曾发生过一起失败的入室盗窃案。达娜停顿了一下，端着盘子，瞥了一眼现在放着电视的客厅。她谢过邻居，把饼干放在台面上。那天晚上，她重新摆放了壁炉架上的几幅相框，然后上楼去整理卧室里的箱子。这栋房子感觉和以前一样。

topic: A homeowner learns their house was a former crime scene
text_en: Lena had lived in the townhouse for a year when her neighbor mentioned that a shooting had occurred in the basement. Lena had never gone down there much; the stairs were steep and the space was mostly for storage. That evening, she looked through the keyhole of the basement door. It was dark and quiet. She locked the door and went upstairs to read. The next week, she finally brought down a box of winter coats. She placed them on the shelf and left quickly, feeling the cool air on her skin.
text_zh: 莉娜在这栋联排别墅里住了一年后，她的邻居提到地下室曾发生过一起枪击事件。莉娜以前很少去那里；楼梯很陡，那个空间主要是用来储物。那天晚上，她透过地下室门的锁孔看了看。里面又黑又安静。她锁上门，上楼去读书。接下来的一周，她终于拿下来一箱冬季外套。她把它们放在架子上，然后迅速离开，感觉到皮肤上的凉意。

topic: A homeowner learns their house was a former crime scene
text_en: Marcus had signed the lease on the duplex without asking many questions. The landlord handed over the keys and mentioned the previous tenant had left suddenly. A week later, while sorting through mail that still arrived for the old occupant, Marcus found a newspaper clipping about a robbery that had occurred at the address. He set the clipping aside and continued sorting. That afternoon, he hung a calendar in the kitchen and tested the smoke detector. He did not mention the clipping to anyone, but he kept it in a drawer with the other papers.
text_zh: 马库斯签了那栋双拼别墅的租约，没有问太多问题。房东交给他钥匙，提到前租客突然离开了。一周后，在整理仍然寄给旧住户的邮件时，马库斯发现了一份关于在该地址发生的一起抢劫案的报纸剪报。他把剪报放在一边，继续整理。那天下午，他在厨房挂了一本日历，并测试了烟雾探测器。他没有向任何人提起剪报，但他把它和其他文件一起放在了一个抽屉里。

topic: A homeowner learns their house was a former crime scene
text_en: Elena closed on the bungalow in early spring. The title search had been routine, and the sellers were eager to move. During a walk through the neighborhood, a longtime resident mentioned that the house had been the site of a shooting years earlier. Elena nodded and kept walking, noting the overgrown hedge along the side yard. Later that day, she measured the windows for curtains and made a list of plants for the garden. She did not bring up the shooting again, but she made a point of learning the names of the other neighbors on the block.
text_zh: 埃琳娜在早春买下了那栋平房。产权调查很常规，卖家也急于搬家。在街区散步时，一位长期住户提到这栋房子多年前曾发生过一起枪击事件。埃琳娜点点头，继续走着，注意到侧院沿边疯长的树篱。那天晚些时候，她量了窗户尺寸准备做窗帘，并列了一张花园植物清单。她没有再提起枪击事件，但她特意去认识了街区上其他邻居的名字。

topic: A homeowner learns their house was a former crime scene
text_en: After moving into the split-level, Tom noticed a faint stain on the hallway carpet near the basement door. He assumed it was from a spilled drink. A few days later, the plumber who came to fix a leaky faucet mentioned that the house had been the scene of a break-in where the owner had been injured. Tom thanked him and watched him work. That evening, he scrubbed the stain with a carpet cleaner, but it did not fully come out. He laid a small rug over it and went back to reading his book.
text_zh: 搬进那栋错层式住宅后，汤姆注意到地下室门附近走廊地毯上有一块淡淡的污渍。他以为是打翻的饮料留下的。几天后，来修漏水水龙头的管道工提到，这栋房子曾发生过一起入室盗窃案，房主受了伤。汤姆谢过他，看着他干活。那天晚上，他用地毯清洁剂擦洗了污渍，但没有完全去掉。他在上面铺了一块小地毯，然后回去看书了。

topic: A homeowner learns their house was a former crime scene
text_en: Priya and her husband bought the craftsman with plans to renovate the kitchen. The previous owner had been an elderly widow who passed away in the hospital, so the house had been empty for a while. During a visit from the inspector, he mentioned that the house had once been the site of a domestic disturbance that made the news. Priya listened, then asked about the wiring in the attic. After he left, she continued sanding the kitchen cabinets. The next morning, she called a contractor about replacing the back door.
text_zh: 普里亚和丈夫买下了那栋工匠风格住宅，计划翻新厨房。前房主是一位年迈的寡妇，在医院去世，所以房子空了一段时间。在一次检查员的来访中，他提到这栋房子曾发生过一起上了新闻的家庭纠纷。普里亚听着，然后问了问阁楼的电线问题。他离开后，她继续打磨厨房橱柜。第二天早上，她打电话给承包商，商量更换后门的事。

topic: A homeowner learns their house was a former crime scene
text_en: When the realtor showed the ranch house, she mentioned that the sellers were downsizing after a divorce. That seemed ordinary enough. After moving in, Carl found an old police report wedged behind a radiator while cleaning. It described an assault that had occurred in the living room. Carl read it briefly, then folded it and placed it in the recycling bin. He spent the rest of the afternoon painting the bedroom walls a soft green. He did not mention the report to his wife, but he did suggest they replace the front door lock.
text_zh: 房产经纪人带看那栋牧场式住宅时，提到卖家离婚后正在缩小住房规模。这看起来相当平常。搬进去后，卡尔在打扫时发现一份旧警察报告卡在散热器后面。报告描述了发生在客厅的一起袭击事件。卡尔简短地读了一下，然后把它折叠起来放进了回收箱。那天下午剩下的时间，他把卧室墙壁刷成了柔和的绿色。他没有向妻子提起这份报告，但他确实建议更换前门锁。

topic: A homeowner learns their house was a former crime scene
text_en: When Margaret bought the old bungalow, the realtor mentioned it had been vacant for a while but didn't say why. Last week, a neighbor brought over a plate of cookies and casually noted that a man had been found there years ago, after a robbery went wrong. Margaret paused, holding the plate, then thanked her and closed the door. She walked through the rooms that evening, noticing the scuffed floorboards and the heavy front door lock. The next morning, she called a locksmith to rekey all the doors and had the carpets cleaned, then went about arranging her furniture.
text_zh: 当玛格丽特买下那栋旧平房时，房产经纪人提到它空置了一段时间，但没有说明原因。上周，一位邻居端来一盘饼干，随口提到多年前曾有一名男子在那里被发现，起因是一起失败的抢劫案。玛格丽特停顿了一下，端着盘子，然后谢过她，关上了门。那天晚上，她走过各个房间，注意到磨损的地板和沉重的前门锁。第二天早上，她叫来锁匠重新配了所有门的钥匙，并让人清洗了地毯，然后开始布置家具。

topic: A homeowner learns their house was a former crime scene
text_en: After inheriting the house from his aunt, Derek flew in to sort through her belongings. The house had been in the family for years, so he knew its layout well. While clearing out the attic, he came across a box of old newspapers. One headline mentioned a robbery at the address that had occurred when his aunt first moved in. Derek paused, then set the paper aside and continued sorting through the boxes. He donated most of the furniture and kept a few pieces for his own apartment. He never mentioned the article to his cousins.
text_zh: 从姑妈那里继承了房子后，德里克飞过来整理她的遗物。这栋房子在家族里已经很多年了，所以他对它的布局很熟悉。在清理阁楼时，他偶然发现一箱旧报纸。其中一个标题提到，在姑妈刚搬进来时，该地址曾发生过一起抢劫案。德里克停顿了一下，然后把报纸放在一边，继续整理箱子。他捐赠了大部分家具，留了几件放在自己的公寓里。他从未向表亲们提起那篇文章。

topic: A homeowner learns their house was a former crime scene
text_en: Evan discovered the house's history through an old newspaper article his aunt had saved. The address matched perfectly, and the story described a dispute between former tenants that ended badly. He set the clipping on the kitchen counter and read it again while his coffee brewed. Later, he mentioned it to his neighbor while checking the mail. They both agreed it was odd, but the neighborhood had changed since then. That weekend, Evan repainted the living room and replaced the front porch light. He didn't dwell on the past, but he did keep the article in a drawer, just in case he wanted to show someone else.
text_zh: 埃文通过他姑姑保存的一篇旧报纸文章发现了这所房子的历史。地址完全吻合，故事描述了前租户之间一场以糟糕结局收场的纠纷。他把剪报放在厨房台面上，在咖啡煮好时又读了一遍。后来，他在查看邮件时向邻居提起了这件事。他们都觉得这很奇怪，但自那以后这个社区已经变了。那个周末，埃文重新粉刷了客厅，并更换了前门廊的灯。他没有沉湎于过去，但他确实把文章放在抽屉里，以防他想给别人看。

topic: A homeowner learns their house was a former crime scene
text_en: When the realtor showed the Victorian, she pointed out the original woodwork and the fireplace. She did not mention anything unusual. After the closing, while unpacking books in the study, Nathan found a handwritten note in a desk drawer that mentioned a break-in and a missing jewelry box. The note was dated years earlier. Nathan read it, then placed it back in the drawer. He spent the rest of the day arranging his books on the shelves. He did not tell his wife about the note, but he did buy a small safe for their valuables.
text_zh: 当房产经纪人展示那栋维多利亚式房屋时，她指出了原有的木制品和壁炉。她没有提到任何不寻常的事情。过户后，内森在书房整理书籍时，在书桌抽屉里发现了一张手写的便条，上面提到了一起入室盗窃和一个丢失的首饰盒。便条的日期是几年前。内森读了便条，然后把它放回了抽屉。他花了一整天的时间把书排列在书架上。他没有告诉妻子关于便条的事，但他确实为他们的贵重物品买了一个小保险箱。

topic: A homeowner learns their house was a former crime scene
text_en: Maya moved into the apartment above a bakery. The smell of bread drifted up each morning, and she liked the location. A week in, the landlord came by to fix a leaky faucet and mentioned that the apartment had once been the scene of a fire that started in the kitchen. Maya looked at her own stove and nodded. After he left, she checked the fire extinguisher under the sink and made a mental note to test the smoke detector. She then went back to arranging her living room furniture.
text_zh: 玛雅搬进了面包店楼上的公寓。每天早晨面包的香味飘上来，她喜欢这个位置。一周后，房东来修理漏水的水龙头，提到这间公寓曾经是一场从厨房开始的火灾的现场。玛雅看了看自己的炉子，点了点头。他离开后，她检查了水槽下的灭火器，并记在心里要测试烟雾报警器。然后她又回去布置客厅家具了。

topic: A homeowner learns their house was a former crime scene
text_en: After buying the split-level, the first thing Greg did was repaint the living room. The previous owners had left the walls a dull beige. While scraping off old wallpaper in the hallway, he uncovered a patch of soot and a scorch mark. A neighbor later told him that the house had been the site of an electrical fire that damaged the kitchen. Greg listened and then asked where the best hardware store was. He finished the hallway and started on the kitchen cabinets. He did not dwell on the scorch mark.
text_zh: 买下这栋错层式房屋后，格雷格做的第一件事就是重新粉刷客厅。前房主把墙壁留成了沉闷的米色。在走廊刮旧壁纸时，他发现了一片烟灰和一块烧焦的痕迹。后来一位邻居告诉他，这栋房子曾发生过一场损坏厨房的电气火灾。格雷格听了，然后问最好的五金店在哪里。他完成了走廊，然后开始处理厨房橱柜。他没有在意那块烧焦的痕迹。

topic: A homeowner learns their house was a former crime scene
text_en: Priya learned about the house's past from a detective who knocked on her door one Tuesday afternoon. He was following up on an old case and asked if she'd noticed anything unusual. She said no, and he explained that a previous owner had been involved in a serious incident on the property. After he left, Priya stood in the hallway, looking at the walls and the ceiling. She checked the basement and the attic, finding nothing but dust and old boxes. That evening, she called her brother and told him about the visit. He said it was probably nothing. She agreed and hung up, then finished unpacking the kitchen.
text_zh: 普里亚从一个侦探那里得知了这所房子的过去，那个侦探在一个星期二的下午敲了她的门。他正在跟进一个旧案件，问她是否注意到什么不寻常的事情。她说没有，他解释说一位前房主曾在这处房产上卷入过一起严重事件。他离开后，普里亚站在走廊里，看着墙壁和天花板。她检查了地下室和阁楼，除了灰尘和旧箱子外什么也没找到。那天晚上，她打电话给她的兄弟，告诉他这次拜访的事。他说可能没什么。她表示同意并挂了电话，然后继续整理厨房。

topic: A homeowner learns their house was a former crime scene
text_en: When Dana bought the small bungalow, the realtor mentioned it had been renovated recently, but nothing about its history. A few weeks after moving in, an older neighbor came over with a plate of cookies and mentioned, almost casually, that the house had once been the site of a police investigation. Dana thanked her and closed the door, holding the plate. Later that evening, while unpacking boxes in the spare room, she noticed a faint outline on the wall where a large picture frame had hung. She ran her fingers along the edge of the mark, then returned to sorting through her books, leaving the outline undisturbed.
text_zh: 当达娜买下那栋小平房时，房产经纪人提到它最近翻新过，但没提它的历史。搬进来几周后，一位年长的邻居端着一盘饼干过来，几乎漫不经心地提到，这栋房子曾经是一起警方调查的现场。达娜谢过她，端着盘子关上了门。那天晚上晚些时候，在备用房间整理箱子时，她注意到墙上有一个大相框挂过的淡淡轮廓。她用指尖沿着痕迹的边缘划过，然后回去整理她的书，没有动那个轮廓。

topic: A homeowner learns their house was a former crime scene
text_en: Nina had always liked the look of the brick house on the corner. When it came up for sale, she made an offer quickly. The inspection went well, and the sellers were cooperative. A few days after moving in, a woman walking her dog stopped to chat and mentioned that the house had been the site of a shooting years ago. Nina nodded and asked about the best route to the grocery store. That evening, she hung curtains in the bedroom and unpacked her grandmother's china. She did not bring up the shooting again.
text_zh: 尼娜一直喜欢街角那栋砖房的样子。当它挂牌出售时，她很快出了价。检查进行得很顺利，卖家也很配合。搬进来几天后，一位遛狗的女人停下来聊天，提到这栋房子多年前曾是一起枪击事件的现场。尼娜点了点头，问去杂货店的最佳路线。那天晚上，她在卧室挂了窗帘，并拆开了祖母的瓷器。她没有再提起那起枪击事件。

topic: A homeowner learns their house was a former crime scene
text_en: After closing on the house, Sandra found a small envelope tucked behind the mail slot. Inside was a handwritten note from the previous owner, apologizing for not mentioning that the house had been the site of a burglary that turned violent. The note said the police had caught the person and that the house had been peaceful since. Sandra folded the note and put it back in the envelope. She walked through the empty rooms, checking the windows and locks. She then called her realtor to ask if she'd known. The realtor said she hadn't. Sandra hung up and spent the afternoon measuring the living room for curtains.
text_zh: 房子过户后，桑德拉在邮箱槽后面发现了一个小信封。里面是前房主写的一张手写便条，为没有提到这栋房子曾是一起演变为暴力的入室盗窃案的现场而道歉。便条说警方已经抓住了那个人，从那以后房子一直很平静。桑德拉把便条折好放回信封。她走过空荡荡的房间，检查窗户和锁。然后她打电话给她的房产经纪人，问她是否知情。经纪人说她不知道。桑德拉挂了电话，花了一下午的时间测量客厅，准备挂窗帘。

topic: A homeowner learns their house was a former crime scene
text_en: When the realtor showed the split-level, she pointed out the new roof and the renovated bathroom. She did not mention the history. After the closing, while cleaning the basement, Chloe found a faded newspaper clipping about a break-in that had occurred at the house. The clipping was tucked behind an old water heater. Chloe read it, then placed it in the recycling bin. She spent the rest of the day arranging the laundry room and hanging shelves. She did not tell her husband about the clipping, but she did suggest they get a security camera.
text_zh: 当房产经纪人展示那栋错层式房屋时，她指出了新屋顶和翻新过的浴室。她没有提到那段历史。过户后，克洛伊在打扫地下室时，发现了一张褪色的报纸剪报，内容是关于发生在这栋房子里的一起入室盗窃案。剪报被塞在一个旧热水器后面。克洛伊读了剪报，然后把它放进了回收箱。她花了一整天的时间整理洗衣房和挂架子。她没有告诉丈夫关于剪报的事，但她确实建议他们装一个安防摄像头。

topic: A homeowner learns their house was a former crime scene
text_en: After moving into the townhouse, the first thing Sam did was hang a mirror in the entryway. The previous owners had left the walls bare. A few days later, a neighbor came over to welcome him and mentioned that the house had been the site of a robbery years ago. Sam thanked him and offered him a beer. They sat on the front steps and talked about the neighborhood. That evening, Sam unpacked his books and arranged them on the shelves. He did not dwell on the robbery, but he did make sure the back door was locked.
text_zh: 搬进联排别墅后，山姆做的第一件事就是在门厅挂了一面镜子。前房主把墙壁留得光秃秃的。几天后，一位邻居过来欢迎他，提到这栋房子多年前曾是一起抢劫案的现场。山姆谢过他，并递给他一瓶啤酒。他们坐在前台阶上聊了聊这个社区。那天晚上，山姆拆开他的书，把它们排列在书架上。他没有沉湎于那起抢劫案，但他确实确保后门锁上了。

topic: Someone finds out they have a half-sibling they never knew about
text_en: Maya was sorting through her late father's desk when she found a letter addressed to a woman she didn't recognize. The letter mentioned a child, a girl named Elena, born around the same time as Maya herself. Maya sat back in the chair, holding the paper. She had always thought she was an only child. Later that day, she called her mother, who was quiet for a long moment before explaining that her father had a relationship before their marriage. Maya listened, then thanked her mother and hung up. She placed the letter back in the drawer and went to make dinner, thinking about Elena.
text_zh: 玛雅正在整理已故父亲的书桌时，发现了一封写给一个她不认识的女人的信。信中提到了一个孩子，一个名叫埃琳娜的女孩，出生时间大约与玛雅自己同期。玛雅坐回椅子上，握着那张纸。她一直以为自己是独生女。那天晚些时候，她给母亲打了电话，母亲沉默了好一会儿，然后解释说她父亲在结婚前曾有过一段感情。玛雅听着，然后向母亲道谢并挂了电话。她把信放回抽屉，去做晚饭，心里想着埃琳娜。

topic: Someone finds out they have a half-sibling they never knew about
text_en: At the family reunion, an older man approached Leo and said, "You must be Tom's boy. You look just like him." Leo explained that his father was named Richard. The man frowned, then said, "Well, you've got the same eyes as your mother, anyway." Leo didn't think much of it until his aunt pulled him aside. She told him that his father had a son from a previous marriage, a man named Daniel, who lived in another state. Leo thanked her and went back to the barbecue, the information settling quietly in his mind.
text_zh: 在家庭聚会上，一位年长的男子走近利奥说：“你一定是汤姆的儿子。你长得真像他。”利奥解释说他的父亲叫理查德。那人皱了皱眉，然后说：“嗯，反正你的眼睛跟你母亲一样。”利奥没太在意，直到他姑姑把他拉到一边。她告诉他，他父亲在前一段婚姻中有一个儿子，名叫丹尼尔，住在另一个州。利奥向她道谢，然后回到烧烤聚会，这个信息在他心中悄然沉淀。

topic: Someone finds out they have a half-sibling they never knew about
text_en: At the family reunion, an older woman approached Tom and asked if he was Richard's son. Tom nodded, and the woman smiled, saying she had a son who was also Richard's. Tom blinked, processing the information. He had never heard of this half-brother. The woman gave him a phone number and walked away. Tom folded the paper and put it in his pocket. He spent the rest of the afternoon helping his cousin set up tables, occasionally glancing at his pocket. That evening, he showed the number to his wife, who suggested he call. Tom said he might, and put the paper on the counter.
text_zh: 在家庭聚会上，一位年长的女士走近汤姆，问他是否是理查德的儿子。汤姆点了点头，女士微笑着说她也有一个儿子，也是理查德的。汤姆眨了眨眼，消化着这个信息。他从未听说过这个同父异母的兄弟。女士给了他一个电话号码，然后走开了。汤姆把纸条折好放进口袋。那天下午剩下的时间，他一直在帮表亲摆桌子，偶尔瞥一眼自己的口袋。那天晚上，他把号码给妻子看，妻子建议他打电话。汤姆说也许吧，然后把纸条放在柜台上。

topic: Someone finds out they have a half-sibling they never knew about
text_en: While cleaning out the attic, Rachel found a box of old photographs. Among them was a picture of her father holding a baby, but the baby wasn't her or her sister. The back had a date and a name: Daniel. Rachel brought the photo downstairs and asked her mother about it. Her mother explained that Daniel was Rachel's half-brother, from a brief marriage before her father met her mother. Rachel looked at the photo again, noting the resemblance. She put it back in the box and continued sorting through the attic, occasionally thinking about Daniel and wondering where he might be.
text_zh: 在清理阁楼时，瑞秋发现了一盒旧照片。其中一张是她父亲抱着一个婴儿的照片，但那个婴儿不是她也不是她姐姐。照片背面有一个日期和一个名字：丹尼尔。瑞秋把照片拿到楼下，问母亲这件事。母亲解释说，丹尼尔是瑞秋同父异母的哥哥，是父亲在遇到她母亲之前一段短暂婚姻中所生。瑞秋又看了看照片，注意到了相似之处。她把它放回盒子里，继续整理阁楼，偶尔想到丹尼尔，想知道他可能在哪儿。

topic: Someone finds out they have a half-sibling they never knew about
text_en: James received an email from a man claiming to be his half-brother. The man explained that their father had a relationship with his mother years ago. James read the email twice, then closed his laptop. He had grown up as an only child, and this news didn't fit with what he knew. He mentioned it to his roommate, who shrugged and said, "That's a lot to take in." James agreed and went back to his work. The email remained in his inbox, unread again, for several days. He thought about it occasionally but didn't feel an urge to respond immediately.
text_zh: 詹姆斯收到一封邮件，来自一个自称是他同父异母兄弟的男人。那人解释说，他们的父亲多年前与他母亲有过一段关系。詹姆斯把邮件读了两遍，然后合上笔记本电脑。他从小是独生子，这个消息与他的认知不符。他跟室友提起了这件事，室友耸耸肩说：“这确实让人难以接受。”詹姆斯表示同意，然后回去工作。那封邮件留在他的收件箱里，好几天都没再读。他偶尔会想到它，但并不急于立即回应。

topic: Someone finds out they have a half-sibling they never knew about
text_en: Mara was sorting through her mother's old paperwork when she found the letter. It was from a man she didn't recognize, thanking her mother for a lovely weekend in the mountains. The date was from before Mara was born. She set it aside and continued organizing, but the name on the envelope stayed in her mind. That evening, she asked her father about it. He paused, then explained that her mother had been married briefly before him. Mara had a half-brother somewhere. She nodded, folded the letter, and placed it back in the box.
text_zh: 玛拉在整理母亲的旧文件时发现了一封信。信来自一个她不认识的男人，感谢她的母亲在山里度过了一个愉快的周末。日期早于玛拉出生。她把信放在一边，继续整理，但信封上的名字一直留在她脑海里。那天晚上，她问父亲关于这件事。他停顿了一下，然后解释说她的母亲在他之前曾短暂结过婚。玛拉在某处有一个同父异母的兄弟。她点点头，把信折好，放回盒子里。

topic: Someone finds out they have a half-sibling they never knew about
text_en: Ethan was helping his aunt clean out his late uncle's study when he came across a stack of old birthday cards. They were all addressed to a boy named Lucas, with return addresses from a town Ethan had never heard of. The cards were signed 'Your father' in a handwriting that matched his uncle's. Ethan's aunt glanced over and said, 'Oh, those are for his son from his first marriage. He never talked about it much.' Ethan nodded and placed the cards back in the box. He finished sorting the remaining papers and then went to help his aunt in the kitchen.
text_zh: 伊森正在帮姑姑清理已故叔叔的书房，偶然发现了一叠旧生日贺卡。它们的收件人都是一个叫卢卡斯的男孩，寄件地址来自一个伊森从未听说过的城镇。卡片上的签名是“你的父亲”，笔迹与他叔叔的相符。伊森的姑姑瞥了一眼说：“哦，那些是他第一段婚姻中儿子的。他很少谈论那事。”伊森点点头，把卡片放回盒子里。他整理完剩下的文件，然后去厨房帮姑姑的忙。

topic: Someone finds out they have a half-sibling they never knew about
text_en: While visiting her hometown, Anna ran into an old neighbor who asked if she had met her brother. Anna was confused, saying she didn't have a brother. The neighbor explained that Anna's father had a son with another woman, and the son had recently moved to town. Anna thanked the neighbor and continued walking. Later, she found herself in front of the library, thinking about the news. She considered looking up the name but didn't. She went home and told her mother, who confirmed the story. Anna nodded and helped her mother with the garden, thinking about the brother she had never known.
text_zh: 回到家乡时，安娜偶遇一位老邻居，邻居问她是否见过她的兄弟。安娜很困惑，说她没有兄弟。邻居解释说，安娜的父亲与另一个女人有一个儿子，而这个儿子最近搬到了镇上。安娜感谢了邻居，继续走着。后来，她发现自己站在图书馆前，想着这个消息。她考虑过查一下那个名字，但没有。她回到家告诉母亲，母亲证实了这个说法。安娜点点头，帮母亲打理花园，想着那个她从未见过的兄弟。

topic: Someone finds out they have a half-sibling they never knew about
text_en: David's aunt showed him a letter from his father, written before David was born. In it, his father mentioned a son named Michael. David read the letter carefully, then asked his aunt if this was real. She said it was, and that Michael had been placed for adoption. David folded the letter and returned it to his aunt. He spent the rest of the visit talking about other family matters. On the drive home, he thought about Michael and what it would mean to have a brother. He didn't take any further steps, but the thought stayed with him.
text_zh: 大卫的姑姑给他看了一封他父亲写的信，写于大卫出生之前。在信中，他父亲提到了一个名叫迈克尔 。大卫仔细读了信，然后问姑姑这是不是真的。她说这是真的，而且迈克尔已经被收养。大卫把信折好还给姑姑。拜访的剩余时间里，他一直在谈论其他家庭事务。开车回家的路上，他想到了迈克尔，以及有一个兄弟意味着什么。他没有采取进一步行动，但这个想法一直伴随着他。

topic: Someone finds out they have a half-sibling they never knew about
text_en: While going through her mother's jewelry box, Emily found a small ring with an inscription. The initials didn't match anyone in her immediate family. Her mother explained that the ring belonged to a man she had been involved with before meeting Emily's father, and that Emily had a half-sister from that relationship. Emily put the ring back and asked a few questions. Her mother answered briefly. Emily then went to her room and sat on her bed, looking at her phone. She didn't search for the sister, but she couldn't stop thinking about her.
text_zh: 在翻看母亲的珠宝盒时，艾米丽发现了一枚刻有字的小戒指。上面的首字母与她直系亲属中的任何人都对不上。母亲解释说，那枚戒指属于一个在认识艾米丽父亲之前与她交往过的男人，而艾米丽在那段关系中有一个同父异母的姐姐。艾米丽把戒指放回去，问了几个问题。母亲简短地回答了。艾米丽然后回到自己房间，坐在床上，看着手机。她没有搜寻那个姐姐，但忍不住一直想着她。

topic: Someone finds out they have a half-sibling they never knew about
text_en: Maya was sorting through her father's old papers when she found a birth certificate tucked inside a folder. The name on it was her father's, but the mother listed was not her mother. Beside it lay a faded photograph of a young woman holding a baby. Maya set the papers aside and finished the task. Later that evening, she mentioned it to her father. He explained that he had a daughter from a brief relationship before he married Maya's mother. Maya nodded and asked if she could meet her half-sister sometime. He said he would look into it.
text_zh: 玛雅正在整理父亲旧文件时，在一个文件夹里发现了一张出生证明。上面的名字是她父亲的，但所列的母亲不是她的母亲。旁边放着一张褪色的照片，照片上是一位年轻女子抱着一个婴儿。玛雅把文件放在一边，完成了任务。那天晚上，她向父亲提起了这件事。他解释说，在娶玛雅的母亲之前，他曾有过一段短暂的感情，并有一个女儿。玛雅点点头，问是否可以在某个时候见见她的同父异母姐姐。他说他会去了解一下。

topic: Someone finds out they have a half-sibling they never knew about
text_en: While organizing old files at work, Laura found a document with her father's signature and a note about a child named Alex. The document was dated years before Laura was born. She took it to her supervisor, who didn't know anything about it. Laura put the document in her bag and brought it home. She showed her mother, who became quiet and then explained that Alex was Laura's half-brother. Laura sat down, holding the paper. She asked if Alex knew about her, but her mother didn't know. Laura filed the document in a drawer and went to make tea.
text_zh: 在工作中整理旧文件时，劳拉发现了一份有父亲签名、并附有关于一个名叫亚历克斯的孩子的说明的文件。这份文件的日期早于劳拉出生多年。她把文件拿给主管看，主管对此一无所知。劳拉把文件放进包里带回了家。她给母亲看，母亲沉默了一会儿，然后解释说亚历克斯是劳拉同父异母的哥哥。劳拉坐下来，手里拿着文件。她问亚历克斯是否知道她的存在，但母亲不知道。劳拉把文件归档到抽屉里，然后去泡茶。

topic: Someone finds out they have a half-sibling they never knew about
text_en: At a wedding, a man approached Peter and introduced himself as his brother. Peter shook his hand, confused. The man explained that they shared a father, who had passed away years ago. Peter had never been told about this. They talked briefly, and the man gave Peter his card. Peter took it and put it in his pocket. He returned to his table and sat down, looking at the card. His wife asked who that was, and Peter explained. She asked if he was okay, and Peter said he was fine. He finished his dinner, occasionally glancing at the card.
text_zh: 在一个婚礼上，一个男人走近彼得，自我介绍说是他的兄弟。彼得困惑地和他握了握手。男人解释说他们有一个共同的父亲，父亲多年前已去世。彼得从未被告知这件事。他们简短地交谈了一会儿，男人给了彼得他的名片。彼得接过名片放进口袋。他回到自己的桌子旁坐下，看着名片。妻子问那是谁，彼得解释了。她问他是否还好，彼得说他没事。他吃完了晚餐，偶尔瞥一眼那张名片。

topic: Someone finds out they have a half-sibling they never knew about
text_en: While cleaning out her late father's garage, Helen found a box of letters. One was addressed to a woman and mentioned a daughter named Grace. Helen opened the letter and read it, realizing it was from her father. She put the letter aside and continued cleaning. Later, she brought the letter to her mother, who read it and confirmed that Grace was Helen's half-sister. Helen asked where Grace was now, but her mother didn't know. Helen placed the letter back in the box and went to the store to buy supplies for the garage sale.
text_zh: 在清理已故父亲的车库时，海伦发现了一盒信件。其中一封是写给一位女士的，并提到了一个名叫格蕾丝的女儿。海伦打开信读了起来，意识到这是父亲写的。她把信放在一边，继续打扫。后来，她把信带给母亲，母亲读了信，确认格蕾丝是海伦同父异母的姐姐。海伦问格蕾丝现在在哪里，但母亲不知道。海伦把信放回盒子里，然后去商店购买车库甩卖的用品。

topic: Someone finds out they have a half-sibling they never knew about
text_en: At a family gathering, a cousin mentioned that there was another sibling in the family, a boy from an old relationship. Kevin looked at his parents, who didn't deny it. Kevin asked who the boy was, but no one knew his current name or location. Kevin let the topic drop and went to get a plate of food. Later, he sat with his siblings, and they talked about the possibility of having another brother. Kevin listened but didn't have much to say. He finished his meal and helped with the dishes, thinking about the unknown sibling.
text_zh: 在一次家庭聚会上，一个表亲提到家里还有另一个兄弟姐妹，是一个旧关系所生的男孩。凯文看着父母，他们没有否认。凯文问那个男孩是谁，但没人知道他现在的名字或下落。凯文不再追问，去拿了一盘食物。后来，他和兄弟姐妹们坐在一起，他们谈论着可能还有一个兄弟的事。凯文听着，但没怎么说话。他吃完饭，帮忙洗碗，心里想着那个未知的兄弟姐妹。

topic: Someone finds out they have a half-sibling they never knew about
text_en: While reading an old diary belonging to her grandmother, Jessica found an entry mentioning a baby boy born to her father's first wife. Jessica had never heard of this. She closed the diary and asked her grandmother about it. Her grandmother explained that the boy had been given up for adoption. Jessica asked if her father ever tried to find him, but her grandmother didn't think so. Jessica returned the diary to its shelf and went for a walk. She thought about the half-brother she might never meet, then came home and started dinner.
text_zh: 在阅读祖母的旧日记时，杰西卡发现了一篇提到她父亲第一任妻子所生男婴的条目。杰西卡从未听说过这件事。她合上日记，向祖母询问此事。祖母解释说，那个男孩已被送养。杰西卡问父亲是否曾试图找到他，但祖母认为没有。杰西卡把日记放回书架，出去散步。她想着那个可能永远不会见面的同父异母兄弟，然后回到家开始做晚饭。

topic: Someone finds out they have a half-sibling they never knew about
text_en: While going through a box of old photographs, Alex found a picture of his father standing next to a woman and a girl who looked about Alex's age. The girl had the same smile as his father. Alex turned the photo over, but there was no writing on the back. He asked his father about it later that week. His father glanced at the photo and said, 'That's your sister. She lives abroad with her mother.' Alex placed the photo back in the box and went to make himself a sandwich. He thought about the girl in the picture for a few days, then forgot about it.
text_zh: 在翻看一盒旧照片时，亚历克斯发现了一张父亲站在一位女士和一个看起来和亚历克斯差不多大的女孩旁边的照片。那个女孩有着和父亲一样的笑容。亚历克斯把照片翻过来，但背面没有字。那周晚些时候，他问父亲这件事。父亲瞥了一眼照片，说：“那是你姐姐。她和母亲住在国外。”亚历克斯把照片放回盒子里，去给自己做了个三明治。他想了那个照片里的女孩几天，然后就忘了。

topic: Someone finds out they have a half-sibling they never knew about
text_en: Jordan was helping his mother move boxes in the garage when he found a manila envelope tucked behind some old paint cans. Inside were legal documents and a few letters. One letter mentioned a daughter named Rachel. Jordan's mother came in and saw what he was holding. 'That's from your father's time before he met me,' she said. 'He had a daughter. We lost touch with them years ago.' Jordan put the envelope back in the box and helped his mother carry it to the car. He didn't ask any more questions, and they finished the move in silence.
text_zh: 乔丹正在帮母亲搬车库里的箱子时，发现了一个藏在旧油漆罐后面的马尼拉纸信封。里面是法律文件和几封信。其中一封信提到了一个名叫瑞秋的女儿。乔丹的母亲走进来，看到他手里的东西。“那是你父亲认识我之前的事，”她说。“他有一个女儿。我们多年前就和他们失去联系了。”乔丹把信封放回箱子里，帮母亲把箱子搬到车上。他没有再问任何问题，他们在沉默中完成了搬家。

topic: Someone finds out they have a half-sibling they never knew about
text_en: While looking through her father's old papers, Linda found a birth certificate for a child she didn't recognize. The father's name matched her father's. She took the paper to her father, who was reading in his chair. He looked at it and said the child was from a relationship he had before marriage. Linda asked if she had any siblings, and he said no, just that one. Linda put the paper back and went to her room. She sat on her bed, looking out the window, thinking about the half-sibling she had never met.
text_zh: 在翻看父亲的旧文件时，琳达发现了一张她不认识的孩子的出生证明。父亲的名字与她的父亲相符。她把文件拿给父亲，父亲正坐在椅子上看书。他看了看，说这个孩子是他婚前一段关系所生。琳达问她是否有兄弟姐妹，他说没有，只有那一个。琳达把文件放回去，回到自己的房间。她坐在床上，望着窗外，想着那个从未见过的同父异母的兄弟姐妹。

topic: Someone finds out they have a half-sibling they never knew about
text_en: At a neighborhood barbecue, a woman introduced herself to Greg and said she was his sister. Greg was taken aback, but the woman explained that they shared a father. She had grown up in a different town and had only recently learned about Greg. Greg listened, then introduced her to his wife. They talked for a while, and the woman gave Greg her phone number. Greg took it and put it in his pocket. Later, he told his wife that he didn't know what to make of it. He finished his burger and watched the kids play, the number still in his pocket.
text_zh: 在社区烧烤聚会上，一位女士向格雷格自我介绍，说她是他的姐姐。格雷格吃了一惊，但女士解释说他们有一个共同的父亲。她在另一个城镇长大，最近才知道格雷格的存在。格雷格听着，然后把她介绍给妻子。他们聊了一会儿，女士给了格雷格她的电话号码。格雷格接过号码放进口袋。后来，他告诉妻子他不知道该怎么看待这件事。他吃完汉堡，看着孩子们玩耍，号码还在口袋里。

topic: A person learns their childhood bully became a therapist
text_en: Maya found the name in an old high school directory while clearing out her parents' garage. Daniel Hartley. The boy who used to call her names in the hallway, who once hid her backpack in a trash can. She typed his name into a search engine and found a professional profile. He was a licensed therapist with an office downtown, specializing in adolescent counseling. Maya closed the laptop and sat with the thought for a moment. Then she called her sister to mention it, laughed a little at the irony, and went back to sorting through boxes of old books and yearbooks.
text_zh: 玛雅在清理父母车库时，在一本旧高中同学录里发现了那个名字。丹尼尔·哈特利。那个曾经在走廊里骂她、把她的背包藏进垃圾桶的男孩。她在搜索引擎里输入他的名字，找到了一个职业简介。他是一名持牌治疗师，办公室在市中心，专攻青少年咨询。玛雅合上笔记本电脑，坐着想了一会儿。然后她给姐姐打了个电话提起这件事，对这份讽刺笑了笑，又回去整理一箱箱旧书和年鉴。

topic: A person learns their childhood bully became a therapist
text_en: At a dinner party, the host introduced a new guest. "This is Dr. Ellis," she said. "He just started at the counseling center." The man across the table smiled, and Nora recognized him instantly. He had been the kid who hid her backpack in the boys' bathroom every day in seventh grade. She remembered the way he laughed when she came out holding it by the strap. He didn't seem to remember her. He was talking about his practice, the sliding scale, the new office. Nora passed the salad bowl and listened. Later, she told her husband she knew him from school. She didn't say more.
text_zh: 在一次晚宴上，主人介绍了一位新客人。“这是埃利斯医生，”她说。“他刚来咨询中心工作。”桌子对面的男人笑了笑，诺拉立刻认出了他。他就是七年级时每天把她的背包藏进男厕所的那个孩子。她记得当她拎着背包带子出来时他大笑的样子。他似乎不记得她了。他正谈论着他的诊所、浮动收费标准和新的办公室。诺拉递过沙拉碗，听着。后来，她告诉丈夫她认识他，是校友。她没有再多说。

topic: A person learns their childhood bully became a therapist
text_en: Maya was flipping through a local directory when she saw his name: Daniel Reeves, LPC. The last time she'd seen him, he was throwing her backpack into a puddle outside the middle school. She stared at the listing for a moment, then closed the browser and went to make lunch. Later that week, her neighbor mentioned she was looking for a therapist, and Maya almost said something. She didn't, though. She just handed over the directory and said the listings were alphabetical. She thought about Daniel sometimes, but she didn't feel the need to do anything about it.
text_zh: 玛雅翻阅着本地目录时看到了他的名字：丹尼尔·里夫斯，LPC。她最后一次见到他时，他正把她的背包扔进中学外面的水坑里。她盯着那则信息看了一会儿，然后关掉浏览器去做午饭。那周晚些时候，她的邻居提到她在找治疗师，玛雅差点要说什么。但她没有。她只是递过目录，说列表是按字母顺序排列的。她有时会想到丹尼尔，但觉得没有必要为此做什么。

topic: A person learns their childhood bully became a therapist
text_en: At the community center's career fair, Elena spotted a familiar face behind a booth with a banner reading "Family Counseling Services." It was Marcus, her childhood neighbor who had once hidden her bike and laughed when she searched for it. He was talking to a parent about adolescent therapy, his voice measured and professional. When he noticed Elena, he smiled and offered a brochure. She took it, glanced at his business card with the title "Licensed Therapist," and said she was just browsing. She walked to the next table, the brochure still in her hand, and later placed it in her bag without reading further.
text_zh: 在社区中心的招聘会上，埃琳娜在一个挂着“家庭咨询服务”横幅的展位后看到了一张熟悉的面孔。是马库斯，她儿时的邻居，曾经藏起她的自行车，在她寻找时大笑。他正与一位家长谈论青少年治疗，语气平稳而专业。当他注意到埃琳娜时，他微笑着递上一本宣传册。她接过，瞥了一眼印着“持牌治疗师”头衔的名片，说她只是随便看看。她走向下一个展位，手里还拿着宣传册，后来把它放进包里，没有再读。

topic: A person learns their childhood bully became a therapist
text_en: Hannah was scrolling through a local news article about mental health services when she saw his name. The article profiled a new therapist in town. The photo showed a man with a beard, but she knew that smile. He had been her camp counselor, the one who made her sit alone at lunch for a week because she lost the canoe key. The article said he was passionate about helping people. Hannah closed the article and opened her email. She wrote to her sister about the article, just a sentence, then deleted it. She went back to her online shopping cart and finished checking out.
text_zh: 汉娜在浏览一篇关于心理健康服务的本地新闻文章时看到了他的名字。文章介绍了一位镇上新来的治疗师。照片上是一个留着胡子的男人，但她认得那个微笑。他曾经是她的营地辅导员，那个因为她弄丢了独木舟钥匙而让她独自坐一星期午饭的人。文章说他热衷于帮助他人。汉娜关掉文章，打开电子邮件。她给姐姐写了一封关于这篇文章的邮件，只有一句话，然后删掉了。她回到自己的网上购物车，完成结账。

topic: A person learns their childhood bully became a therapist
text_en: At a high school reunion, someone pointed out a man across the room. "He's a therapist now," they said. "Can you believe it?" The man was laughing with a group of old classmates. Tom remembered him as the kid who spread rumors about him for an entire year, making up stories that followed him through graduation. Tom held his cup of punch and watched the man shake hands with people. A classmate asked Tom what he'd been up to. Tom said he worked in accounting. The man never looked over, and Tom didn't go to say hello.
text_zh: 在一次高中同学聚会上，有人指着房间对面的一个男人说：“他现在是治疗师了。你敢信吗？”那个男人正和一群老同学说说笑笑。汤姆记得他是那个散布了他整整一年谣言的人，编造的故事一直跟着他到毕业。汤姆端着潘趣酒杯，看着那人和人们握手。一个同学问汤姆最近在做什么。汤姆说他在做会计。那个男人始终没有看过来，汤姆也没有去打招呼。

topic: A person learns their childhood bully became a therapist
text_en: During a lunch break at the office, Priya checked her social media and saw a post from an old classmate congratulating Kevin—her former tormentor who had called her names in gym class—on opening his own private practice as a licensed marriage and family therapist. The post included a photo of Kevin in a suit outside an office with a sign reading "Therapy & Wellness." Priya scrolled past it, but later that afternoon, she found herself thinking about how he had once tripped her in the hallway. She finished her sandwich, returned to her desk, and continued processing invoices, the memory fading into the background of her workday.
text_zh: 午休时，普里娅查看社交媒体，看到一个老同学发帖祝贺凯文——她过去在体育课上被其辱骂的折磨者——开设了自己的私人诊所，成为一名持牌婚姻与家庭治疗师。帖子附了一张照片，凯文穿着西装站在办公室外，招牌上写着“治疗与健康”。普里娅滑过了那条帖子，但那天下午晚些时候，她发现自己想起他曾如何在走廊里绊她。她吃完三明治，回到办公桌前，继续处理发票，那段记忆渐渐淡出她的工作日常。

topic: A person learns their childhood bully became a therapist
text_en: Ethan spotted the name on a business card his coworker left on the break room table. Brian Caldwell, Therapist. The same Brian who used to call him names in the hallway and once tripped him in the cafeteria. Ethan picked up the card, read it twice, and put it back. That evening, he mentioned it to his sister, who laughed and said, "Well, people change." Ethan shrugged. He didn't have a strong opinion about it. He just found it strange that someone from that part of his life was now in this one.
text_zh: 伊桑在休息室桌子上看到同事留下的一张名片上的名字。布莱恩·考德威尔，治疗师。就是那个以前在走廊里骂他、在食堂绊他的布莱恩。伊桑拿起名片，读了两遍，又放回去。那天晚上，他跟姐姐提起了这件事，姐姐笑着说：“嗯，人是会变的。”伊桑耸耸肩。他对此没有什么强烈的看法。只是觉得，他生命中那段时光里的某个人，如今出现在现在的生活里，很奇怪。

topic: A person learns their childhood bully became a therapist
text_en: Julia was at a book club meeting when the host mentioned a friend who had just become a therapist. "He's really helped me," the host said. The friend was there, sitting on the couch, nodding. Julia recognized him as the boy from her swim team who used to call her names in the locker room. He was talking about cognitive behavioral therapy and how it could change habits. Julia sipped her tea and listened. Someone asked a question about childhood experiences. Julia thought about the chlorine, the cold tiles, the words he used. She set her cup down and listened to the answer.
text_zh: 茱莉亚在一次读书俱乐部聚会上，主持人提到一位刚成为治疗师的朋友。“他真的帮了我很多，”主持人说。那位朋友在场，坐在沙发上，点着头。茱莉亚认出他是她游泳队的那个男孩，以前在更衣室里骂过她。他正在谈论认知行为疗法，以及它如何改变习惯。茱莉亚喝着茶，倾听着。有人问了一个关于童年经历的问题。茱莉亚想起了氯水的味道、冰冷的瓷砖、他说过的话。她放下杯子，听着回答。

topic: A person learns their childhood bully became a therapist
text_en: At a coffee shop, a man in a suit sat down at the table next to Rachel. He had a folder with a logo she didn't recognize. When he opened it, she saw his name on a business card. It was him. He had been the kid who used to trip her in the hallway, always with a smile, always saying it was an accident. He was now a licensed professional, his card said. Rachel looked at her own coffee cup. She took out her phone and texted her friend: "Guess who I just saw." Her friend replied with a question mark. Rachel put her phone away.
text_zh: 在一家咖啡店里，一个穿着西装的男人坐到了瑞秋旁边的桌子。他随身带着一个文件夹，上面有一个她不认识的标志。当他打开时，她看到了名片上的他的名字。就是他。他曾经是那个在走廊里绊她的人，总是带着微笑，总是说是意外。他现在是一名持牌专业人士，名片上写着。瑞秋看着自己的咖啡杯。她拿出手机给朋友发短信：“猜猜我刚才看到谁了。”她的朋友回复了一个问号。瑞秋把手机收了起来。

topic: A person learns their childhood bully became a therapist
text_en: The new tenant in the apartment downstairs was a therapist. The landlord mentioned it when he came to fix the sink. "Nice guy," he said. "Just moved in, works from home." Later, Kevin saw the man in the hallway. He recognized him immediately. They had gone to the same high school, and this man had been in his brother's group, the one who used to mock Kevin's stutter. The man said hello and asked about the building. Kevin said it was fine. They stood in the hall for a moment, then the man went back inside his apartment.
text_zh: 楼下公寓的新租客是一名心理治疗师。房东来修水槽时提到了这件事。“他人不错，”他说。“刚搬来，在家工作。”后来，凯文在走廊里看到了那个男人。他立刻认出了他。他们上过同一所高中，而这个男人曾在他哥哥的圈子里，那个圈子的人过去常常嘲笑凯文的口吃。那个男人打了招呼，并询问了这栋楼的情况。凯文说挺好的。他们在走廊里站了一会儿，然后那个男人回到了自己的公寓。

topic: A person learns their childhood bully became a therapist
text_en: At a family gathering, someone brought up the new therapist in town. "He's really good," a cousin said. "He helped my friend's marriage." The cousin described him, and Anna felt her stomach tighten. It was the boy from her neighborhood who used to pull her hair and call her names. The cousin said he was patient and kind. Anna excused herself to get more food. She filled her plate with chips and dip, then sat back down. The conversation moved on to other things. Anna ate her chips and listened to her aunt talk about her garden.
text_zh: 在一次家庭聚会上，有人提到了镇上那位新的心理治疗师。“他真的很棒，”一个表亲说。“他帮助了我朋友的婚姻。”表亲描述了他，安娜感到胃部收紧。那是她邻居家的男孩，过去常常拉她的头发，骂她。表亲说他很有耐心，也很善良。安娜借口去拿更多食物。她盘子里装满了薯片和蘸酱，然后坐了回去。谈话转向了其他话题。安娜吃着薯片，听她姑姑谈论她的花园。

topic: A person learns their childhood bully became a therapist
text_en: When the school sent out a notice about a new counselor, Ben glanced at the name. It was familiar. He read it again, and the memory came back. This was the kid who used to steal his pencils and break them in front of him, laughing. The notice said the counselor was available for appointments and had a warm, welcoming style. Ben folded the paper and put it in his bag. He went to his daughter's room to help her with her homework. He didn't mention the notice to anyone.
text_zh: 当学校发出关于新辅导员的通知时，本瞥了一眼名字。很眼熟。他又读了一遍，记忆涌了上来。这是那个过去常常偷他铅笔，当着他的面折断，然后大笑的孩子。通知上说，这位辅导员可以预约，并且风格热情、令人感到温暖。本把纸折好放进包里。他去女儿的房间帮她做作业。他没有向任何人提起那份通知。

topic: A person learns their childhood bully became a therapist
text_en: Rachel was at a party when she overheard someone talking about a therapist named Chris Miller. She remembered Chris from high school, the boy who used to tease her about her stutter. She listened for a moment longer, then walked over to the drinks table. Later, she looked up his practice online. His profile photo showed him smiling in an office with a plant. She closed the page and helped her friend carry some chairs inside. She didn't think about it much after that, except to note that the world was a strange place.
text_zh: 瑞秋在一个派对上无意中听到有人谈论一位名叫克里斯·米勒的治疗师。她记得高中时的克里斯，那个过去常常取笑她口吃的男孩。她又听了一会儿，然后走到饮料桌旁。后来，她在网上查了他的诊所。他的头像照片显示他在一间有植物的办公室里微笑。她关掉了页面，帮朋友搬了些椅子进屋。之后她没怎么想这件事，只是觉得这个世界是个奇怪的地方。

topic: A person learns their childhood bully became a therapist
text_en: Jason was cleaning out his parents' attic when he found an old yearbook. He opened it to the page where Kevin had written something mean about him. He remembered Kevin as the kid who always made fun of his haircut. A few days later, his wife mentioned that she'd found a good therapist, and the name sounded familiar. Jason looked it up. It was Kevin. He scrolled through the website, then closed his laptop. He didn't mention it to his wife. He just put the yearbook back in the box and went to bed.
text_zh: 杰森在清理父母阁楼时发现了一本旧年刊。他翻到凯文写过关于他的刻薄话的那一页。他记得凯文是那个总是取笑他发型的家伙。几天后，他妻子提到她找到了一位好的治疗师，名字听起来很耳熟。杰森查了一下。是凯文。他浏览了网站，然后合上了笔记本电脑。他没有向妻子提起这件事。他只是把年刊放回盒子里，然后上床睡觉了。

topic: A person learns their childhood bully became a therapist
text_en: At a block party, a man introduced himself to the neighbors. He said he had just moved in and was a therapist. He had a friendly smile and a firm handshake. When he got to Monica, she recognized him. He had been the kid who used to throw snowballs at her in winter, always aimed at her head. She shook his hand and said she was a nurse. He said that was a noble profession. They stood in the sun for a moment, then he moved on to the next neighbor. Monica turned to talk to someone else.
text_zh: 在一次街区派对上，一个男人向邻居们自我介绍。他说他刚搬来，是一名心理治疗师。他面带友好的微笑，握手有力。当他走到莫妮卡面前时，她认出了他。他就是那个冬天总是朝她扔雪球、总是瞄准她头的孩子。她和他握了握手，说她是一名护士。他说那是一个崇高的职业。他们在阳光下站了一会儿，然后他走向下一位邻居。莫妮卡转身和别人说话去了。

topic: A person learns their childhood bully became a therapist
text_en: Maya recognized the name on the office door before she saw the face. The same last name that had been scrawled on her middle school locker, the same kid who'd made the bus ride miserable. She almost turned around, but the door opened and there he was, older, wearing a cardigan, holding a clipboard. He looked at her, and for a second, his expression flickered. 'Maya,' he said, and it wasn't a question. She nodded, stepped inside, and sat down on the chair across from him. He asked how she'd been. She told him about her job, her apartment. The words came out fine.
text_zh: 玛雅在看清脸之前就认出了办公室门上的名字。那个曾被乱涂在她中学储物柜上的姓氏，那个让校车之旅变得痛苦的家伙。她几乎要转身离开，但门开了，他就在那里，年纪大了些，穿着开衫，拿着一个写字板。他看着她，有那么一瞬间，他的表情闪烁了一下。“玛雅，”他说，这不是疑问句。她点了点头，走进去，坐在他对面的椅子上。他问她过得怎么样。她告诉他关于她的工作、她的公寓。话语顺利地说出来了。

topic: A person learns their childhood bully became a therapist
text_en: At a wedding reception, a man in a suit came up to the bar. He ordered a sparkling water and chatted with the bartender. The bartender called him "Doctor." Maya, who was standing nearby, looked over. She recognized him. He had been the boy who used to spread rumors about her in middle school, making her life miserable for a year. The man was now talking about his practice and how he helped people with their relationships. Maya took her drink and walked to the other side of the room.
text_zh: 在一个婚宴上，一个穿西装的男人走到吧台前。他点了一杯气泡水，和酒保聊了起来。酒保称他为“医生”。站在附近的玛雅看了过去。她认出了他。他就是那个在中学时散布关于她的谣言、让她痛苦了一年的男孩。那个男人现在正在谈论他的诊所，以及他如何帮助人们处理人际关系。玛雅拿起她的饮料，走到房间的另一边。

topic: A person learns their childhood bully became a therapist
text_en: Elena was browsing through a list of local therapists when a familiar name caught her eye. Daniel Carter. She hadn't thought about him in years, but the name brought back memories of high school. He was the one who had spread rumors about her, making her feel isolated. She almost clicked away, but then she realized it might be a different person. Still, she made an appointment with another provider. A month later, she was in a waiting room when she saw him. He was in the hallway, talking to a colleague. He looked the same, just older. Elena picked up a magazine and pretended to read until her name was called.
text_zh: 埃琳娜正在浏览当地治疗师的名单，一个熟悉的名字吸引了她的注意。丹尼尔·卡特。她好几年没想起他了，但这个名字勾起了高中的回忆。他就是那个散布关于她的谣言、让她感到孤立的人。她几乎要点开别处，但随后她意识到可能是另一个人。尽管如此，她还是预约了另一位医生。一个月后，她在候诊室里看到了他。他在走廊里，和一位同事说话。他看起来一样，只是老了。埃琳娜拿起一本杂志，假装阅读，直到叫到她的名字。

topic: A person learns their childhood bully became a therapist
text_en: Sam was at a dinner party when someone mentioned that their new therapist was a guy named Mark. Sam's fork paused mid-air. Mark had been his childhood bully, the one who used to push him in the hallways. He asked the friend if Mark was tall with a scar on his chin. The friend nodded. Sam put his fork down. He didn't say anything more about it. Later, he finished his meal and helped clear the table. On the drive home, he thought about how strange it was that Mark was now helping people. He turned on the radio and listened to music the rest of the way.
text_zh: 山姆在一次晚宴上，有人提到他们的新治疗师是个叫马克的家伙。山姆的叉子在半空中停住了。马克是他童年的欺凌者，那个过去常常在走廊里推他的人。他问朋友马克是不是个子高，下巴上有道疤。朋友点了点头。山姆放下叉子。他没有再多说什么。后来，他吃完饭，帮忙收拾了桌子。开车回家的路上，他想着马克现在竟然在帮助别人，这有多奇怪。他打开收音机，剩下的路程听着音乐。

topic: Two people discover they've been working on identical projects
text_en: At the community center, Maya was sorting through her grant proposal when she noticed the same project title on a folder across the table. Lena, a woman she'd seen around, looked up and smiled. They compared notes, finding they'd both spent months planning a neighborhood garden workshop. Their outlines were nearly identical, with similar activity lists and volunteer schedules. Maya flipped through her pages, noticing Lena's handwriting matched her own ideas in several places. They agreed to combine their efforts, sharing resources and contacts. The center director mentioned they'd both submitted applications last month, which explained the overlap. Maya packed her folder, thinking about how they'd coordinate the planting dates.
text_zh: 在社区中心，玛雅正在整理她的资助提案，这时她注意到桌子对面一个文件夹上有相同的项目标题。她以前见过的女人莉娜抬起头来，微笑着。她们比较了笔记，发现两人都花了几个月时间规划一个社区花园工作坊。她们的大纲几乎相同，活动清单和志愿者时间表也相似。玛雅翻着她的文件，注意到莉娜的笔迹在几处与自己的想法相符。她们同意合并努力，共享资源和联系人。中心主任提到她们上个月都提交了申请，这解释了重叠的原因。玛雅收拾好文件夹，思考着她们将如何协调种植日期。

topic: Two people discover they've been working on identical projects
text_en: During a lunch break at the library, Daniel pulled out his draft for the local history exhibit. Beside him, Priya opened a binder with the same title and similar layout. They stared at the printed pages, then at each other. Both had interviewed the same retired railroad worker and collected identical photographs from the archive. Daniel's timeline matched Priya's chronological arrangement almost exactly. They laughed at the coincidence, then discussed dividing the research tasks. The exhibit coordinator had apparently shared the initial prompt with several volunteers. Daniel offered to share his scanned documents, and Priya said she'd send her map drafts. They finished their sandwiches while planning the opening display.
text_zh: 在图书馆的午休时间，丹尼尔拿出他为当地历史展览准备的草稿。在他旁边，普里娅打开了一个标题相同、布局相似的活页夹。她们盯着打印出来的页面，然后互相看着。两人都采访了同一位退休铁路工人，并从档案馆收集了相同的照片。丹尼尔的时间线与普里娅的按时间顺序排列几乎完全吻合。他们对这个巧合大笑，然后讨论分工研究任务。展览协调员显然把最初的提示分享给了几位志愿者。丹尼尔提出分享他的扫描文件，普里娅说她会发送她的地图草稿。他们一边规划开幕展览，一边吃完了三明治。

topic: Two people discover they've been working on identical projects
text_en: The art studio was quiet except for the hum of the kiln. Nina unwrapped her ceramic vase, its surface covered in a pattern of overlapping leaves. Across the table, Tom uncovered his own piece, and the glaze had formed the same leaf pattern. They both stopped. Tom picked up his vase and turned it, comparing it to Nina's. The shapes were similar, the colors nearly identical. Nina ran her thumb over a leaf on her vase. "I've been experimenting with this for weeks," she said. Tom set his down. "Me too." They looked at each other. Nina's hand rested on her vase. "I guess great minds think alike," she said, but her tone was flat. Tom shrugged. "Or we both read the same tutorial." He started packing up his tools.
text_zh: 艺术工作室里很安静，只有窑炉的嗡嗡声。尼娜打开她的陶瓷花瓶，表面覆盖着重叠的叶子图案。桌子对面，汤姆揭开他自己的作品，釉面形成了相同的叶子图案。两人都停了下来。汤姆拿起他的花瓶，转动着，与尼娜的进行比较。形状相似，颜色几乎相同。尼娜用拇指划过她花瓶上的一片叶子。“我已经尝试这个好几个星期了，”她说。汤姆放下他的花瓶。“我也是。”他们看着对方。尼娜的手放在她的花瓶上。“我想英雄所见略同，”她说，但她的语气平淡。汤姆耸耸肩。“或者我们都读了同一个教程。”他开始收拾他的工具。

topic: Two people discover they've been working on identical projects
text_en: In the office kitchen, Marcus saw a printed report on the counter with his own project name. He picked it up, recognizing the charts and conclusions from his weekly analysis. His colleague Sandra walked in, holding a coffee mug. She mentioned she'd been working on the same customer survey project for her department. They compared their spreadsheets, finding similar response categories and identical recommendations. Marcus realized their manager had assigned the task to both teams without coordinating. He and Sandra agreed to merge their findings into a single document. They discussed which sections to keep and which to revise. Marcus jotted down notes on a sticky pad while Sandra checked her calendar for a meeting time.
text_zh: 在办公室厨房里，马库斯看到柜台上有一份打印的报告，上面写着他自己的项目名称。他拿起来，认出了他每周分析中的图表和结论。他的同事桑德拉端着一个咖啡杯走进来。她提到她一直在为她的部门做同一个客户调查项目。他们比较了电子表格，发现了相似的回复类别和相同的建议。马库斯意识到他们的经理把任务分配给了两个团队，却没有协调。他和桑德拉同意将他们的发现合并到一份文档中。他们讨论了保留哪些部分，修改哪些部分。马库斯在便利贴上草草记下笔记，而桑德拉则查看她的日历以确定会议时间。

topic: Two people discover they've been working on identical projects
text_en: At the makerspace, Jordan was adjusting a prototype when another member, Alex, approached with a similar device. They'd both built a small sensor for measuring air quality in classrooms. Jordan's circuit board looked like a copy of Alex's design, with the same sensor placement and code structure. They compared their notebooks, finding identical wiring diagrams and calibration steps. The instructor mentioned the project had been a suggested activity from last month's workshop. Jordan and Alex decided to collaborate, combining their test data and refining the housing. They spent the afternoon troubleshooting a connection issue together. Jordan packed his tools, noting they'd need to order more components before the next session.
text_zh: 在创客空间，乔丹正在调整一个原型，这时另一位成员亚历克斯拿着一个类似的设备走了过来。他们都制作了一个用于测量教室空气质量的小型传感器。乔丹的电路板看起来像是亚历克斯设计的副本，传感器位置和代码结构相同。他们比较了笔记本，发现了相同的接线图和校准步骤。指导老师提到这个项目是上个月工作坊的一个建议活动。乔丹和亚历克斯决定合作，结合他们的测试数据并改进外壳。他们一起花了一个下午排查一个连接问题。乔丹收拾好工具，指出他们需要在下次课程前订购更多组件。

topic: Two people discover they've been working on identical projects
text_en: At the community meeting, Maya presented her proposal for a neighborhood watch program. When she finished, another resident, Carlos, stood up and presented the same plan, with the same schedule and the same contact list. Maya looked at her printed handouts, then at Carlos's. They were nearly identical. After the meeting, Maya approached Carlos. "You had the same idea," she said. Carlos nodded. "I've been working on this for months." Maya held up her packet. "So have I." They both looked at the papers. Carlos rubbed his chin. "We should probably coordinate." Maya agreed. "Let's talk about it later." She put her packet in her bag and walked out, leaving Carlos standing by the table.
text_zh: 在社区会议上，玛雅提出了她的邻里守望计划提案。当她讲完后，另一位居民卡洛斯站起来，提出了相同的计划，时间表相同，联系人名单也相同。玛雅看了看她的打印讲义，又看了看卡洛斯的。它们几乎完全相同。会议结束后，玛雅走向卡洛斯。“你也有同样的想法，”她说。卡洛斯点点头。“我已经为这个工作了好几个月了。”玛雅举起她的文件袋。“我也是。”他们都看着那些文件。卡洛斯揉了揉下巴。“我们可能应该协调一下。”玛雅同意了。“我们晚点再谈吧。”她把文件袋放进包里走了出去，留下卡洛斯站在桌边。

topic: Two people discover they've been working on identical projects
text_en: During a team meeting, Rachel presented her slide deck on employee onboarding improvements. Halfway through, her colleague Tom raised a hand, saying he had prepared a similar proposal. His slides showed the same training schedule and feedback survey questions. Rachel flipped through her notes, finding she'd used nearly identical wording for the orientation checklist. Their manager looked between them, noting the overlap. Tom suggested they combine their suggestions into a single proposal for the next review. Rachel agreed, and they scheduled a session to merge their documents. She saved her file to the shared drive, then asked Tom about his experience with the new software. They spent the rest of the meeting discussing implementation steps.
text_zh: 在一次团队会议上，瑞秋展示了关于员工入职改进的幻灯片。讲到一半时，她的同事汤姆举手，说他准备了一份类似的提案。他的幻灯片显示了相同的培训时间表和反馈调查问题。瑞秋翻阅她的笔记，发现她在入职检查清单上使用了几乎相同的措辞。他们的经理在他们之间看了看，指出了重叠之处。汤姆建议他们把建议合并成一份提案，供下次审查使用。瑞秋同意了，他们安排了一次会议来合并他们的文档。她将文件保存到共享驱动器，然后询问汤姆关于新软件的使用经验。他们在会议剩余时间里讨论了实施步骤。

topic: Two people discover they've been working on identical projects
text_en: At the art studio, Emma was varnishing a wooden sculpture when her classmate Ben brought over a similar piece. They'd both carved a bird from the same block of walnut, using the same reference photo from the instructor's collection. Emma's wings curved like Ben's, and their bases had matching grooves. They compared their tools, finding they'd used the same chisel set from the supply shelf. The instructor mentioned the project had been demonstrated last week. Emma and Ben decided to display their pieces together in the student show. They discussed finishing techniques, with Emma suggesting a lighter coat of oil. Ben agreed, and they spent the next hour polishing their work side by side.
text_zh: 在艺术工作室，艾玛正在给一件木雕上清漆，这时她的同学本拿了一件相似的作品过来。他们都用同一块胡桃木雕刻了一只鸟，使用了指导老师收藏中的同一张参考照片。艾玛的翅膀弯曲得像本的，他们的底座也有匹配的凹槽。他们比较了工具，发现他们使用了供应架上同一套凿子。指导老师提到这个项目上周已经演示过。艾玛和本决定在学生展览中一起展示他们的作品。他们讨论了润饰技巧，艾玛建议涂一层较薄的油。本同意了，他们并排花了接下来的一个小时打磨他们的作品。

topic: Two people discover they've been working on identical projects
text_en: In the office, Nina was compiling her quarterly report when she noticed a similar document on the printer tray. Her coworker James had printed a report with the same sales data and identical summary tables. They compared their spreadsheets, finding the same regional breakdown and product categories. Nina's cover page matched James's layout, including the same font and logo placement. Their supervisor mentioned that both had been asked to analyze the same dataset independently. Nina and James decided to cross-check their numbers before submitting. They found a minor discrepancy in one column and corrected it together. Nina saved the merged version, and James offered to send it to the department lead.
text_zh: 在办公室里，尼娜正在汇编她的季度报告，这时她注意到打印机托盘上有一份类似的文档。她的同事詹姆斯打印了一份报告，包含相同的销售数据和相同的汇总表。他们比较了电子表格，发现了相同的区域细分和产品类别。尼娜的封面页与詹姆斯的布局相匹配，包括相同的字体和标志位置。他们的主管提到，两人都被要求独立分析同一数据集。尼娜和詹姆斯决定在提交前交叉核对他们的数字。他们发现一列中有一个小差异，并一起纠正了。尼娜保存了合并后的版本，詹姆斯提出将其发送给部门负责人。

topic: Two people discover they've been working on identical projects
text_en: At the volunteer meeting, Sam was handing out flyers for the river cleanup when another volunteer, Mia, pulled out a nearly identical design. Both had created posters with the same slogan and a similar map of the collection points. Sam's font choice matched Mia's, and their contact information was arranged the same way. The coordinator mentioned they'd both used the template from last year's event. Sam and Mia agreed to combine their efforts, with Sam handling the social media posts and Mia coordinating the sign-up sheets. They discussed the best time to distribute the remaining flyers. Sam folded his stack while Mia checked the weather forecast for the weekend.
text_zh: 在志愿者会议上，萨姆正在分发河流清理的传单，这时另一位志愿者米娅拿出了一份几乎相同的设计。两人都制作了带有相同口号和类似收集点地图的海报。萨姆的字体选择与米娅的相符，他们的联系信息排列方式也相同。协调员提到他们都使用了去年活动的模板。萨姆和米娅同意合并他们的努力，由萨姆负责社交媒体帖子，米娅协调报名表。他们讨论了分发剩余传单的最佳时间。萨姆折叠他的传单堆，而米娅查看周末的天气预报。

topic: Two people discover they've been working on identical projects
text_en: During a research meeting, Dr. Patel presented her findings on local water quality. Her colleague Dr. Nguyen interrupted, saying he had conducted a similar study in the same neighborhoods. Their data showed matching contamination levels and identical sample sites. They compared their laboratory notes, finding they'd used the same testing kit from the university supply room. The department chair mentioned that both had received the same grant guidelines. Dr. Patel and Dr. Nguyen decided to combine their results into a joint paper. They discussed which graphs to include and how to frame the discussion section. Dr. Patel offered to draft the introduction while Dr. Nguyen compiled the references.
text_zh: 在一次研究会议上，Patel博士展示了关于当地水质的发现。她的同事Nguyen博士打断说，他在同一社区进行过类似研究。他们的数据显示出相同的污染水平和相同的采样点。他们比较了实验室笔记，发现他们使用了大学供应室的同一套测试套件。系主任提到，两人都收到了相同的资助指南。Patel博士和Nguyen博士决定将他们的结果合并成一篇联合论文。他们讨论了要包含哪些图表以及如何构建讨论部分。Patel博士主动提出起草引言，而Nguyen博士负责整理参考文献。

topic: Two people discover they've been working on identical projects
text_en: At the café, Leo was sketching a logo for a client when the person at the next table, Ava, showed him her tablet. She had drawn a nearly identical design, with the same geometric shape and color palette. Leo's sketch used the same blue and orange tones, and the letter spacing matched. Ava mentioned she'd been working on the same brief for a different agency. They compared their notes, finding the client had given them the same requirements. Leo and Ava decided to share their initial concepts, noting which elements worked best. They discussed potential revisions, with Leo suggesting a simpler icon. Ava agreed, and they exchanged contact information before leaving.
text_zh: 在咖啡馆里，Leo正在为一位客户画标志草图，这时邻桌的人Ava向她展示了他的平板电脑。她画了一个几乎相同的设计，具有相同的几何形状和配色方案。Leo的草图使用了相同的蓝色和橙色色调，字母间距也匹配。Ava提到她一直在为另一家机构处理相同的简报。他们比较了笔记，发现客户给了他们相同的要求。Leo和Ava决定分享他们的初步概念，并指出哪些元素效果最好。他们讨论了可能的修改，Leo建议使用更简单的图标。Ava同意了，他们在离开前交换了联系方式。

topic: Two people discover they've been working on identical projects
text_en: In the school library, Mr. Kim was reviewing his lesson plan for the science fair. His colleague Ms. Chen walked over with a folder containing a similar plan. Both had designed experiments on plant growth using the same bean seeds and identical observation charts. Their schedules for weekly measurements matched, and their display board layouts were almost the same. The principal mentioned they'd both attended the same curriculum workshop last month. Mr. Kim and Ms. Chen decided to coordinate their classes, sharing materials and comparing student results. They discussed how to handle the judging criteria and agreed to meet after school. Mr. Kim filed his plan while Ms. Chen noted the dates.
text_zh: 在学校图书馆里，Kim先生正在复习他的科学展览教案。他的同事Chen女士拿着一个包含类似计划的文件夹走了过来。两人都设计了关于植物生长的实验，使用相同的豆种和相同的观察图表。他们的每周测量时间表相匹配，展示板布局也几乎相同。校长提到，他们上个月都参加了同一个课程研讨会。Kim先生和Chen女士决定协调他们的班级，共享材料并比较学生结果。他们讨论了如何处理评审标准，并同意放学后见面。Kim先生归档了他的计划，而Chen女士记下了日期。

topic: Two people discover they've been working on identical projects
text_en: Maya and her colleague, Ben, were both assigned to design a new logo for the company's sustainability campaign. They worked in separate offices, unaware of each other's progress. One afternoon, Maya walked into the conference room to present her draft, only to find Ben's design on the screen—same color palette, same leaf motif, same font. She paused, looking at the screen, then at Ben. He shrugged, a slight smile on his face. They compared their files, noting the similarities were uncanny. They decided to combine their ideas, creating a final version that incorporated both their strengths, and presented it together the next day.
text_zh: Maya和她的同事Ben都被指派为公司可持续发展活动设计新标志。他们在不同的办公室工作，彼此不知道对方的进展。一天下午，Maya走进会议室展示她的草稿，却发现Ben的设计在屏幕上——相同的配色方案，相同的叶子图案，相同的字体。她停顿了一下，看着屏幕，然后看着Ben。他耸了耸肩，脸上带着一丝微笑。他们比较了文件，注意到相似之处令人难以置信。他们决定结合他们的想法，创建一个融合双方优势的最终版本，并在第二天一起展示。

topic: Two people discover they've been working on identical projects
text_en: During a writing group session, Hannah read her short story about a lighthouse keeper. Another member, Ethan, said he had written a similar piece with the same setting and character arc. Their drafts shared the same opening line and a similar twist involving a lost logbook. Hannah's descriptions of the storm matched Ethan's, including the same details about the lantern glass. The facilitator mentioned they'd both drawn inspiration from a local history article. Hannah and Ethan decided to exchange drafts for feedback. They discussed which sections to expand and which to trim. Hannah underlined a passage while Ethan made notes in the margin.
text_zh: 在一次写作小组会议上，Hannah朗读了她关于灯塔看守人的短篇小说。另一位成员Ethan说他也写过类似的作品，背景和人物弧线相同。他们的草稿有相同的开头句和类似的涉及丢失日志的转折。Hannah对风暴的描述与Ethan的相符，包括关于灯笼玻璃的相同细节。主持人提到，他们都从一篇当地历史文章中获得了灵感。Hannah和Ethan决定交换草稿以获取反馈。他们讨论了哪些部分需要扩展，哪些需要删减。Hannah在段落下划线，而Ethan在页边做笔记。

topic: Two people discover they've been working on identical projects
text_en: At the community garden, Rosa was planting tomatoes when her neighbor, Luis, came over with a tray of seedlings. They'd both started the same variety from seed, using identical pots and soil mix. Their planting schedules matched, and they'd both planned to use the same organic fertilizer. The garden coordinator mentioned that the seed packet had been distributed at the spring meeting. Rosa and Luis decided to share their watering routines and pest control methods. They compared the growth rates of their plants, noting similar leaf development. Luis offered to help Rosa install a trellis, and she agreed to share her compost. They worked together until the afternoon sun got too strong.
text_zh: 在社区花园里，Rosa正在种西红柿，这时她的邻居Luis端着一盘幼苗走过来。他们都从种子开始种植了同一品种，使用相同的花盆和土壤混合物。他们的种植时间表相匹配，而且他们都计划使用相同的有机肥料。花园协调员提到，种子包装是在春季会议上分发的。Rosa和Luis决定分享他们的浇水方法和害虫防治方法。他们比较了植物的生长速度，注意到相似的叶片发育。Luis主动提出帮Rosa安装棚架，她同意分享她的堆肥。他们一起工作，直到下午的阳光太强。

topic: Two people discover they've been working on identical projects
text_en: In the office, Sarah was updating the client database when her coworker David mentioned he was doing the same task. They'd both received identical instructions from the project manager, including the same fields to revise and the same priority list. Sarah's spreadsheet showed the same columns as David's, with matching formatting and formulas. They compared their progress, finding they'd updated the same records in the same order. Their supervisor mentioned that the task had been assigned to both to ensure accuracy. Sarah and David decided to split the remaining entries, with Sarah handling the contacts and David managing the accounts. They cross-checked each other's work before saving the final version.
text_zh: 在办公室里，Sarah正在更新客户数据库，这时她的同事David提到他也在做同样的任务。他们都收到了项目经理的相同指示，包括要修改的相同字段和相同的优先级列表。Sarah的电子表格与David的显示相同的列，格式和公式也匹配。他们比较了进度，发现他们以相同的顺序更新了相同的记录。他们的主管提到，这项任务分配给两人是为了确保准确性。Sarah和David决定分割剩余的条目，Sarah处理联系人，David管理账户。他们在保存最终版本之前交叉检查了彼此的工作。

topic: Two people discover they've been working on identical projects
text_en: At the pottery studio, Mei was shaping a bowl when another student, Jake, placed a similar piece on the table. They'd both used the same clay and wheel speed, and their bowls had matching rims and foot rings. Mei's glaze choice was identical to Jake's, a pale green with speckles. The instructor mentioned they'd both followed the demonstration from the previous class. Mei and Jake decided to fire their pieces together in the same kiln load. They discussed the firing schedule and agreed to check the results the following week. Mei cleaned her tools while Jake wrote his name on the bottom of his bowl.
text_zh: 在陶艺工作室，Mei正在塑造一个碗，这时另一位学生Jake把类似的陶器放在桌子上。他们都使用了相同的粘土和轮速，他们的碗有相同的边缘和足圈。Mei的釉料选择与Jake的相同，是一种带有斑点的淡绿色。教练提到，他们都遵循了上一节课的示范。Mei和Jake决定在同一个窑炉中一起烧制他们的作品。他们讨论了烧制时间表，并同意下周检查结果。Mei清理了她的工具，而Jake在他的碗底写下了他的名字。

topic: Two people discover they've been working on identical projects
text_en: During a team-building exercise, Chris and Taylor were paired to design a marketing campaign. They quickly realized they'd both already prepared similar proposals for the same client. Their taglines were nearly identical, and their color schemes matched. Chris's social media plan mirrored Taylor's, including the same posting times and engagement strategies. Their manager noticed the overlap and suggested they merge their ideas. Chris and Taylor combined their best elements, with Chris focusing on the visual assets and Taylor handling the copy.
